title: Wonder: Video World Model Done Better
authors: Jiacong Xu, Hanwen Jiang, Zhixin Shu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Vishal M. Patel
abstract: We present Wonder, a general-purpose video world model for real-time, camera-controllable world exploration. Given an image or a conditional video, Wonder constructs a playable world where users can navigate interactively by moving the camera, discovering unseen regions, and revisiting previously observed areas in real time and over a long-term horizon. Achieving this capability requires a system-level co-design of control method, memory mechanism, and training strategy. We introduce a novel cam

infographic.key_insight: Wonder turns a single image or conditional video into a playable, real-time world model that users can explore by moving the camera. Its core advance is co-designing control, memory, and training so the model can revisit known areas and discover unseen regions over long horizons.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of building a general-purpose video world model that is both interactive and temporally consistent, while supporting real-time camera control and long-term exploration.
method: Builds a camera-controllable video world model from an image or conditional video input.
Uses a system-level co-design of control mechanisms, memory for preserving past observations, and training strategy for stable long-horizon generation.
Supports interactive navigation in a playable environment, enabling users to explore unseen regions and return to previously viewed areas in real time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Wonder provides a practical step toward interactive generative environments for simulation, planning, and content creation. It highlights how combining control, memory, and training design can improve realism and consistency in world models.

title: Pictura: Perspective-View Self-Play at Scale for Driving
authors: Yuan Yin, Elias Ramzi, Marc Lafon, Valentin Charraut, Victor Bares
abstract: Self-play in simulation produces robust driving policies at scale. Demonstrations of such behavior have been made using privileged vectorized observations such as exact poses and velocities, even for occluded agents. This assumes that perception is solved and introduces a representation gap with the partial observation of a deployed agent driving from the perspective view of egocentric cameras. A common fix, distilling the privileged policy into a camera-input student, leaves the student imitati

infographic.key_insight: Pictura closes the gap between high-performing self-play driving policies trained with privileged simulation data and real camera-based driving agents. It does this by learning directly from perspective-view observations at scale, instead of relying only on a later distillation step.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the mismatch between simulation-trained driving policies that use full privileged state information and deployed agents that only see partial egocentric camera views. This representation gap makes it hard to transfer strong self-play behavior into real-world perception-driven driving systems.
method: Train self-play driving policies using perspective-view inputs rather than exact privileged vectors.
Scale learning in simulation so the policy can develop robust driving behavior from camera-like observations.
Reduce the need for a separate teacher-student distillation pipeline that can limit performance when transferring privileged knowledge.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more realistic path to training autonomous driving agents that work from the same kind of inputs they will see at deployment. It can improve transferability, reduce reliance on privileged annotations, and simplify the pipeline from simulation to real-world use.

title: MDTransformer: A Hardware-Software Co-Design of Mode-Division Photonic Transformer Accelerator with Inverse-Designed Coherent Crossbar
authors: Solomon Micheal Serunjogi, Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Ayat Taha, Muhammad Shafique, Mahmoud Rasras
abstract: Recently, photonic transformer accelerators (PTAs) have successfully achieved significant speedup and energy efficiency improvements over electronic accelerators for expediting Transformer inference. However, state-of-the-art rely on expensive multi-wavelength light generation and large dot-product units due to active phase-shifter components, thus making their approach inefficient and impractical. To address this, we propose MDTransformer, a novel hardware-software co-design of PTA based on mod

infographic.key_insight: MDTransformer proposes a hardware-software co-design for photonic Transformer acceleration that reduces reliance on expensive multi-wavelength sources and large dot-product units. It uses a mode-division photonic architecture with an inverse-designed coherent crossbar to make Transformer inference more efficient and practical.
infographic.problem_solved: Current photonic Transformer accelerators are limited by costly light-generation requirements and bulky, inefficient dot-product hardware built around active phase-shifters, making them hard to scale and deploy.
method: Designs a mode-division photonic Transformer accelerator to improve hardware efficiency.
Introduces an inverse-designed coherent crossbar to support compact and scalable optical computation.
Co-optimizes hardware and software to better match Transformer inference workloads with photonic circuitry.
infographic.impact: This work could make photonic AI acceleration more realistic for high-throughput, energy-efficient Transformer inference. For practitioners, it points to a path toward faster inference hardware with lower power and potentially better scalability than conventional photonic designs.

title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
authors: Malena Loza, David Chushig-Muzo, Eva Milara, Luis Bote-Curiel, Luis Estrada-Petrocelli
abstract: Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) have emerged as novel approaches for tabular predictive tasks, demonstrating competitive predictive performance to ensemble tree-based models. Most TFMs are trained and evaluated on independent and identically distributed data, but this assumption changes in real-world scenarios due to distribution shifts, which compromise the robustness of models. Limited research has been conducted of TFMs under distribution shifts. We present an empirical evaluation of Out-Of-

infographic.key_insight: This paper evaluates how tabular foundation models behave when the data changes at test time, rather than only when training and testing data come from the same distribution. The core takeaway is that strong in-distribution performance does not necessarily guarantee robustness under real-world distribution shifts.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the gap in understanding whether tabular foundation models remain reliable when faced with out-of-distribution data, a common challenge in practical ML deployments.
method: Conducts an empirical evaluation of tabular foundation models under distribution shifts.
Compares model performance across shifted and non-shifted tabular settings to assess robustness.
Benchmarks TFMs against common baselines, including ensemble tree-based approaches, to contextualize results.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, this helps reveal when TFMs are suitable for deployment and when they may fail under changing data conditions. It supports better model selection, risk assessment, and robustness-aware evaluation for tabular ML applications.

title: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Reasoning over Interacting Streams for Video-Level Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition
authors: Podakanti Satyajith Chary, Barath Parthiban, Pranesh Velmurugan, Adeeba Khan, Nagarajan Ganapathy
abstract: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are conflicting affective states that precede the delay or abandonment of health behaviour change. Recognition of A/H at the video level is difficult, since the signal arises from disagreement across and within facial, vocal, linguistic, and bodily modalities, and manifests differently across individuals. The proposed PRISM-AH (Predictive Reasoning over Interacting Streams for Multimodal Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition), is a framework that treats A/H as a multi

infographic.key_insight: PRISM-AH frames ambivalence and hesitancy as a multimodal reasoning problem, where useful signals come from disagreements and interactions across face, voice, language, and body cues. It aims to detect these subtle states at the video level by combining predictive reasoning with knowledge-guided fusion across streams.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of recognizing ambivalence and hesitancy in videos, where the emotional signal is not obvious and may appear differently across people and modalities. Standard multimodal models often miss these conflicting, weak, and interaction-based cues.
method: Uses PRISM-AH, a framework for Predictive Reasoning over Interacting Streams, to model multimodal inputs jointly.
Treats A/H as a video-level phenomenon driven by cross-modal disagreement and within-modal dynamics, rather than single-frame or single-modality cues.
Incorporates knowledge-guided reasoning to better capture subtle, conflicting affective patterns across facial, vocal, linguistic, and bodily streams.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shows how to model subtle human affect in real-world videos where signals are ambiguous and distributed across modalities. The approach is relevant for health-behavior applications, affective computing, and any task requiring robust multimodal reasoning under uncertainty.

title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
authors: Haolei Xu, Xiaowen Xu, Haiwen Hong, Zixuan Ni, Hongxing Li
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) grounds token-level supervision in the student's own trajectory, yet suffers from prefix failure: once the student commits to a wrong reasoning direction, all subsequent generation builds on this deviation, producing misdirected continuations that elicit unreliable supervision and waste compute. We identify a teacher-student continuation asymmetry on failed prefixes, where the teacher tends to redirect while the student continues along the original direction, and con

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that on-policy distillation fails when a student makes an early reasoning mistake, because the student keeps following the wrong path while the teacher would often recover or redirect. Their key idea is to relay the trajectory so supervision stays aligned with a more useful continuation.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses prefix failure in on-policy distillation: once a student enters a bad reasoning branch, later token-level supervision becomes misaligned, less reliable, and wastes computation.
method: Identify teacher-student continuation asymmetry on failed prefixes, where the teacher and student diverge in how they continue after an error.
Relay the trajectory to replace or adjust the student’s failed continuation with a teacher-guided path that better preserves meaningful supervision.
Use this relayed on-policy setup to keep training grounded in the student’s own generation while avoiding compounding mistakes.
infographic.impact: This can make distillation more robust and compute-efficient for reasoning-heavy models. Practitioners may get better student behavior from fewer wasted rollouts and more informative training signals.

title: LaP-Forensics: Latent-Pixel Consistency Guided Multimodal Reasoning for Deepfake Detection
authors: Can Wang, Yuhao Wang, Yushe Cao, Canran Xiao, Fei Shen
abstract: Recent generative models can produce images with few obvious visual artifacts, weakening detectors and explanations that rely only on surface appearance. We present LaP-Forensics, a multimodal framework that augments RGB semantics with reconstruction-based forensic evidence. A frozen Stable Diffusion DDIM inversion-reconstruction model provides a fixed reconstruction reference, and its residual map measures local compatibility with that reference. Independent projectors encode the RGB image and

infographic.key_insight: LaP-Forensics improves deepfake detection by combining what an image looks like with how well it matches a diffusion-model reconstruction reference. This latent-pixel consistency signal exposes subtle manipulations that are hard to catch with RGB appearance alone.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the growing challenge of detecting and explaining deepfakes generated by modern models that leave few obvious visual artifacts, making surface-level detectors unreliable.
method: Use a frozen Stable Diffusion DDIM inversion-reconstruction model to create a fixed reconstruction reference for each image.
Compute a residual map that measures local compatibility between the input image and the reconstructed reference, providing forensic evidence.
Encode RGB semantics and reconstruction-based forensic cues with independent projectors, then fuse them for multimodal reasoning and detection.
infographic.impact: This matters because it gives practitioners a more robust way to detect high-quality synthetic images when visual artifacts are minimal. It also improves interpretability by grounding decisions in both semantic content and reconstruction inconsistency.

title: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams
authors: Siyu Xia, Chenheng Zhang, Yanting Wu, Haoxuan Li, Jiajun Chai
abstract: Memory is essential for LLM agents to accumulate task experience and reuse task-specific execution strategies. However, real-world deployment over boundary-agnostic and evolving task streams exposes a fundamental stability-plasticity dilemma. External retrieval-based memory can rapidly absorb new evidence, but it often fails to internalize recurring execution patterns and incurs inference-time retrieval overhead. Parametric memory enables stable and efficient execution once learned, but typicall

infographic.key_insight: UniMem combines fast episodic memory with stable parametric memory so LLM agents can learn from experience and keep using recurring task patterns efficiently, even when task boundaries are unclear.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the stability-plasticity dilemma in long-running, boundary-agnostic task streams: external retrieval memory adapts quickly but does not internalize reusable behaviors, while parametric memory is efficient but difficult to update without forgetting.
method: Builds a complementary memory system that stores raw episodic experiences and distills recurring patterns into parametric memory.
Uses episodic-to-parametric transfer so repeated task strategies can be absorbed into the model rather than repeatedly retrieved.
Aims to reduce inference-time retrieval overhead while improving long-term adaptation to evolving tasks.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means agents can become more reliable and efficient over time by learning reusable execution strategies instead of depending only on expensive retrieval. It is especially useful for deployed systems operating on continual, messy, real-world task streams.

title: Co-Learning for Missing Arbitrary Modalities in Multi-modal Classification
authors: Francisco Mena, Dino Ienco, Roberto Interdonato, Cassio F. Dantas, Simon Besnard
abstract: Multi-modal classification leverages complementary information across diverse data sources to enhance predictive performance. However, real-world scenarios subject to operational constraints, such as sensor failures or privacy restrictions, lead to inconsistent modality availability between training and inference times. To handle missing modalities, prior studies have mainly covered bimodal data setups and focused on designing robust fusion processes. Instead, we adopt a multi-modal co-learning

infographic.key_insight: This paper tackles a practical gap in multi-modal learning: models often fail when some modalities are missing at training or test time. Its core idea is to use co-learning so information from available modalities can help compensate for missing arbitrary modalities, beyond the usual bimodal setting.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses multi-modal classification under inconsistent modality availability caused by real-world issues such as sensor failures, privacy limits, or deployment constraints. The goal is to make classification models more robust when any subset of modalities may be absent.
method: Adopts a multi-modal co-learning framework instead of relying only on robust fusion across fixed modality pairs.
Designed to handle arbitrary missing modalities, not just simple bimodal missingness.
Uses information from observed modalities during learning to improve performance when modality patterns differ between training and inference.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, this means multi-modal systems can be deployed more reliably in messy real-world settings where inputs are incomplete. It supports stronger generalization and reduces performance drops when data sources are unavailable.

title: Spatio-Temporal Conditional Denoising Transformer for Modality-Missing RGBT Tracking
authors: Andong Lu, Ziyi Zha, Jiandong Jin, Shihao Li, Chenglong Li
abstract: Missing modalities in RGBT tracking often lead to incomplete and unstable multimodal feature representations that greatly degrade the performance. Existing methods typically attempt to recover missing modalities from available ones, but the quality of data generated in challenging scenarios might be unsatisfactory. In addition, current approaches exhibit limited flexibility in processing both missing and complete data. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Spatio-temporal Conditional Denoi

infographic.key_insight: The paper tackles RGBT tracking when one modality is missing by using a conditional denoising transformer that can work with both complete and incomplete inputs. The core idea is to make tracking robust to missing thermal or RGB information without relying on fragile modality reconstruction.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing RGBT trackers often break down when one modality is absent or degraded, because they depend on reconstructing missing data from the other modality. This creates unstable features and poor performance in challenging real-world scenes, while also limiting flexibility for handling both full and partial modality inputs.
method: Introduces a spatio-temporal conditional denoising transformer for modality-missing RGBT tracking.
Uses conditional denoising to fuse available modalities and suppress noise caused by missing or incomplete inputs.
Designed to handle both complete and missing-modality scenarios more flexibly than methods that only focus on modality recovery.
infographic.impact: This approach can improve the robustness of multimodal tracking systems in real-world settings where sensors may fail or be partially unavailable. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable way to build trackers that gracefully degrade under missing data instead of collapsing.

title: ClinFusion: A Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM System for Holistic Medical Understanding
authors: Hangjie Yuan, Yichen Qian, Zhiwei Tang, Xianzhe Xu, Lirong Wu
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) hold immense potential to revolutionize clinical practice, yet deploying them in the medical domain is fundamentally a vision-centric challenge: models must absorb knowledge from heterogeneous 2D and 3D medical images, and evaluation protocols must align with radiologists' clinical practice and provide an accurate, fine-grained and factualness-driven assessment. In this paper, we introduce ClinFusion, a vision-centric MLLM designed for holistic medical un

infographic.key_insight: ClinFusion reframes medical MLLMs as a vision-first problem: success depends not just on language reasoning, but on learning from diverse 2D and 3D medical images and being judged with clinically realistic evaluation. It aims to provide more holistic medical understanding with finer, more factual assessments.
infographic.problem_solved: Current medical MLLMs struggle with heterogeneous clinical imaging and are often evaluated with benchmarks that do not match radiologists' workflows, making results less accurate and less clinically meaningful.
method: Builds a vision-centric multimodal LLM system tailored to medical imaging rather than general-purpose text-heavy reasoning.
Integrates knowledge from heterogeneous 2D and 3D medical image sources to support broader clinical understanding.
Uses evaluation protocols designed to better reflect radiologists' practice, emphasizing fine-grained, accurate, and factual assessment.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ClinFusion highlights that medical multimodal systems need domain-specific vision handling and domain-aligned evaluation to be truly useful in clinical settings. This can lead to more reliable models and more trustworthy benchmarking in healthcare AI.

title: ERUnderstand: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Structured ER Diagrams
authors: Ali Ansari, Yasmin Mohammadi, Farnoush Nili, Parsa Esmaeilkhani, Longin Jan Latecki
abstract: Entity-Relationship Diagrams (ERDs) are central to conceptual database design, yet they are typically available only as rendered images rather than machine-readable schemas, limiting AI-assisted database engineering. We introduce ERUnderstand, the first large-scale benchmark for structured understanding of ER diagrams, comprising 2,960 diagrams collected from curated educational sources, real-world schemas, and synthetically generated examples spanning diverse domains, notations, complexity leve

infographic.key_insight: ERUnderstand is the first large-scale benchmark designed to test whether vision-language models can truly understand structured Entity-Relationship diagrams, not just recognize their visual appearance. It fills a major gap by turning ERD understanding into a measurable AI evaluation task.
infographic.problem_solved: AI systems struggle to use ER diagrams because they are usually stored as images rather than machine-readable schemas, making database design and analysis hard to automate. This paper addresses the lack of a standard benchmark for evaluating structured ER diagram understanding.
method: Introduces ERUnderstand, a benchmark of 2,960 ER diagrams.
Covers diverse sources including educational materials, real-world schemas, and synthetic examples.
Includes variation in domain, notation, and diagram complexity to evaluate robustness across settings.
infographic.impact: This benchmark gives researchers and practitioners a standardized way to measure how well vision-language models can interpret database design diagrams. It can accelerate progress toward AI tools for schema extraction, database engineering, and diagram-based reasoning.

title: Data Pyramid for Embodied Manipulation
authors: Yifan Ye, Yankai Fu, Yaoxu Lv, Bohan Hou, Jun Cen
abstract: Multimodal foundation models learned to see and to speak by consuming the whole internet. Embodied agents admit no such shortcut, since they require data that couple observations with physical states and actions. These signals can be provided, to varying degrees, by multiple data sources. In this work, we organize the embodied data ecosystem as a "pyramid" spanning five complementary sources: real-robot data, UMI-style data, egocentric and exocentric data, simulation data, and general vision-lan

infographic.key_insight: Embodied manipulation needs a structured data strategy, not just more data. This paper proposes a five-level "data pyramid" that ranks embodied data sources by how directly they connect observations, physical state, and actions.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a unified way to organize and compare data sources for embodied agents. Unlike web-scale language/vision models, embodied systems need data tied to real physical interactions, which comes from many fragmented sources with different levels of realism and supervision.
method: Organize embodied data into a pyramid of five complementary sources: real-robot data, UMI-style data, egocentric/exocentric data, simulation data, and general vision-language data.
Use the pyramid to show how each source contributes different strengths, from high-fidelity action grounding to broad visual-language coverage.
Provide a framework for thinking about data collection and model training across the embodied AI ecosystem.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this gives a practical roadmap for choosing and combining datasets when training embodied agents. It helps balance realism, scale, and cost, making it easier to design more capable manipulation systems.

title: Panda: Unsupervised Pelvic Anomaly Detection for Real-Time MR Imaging
authors: Anika Knupfer, Maximilian Lindholz, Johanna Paula Müller, Jordina Aviles Verdera, Smiti Tripathy
abstract: Female pelvic diseases remain an under researched area characterized by often delayed diagnosis. While pelvic MRI offers superior soft-tissue contrast for diagnosis and image-guided procedures, real-time anomaly detection remains challenging due to physiological motion, tissue deformation, and instrument artifacts. Existing supervised approaches are impractical, as adverse events are rare, heterogeneous, and difficult to annotate. We present a Dinomaly-based unsupervised anomaly detection framew

infographic.key_insight: This paper proposes an unsupervised anomaly detection framework for real-time pelvic MRI, aiming to flag abnormal regions without needing rare, labor-intensive labeled adverse-event data. The key idea is to make pelvic MR imaging safer and more responsive by detecting anomalies on the fly.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of detecting pelvic anomalies in real time during MRI, where motion, tissue deformation, and instrument artifacts make interpretation hard. Supervised methods are not practical because true adverse events are rare, diverse, and expensive to annotate.
method: Uses a Dinomaly-based unsupervised anomaly detection framework.
Targets real-time pelvic MRI settings where labeled abnormal cases are scarce or unavailable.
Focuses on identifying deviations from normal anatomy and imaging appearance despite motion and artifact noise.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how anomaly detection can be used in high-stakes medical imaging settings where supervised learning is limited by missing labels. It is especially relevant for building robust real-time systems that support clinical decision-making and image-guided procedures.

title: DreamStyle3D: Efficient 3D Stylized Asset Generation via Dual-Attention Disentanglement
authors: Kai Wang, Ziheng Ouyang, Xuying Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Qibin Hou
abstract: With the growth of gaming, animation, and virtual reality industries, the demand for efficient generation of stylized 3D assets is rapidly increasing. However, existing approaches still struggle to jointly preserve style fidelity, geometric consistency, and generation efficiency, as most of them still rely on indirect 2D-to-3D stylization pipelines. This motivates a native 3D stylization framework that can explicitly disentangle style from geometry while remaining efficient. To this end, we prop

infographic.key_insight: DreamStyle3D introduces a native 3D stylization framework that separates style from geometry, aiming to generate stylized assets more efficiently and consistently than indirect 2D-to-3D pipelines. The core idea is dual-attention disentanglement: preserve appearance style without corrupting 3D structure.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of creating stylized 3D assets that simultaneously maintain style fidelity, geometric consistency, and high generation efficiency—something current 2D-to-3D stylization methods often fail to achieve.
method: Uses a native 3D stylization pipeline instead of relying on indirect 2D-to-3D conversion.
Applies dual-attention disentanglement to explicitly separate style features from geometric structure.
Optimizes for efficient generation while preserving both visual style and 3D consistency.
infographic.impact: This work is useful for practitioners building game assets, animation content, and VR scenes because it points toward faster production of high-quality stylized 3D models. It also offers a cleaner design principle for future generative 3D systems: disentangle appearance from shape.

title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
authors: Bingnan Li, Haozhe Wang, Haozhong Xiong, Fangtai Wu, Jinpeng Yu
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) adapts diffusion models by querying a teacher along trajectories generated by the current student, but how it should behave under classifier-free guidance (CFG), a default component of modern diffusion systems, remains poorly understood. Existing OPD methods naturally extend velocity matching to the CFG-composed prediction, directly matching teacher and student guided velocities. We show that this objective is under-identified at the branch level: positive- and negat

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that directly matching classifier-free guided outputs in on-policy diffusion distillation can be ambiguous at the branch level: the positive and negative guidance branches are not uniquely identified. The authors argue that distillation should account for this under-identification instead of treating the guided prediction as a single target.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses how to correctly perform on-policy distillation for diffusion models when classifier-free guidance (CFG) is used, since existing methods can mismatch teacher and student behavior by only matching the composed guided prediction.
method: Analyze why standard velocity matching on CFG-composed outputs is under-identified at the branch level.
Reformulate distillation to better respect the separate roles of positive and negative guidance branches.
Compare teacher and student behavior along on-policy trajectories rather than relying only on static guidance targets.
infographic.impact: This makes diffusion distillation more reliable for modern CFG-based systems, helping practitioners train smaller or faster models without silently losing guidance fidelity. It is especially relevant for text-to-image and other conditional diffusion applications where CFG is a default design choice.

title: Beyond Scale and Generation: Understanding Language Model-based Entity Matching
authors: Zeyu Zhang, Xue Li, Iacer Calixto, Paul Groth, Sebastian Schelter
abstract: Entity matching identifies records that refer to the same real-world entity. Language models can be adapted to this task through bi-encoder, cross-encoder, and generative matcher architectures. However, prior studies often conflate matcher architecture with differences in model backbone, model variant(reflecting different pretraining objectives), and model size, making it difficult to isolate the sources of performance gains. We address this issue through a controlled factorial study spanning th

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that improvements in language-model-based entity matching cannot be attributed to architecture alone; backbone, pretraining variant, and model size all interact and must be controlled separately. By disentangling these factors, it identifies what actually drives performance gains.
infographic.problem_solved: Prior entity-matching studies often mix together different matcher architectures, model backbones, model variants, and sizes, making it unclear which design choices really improve results.
method: Runs a controlled factorial study over entity-matching setups to isolate architecture effects from backbone, variant, and size.
Compares bi-encoder, cross-encoder, and generative matcher architectures under matched experimental conditions.
Analyzes performance differences systematically to identify the true sources of gains.
infographic.impact: This gives practitioners a clearer basis for choosing and tuning language models for entity matching. It reduces misleading comparisons and helps teams invest in the model choices that genuinely improve accuracy and efficiency.

title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability
authors: Krithi Shailya, Ananya Lakshmi Ravi, Venkatanathan K. V., Sowmya S. Sundaram, Gokul S. Krishnan
abstract: Computer vision models have become highly effective for medical applications, yet their black-box nature continues to undermine clinician trust. In clinical workflows, chest X-ray classifiers are increasingly paired with Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to generate natural-language explanations. However, these systems add linguistic fluency without addressing the underlying opacity of the visual model. With the emergence of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), whose spline-based components provide in

infographic.key_insight: KANEx aims to turn the interpretability of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) into clinically useful explanations for medical imaging, going beyond fluent but shallow text generated by vision-language models. It connects the visual model’s internal structure to explanation generation so clinicians can better understand why a chest X-ray prediction was made.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between prediction accuracy and explainability in medical AI, where chest X-ray classifiers may be accurate but remain black boxes. It also tackles the limitation of current VLM-based explanation systems that produce natural-language rationales without exposing the underlying decision process of the visual model.
method: Uses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to leverage spline-based, more interpretable components in the image classifier.
Translates model internals into explanation signals that can support medical explainability.
Integrates the interpretability of KANs with chest X-ray analysis to produce explanations that are more grounded in the model’s behavior.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights a path toward explainable medical imaging systems that are both accurate and trustworthy. It is especially relevant for deploying models in clinical settings where transparency, auditability, and clinician confidence are essential.

title: MicroZoom: Structure-Preserving Detail Synthesis at Extreme Scale
authors: Huy Huynh, Jingwei Ma, Brian Curless, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman, Steven M. Seitz
abstract: We introduce MicroZoom, a generative framework for gigapixel image synthesis at the microscopic scale. Given a standard photograph and a sparse set of consumer-grade microscope close-ups, MicroZoom synthesizes a seamless, gigapixel-resolution image grounded in the material character of the real references, enabling exploratory visualization of microscopic texture across the full spatial extent of an object. Our goal is plausible synthesis, not exact reconstruction. We focus on full-image, refere

infographic.key_insight: MicroZoom can turn a normal photo plus a few microscope close-ups into a seamless gigapixel-scale microscopic image. It preserves the real material character of the references while generating plausible fine detail across the whole object.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of creating extremely high-resolution microscopic imagery over an entire object when only a standard photograph and sparse local microscope samples are available. It aims for believable detail synthesis rather than exact reconstruction.

It also supports exploratory visualization of materials at microscopic resolution from minimal input data.

title: MineValiCoder: Reliable Code Generation with Test Case Quality Mining and Bipartite Graph-Based Mutual Validation
authors: Zhen Zhao, Qihang Yang, Feifei Dai, Xiangfang Li, Bo Li
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based Test-Driven Development (TDD) has advanced automated code generation. However, existing approaches depend heavily on human-crafted test cases and cannot operate effectively when only natural-language requirements are available. Although recent work enables automatic test generation, it often overlooks the inherent stochasticity of LLMs, leading to two key defects: faulty tests generate misleading feedback that distorts code optimization, while mixed-quality test

infographic.key_insight: MineValiCoder improves LLM-based code generation by filtering and validating test cases before using them to optimize code. Its core idea is that better test quality leads to more reliable code, especially when only natural-language requirements are available.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses unreliable automated code generation when test cases are generated by LLMs and may be noisy, faulty, or mixed-quality. These weak tests can mislead the code improvement loop and degrade final output quality.
method: Mines test-case quality to identify and remove faulty or low-confidence tests.
Uses bipartite graph-based mutual validation to cross-check relationships between tests and candidate code outputs.

infographic.impact: This matters because it makes test-driven code generation more trustworthy in realistic settings where human-written tests are unavailable. For practitioners, it offers a practical way to reduce error propagation from bad tests and improve code quality from natural-language specs.

title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
authors: Kaixiong Gong, Xin Cai, Bin Lin, Hao Wang, Yunlong Lin
abstract: Unified multimodal models seek a shared visual token space that supports both multimodal understanding and image generation. Discrete methods unify the interface via a shared codebook, whereas continuous pipelines often rely on two disparate representations -- semantic features (e.g., ViT) for understanding and low-level latents (e.g., VAE) for synthesis -- resulting in mismatched latent spaces. We propose Twins, a unified continuous token space formed by channel-wise concatenating ViT and VAE f

infographic.key_insight: Twins proposes a single continuous token space that unifies multimodal understanding and image generation, instead of forcing these tasks to use separate latent representations. It does this by combining ViT semantic features and VAE low-level latents, then training them with a focal loss to better predict unified representations.
infographic.problem_solved: Unified multimodal models often need one interface for both understanding and synthesis, but existing continuous pipelines split this into two mismatched spaces: semantic embeddings for understanding and latent image codes for generation. This mismatch makes it harder to align tasks and train a truly unified model.
method: Channel-wise concatenate ViT features and VAE latents to form a unified continuous token space.
Use focal loss to improve prediction of the unified representation, emphasizing harder-to-learn tokens.
Train the model so the same token space can support both multimodal understanding and image generation.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a cleaner multimodal design that reduces the gap between understanding and generation. It can simplify model interfaces and potentially improve transfer across tasks that need both semantic reasoning and image synthesis.

title: Dysphagia Risk Stratification in Head and Neck Cancer via Two-Stage PRO-Clinical Stacking
authors: Siyuan Zhao, Eric Ababio Anyimadu, Zachary G. Brumm, Yue Ma, Clifton David Fuller
abstract: Dysphagia is a debilitating late effect of head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, yet timely identification of at-risk patients remains challenging in survivorship care. Definitive assessment relies on videofluoroscopic imaging, as captured by the Dynamic Imaging Grade of Swallowing Toxicity (CTCAE-DIGEST), which, while validated, requires specialized equipment, trained personnel, and significant patient burden, limiting its routine use in surveillance. Patient-reported outcomes (PROs), by contra

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows that swallowing-risk in head and neck cancer survivors can be predicted by stacking patient-reported outcome data with clinical information in a two-stage model. The approach aims to flag patients at high risk of dysphagia earlier and more cheaply than relying on videofluoroscopy alone.
infographic.problem_solved: Routine dysphagia surveillance after head and neck cancer treatment is difficult because the gold-standard assessment (videofluoroscopic CTCAE-DIGEST) is resource-intensive, requires specialized staff/equipment, and is burdensome for patients. The paper addresses the need for scalable, timely risk stratification in survivorship care.
method: Uses a two-stage PRO-clinical stacking framework to combine patient-reported outcomes with clinical variables.
Learns an intermediate risk representation from PROs, then integrates that signal with clinical data for improved prediction of dysphagia risk.
Targets risk stratification rather than replacing imaging, helping prioritize who should receive more definitive swallow evaluation.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a practical example of multimodal clinical prediction that leverages low-cost, high-coverage PROs to augment sparse medical assessments. It highlights how stacked models can improve triage and screening in healthcare workflows where gold-standard labels are expensive or inconvenient.

title: PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest
authors: Olafur Gudmundsson, Bo Zhao, Huayi Liao, Anna Kiyantseva, Sai Xiao
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new solution for addressing the content cold-start problem in industry-scale search and recommender systems. Compared to prior approaches, we have made the following new contributions: 1) our solution spans the entire multi-stage funnel and generalizes well for both search and recommendation surfaces, 2) our solution reduces bias favoring existing content, allowing more accurate model prediction across content types and reducing short-term tradeoffs associated with hi

infographic.key_insight: PinEqualizer tackles content cold-start by improving how new or underexposed content is explored and ranked across the full search-and-recommendation funnel. It also reduces the system's bias toward already popular content, helping models make fairer predictions across different content types.
infographic.problem_solved: Industry-scale search and recommender systems often struggle to surface new content because existing content is over-favored, creating a cold-start and exploration bias problem across multiple ranking stages.
method: Applies a full-funnel solution that works across multiple stages of retrieval, ranking, and final selection.
Generalizes across both search and recommendation surfaces instead of being limited to one product area.
Reduces popularity bias so the system can better explore new content and improve prediction accuracy across content types.
infographic.impact: This matters because it helps AI systems discover fresh content more effectively without sacrificing ranking quality. For practitioners, it offers a practical path to reduce bias and improve long-term content health in large-scale recommender and search systems.

title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
authors: Siyuan Huang, Pengyu Cheng, Haotian Liu, Tao Chen, Yihao Liu
abstract: LLM training is shifting from manual design and annotation to interaction-driven self-evolution. However, existing self-evolutionary methods face a fundamental dilemma between task diversity and verification reliability: environment-bound methods obtain precise feedback but confine learning to narrow domains, while open-ended self-generation broadens the task space but lacks reliable verification, allowing misleading rewards to pollute the training loop. We identify agent skills as a powerful mi

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that agent skills can serve as the right unit for self-improvement: by co-evolving skills, LLMs can explore a broader space of tasks without losing reliable feedback. This aims to push capability beyond narrow, environment-bound training loops.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the tradeoff in self-evolutionary LLM training between task diversity and verification reliability. Existing methods either stay in narrow domains with strong feedback or generate diverse tasks with weak, error-prone supervision.
method: Treat skills as reusable building blocks for self-play and self-evolution rather than optimizing only on isolated tasks.
Co-evolve skills through interaction-driven training so task generation and verification reinforce each other.
Use the skill-centric loop to expand the task space while keeping feedback grounded and trustworthy.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a promising way to train LLM agents that improve through interaction without depending heavily on manual annotation. It could enable more scalable, generalizable, and reliable capability growth across diverse real-world tasks.

title: \k{appa}-LoRA: Condition Numbers Reveal Which LoRA Matrices Worth Updating
authors: Jianghui Wang, Silong Yong, Francesco Orabona, Marco Canini, Katia P. Sycara
abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely adopted technique for efficient neural network fine-tuning, decomposing model updates into low-rank matrices. However, LoRA remains computationally costly because it updates all matrices uniformly, regardless of their actual contribution to adaptation. This cost is especially prohibitive for large-scale models with billions of parameters and for resource-constrained settings such as edge deployment and on-device fine-tuning. We show for the first ti

infographic.key_insight: kappa-LoRA argues that not all LoRA matrices are equally worth updating. By using condition numbers to identify which matrices matter most, it targets adaptation where it is most effective and avoids wasting compute on less useful updates.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard LoRA fine-tuning updates all low-rank matrices uniformly, which is expensive and inefficient for very large models and edge/on-device settings. This paper addresses the need to reduce adaptation cost without sacrificing performance.
method: Analyze LoRA matrices using condition numbers to estimate how important each matrix is for adaptation.
Selectively update the matrices that are most likely to benefit from training, instead of updating every LoRA module equally.
Use this importance-based filtering to reduce compute and memory overhead while preserving fine-tuning effectiveness.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, kappa-LoRA offers a more efficient way to fine-tune large models, especially when compute, memory, or latency are constrained. It can make adaptation more practical for billion-parameter models, edge deployment, and on-device learning.

title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
authors: Shing Ho J. Lin, Wenzhao Zheng, Dong Zhuo, Yuqi Wu, Jie Zhou
abstract: Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs) have substantially advanced monocular 3D reconstruction, yet extending this capability to 4D dynamic understanding remains a fundamental challenge. Most existing motion perception methods (e.g., sparse tracking, dense point-wise flow) treat motion as independent point-wise displacements, ignoring the structured nature of physical motion. However, real-world objects usually obey rigid-body kinematics, and points thus usually move collectively, not in isolation. M

infographic.key_insight: SM4RT argues that motion in dynamic scenes should be modeled as structured geometry, not as independent point-by-point movement. By leveraging rigid-body kinematics, it aims to make 4D reconstruction more physically consistent and accurate.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between strong monocular 3D reconstruction and true 4D dynamic understanding. Existing motion methods often ignore the fact that many real-world objects move as coherent structures, which limits reconstruction quality in dynamic scenes.
method: Learn structured motion geometry instead of predicting isolated point-wise flow or sparse tracks.
Exploit physical regularities such as rigid-body motion to group points into collectively moving units.
Use this structured motion prior to improve 4D reconstruction of dynamic scenes over time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shifts dynamic reconstruction from noisy local motion estimation toward more physically grounded scene modeling. That can improve robustness, interpretability, and downstream performance in robotics, AR/VR, and autonomous systems.

title: Hyperball May Not Be a Free Lunch
authors: Yihao Xiao, Jialong Sun, Zitian Gao, Zeming Wei, Chutian Wang
abstract: For scale-invariant deep networks, Hyperball-style optimizers have shown strong performance in large-scale training by fixing the norms of matrix-valued parameters and normalizing updates. However, the source of their advantage remains unclear. Starting from the angular displacement between consecutive parameter states, we derive an angular effective learning rate that accounts for the parameter-update angle, parameter norm, and update norm. We also show that the conventional norm-based measure

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that Hyperball-style optimizers are not automatically a "free lunch": their apparent gains depend on the geometry of parameter updates, not just norm control. The authors introduce an angular effective learning rate that better explains optimization behavior by combining parameter angle, parameter norm, and update norm.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the open question of why Hyperball optimizers work well for scale-invariant deep networks and whether their benefits come from a genuinely better learning dynamic or from a misleading norm-based interpretation of progress.
method: Derive an angular effective learning rate based on the angular displacement between consecutive parameter states.
Incorporate three factors into the update analysis: parameter-update angle, parameter norm, and update norm.
Compare the new angle-aware measure against conventional norm-based measures to explain Hyperball-style behavior more accurately.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, this work provides a more faithful way to understand and tune optimizers for scale-invariant models. It suggests that controlling norms alone may not explain training success, so angle-aware diagnostics can lead to better optimizer design and more reliable training decisions.

title: CARA: Concept-Aware Risk Attention for Interpretable Collision Anticipation
authors: Zhishan Tao, Ruoyu Wang, Yucheng Wu, Enjun Du, Yilei Yuan
abstract: Collision anticipation in autonomous driving requires not only accurate early warnings but also interpretable reasoning about what risk factors are being tracked and how risk evolves over time. Existing methods fall short in this regard: feature-driven models are opaque, post-hoc explanations often lack fidelity, and concept-based methods are mostly designed for static recognition rather than dynamic driving scenes. We propose CARA (Concept-Aware Risk Attention), an intrinsically interpretable s

infographic.key_insight: CARA makes collision anticipation interpretable by explicitly tracking human-understandable risk concepts over time, rather than relying on opaque features alone. It aims to explain not just whether a collision is likely, but which risk factors are driving the prediction and how they evolve.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of faithful, interpretable early-warning systems for autonomous driving collision anticipation. Existing approaches are either accurate but opaque, or interpretable only through post-hoc explanations that do not reliably reflect the model's true reasoning, especially in dynamic driving scenes.
method: Introduces Concept-Aware Risk Attention (CARA), an intrinsically interpretable framework for collision anticipation.
Uses concept-level representations to track semantically meaningful risk factors in driving scenes over time.
Learns attention over risk concepts to show how evidence for collision builds and changes across frames.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CARA shows how to build predictive models that are both effective and transparent, which is especially important in safety-critical systems like autonomous driving. It supports debugging, trust, and decision-making by making temporal risk reasoning visible.

title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
authors: Ritik Raj, Souvik Kundu, Sarbartha Banerjee, Dheemanth Joshi, Ishita Vohra
abstract: Routing to select large language models (LLMs) with different cost-quality trade-offs has become a fundamental deployment feature of enterprise AI. Existing routers, primarily make independent routing decisions for each LLM call. However, agentic applications execute as long-horizon workflows whose quality is determined only by a delayed, task-level outcome. This mismatch prevents per-call routers from correctly attributing feedback to individual routing decisions. Towards mitigating this, we pr

infographic.key_insight: TRACE-ROUTER reframes LLM routing for agentic AI as a task-level decision problem, rather than optimizing each call in isolation. This lets the router adapt to delayed feedback and choose models that better balance quality and cost across long-horizon workflows.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing LLM routers make independent per-call choices, but agentic applications are multi-step workflows where success is only known after the full task completes. This creates a credit-assignment problem: it is hard to tell which routing decisions helped or hurt the final outcome.
method: Uses task-consistent routing so decisions are optimized for the final workflow outcome, not just immediate call-level signals.
Adapts online to feedback from completed agentic tasks, enabling continual improvement as workloads change.
Balances cost and quality by routing different steps to different LLMs based on learned task-level utility.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this approach can improve the reliability and efficiency of agentic systems that use multiple models across long workflows. It is especially useful in enterprise settings where minimizing cost without sacrificing task success is critical.

title: Thinking and rethinking data AI readiness
authors: Unknown
abstract:

Training machine learning models on high-quality biological datasets can quickly produce abundant results. But as datasets often evolve over time, further work is required to update models and maintain alignment between models and datasets.

infographic.key_insight: High-quality biological data can make models useful quickly, but that usefulness fades if the data changes and the model is not updated. The paper highlights that AI readiness is not a one-time state—it needs continual reassessment and re-alignment between datasets and models.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of keeping machine learning models aligned with evolving biological datasets over time, so models remain accurate, relevant, and trustworthy as new data arrives or existing data changes.
method: Train models on high-quality biological datasets to establish strong initial performance.
Continuously monitor dataset evolution and detect when data shifts away from the model’s original training conditions.
Update, retrain, or re-evaluate models to maintain alignment and preserve AI readiness over time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reinforces that deployment does not end at training—data drift and dataset evolution must be managed continuously. It is especially important in biology and other fast-moving domains where model validity can degrade quickly.

title: grapheme-kit: Grapheme-Level Metrics and Text Processing for Multilingual NLP
authors: Izzath Nisfer, Ashini Kavindya, Ovindu Atukorala, Purushoth Velayuthan, Menan Velayuthan
abstract: Existing lexical distance, similarity, and evaluation metrics operate on Unicode code points, which can misrepresent errors in writing systems where a single grapheme is represented by multiple Unicode code points. We introduce grapheme-kit, an open-source Python library that extends these metrics to operate on grapheme clusters instead. The library also provides improved grapheme processing for Tamil and Sinhala, including accurate grapheme cluster identification and grapheme composition/decomp

infographic.key_insight: grapheme-kit shifts text evaluation from Unicode code points to grapheme clusters, making multilingual metrics more faithful to how characters are actually perceived and written. This is especially important for scripts where one visible character can be made of multiple code points, such as Tamil and Sinhala.
infographic.problem_solved: Many NLP distance, similarity, and evaluation metrics miscount errors in languages whose writing systems use multi-code-point graphemes. This can lead to inaccurate scoring, poor analysis of model outputs, and misleading comparisons across multilingual text.
method: Reimplements common lexical distance, similarity, and evaluation metrics to operate on grapheme clusters instead of raw Unicode code points.
Adds improved grapheme processing utilities for Tamil and Sinhala, including grapheme cluster identification and grapheme composition/decomposition.
Provides an open-source Python library for integrating grapheme-aware text processing into multilingual NLP pipelines.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means more accurate evaluation of spelling, transliteration, normalization, and generation tasks in multilingual settings. It reduces hidden errors caused by Unicode-level mismatch and improves fairness across scripts.

title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
authors: Yubin Kim, Ken Gu, Chanwoo Park, Chunjong Park, Samuel Schmidgall
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01268-y

A controlled study of large language model agents across 260 configurations shows when multi-agent collaboration helps or hurts performance, and introduces a predictive model that selects the best architecture in 87% of held-out within-domain configurations.

infographic.key_insight: Multi-agent collaboration is not always better: for capable language models, adding more agents or coordination can sometimes reduce performance instead of improving it. The paper shows these tradeoffs can be predicted well enough to choose the best setup in most within-domain cases.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the practical question of when multi-agent language model systems actually help, and when they introduce overhead, redundancy, or conflict that harms results.
method: Ran a controlled study over 260 multi-agent configuration settings.
Compared performance across different collaboration architectures to identify conditions where collaboration helps or hurts.
Trained a predictive model to recommend the best architecture for a given setting, achieving 87% accuracy on held-out within-domain configurations.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps avoid assuming that more agents automatically means better performance. It provides a data-driven way to design multi-agent systems more efficiently and select the right architecture for a task.

title: Learning to Prepare Molecular Ground States with Transformer Models
authors: Alex Koziell-Pipe, Jasmine Brewer, Jem Guhit, Marwa H. Farag, Kripa Panchagnula
abstract: Quantum state preparation is a key component of many quantum algorithms. Performing this step efficiently is essential for realizing practical quantum advantage in quantum chemistry applications. Iterative algorithms like ADAPT-VQE can produce shallow ground-state preparation circuits, but become computationally prohibitive for the larger molecules relevant to materials science and pharmaceutical development. Here, we introduce ADAPT-GQE, a generative AI framework that learns to synthesize groun

infographic.key_insight: This paper introduces ADAPT-GQE, a generative AI approach that learns to construct quantum circuit ansätze for molecular ground-state preparation. Instead of relying on expensive iterative optimization alone, it aims to generate efficient circuits directly for harder chemistry problems.
infographic.problem_solved: Quantum state preparation is a bottleneck in quantum chemistry, especially for larger molecules where methods like ADAPT-VQE become too costly to run. The paper addresses the need for scalable, shallow circuit generation for preparing molecular ground states.
method: Uses a transformer-based generative model to learn patterns in successful ground-state preparation circuits.
Synthesizes candidate quantum circuits for molecular systems, reducing dependence on exhaustive iterative search.
Targets efficient ansatz generation to support scalable quantum chemistry workflows.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how sequence models can be applied to scientific discovery and quantum algorithm design. It highlights a path toward using generative models to accelerate domain-specific optimization problems that are otherwise computationally expensive.

title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
authors: Athanasios Papastathopoulos-Katsaros, Steven T. Lee, Lin Yao, Ajay Thomas, Junseok Park
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to diagnose neurological conditions, but its analysis usually relies on either predefined spectral features or deep neural networks. Predefined features carry a strong bias, since they fix in advance what counts as informative, while deep neural networks and foundation models are hard to interpret and need large amounts of data and compute. We present bag-of-waves, an interpretable framework that learns a small dictionary of recurring EEG waveform temp

infographic.key_insight: Bag-of-waves learns a compact, human-interpretable dictionary of recurring EEG waveforms instead of relying on fixed handcrafted features or opaque deep models. This makes EEG analysis more explainable and better suited to low-data settings.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the tradeoff between interpretability and performance in EEG analysis, especially when labeled data are scarce. It aims to replace rigid predefined spectral features and data-hungry deep networks with a learnable, understandable representation.
method: Learn a small dictionary of recurring EEG waveform patterns from data.
Represent each EEG signal as a bag of these learned waves, capturing spatial and temporal structure.
Use the learned waveform tokens for downstream evaluation tasks in low-data regimes while keeping the model interpretable.

title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
authors: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan, Joon-Young Lee
abstract: Scene understanding requires simultaneous prediction about geometry, appearance, and semantics. However, existing task-specific annotations are fragmented across incompatible, domain-specific datasets. Current unified systems circumvent this by restricting training to fully co-annotated data, or by incurring the large computational cost of pseudo-labeling. To mitigate this, we introduce UniD, a unified video model that jointly predicts eight dense scene properties-depth, surface normals, semanti

infographic.key_insight: UniD shows that a single video model can learn to predict many dense scene properties at once, even when the training annotations come from different datasets that do not overlap. The key idea is to unify fragmented supervision without relying on expensive pseudo-label generation.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the problem of training unified scene-understanding models when annotations for depth, normals, semantics, motion, and other dense tasks are scattered across incompatible datasets. Existing approaches either require fully co-annotated data or costly pseudo-labeling, which limits scalability.
method: Train one unified video model (UniD) to jointly predict eight dense scene properties from disjoint training data.
Use a shared representation so knowledge transfers across tasks and video frames, reducing dependence on task-specific fully labeled datasets.
Avoid large-scale pseudo-labeling by directly learning from fragmented annotations across datasets.
infographic.impact: This matters because it makes multi-task dense prediction more practical and scalable for real-world AI systems. Practitioners can build stronger unified models from the data they already have, instead of collecting expensive all-in-one annotations.

title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
authors: Dongjie Fu, Di Cao, Xize Cheng, Zihan Zhang, Wenxu Jia
abstract: While large audio-language models have achieved remarkable progress in auditory perception, they still lag behind text-based large language models in deep logical reasoning, primarily due to the scarcity of high-quality audio reasoning data. To bridge this gap, we propose X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework that transfers reasoning capabilities from a powerful text teacher to an audio-language student. During training, the student generates reasoning trajectories conditione

infographic.key_insight: X^3-OPD teaches large audio-language models to reason better by distilling step-by-step reasoning from a strong text teacher during training, instead of relying on scarce audio reasoning labels. The result is a cross-modal alignment method that directly improves logical reasoning in audio tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Large audio-language models can perceive sounds well, but they still struggle with deep logical reasoning because high-quality audio reasoning data is limited and expensive to collect.
method: Use a powerful text-based teacher model to generate reasoning targets for the audio student.
Train the audio-language student with on-policy alignment, letting it produce its own reasoning trajectories during training.
Distill cross-modal reasoning ability so the student learns to connect audio inputs with structured logical steps rather than only surface-level predictions.
infographic.impact: This matters because it offers a practical way to improve reasoning in audio AI without needing massive annotated audio reasoning datasets. Practitioners building speech, sound, and audio-assistant systems can use this framework to make models more capable of multi-step inference and decision-making.

title: Scale Up Strategically: Learning Compositional Generalization via Bias-Aware Evaluation and Data Collection for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Yu Qi, Zhang Ye, Xinyi Xu, Yuxuan Lu, Amitoj Sandhu
abstract: Compositional generalization is essential for robot to follow diverse instructions. However, pretrained policies are known to take shortcuts, deferring to salient cues rather than grounding language. We introduce a diagnostic framework that localizes this failure to individual \textit{instruction factors}, \textit{e.g.,} reusable semantic components such as color, verb, object, size, and spatial attribute. Our framework formalizes instruction factor bias, the tendency of fine-tuned policies to o

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows that robotic policies often generalize poorly because they rely on biased instruction shortcuts instead of truly composing language factors like color, object, verb, size, and spatial relations. The authors propose a bias-aware diagnostic and data-collection strategy to expose these failures and improve compositional generalization.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of robots failing to follow novel combinations of instructions, especially when fine-tuned policies overfit to salient cues rather than learning the underlying meaning of each instruction component.
method: Introduces a diagnostic framework that breaks instructions into reusable factors such as verb, object, color, size, and spatial attribute.
Measures instruction factor bias to identify which components a policy over-relies on or ignores.
Uses bias-aware evaluation to localize generalization failures and guide more strategic data collection for robotic manipulation.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical way to evaluate whether a robot is actually understanding language or just exploiting shortcuts. It can improve data efficiency and make policy training more reliable for diverse real-world instructions.

title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
authors: Qian Wu, Xinrong Zhou, Zizhan Ma, Kai Chen, Zheyao Gao
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise for medical education, but most existing systems focus on localized interactions such as question answering or single-turn feedback, rather than organizing an entire clinical case into a decision-centered learning trajectory. We introduce \textit{MedGame}, a framework that transforms static clinical cases into structured, executable storytelling games. MedGame uses a dual-engine design: a Medical Narrative Designer synthesizes case-grounded clinical stor

infographic.key_insight: MedGame turns static medical cases into interactive, story-driven learning games powered by large language models. Instead of isolated Q&A, it guides learners through a full clinical decision journey.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap in medical-education AI systems that only support localized interactions, such as single-turn question answering or feedback, rather than structured, end-to-end case learning.
method: Uses a dual-engine framework to generate executable storytelling games from clinical cases.
A Medical Narrative Designer transforms case-grounded clinical information into a coherent narrative learning flow.
The system organizes the case into decision points so learners actively choose actions and experience consequences within the storyline.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how LLMs can be used beyond chatbots to build interactive, pedagogically structured training tools. It suggests a scalable way to convert domain content into engaging decision-based simulations.

title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
authors: Xiao Yu, Baolin Peng, Ruize Xu, Hao Zou, Qianhui Wu
abstract: Modern AI agents rely on elaborate inference harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw to drive multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and access to external systems. While powerful, these complex harnesses also make agents hard to train end-to-end with open infrastructure, whose SFT/RL stacks cannot natively express stateful, multi-process harness inference. To address this, we present OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework for training harness-based agents end-to-end in diverse environments.

infographic.key_insight: OpenForgeRL makes it possible to train agents end-to-end inside the same kind of complex, stateful harnesses used at inference time. This helps close the gap between how modern agents are trained and how they actually operate in real environments.
infographic.problem_solved: Current open-source SFT/RL systems struggle to represent harness-based agent inference because it is stateful, multi-turn, and often multi-process. As a result, agents that work well in sophisticated inference harnesses are difficult to train end-to-end with open infrastructure.
method: Provides an open-source framework for training harness-based agents end-to-end.
Supports diverse environments where agents need multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and external system access.
Bridges inference harness behavior with training workflows so agents can be optimized in the same operational setup they will use at deployment.
infographic.impact: This matters because it gives practitioners a practical path to train more realistic agents without relying on closed or brittle infrastructure. It can improve reproducibility, flexibility, and the alignment between training and deployment for agentic AI systems.

title: UnDA: Unpaired Domain Alignment for Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer in Medical Imaging
authors: Rafsan Jany, Shadab Tanjeed Ahmad, Ahsan Bulbul, Tahsinul Islam, Md Azam Hossain
abstract: Multimodal based approaches often outperform single modality approaches in downstream tasks as the different modalities provide complementary information, yet acquiring paired clinical data remains a significant challenge in real world scenarios. While cross-modal knowledge distillation addresses this, existing methods often struggle with large modality gaps and the propagation of noise from uncertain source-domain predictions. To overcome these challenges, we propose UnDA, an anchor-guided fram

infographic.key_insight: UnDA enables knowledge transfer between medical imaging modalities without requiring paired training data, reducing the gap between source and target domains. It improves cross-modal distillation by using anchors to guide alignment and limit the spread of noisy predictions.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of learning from unpaired multimodal medical data, where paired clinical samples are scarce and modality differences are large. It also tackles the issue of noisy source-model predictions being transferred into the target modality during cross-modal distillation.
method: Uses anchor-guided unpaired domain alignment to bridge large modality gaps.
Transfers knowledge across modalities without relying on paired samples.
Reduces noise propagation by stabilizing alignment with reliable anchor information.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, UnDA offers a practical way to leverage multimodal medical data when pairing is infeasible in real clinical settings. This can improve robustness and performance in cross-modal transfer tasks while making better use of limited data.

title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
authors: Wenhao Li, Xueying Jiang, Quanhao Qian, Deli Zhao, Ran Xu
abstract: Despite rapid progress, most existing vision-language models (VLMs) built from 2D visual inputs often struggle when handling various 3D tasks that require fine-grained spatial understanding and reasoning. To bridge this gap, we present VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that enhances the 3D spatial awareness of VLMs by equipping them with both implicit and explicit 3D geometries learned from RGB videos. Our VLM-IE3D introduces Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) that capture high-level geometric priors f

infographic.key_insight: VLM-IE3D makes standard vision-language models more 3D-aware by adding learned geometric representations from RGB videos. This helps the model reason better about spatial relationships, depth, and object layout in 3D tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Most VLMs are trained on 2D images and struggle with tasks that require precise 3D spatial understanding, such as depth reasoning, viewpoint changes, and geometric inference.
method: Learns Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to encode high-level 3D geometric priors from RGB video.
Uses explicit geometry representations to provide more concrete spatial structure alongside the implicit cues.
Combines both geometry types in a unified VLM framework to improve 3D reasoning without relying on specialized 3D sensors.
infographic.impact: This approach can improve how VLMs handle robotics, AR/VR, autonomous systems, and embodied AI tasks where 3D understanding matters. For practitioners, it offers a path to make existing multimodal models more spatially intelligent using video data.

title: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation
authors: Yijun Liang, Yunjie Tian, Yijiang Li, Yuqi Jia, Furong Huang
abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is promising as it removes the external teacher required by on-policy distillation (OPD), yet it still needs asymmetric information between teacher and student to ensure that the self-teacher provides a stronger learning signal than the student. Existing methods create this asymmetry either through privileged answers or visual evidence. We ask whether both can be removed, yielding a simpler form of OPSD driven purely by input conditioning. For this purpose, we

infographic.key_insight: The paper explores whether on-policy self-distillation can work without privileged answers or extra visual evidence, relying only on input conditioning to create the learning signal. This points to a simpler form of self-distillation that removes the need for asymmetric side information.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of how to make self-distillation effective when the teacher and student do not have access to special extra information. The goal is to eliminate external teachers and other asymmetry sources while still keeping the self-teacher stronger than the student.
method: Start from on-policy self-distillation, where the model teaches itself from its own predictions.
Remove reliance on privileged answers and visual evidence as sources of teacher-student asymmetry.
Use input conditioning alone to create a stronger self-teacher signal for learning.
infographic.impact: This matters because it simplifies self-distillation pipelines and reduces dependence on extra annotations or specialized input setups. For practitioners, that can mean easier-to-deploy training methods with fewer assumptions and lower data engineering overhead.
