title: Simple Domain Generalization for Strong Pixel-Level Image Tampering Detection in Modern VLMs
authors: Yi Tang, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Cui, Sondos Mahmoud Bsharat, Jiacheng Liu
abstract: Modern vision-language models (VLMs) have significantly improved image generation and editing capabilities, making pixel-level image tampering detection increasingly important yet challenging under cross-model and out-of-distribution shifts. This work studies domain generalization for pixel-level image tampering detection in modern VLMs like ChatGPT, Gemini, Qwen-Image, etc., aiming to learn tampering localization models that remain robust across diverse VLM-generated manipulation distributions.

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that simple domain generalization can make pixel-level tampering detectors robust across different modern VLMs, despite major shifts in how edits are generated. In short: train for cross-model diversity, and localization becomes much more reliable on unseen manipulations.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of detecting and localizing image tampering when the manipulated images come from different VLMs and unseen distributions. Existing detectors often fail to generalize across models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Qwen-Image.
method: Study domain generalization specifically for pixel-level tampering localization in modern VLM-generated images.
Learn a detector that captures manipulation patterns shared across different VLMs rather than overfitting to one generation model.
Evaluate robustness under cross-model and out-of-distribution shifts to ensure the detector works on unseen tampering sources.
infographic.impact: This matters for practitioners building forensic tools, content moderation systems, and trust/safety pipelines because VLM-generated edits are rapidly evolving. A detector that generalizes across models is more practical for real-world deployment than one tuned to a single generator.

A growing landscape of pathology foundation models now spans diverse data sources, architectures, and downstream applications. However, most pretrained models operate only at the image-tile level, use restrictive licenses, and remain computationally expensiv

They push beyond tile-only pretrained models toward more efficient slide-level representation learning and downstream use.

It also tackles common limitations of existing models, such as tile-only operation, restrictive licensing, and high inference cost.
method: Develops efficient foundation model variants tailored for pathology workflows at whole-slide scale.
Targets both whole-slide image understanding and tumor microenvironment analysis rather than only local tile features.
Emphasizes computational efficiency to reduce the cost and latency of pathology inference and deployment.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, these models suggest a more deployable pathway for using foundation models in digital pathology. They could enable faster, more scalable cancer analysis while improving access to practical pretrained models for research and clinical applications.

title: A neural network model of free recall learns multiple memory strategies
authors: Moufan Li, Kristopher T. Jensen, Qiong Zhang, Qihong Lu, Marcelo G. Mattar

infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the question of how AI models can explain and reproduce human free recall behavior, especially whether a single temporal-context model is sufficient to capture the diversity of memory strategies people use.

infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that end-to-end training on cognitive tasks can uncover richer internal algorithms than hand-designed assumptions. It also suggests new architectures for memory-intensive systems that use multiple retrieval strategies instead of a single fixed mechanism.

title: Causal Discovery on Irregular Time Series
authors: Martim Penim, Ricardo Ribeiro Pereira, Jacopo Bono, Hugo Ferreira, Mário A. T. Figueiredo
abstract: Causal discovery methods have shown strong performance in temporal systems, but they typically rely on regular and discrete lag structures, limiting their applicability to regularly sampled data. However, many real-world tasks require dealing with irregularly sampled streams of events, such as sensor streams, healthcare data, and financial transactions. In this work, we propose an extension of PCMCI+, a state-of-the-art method for causal discovery on regular multivariate time series, to allow fo

infographic.key_insight: This paper extends causal discovery beyond regularly sampled data, enabling PCMCI+ to work on irregular time series. The result is a more practical way to uncover causal relationships in real-world event streams like sensors, healthcare records, and financial data.
infographic.problem_solved: Most causal discovery methods assume evenly spaced observations and fixed lag structures, which breaks down for irregularly sampled time series. This paper addresses the challenge of learning causal structure when events arrive at uneven times.
method: Builds on PCMCI+, a strong causal discovery method for multivariate time series.
Adapts the method to handle irregular sampling instead of requiring regular time intervals.
Targets event-driven data settings where timestamps are uneven and standard lag-based assumptions do not hold.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes causal discovery usable in many messy real-world datasets that were previously hard to analyze. It can improve interpretation, root-cause analysis, and decision-making in domains with irregular event logs.

title: A Continual Validation, Updating, and Decision-Making Framework for Self-Adaptive Digital Twins via Robust Model Predictive Control: A Case Study in Additive Manufacturing
authors: Yi-Ping Chen, Ying-Kuan Tsai, Vispi Karkaria, Seul Lee, Daniel Apley
abstract: Digital Twins rely on surrogate models to mirror physical systems in real time, yet these models can degrade as operating conditions evolve, a phenomenon known as concept drift. Maintaining surrogate fidelity under drift, particularly when models must also capture aleatoric uncertainty, remains an open challenge. Existing adaptive frameworks lack principled mechanisms for detecting when updates are needed, for efficiently adapting models from limited streaming data, and for certifying that updat

infographic.key_insight: The paper proposes a closed-loop framework that continuously checks whether a digital twin’s surrogate model is still trustworthy, updates it when drift is detected, and uses robust control to make safe decisions under uncertainty. In short, it helps self-adaptive digital twins stay accurate and actionable as real-world conditions change.
infographic.problem_solved: Digital twins often rely on surrogate models that become outdated when operating conditions drift, causing prediction errors and poor decisions. This paper addresses the lack of a principled way to detect drift, update models from limited streaming data, and certify that the updated twin remains reliable for decision-making.
method: Uses continual validation to monitor surrogate-model fidelity and detect when concept drift is occurring.
Updates the model adaptively using limited online data so the digital twin can track changing system behavior.
Integrates robust model predictive control to make decisions while accounting for uncertainty and maintaining safe performance.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical blueprint for building digital twins that do not just predict, but also know when they are no longer reliable. It is especially valuable in safety-critical or high-variability settings where model drift can quickly undermine decisions.

title: TRIM: Reducing AI-Generated CodeSlop via Agent Trajectory Minimization
authors: Alex Mathai, Shobini Iyer, Aleksandr Nogikh, Petros Maniatis, Franjo Ivancic
abstract: Coding agents are increasingly used to accelerate code generation in many downstream tasks, such as fixing bugs, building applications, and prototyping. However, despite their value as coding assistants, agent-generated code tends to be larger and more verbose than the corresponding human-written implementation. In this work, we show that the cause lies in the agent's own search process: while iterating toward a passing solution, an agent accumulates speculative edits, abandoned hypotheses, and

infographic.key_insight: AI coding agents often produce bloated, verbose code not because the final solution needs it, but because the agent’s search process leaves behind speculative edits and abandoned attempts. TRIM shows that reducing the trajectory of the agent’s reasoning/editing path can reduce this "codeSlop."
infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the problem of AI-generated code being unnecessarily long, messy, and overcomplicated compared with human-written implementations, especially after iterative agentic coding.
method: Analyze the agent’s edit/search trajectory to identify where unnecessary code accumulation happens.
Minimize or prune speculative intermediate steps so only the most useful path to a correct solution remains.
Evaluate how trajectory minimization affects code verbosity and output quality in coding-agent workflows.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that better coding-agent outputs may come from improving the search process, not just the final model. It can lead to cleaner, shorter, more maintainable generated code without sacrificing correctness.

title: FVAttn: Adaptive Sparse Attention with Runtime Load Balancing for Video Generation
authors: Hao Liu, Chenghuan Huang, Ye Huang, Zhiying Wen, Hao Liu
abstract: Video Diffusion Transformers process long spatio-temporal sequences, making self-attention the main bottleneck in high-resolution video generation. Training-free sparse attention reduces this cost, but adaptive Top-$p$ routing creates uneven per-head workloads under multi-GPU sequence parallelism. The resulting workload heterogeneity turns sparse attention into a rank-level straggler problem. We present \method{}, a training-free sparse-attention system that improves the distributed execution ef

infographic.key_insight: FVAttn makes sparse attention for video generation faster and more scalable by balancing work across GPUs at runtime. It turns uneven adaptive Top-p routing from a bottleneck into a distributed efficiency gain.
infographic.problem_solved: Video Diffusion Transformers rely on self-attention over long spatio-temporal sequences, which is expensive for high-resolution video generation. Existing training-free sparse attention methods reduce compute, but adaptive Top-p routing creates uneven per-head workloads across GPUs, causing rank-level stragglers during sequence parallelism.
method: Introduces a training-free sparse-attention system for video generation.
Uses runtime load balancing to smooth out workload heterogeneity across attention heads and GPUs.
Improves distributed execution efficiency under multi-GPU sequence parallelism without requiring model retraining.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means faster and more reliable high-resolution video generation with lower distributed overhead. It is especially useful for scaling diffusion transformers where attention cost and GPU imbalance limit throughput.

title: An Exam for Active Observers
authors: Jiarui Zhang, Muzi Tao, Shangshang Wang, Ollie Liu, Xuezhe Ma
abstract: Human vision is a closed loop: gaze is continuously redirected by intermediate hypotheses rather than a single snapshot. Decades of psychophysics and cognitive science have argued that this active observation is essential for a wide range of tasks. Whether today's multimodal large language models (MLLMs) exercise active observation is an empirical question that current vision-language benchmarks do not answer. We introduce ActiveVision, a benchmark that makes active observation measurable for ML

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that true visual understanding is not a one-shot snapshot process, but a loop of observing, hypothesizing, and re-checking. It introduces ActiveVision to measure whether multimodal LLMs actually perform this kind of active observation.
infographic.problem_solved: Current vision-language benchmarks mainly test final answers, not whether models actively direct attention or gaze based on intermediate hypotheses. This paper addresses the lack of an empirical way to evaluate active observation in multimodal large language models.
method: Introduces ActiveVision, a benchmark designed to make active observation measurable for MLLMs.
Frames evaluation around whether models revise or redirect their visual focus in response to intermediate reasoning.
Compares model behavior against the idea of human-like closed-loop vision rather than static image understanding.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a new way to test whether multimodal systems truly inspect images intelligently instead of relying on superficial pattern matching. It can guide the design of models that reason more like humans in visually complex tasks.

title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
authors: Tam Bang, Hussam Abubakr, Emiliano de la Garza Villarreal, Truc Phuong Nguyen, Austin Harris
abstract: Urban intersections are among the most hazardous locations in road networks, posing significant risks to vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs) such as pedestrians and cyclists. The complexity of multi-agent interactions demands continuous, real-time monitoring systems capable of anticipating conflicts before they escalate into crashes. We present PRISA, a modular infrastructure LiDAR framework leveraging privacy-preserving, low-light-robust roadside sensors for long-term traffic observation

infographic.key_insight: PRISA introduces a proactive roadside LiDAR framework that continuously monitors intersections to identify safety risks before they turn into crashes. It is designed to work in real-world conditions, including low light, while preserving privacy.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of safely monitoring complex urban intersections, where vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists interact in ways that can quickly lead to conflicts and crashes. Existing approaches often lack real-time, long-term, and privacy-preserving roadside sensing.
method: Uses modular infrastructure LiDAR sensors deployed at intersections for continuous observation of traffic scenes.
Focuses on proactive safety assessment by tracking multi-agent interactions and anticipating conflicts before escalation.
Designed for privacy-preserving and low-light-robust sensing to support long-term real-world deployment.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, PRISA shows how infrastructure sensing can move beyond detection toward predictive safety analytics in dynamic urban environments. It also highlights a practical deployment path for robust, privacy-aware perception systems.

title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
authors: Binglin Zhou, Peng Shi, Ryo Kamoi, Nan Zhang, Rui Zhang
abstract: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV) requires models to verify scientific claims using visually grounded evidence from papers, including figures, tables, charts, and textual context. However, existing methods often fail because they struggle to locate decisive visual evidence, accurately read structured scientific visuals, and integrate multimodal observations into reliable reasoning. We introduce ToolSciVer, the first tool-augmented framework for MSCV to our knowledge. ToolSciVer equ

infographic.key_insight: ToolSciVer introduces a tool-augmented reinforcement learning framework for multimodal scientific claim verification, helping models find and use the right visual evidence from papers more reliably. It aims to improve reasoning over figures, tables, charts, and surrounding text instead of relying on text alone.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of verifying scientific claims when crucial evidence is spread across visuals and text. Existing methods often miss decisive figures, misread structured scientific visuals, and struggle to combine multimodal observations into trustworthy conclusions.
method: Uses external tools to locate and inspect evidence in scientific documents, especially figures, tables, and charts.
Trains the system with visual tool augmented reinforcement learning so it learns when and how to use tools for better verification.
Integrates visual findings with textual context to produce more reliable claim verification decisions.
infographic.impact: This matters because many scientific claims cannot be checked accurately from text alone. For AI/ML practitioners, ToolSciVer points toward more dependable multimodal systems for research review, fact-checking, and evidence-based scientific analysis.

title: Toward Semantic Communication for Real-time Mobile 3D Reconstruction
authors: Fangzhou Zhao, Yao Sun, Xuesong Liu, Runze Cheng, Shang Kai
abstract: Real-time mobile 3D reconstruction is fundamental to many emerging applications such as autonomous navigation and digital twin construction, where a moving platform continuously captures an image stream and transmit to a computing server for scene understanding. Unlike offline reconstruction, camera poses and scene geometry are estimated on-the-fly during acquisition, making multi-view consistency a real-time requirement and rendering geometric estimation highly sensitive to communication-induce

infographic.key_insight: This paper frames real-time mobile 3D reconstruction as a semantic communication problem, where what matters is not just sending images efficiently, but preserving the scene information needed for accurate reconstruction. The key idea is to make transmission aware of multi-view consistency so pose and geometry estimation remain stable under communication constraints.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing 3D scenes in real time from a moving camera while transmitting image streams to a server, where bandwidth limits and communication noise can degrade camera pose estimation and scene geometry recovery.
method: Treats the reconstruction pipeline as a semantic communication task, prioritizing information most useful for downstream 3D scene understanding.
Accounts for on-the-fly camera pose and geometry estimation, where multi-view consistency must be maintained during live capture.
Designs the communication/reconstruction process to reduce sensitivity to communication-induced errors in the transmitted image stream.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more task-aware way to design edge-to-cloud vision systems: optimize what is transmitted based on the reconstruction objective, not just image fidelity. This is especially relevant for robotics, autonomous navigation, and digital twin applications where reliability and latency are critical.

title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
authors: Wendi Yu, Lianhao Zhou, Xiangjue Dong, Sai Sudarshan Barath, Declan Staunton
abstract: LLM powered multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a promising paradigm for complex tasks. However, their advantages over single-agent systems (SAS) remain unclear, with performance varying inconsistently across settings. Here, we provide an information bottleneck perspective on elucidating the differences between MAS and SAS. Specifically, our key observation is that a SAS accumulates its full reasoning trace in one shared context, while a MAS uses isolated local contexts connected by bounde

infographic.key_insight: Multi-agent systems are not universally better than single-agent systems. The paper argues that their advantage depends on how information is distributed and bottlenecked across isolated local contexts versus one shared reasoning trace.
infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the unclear and inconsistent performance gap between multi-agent systems and single-agent systems on complex tasks, asking when splitting reasoning across multiple agents actually helps.
method: Apply an information bottleneck perspective to compare how single-agent systems and multi-agent systems store, transform, and pass reasoning information.
Characterize a single-agent system as accumulating the full reasoning trace in one shared context, while a multi-agent system relies on separate local contexts connected by limited communication.
Use this framework to explain when distributed reasoning improves performance and when communication constraints can hinder it.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this gives a principled way to decide whether to use a multi-agent setup instead of a single model. It can guide system design by matching task structure to the right reasoning architecture.

title: Knowing the Self, Understanding the World: A Dual-Cognition Benchmark for UAV Spatio-temporal Reasoning with MLLMs
authors: Like Liu, Zhengzheng Xu, Haitao He, Hongzhe Li, Shuchang Zhang
abstract: Multimodal large language models have achieved strong performance across diverse vision-language tasks, yet their capabilities in UAV scenarios remain insufficiently explored. Recent UAV-oriented benchmarks have begun to evaluate MLLMs in aerial scenarios, but they typically focus on scene understanding, event recognition, or navigation completion, rather than jointly assessing the dual-cognition capability required for UAV agents: reasoning about both the UAV's own state and the external enviro

It introduces a benchmark to evaluate this combined spatio-temporal reasoning ability instead of testing only scene understanding or navigation.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing UAV benchmarks mostly assess isolated skills like scene recognition, event detection, or navigation completion. They do not measure whether MLLMs can jointly understand self-state and environment state, which is essential for real UAV agents.
method: Defines a dual-cognition benchmark for UAV spatio-temporal reasoning.
Evaluates MLLMs on both self-related awareness (e.g., UAV position, motion, status) and environment-related understanding (e.g., objects, events, temporal changes).
Targets realistic UAV reasoning demands rather than single-task aerial perception.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more realistic way to measure whether MLLMs are ready for UAV applications. It can help identify capability gaps and guide the design of models that better support autonomous aerial decision-making.

abstract: To address the escalating energy and latency demands of machine-learning workloads, we introduce a blueprint for an energy-efficient and fast thermodynamic computing stack that leverages stochastic analog processes in physical hardware. In this work, we focus on energy-based thermodynamic computing where the stochastic process is well described by Langevin dynamics with tunable energy potentials. infographic.key_insight: The paper outlines a hardware blueprint for thermodynamic computing that uses stochastic physical processes and tunable energy landscapes to efficiently generate and sample data. In simple terms, it aims to turn noise into a computing advantage for faster, lower-energy AI inference and sampling.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the growing energy consumption and latency of machine-learning workloads by proposing a physical computing stack that can sample complex distributions more efficiently than conventional digital approaches.

title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
authors: Kai Ruan, Jinghao Lin, Zihe Huang, Ziqi Zhou, Qianshan Wei
abstract: Muon is competitive with AdamW in large-scale pre-training, but its value for reinforcement-learning (RL) post-training remains unclear. We study vanilla Muon in sparse-reward agentic RL through matched single-seed comparisons with AdamW on ALFWorld using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. Under Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO), applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices raises final-window validation success from 0.290 to 0.546 (+88%); high-rate AdamW controls retain no post-update success. The

infographic.key_insight: Muon can substantially improve agentic reinforcement learning when used selectively: in sparse-reward RL on ALFWorld, applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices nearly doubled final validation success versus AdamW. The paper shows Muon’s benefit is context-dependent rather than universally better across all RL settings.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses whether Muon, which is strong in large-scale pre-training, also helps during RL post-training for agentic tasks with sparse rewards. It specifically tests if Muon can overcome the instability and weak learning progress often seen in such RL setups.
method: Matched single-seed comparisons of Muon vs. AdamW on ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
Use of Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) as the RL training framework.
Applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices while keeping other settings controlled, then comparing validation success and post-update behavior.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, this suggests optimizer choice can materially affect RL fine-tuning performance, especially in sparse-reward agentic environments. It also highlights that partial optimizer substitution may deliver gains without changing the entire training stack.

title: CLIFE: Camera-LiDAR Fusion Framework for Edge-Deployable Roadside VRU Perception
authors: Tam Bang, Hoang H. Nguyen, Lei Cheng, Lihao Guo, Siyang Cao
abstract: Reliable roadside perception of vulnerable road users (VRUs) remains challenging under occlusions, variable lighting, and diverse weather conditions, particularly under strict edge-computing and latency constraints. Existing multi-sensor fusion systems rely on cloud or server-grade infrastructure, creating a deployment gap at real-world intersections. We present CLIFE, an edge-native camera-LiDAR fusion framework that integrates targetless online calibration and lightweight late-fusion tracking

infographic.key_insight: CLIFE makes roadside VRU perception practical on edge devices by combining camera and LiDAR with online calibration and lightweight fusion. The key breakthrough is delivering robust multi-sensor detection and tracking without relying on cloud or server-grade hardware.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of reliably detecting vulnerable road users at intersections under occlusion, changing lighting, and adverse weather, while also meeting strict latency and compute limits for edge deployment.
method: Uses an edge-native camera-LiDAR fusion pipeline designed for real-world roadside intersections.
Performs targetless online calibration to align sensors without needing special calibration objects or manual setup.
Applies lightweight late-fusion tracking to maintain robustness while keeping inference efficient for edge computing.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CLIFE shows how to move multimodal perception from lab settings to deployable roadside systems. It highlights a practical path to robust sensing under real-world constraints without sacrificing latency or scalability.

title: Searching Videos as Trees: Self-Correcting Agents for Grounded Long Video QA
authors: Ce Zhang, Ziyang Wang, Yulu Pan, Oluwatumininu Oguntola, Pranav Wagh
abstract: Grounded long-video question answering (Grounded LVQA) requires answering a question about a long video while localizing the short evidence interval that supports the answer. Recent agentic methods frame this task as multi-turn exploration with a single crop_video(start, end) action, which supports coarse-to-fine narrowing but provides no primitive for fine-to-coarse backtracking. As a result, these agents typically converge prematurely and cannot recover from an early mistake. We propose VideoT

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that long-video QA agents need a way to recover from early search mistakes, not just zoom in on a single interval. By organizing video search like a tree with self-correction, the agent can backtrack and refine evidence localization more reliably.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses grounded long-video question answering, where models must both answer a question and identify the short video segment that supports the answer. The key challenge is that existing agents using only coarse-to-fine cropping often get stuck after an early wrong choice and cannot recover.
method: Reframes video exploration as a tree search problem instead of a one-way narrowing process.
Introduces self-correcting agent behavior so the model can backtrack from poor evidence selections.
Uses grounded long-video QA actions to localize supporting intervals while improving robustness to early errors.
infographic.impact: This makes long-video QA agents more reliable in realistic settings where the first guess is often wrong. For practitioners, it suggests better debugging, higher answer grounding quality, and more trustworthy evidence localization in video understanding systems.

title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
authors: Yuyao Zhang, Junjie Gao, Zhengxian Wu, Jiaming Fan, Jin Zhang
abstract: Recent advances in Tool-Integrated Large Language Models have made web search a core capability of information-seeking agents. However, as interaction histories grow, agents increasingly struggle to track task progress. When search attempts fail to yield useful evidence, current single- and multi-agent systems can become trapped in repetitive loops, wasting search budgets and ultimately compromising the quality and completeness of the final output. We introduce SearchOS, a system-level multi-age

infographic.key_insight: SearchOS-V1 aims to make open-domain search agents more reliable by helping them track progress and avoid getting stuck in repetitive search loops. The key idea is system-level collaboration that improves evidence gathering when web searches fail.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses a common failure mode in information-seeking agents: as search histories grow, agents lose track of task progress, repeat unhelpful searches, waste budget, and produce incomplete or low-quality answers.
method: Introduces a multi-agent system designed to coordinate search behavior in open-domain information-seeking tasks.
Focuses on maintaining task progress awareness so agents can better decide when to continue, switch strategies, or stop searching.
Aims to reduce repetitive loops after unsuccessful search attempts and improve evidence collection efficiency.
infographic.impact: This matters for practitioners building search-enabled LLM systems because it can improve answer quality, reduce wasted tool calls, and make agent workflows more robust in long-horizon tasks. It is especially useful for applications where completeness and budget efficiency are critical.

title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
authors: Sushant Gautam, Vajira Thambawita, Michael A. Riegler, Pål Halvorsen, Steven A. Hicks
abstract: Healthcare multimodal AI must combine visual and textual evidence while remaining reliable and interpretable. Using MediaEval Medico 2025 as a retrospective GI endoscopy case study, we analyze design choices across nine documented systems for question answering and explanation quality. Parameter-efficient adaptation of pretrained backbones provides strong challenge performance, but answer-level gains do not consistently translate into faithful and complete clinical reasoning. Methods enforcing s

infographic.key_insight: Strong leaderboard performance in multimodal VQA does not automatically mean the model is truly trustworthy or clinically grounded. In this GI endoscopy case study, methods that improve answer accuracy can still fail to produce faithful, complete explanations.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between high-performing multimodal question answering systems and their reliability, interpretability, and explanation quality in healthcare settings.
method: Retrospective analysis of nine documented systems from the MediaEval Medico 2025 GI endoscopy challenge.
Comparison of design choices for multimodal question answering and explanation generation across different model pipelines.
Evaluation of how parameter-efficient adaptation and other training choices affect answer quality versus faithfulness and completeness of clinical reasoning.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper shows that optimizing for benchmarks alone is not enough in healthcare multimodal AI. It highlights the need to evaluate not just whether a model is correct, but whether its reasoning is trustworthy, interpretable, and clinically useful.

title: Hierarchical Denoising For Multi-Step Visual Reasoning
authors: Zezhong Qian, Xiaowei Chi, Chak-Wing Mak, Tianze Zhou, Ruibin Yuan
abstract: Video models are evolving into vision foundation models, yet they still lack human-like multi-step reasoning. Streaming autoregressive diffusion models are efficient but limited in reasoning, while bidirectional diffusion enables global revision with high inference costs due to dense frame-level denoising. Both paradigms struggle to achieve logical consistency and low-latency streaming for complex reasoning tasks. We propose HDR (Hierarchical Denoising for Visual Reasoning), a unified framework

infographic.key_insight: HDR (Hierarchical Denoising for Visual Reasoning) aims to combine the efficiency of streaming autoregressive diffusion with the global consistency of bidirectional diffusion, so video models can reason through multi-step visual problems more like humans. The core idea is to denoise at multiple hierarchical levels instead of densely revising every frame, reducing latency while improving logical coherence.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between fast but limited streaming video generation/reasoning and globally consistent but expensive bidirectional diffusion. Existing methods struggle to maintain multi-step logical consistency in complex visual reasoning tasks without high inference cost.
method: Introduces a unified hierarchical denoising framework (HDR) for visual reasoning.
Performs denoising at multiple abstraction levels rather than dense frame-level revision, improving efficiency.
Aims to preserve streaming-friendly low latency while enabling global corrections for better reasoning consistency.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a path toward video foundation models that can reason over complex visual sequences without the usual tradeoff between speed and consistency. It is especially relevant for real-time applications where both latency and multi-step understanding matter.

title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
authors: Yushi Huang, Xiangxin Zhou, Jun Zhang, Liefeng Bo, Tianyu Pang
abstract: MeanFlow generators achieve fast few-step sampling by predicting average velocities over time intervals, making them attractive for efficient generation. Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a powerful way to align diffusion and flow models with human preferences and task-specific objectives. In particular, DiffusionNFT offers an efficient forward-process RL framework that does not require reverse-process trajectories or likelihood estimation. However, applying such RL methods to MeanFlow rema

infographic.key_insight: MeanFlowNFT extends forward-process reinforcement learning to MeanFlow generators, enabling preference alignment without needing reverse trajectories or likelihood estimates. The result is a practical way to improve fast few-step generation while keeping the training pipeline efficient.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses how to apply RL-based alignment methods, originally designed for diffusion/flow models, to MeanFlow models that predict average velocity over time intervals. It targets the gap between fast sampling efficiency and reward-driven optimization.
method: Builds on DiffusionNFT’s forward-process RL framework, avoiding reverse-process rollout requirements.
Adapts the RL objective to MeanFlow’s average-velocity formulation so the model can be optimized directly in its native generation space.
Uses preference or task rewards to steer generation while preserving MeanFlow’s few-step sampling speed.
infographic.impact: This matters because it makes alignment techniques more broadly applicable to efficient generative models, not just standard diffusion systems. Practitioners gain a route to improve quality, controllability, and preference alignment without paying the cost of reverse-process training.

title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
authors: Yasheng Sun, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Wenyi Wang
abstract: Editing the figures in a research paper is a routine and time-consuming part of everyday research practice: authors relabel components, rearrange panels, and restyle visuals as they revise their manuscripts. Automating this editing workflow under a natural-language instruction, however, is challenging, because a scientific figure is a dense infographic in which heterogeneous visual elements such as schematics, plots, photos, captions, and arrows are composed under a tight visual grammar to advan

It treats scientific diagrams as complex, structured infographics and learns to apply realistic edits such as relabeling, rearranging, and restyling.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of automating figure editing in research papers, where dense scientific diagrams contain many heterogeneous elements arranged under strict visual conventions. Existing tools struggle to understand and modify these figures from text instructions alone.
method: Builds a learning framework from paper revisions to model how scientific figures are edited over time.
Interprets natural-language edit requests and applies them to multi-element scientific diagrams with tight visual structure.

infographic.impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it could reduce the manual effort required to update figures during paper writing and revision. It also points toward more reliable multimodal systems for structured graphic editing in scientific workflows.

title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
authors: Yunfan Jiang, Yevgen Chebotar, Ruijie Zheng, Fengyuan Hu, Yunhao Ge
abstract: Recent robot foundation models operate with single-step or short-history visuomotor context. We introduce Test-Time-Training Robot Policies (RoboTTT), a robot model and training recipe that scale visuomotor context to 8K timesteps, three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies, without growing inference latency. At this context length, we unlock new robot capabilities: one-shot in-context imitation from human video demonstrations, on-the-fly policy improvement, robustness to perturb

infographic.key_insight: RoboTTT shows that robot policies can use extremely long visuomotor context—up to 8K timesteps—without increasing inference latency. This unlocks new abilities like one-shot imitation from human video, online policy improvement, and greater robustness.
infographic.problem_solved: Most robot foundation models rely on short history or single-step context, limiting their ability to learn from long demonstrations, adapt during deployment, and use richer temporal information.
method: Introduces Test-Time-Training Robot Policies (RoboTTT), a robot model and training recipe designed to scale context length dramatically.
Uses long-horizon visuomotor context during training and inference while keeping runtime cost effectively unchanged.
Enables test-time adaptation so the policy can improve from context and demonstrations in real time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this expands what robot policies can do with the same inference budget, making long-context adaptation practical for real-world robotics. It also suggests a new path toward more flexible, data-efficient, and robust embodied AI systems.

title: ARMOR++: Agentic Orchestration of a Multi-Domain Primitive Set for Transferable Attacks on Deepfake Detectors
authors: Christos Korgialas, Gabriel Lee Jun Rong, Dion Jia Xu Ho, Pai Chet Ng, Xiaoxiao Miao
abstract: The reliability of deepfake detectors frequently degrades under black-box adversarial transfer, as these models often rely on fragile, architecture-dependent forensic cues. Existing transfer attacks often lack semantic awareness and struggle to maintain effectiveness under strict no-query constraints, particularly when perturbations are transferred from convolutional surrogates to transformer-based targets. To address these limitations, this paper introduces ARMOR++, a robust multi-agent framewo

infographic.key_insight: ARMOR++ uses an agentic, multi-domain primitive set to craft transferable adversarial attacks that remain effective against deepfake detectors even in strict black-box, no-query settings. The core idea is to combine semantic awareness with coordinated attack generation so perturbations transfer better from surrogate models to modern transformer-based targets.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the drop in deepfake detector reliability under black-box adversarial transfer, especially when attacks must work without queries and across different model families. Existing transfer attacks often depend on architecture-specific cues and fail to generalize well from CNN surrogates to transformer-based detectors.
method: Introduces ARMOR++, a multi-agent framework that orchestrates multiple attack primitives across different domains.
Uses semantic-aware attack generation to better preserve transferability under no-query constraints.
Coordinates surrogate-crafted perturbations to improve effectiveness on target deepfake detectors, including transformer-based models.
infographic.impact: This matters because it highlights a stronger threat model for deepfake detection systems and shows that current defenses may be more fragile than expected. For practitioners, it emphasizes the need to evaluate detectors against transferable, black-box attacks rather than only white-box or query-based settings.

title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
authors: Mingfei Chen, Zijun Cui, Ruoke Zhang, Hyeonggon Ryu, Eli Shlizerman
abstract: We present SceneBind, an omni-modal representation of realistic scenes with joint semantic and 3D spatial understanding across vision, audio and language. Existing omni-modal encoders excel at instance-level semantics (i.e., what is present), but often lack explicit spatial structure (i.e., where it is). SceneBind addresses this gap by representing each scene as a semantic-spatial entity, combining a global semantic embedding with object-centric semantic-spatial slots. This representation explic

infographic.key_insight: SceneBind unifies "what" and "where" by learning scene representations that combine semantic meaning with 3D spatial structure across vision, audio, and language. This lets models reason about realistic scenes more like humans do: identifying objects and understanding their locations at the same time.
infographic.problem_solved: Current omni-modal encoders are strong at recognizing instance-level semantics, but they often miss explicit spatial relationships and 3D layout. SceneBind addresses the lack of a representation that jointly captures semantic content and spatial organization in real scenes.
method: Represents each scene as a semantic-spatial entity rather than only a global semantic embedding.
Combines a global scene-level semantic representation with object-centric semantic-spatial slots.
Aligns information across vision, audio, and language to support joint understanding of content and spatial context.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SceneBind offers a more structured representation for multimodal scene understanding, which can improve tasks that depend on both recognition and localization. It is especially useful for applications where models must connect descriptions, sounds, and visible objects in real-world environments.

title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
authors: Moein Taherinezhad, Sebastian Maier, Gerardo Vitagliano, Francesco Pierri, Stefan Feuerriegel
abstract: Evidence synthesis is crucial for turning primary research into reliable knowledge for science, medicine, education, and policy. infographic.key_insight: AutoSynthesis is an end-to-end multi-agent system that automates the most time-consuming parts of meta-analysis from a natural-language research question. It aims to turn evidence synthesis into a scalable, repeatable workflow rather than a largely manual process.

title: HoloGeo: Mitigating Landmark Bias in Geo-localization via Evidence-Driven Reasoning
authors: Pengcheng Zhou, Xuanyu Liu, Yanchen Yin, Bobo Li, Shengqiong Wu
abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have significantly improved image geo-localization, yet existing models remain susceptible to landmark bias, causing them to overlook geographical cues or form spurious correlations, ultimately resulting in inaccurate localization. To systematically investigate this issue, we first design two quantitative metrics, Bias Intensity (BI) and Bias Harmfulness (BH), to characterize the impact of landmarks exerted on model reasoning, and establish a comp

infographic.key_insight: HoloGeo shows that vision-language models can be misled by landmark cues when doing geo-localization, and introduces evidence-driven reasoning to reduce this bias. The paper quantifies how strong the bias is and how harmful it becomes, then uses that analysis to improve localization reliability.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses landmark bias in image geo-localization, where models over-rely on recognizable landmarks, ignore broader geographic evidence, and make spurious predictions.

title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
authors: Baback Elmieh, Lynn Tsai, Zeman Li, Srinivas Kaza, Tiancheng Sun
abstract: Online novel view synthesis from multi-view streaming videos faces a fundamental trade-off: maintaining a persistent, long-horizon memory to reconstruct temporarily occluded regions while operating under strict real-time constraints. While Test-Time Training (TTT) offers a powerful memory mechanism, standard models mandate gradient-based memory updates at every frame to adapt to the changing motion in dynamic scenes. The computational cost of heavy memory updates precludes real-time application

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces an online memory mechanism for dynamic novel view synthesis that keeps useful long-term scene information without requiring expensive gradient updates at every frame. In simple terms, it aims to make real-time rendering of changing scenes both faster and more memory-aware.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing dynamic scenes from streaming multi-view video under real-time constraints, where models must remember occluded content over long periods while adapting to motion changes efficiently.
method: Uses an online neural space-time memory to store and retrieve scene information across frames.
Reduces reliance on heavy test-time gradient-based updates, which are too slow for real-time use.
Balances short-term motion adaptation with long-horizon memory to improve dynamic novel view synthesis.
infographic.impact: This matters because it could make real-time 3D scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis more practical for robotics, AR/VR, telepresence, and streaming vision systems. For practitioners, it points to a more efficient alternative to costly test-time adaptation in dynamic environments.

title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
authors: Victoria Graf, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Noah A. Smith, David Kohlbrenner, Kyle Lo
abstract: Poisoning pretraining data can introduce harmful behaviors to LMs that are difficult to detect and mitigate. Prior work on poisoning pretraining data has largely exploited established data sources such as Wikipedia, which do not represent the large scale and heterogeneity typical of pretraining corpora, and has ignored the interaction between poisoned data and data curation pipelines. We demonstrate that poisoning attacks on pretraining data are feasible beyond this limited setting through an ex

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that poisoning pretraining data is feasible even in realistic, large-scale settings, not just in controlled sources like Wikipedia. It also highlights that data curation pipelines can fail to filter out harmful poisoned content, making attacks harder to detect and defend against.
infographic.problem_solved: This work addresses the challenge of whether pretraining data poisoning can still succeed in heterogeneous, web-scale corpora and under modern data curation pipelines, where prior attacks were tested only in limited settings.
method: Studies poisoning attacks on pretraining data in a more realistic corpus setting with large-scale and heterogeneous data.
Examines how poisoned examples interact with data filtering and curation pipelines.
Demonstrates that harmful behaviors can be introduced into language models through poisoned pretraining data beyond previously assumed constraints.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this raises the bar for dataset security and provenance tracking in pretraining pipelines. It suggests that defenses must account for both the scale of the web and the weaknesses of curation filters, not just obvious bad sources.

title: Motion-Conditioned Multi-View Fusion for Myocardial Infarction Localization from Echocardiography
authors: Guang Yang, Wentian Xu, Siyu Wang, Betty Raman, Lei Li
abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Echocardiography (Echo) is a widely available modality for MI assessment, where regional wall motion abnormality is a key indicator. Prior learning based methods for myocardial motion analysis often use handcrafted descriptors or densely supervised estimation, but the need for extensive annotation limits applicability. Foundation models have recently improved vision-based Echo analysis; however, most methods operate on si

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces a motion-conditioned, multi-view fusion approach to localize myocardial infarction from echocardiography using the heart’s motion patterns rather than requiring dense manual annotations. It aims to make MI detection more practical and robust by leveraging complementary echo views and learned motion cues.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of localizing myocardial infarction from echocardiography when prior methods depend on handcrafted motion descriptors or dense supervision that is costly and hard to scale.
method: Extracts motion information from echocardiography to identify regional wall motion abnormalities associated with MI.
Fuses information across multiple echo views to improve localization and reduce ambiguity from single-view analysis.
Uses a motion-conditioned learning strategy to reduce reliance on extensive annotation and improve generalization.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how foundation-model-style vision methods can be adapted to clinically meaningful tasks with weaker supervision. It also provides a template for combining temporal motion signals and multi-view fusion in medical imaging.

title: Lighthouse RL: Sample-Efficient Circuit Optimization via Strategic Reset Points
authors: Mustafa Emre Gürsoy, Stefan Uhlich, Ryoga Matsuo, Yağız Gençer, Arun Venkitaraman
abstract: In this paper, we introduce Lighthouse RL, a sample-efficient reinforcement learning (RL) approach for analog circuit sizing. Traditional methods lack generalization across different performance targets, while standard RL approaches waste resources exploring unpromising regions. Our method addresses these inefficiencies through a strategic reset strategy that initializes episodes from high-performing configurations discovered during training, called "lighthouses". These states, which are closer

infographic.key_insight: Lighthouse RL improves sample efficiency in analog circuit sizing by restarting training from strong intermediate solutions instead of repeatedly exploring from scratch. This helps RL focus on promising regions of the design space and adapt better to different performance targets.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses two core issues in analog circuit optimization: poor generalization across changing performance targets and wasted samples spent exploring low-value or unpromising regions during RL training.
method: Use reinforcement learning for analog circuit sizing, but periodically reset episodes from high-performing configurations discovered during training.
Treat these strong configurations as "lighthouses" that guide exploration toward more promising areas of the design space.
Improve sample efficiency by reducing time spent on ineffective exploration and reusing good partial solutions.
Enable better adaptation to varied performance targets compared with conventional optimization strategies.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how carefully designed reset strategies can make RL far more efficient in expensive real-world optimization tasks. It is especially relevant for domains like hardware design where each trial is costly and sample budgets are limited.

title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes
authors: Jeremy Guntoro, Alexander Dack, Dylan Danno, Michaela Jančovičová, Križan Jurinović
abstract: Genomic foundation models such as Evo 2 learn rich sequence representations, but their value for biosecurity screening is largely unexplored. We ask how much biosecurity-relevant signal is linearly accessible in these representations by training minimal linear and attention probes on frozen Evo 2 layer-26 activations, without fine-tuning the underlying model. Across held-out metagenomic test sets, the probes detect antimicrobial resistance (AMR) with strong discrimination: a linear probe reaches

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that Evo 2’s frozen internal representations already contain biosecurity-relevant signals that can be extracted with very simple probes. In particular, minimal linear and attention-based probes can detect antimicrobial resistance in metagenomic data without fine-tuning the base model.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of screening metagenomic sequences for biosecurity risks using foundation models, specifically asking whether dangerous biological features are linearly accessible in pretrained genomic embeddings.
method: Freeze Evo 2 and extract layer-26 activations from genomic sequences.
Train lightweight linear and attention probes on top of these fixed representations.
Evaluate probe performance on held-out metagenomic test sets for detecting antimicrobial resistance and related biosecurity signals.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that pretrained sequence models may be useful for security screening with minimal additional modeling cost. It also highlights a practical path for auditing model representations for biosecurity applications without modifying the foundation model itself.

title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders
authors: Zhihao Xie, Junfeng Wu, Xinting Hu, Junchao Huang, Li Jiang
abstract: Video generative models commonly rely on latent spaces learned by 3D Variational Autoencoders (3D-VAEs). However, conventional 3D-VAEs are mainly optimized for pixel-level reconstruction, which can limit the semantic and spatio-temporal structure captured by their latents. Meanwhile, Video Foundation Models (VFMs) such as V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAEv2 show strong video understanding capabilities, yet whether their frozen representations can be transformed into compact, reconstruction-capable, and gene

infographic.key_insight: VideoRAE shows that frozen Video Foundation Model representations can be turned into compact latent spaces that support both reconstruction and generation, reducing reliance on conventional 3D-VAEs. The result is a more semantic, spatio-temporal representation for video generation.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the limitation of standard 3D-VAEs, whose pixel-focused training often produces latents that miss higher-level video semantics and temporal structure. It also tackles the challenge of making strong video understanding models usable as generative latent backbones.
method: Use frozen representations from Video Foundation Models as the basis for a Representation Autoencoder (RAE).
Learn a compact latent space that preserves semantic and spatio-temporal information while remaining reconstruction-capable.
Adapt the latent representation for video generation, aiming to improve generative quality over conventional VAE-based pipelines.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new route to better video generation by leveraging pretrained video understanding models instead of training purely reconstruction-driven VAEs. It can improve latent quality, reduce representation mismatch, and potentially boost downstream generative fidelity and coherence.

title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
authors: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng
abstract: Multi-turn agents solve complex tasks through extended sequences of tool interactions before producing a final answer, making credit assignment a fundamental challenge during post-training. Outcome rewards provide reliable supervision for short-horizon reasoning, but become sparse and high-variance as trajectories grow to tens or hundreds of tool calls. They can also be misleading: a failed rollout may contain many useful actions that move the agent closer to the goal, yet outcome-only training

infographic.key_insight: TRACE improves training for long-horizon agents by assigning reward at the turn level instead of relying only on the final outcome. This gives credit to useful intermediate actions even when the overall rollout fails.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the credit assignment problem in multi-turn tool-using agents, where long trajectories make outcome-only rewards sparse, noisy, and misleading.
method: Estimate credit at each turn rather than only at the end of the trajectory.
Use reward assignment to identify which intermediate actions contributed to progress toward the goal.
Train agents with denser supervision so useful steps are reinforced even in failed rollouts.
infographic.impact: This can make post-training more stable and effective for agents that perform many tool calls or reasoning steps. For practitioners, it offers a way to learn from partially successful trajectories instead of wasting informative intermediate behavior.

title: Earthquaker-AI: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework with Rubric-Based Assessment for Primary School Earthquake Education
authors: Xanthi Kokkinou, Chaido Mizeli, Nafsika Koulaxidou, Marina Delianidi, Konstantinos Diamantaras
abstract: This paper presents Earthquaker-AI, a hybrid educational framework building upon a previously implemented educational robotics project by integrating a conversational AI assistant based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It aims to enhance earthquake preparedness and conscious action among primary-school students. The system extends the award-winning STEM project Earthquaker moving from mechanical simulation with Lego WeDo2 to cognitive and metacognitive processing. The robotics component uses L

infographic.key_insight: Earthquaker-AI combines a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant with hands-on robotics to teach earthquake preparedness to primary school students. It shifts learning from only physical simulation to deeper cognitive and metacognitive understanding of safe actions during earthquakes.
infographic.problem_solved: Primary school earthquake education often lacks interactive, personalized support that helps students understand not just what to do, but why and when to act. This paper addresses the need for a more engaging, scalable, and conceptually rich learning framework.

Uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation to provide grounded, education-focused responses from relevant sources.
Includes rubric-based assessment to evaluate student understanding and preparedness.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper shows how RAG can be used beyond general chatbots to support safety education in a trustworthy, curriculum-aligned way. It is a useful example of combining generative AI with robotics and assessment to create measurable learning experiences.

title: From Pixels to States: Rethinking Interactive World Models as Game Engines
authors: Zhen Li, Zian Meng, Shuwei Shi, Mingliang Zhai, Jiaming Tan
abstract: Building interactive worlds that respond coherently to player actions has long been a shared goal of computer graphics, games, and artificial intelligence. Recent video generative models provide a data-driven route toward this goal by predicting future observations conditioned on user actions, and are increasingly regarded as potential next-generation game engines. Realizing a genuinely interactive game world, however, requires interaction outcomes that follow rules over evolving game conditions

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that future interactive world models should be treated less like frame-predicting video generators and more like game engines that maintain state, rules, and long-term consistency. This shift enables interactions to produce coherent outcomes as the world evolves, not just visually plausible next frames.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the gap between current video generative models and truly interactive worlds: existing models can predict observations from actions, but they often fail to enforce persistent game state and rule-based behavior over time.
method: Reframe interactive world modeling as a stateful engine problem rather than purely pixel prediction.
Condition future predictions on user actions while tracking evolving world conditions and rules.
Emphasize interaction outcomes that remain coherent across time, supporting longer-horizon consistency in dynamic environments.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer design target for building interactive simulations, agents, and game-like environments that behave consistently under user control. It can improve research in generative world models, embodied AI, and controllable content generation.

title: Enabling local neural operators to perform equation-free system-level analysis
authors: Gianluca Fabiani, Hannes Vandecasteele, Somdatta Goswami, Constantinos Siettos, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01265-1

Moving beyond brute-force simulations, local neural operators—combined with equation-free methods and Krylov subspace techniques—enable system-level stability and bifurcation analysis of complex spatiotemporal systems directly from data.

infographic.key_insight: Local neural operators can act as data-driven surrogates for complex dynamical systems, allowing researchers to study stability and bifurcations without writing explicit equations or running expensive full simulations. By pairing them with equation-free and Krylov subspace methods, the paper enables system-level analysis directly from data.
infographic.problem_solved: Traditional stability and bifurcation analysis of spatiotemporal systems usually requires explicit governing equations and costly brute-force simulation. This paper addresses the challenge of extracting system-level behavior from data when the equations are unknown, incomplete, or too expensive to simulate at scale.
method: Train local neural operators to approximate the evolution of spatially extended dynamical systems from data.
Embed these learned operators into an equation-free analysis pipeline to estimate macroscopic behavior.
Use Krylov subspace techniques to efficiently compute stability-related quantities and perform bifurcation analysis.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how learned operators can move beyond prediction and become tools for scientific discovery and analysis. It expands the role of neural surrogates from fast emulation to interpretable, system-level decision support in complex physical and biological systems.

title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
authors: Xiao Ye, Jacob Dineen, Evan Zhu, Shijie Lu, Kevin Song
abstract: Forecasters are evaluated by backtesting, which replays resolved questions and grades the probability the system would have assigned before the outcome was known. For LLMs, two channels leak the answer into this test. A model that retrieves can surface reports written after the event, turning forecasting into a lookup, and each new model is trained on data closer to the event, so a question that lay in the future for last year's models sits inside this year's training data. Either way, the test

infographic.key_insight: Backtesting LLM forecasters can be misleading because models may "cheat" by seeing post-event information through retrieval or by being trained on data that already includes the event. Hindcast proposes replaying prediction markets in a way that helps evaluate forecasts without leaking the answer.
infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the evaluation problem for LLM-based forecasting systems: standard backtests can overestimate performance when future information enters via web retrieval or training data contamination.
method: Replay resolved prediction-market questions to simulate the forecasting context before outcomes were known.
Account for two leakage channels: retrieval of post-event reports and training-data temporal leakage across model generations.
Use hindcasting as an evaluation framework to more faithfully measure whether an LLM could have made the forecast at the time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves trustworthiness of benchmark results for forecasting models and helps distinguish genuine predictive ability from information leakage. It also encourages fairer evaluation practices for time-sensitive tasks.

authors: Daniel Grillmeyer, Marius Hadry, Michael Stenger, Vanessa Borst, Veronika Lesch
abstract: With rising global energy demand and growing awareness of climate change and its impacts, the share of renewable energies in the global energy mix continues to grow. Unlike conventional power generation, the output of renewable energy sources cannot be controlled as consistently due to their dependence on environmental conditions. Therefore, reliable prediction of current and future energy production is essential. In this paper, we report findings from two structured literature reviews on real-w

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that efficient wrapper-based feature selection can improve wind and solar power prediction by identifying the most useful inputs and reducing noise. In practice, this can make renewable energy forecasts more accurate and computationally efficient.
infographic.problem_solved: Renewable energy output is highly variable because it depends on weather and environmental conditions. This paper addresses the challenge of building reliable wind and solar power prediction models from complex, high-dimensional data.
method: Conducted two structured literature reviews focused on real-world wind and solar power forecasting.
Analyzed wrapper-based feature selection methods that evaluate feature subsets using model performance.
Compared efficient selection strategies to understand how they can improve predictive accuracy and reduce unnecessary input variables.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the study highlights a practical way to improve forecasting models without simply adding more data. It is especially relevant for energy applications where accuracy, interpretability, and efficiency all matter.

title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
authors: Hefeng Zhou, Jinxuan Zhang, Jiong Lou, Yuxin Liu, Chaochao Lu
abstract: The emergence of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning has significantly enhanced the ability of large language models (LLMs) to tackle complex, multi-step tasks. However, when errors occur, current interaction approaches typically involve re-generating another response that may make mistakes again, or users laboriously flag the faulty step in follow-up turns that may get responses <You are right, I made a mistake here> followed by similar errors recurring. To address this issue, we propose an effici

infographic.key_insight: Deep Interaction proposes a more efficient way for humans to correct large reasoning models by targeting the exact faulty step instead of re-running the whole reasoning process. This aims to reduce repeated mistakes and make human-AI collaboration more reliable.
infographic.problem_solved: Current human-AI interaction for chain-of-thought reasoning is inefficient: when a model makes an error, users often need to regenerate answers or repeatedly point out mistakes, but the model may still produce similar errors. The paper addresses the need for precise, step-level correction in long reasoning tasks.
method: Introduces an interaction method designed to let users pinpoint and correct specific reasoning steps.
Focuses on improving efficiency compared with full regeneration or broad follow-up prompting.
Aims to reduce repeated error loops by making corrections more local and actionable.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could make debugging and steering large reasoning models much faster and more dependable. It is especially useful in workflows where correctness matters and iterative prompting is too slow or error-prone.

abstract: Driving-world generation has emerged as a core capability for scalable autonomous-driving simulation, yet existing methods remain limited in object-level controllability and long-horizon stability. We present M$^\text{4}$World, a Multi-view and Multimodal generative driving world model that synthesizes future surround-view video streams and synchronized LiDAR scans while supporting interactive object Manipulation and stable Minute-long streaming. Fine-grained object manipulation is realized thro

infographic.key_insight: M^4World is a driving world model that can generate realistic future surround-view video and LiDAR together, while letting users interactively manipulate objects over long time horizons. Its key advance is combining multi-view, multimodal prediction with stable minute-long streaming.
infographic.problem_solved: Current driving world models struggle with two major issues: they cannot precisely control individual objects in the scene, and they often lose stability or realism when generating long sequences. This paper addresses both object-level controllability and long-horizon consistency for autonomous-driving simulation.
method: Generates synchronized future surround-view camera streams and LiDAR scans as a unified driving world model.
Supports interactive object manipulation, enabling fine-grained edits to scene elements during generation.
Uses a streaming generation framework designed for stable minute-long rollouts rather than short clipped predictions.

title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
authors: Ximeng Mao, Nanda H. Krishna, Avery Hee-Woon Ryoo, Matthew G. Perich, Guillaume Lajoie
abstract: Robust and accurate neural decoders are integral to neurotechnologies such as brain-computer interfaces and closed-loop experiments. Recent work has shown that tokenizing neural data at the spike level facilitates multi-session pretraining and delivers state-of-the-art decoding performance. However, current spike-based models are restricted to supervised learning (SL), limiting training to datasets with paired behavioural labels. To address this limitation, we introduce MOJO (Masked autOencoder-

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows that neural decoders can benefit from large amounts of unlabelled spike data, not just labelled sessions, by pretraining a model that learns general neural patterns before decoding behavior. The result is a more robust decoder that transfers better across sessions and likely improves performance when labels are scarce.
infographic.problem_solved: Current spike-based neural decoding models usually require paired neural activity and behavioural labels, which limits training to small supervised datasets. This paper tackles the lack of scalable pretraining for neural population decoding on unlabelled data.
method: Introduce MOJO, a masked autoencoder-style framework for neural spike data.
Pretrain on unlabelled neural recordings by masking parts of the spike sequence and learning to reconstruct them.
Transfer the pretrained representations to downstream decoding tasks, improving generalization across sessions and subjects.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners working in neurotechnology, this offers a path to build stronger decoders with less reliance on expensive labelled data. It also aligns neural decoding with modern self-supervised learning, opening the door to larger-scale and more generalizable models.

title: SPECS: Speciated Evolutionary Circuit Synthesis
authors: Yağız Gençer, Stefan Uhlich, Andrea Bonetti, Arun Venkitaraman, Chia-Yu Hsieh
abstract: We propose SPECS, a genetic algorithm for automated analog circuit synthesis with joint topology and sizing optimization. SPECS is inspired by NeuroEvolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT), an evolutionary algorithm originally developed to synthesize neural networks. By reformulating the genome representation and adapting the genetic operators to the analog circuit domain, we successfully transfer the core principles of NEAT to analog circuit synthesis. Circuit-specific wiring constraints are i

infographic.key_insight: SPECS adapts the core idea of NEAT to analog circuit design, enabling the joint search for circuit topology and component sizing in one evolutionary process. This lets the algorithm synthesize circuits while respecting domain-specific wiring constraints.
infographic.problem_solved: Automated analog circuit synthesis is difficult because designers must optimize both the circuit structure and the component values at the same time, while also obeying strict wiring and connectivity rules. Existing methods often struggle to explore this large, constrained design space efficiently.
method: Uses a genetic algorithm to evolve analog circuits with joint topology and sizing optimization.
Reformulates the genome representation from NEAT-style neural networks to analog circuits.
Adapts genetic operators and speciation to the circuit domain, incorporating circuit-specific wiring constraints.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SPECS shows how an evolutionary algorithm can be transferred from neural architecture search to physical design problems with minimal conceptual changes. This expands the reach of automated design methods into analog hardware synthesis.

title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
authors: Zhouchonghao Wu, Akshay Rangesh, Weixin Li, Wei-Jer Chang, Zachary Lee
abstract: Training robust autonomous driving agents requires a simulator that is fast enough for reinforcement learning at scale, realistic enough to ground behavior in real-world map structure, and diverse enough to cover the safety-critical long tail that logged data rarely contains. We present TerraZero, a procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack. A configurable C engine runs simulation on the CPU and policy inference on the GPU over a zero-copy path, sustaining 1.3M agent-steps per se

infographic.key_insight: TerraZero shows that autonomous driving policies can be trained at large scale without expert demonstrations by combining procedural simulation with self-play. Its key breakthrough is a fast CPU/GPU co-design that can run millions of agent-steps per second while still capturing realistic map structure and long-tail driving scenarios.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the bottleneck in training robust driving agents: existing simulators are often too slow for scalable RL, too limited in realism, or too narrow to include rare but safety-critical events that are missing from logged data.
method: Builds a procedural driving simulator that generates diverse road environments and scenarios on demand.
Uses a configurable C engine with CPU simulation and GPU policy inference connected through a zero-copy path to maximize throughput.
Trains agents with zero-demonstration self-play, reducing dependence on human driving logs and expert labels.

Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 14 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01259-z

Kindt et al. present a unifying framework for superposition in neural networks. Their three-step approach clarifies how latent features can be identified, disentangled and assessed.

infographic.key_insight: This paper proposes a single framework that links neural superposition to sparse, interpretable latent codes. In simple terms, it shows how hidden features in neural networks can be identified, separated, and evaluated in a consistent way.
infographic.problem_solved: Neural networks often mix multiple latent features into shared representations, making them hard to interpret. This work addresses the challenge of disentangling those features and judging whether the resulting codes are truly meaningful and sparse.
method: Introduces a three-step pipeline for identifying latent features in superposed neural representations.
Provides a framework to disentangle overlapping features into sparse, interpretable codes.
Includes a way to assess the quality and interpretability of the recovered latent representations.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes it easier to understand what a model has learned and why it makes certain predictions. It can support debugging, interpretability, and more trustworthy model design.
