title: OPSD-V: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Post-Training Few-Step Autoregressive Video Generators
authors: Hongyu Liu, Chun Wang, Feng Gao, Xuanhua He, Yue Ma
abstract: We propose OPSD-V, an on-policy self-distillation paradigm for post-training few-step autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models. Existing few-step AR video generators can produce long videos with low latency, but still suffer from error accumulation and weakened motion dynamics during long autoregressive rollout. OPSD-V reduces long-horizon degradation while preserving the original few-step inference path. The key idea is to introduce real long-video data as temporal context during training and

infographic.key_insight: OPSD-V improves few-step autoregressive video generation by self-distilling from real long-video context during training, reducing long-horizon drift without changing the fast inference path. In simple terms, it helps short-step video models stay coherent and dynamic over longer rollouts.
infographic.problem_solved: Few-step autoregressive video generators are fast, but they often accumulate errors over time and produce weaker motion as the generated video gets longer. This paper addresses long-range degradation while keeping low-latency inference intact.
method: Uses an on-policy self-distillation training scheme for post-training few-step AR video diffusion models.
Injects real long-video data as temporal context during training to better match long-horizon generation conditions.
Preserves the original few-step inference path, improving long-rollout quality without adding inference cost.
infographic.impact: This approach makes fast video generators more reliable for longer sequences, which is important for practical video creation, simulation, and content generation. Practitioners can gain better temporal consistency and motion quality without sacrificing speed.

title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
authors: Yifan Wu, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, Mingyi Wang, Bo Peng
abstract: In long-horizon tasks, decision-relevant state is often scattered across an expanding trajectory, while the action agent must surface it and act. As trajectories grow, task requirements, environment facts, prior attempts, diagnoses, and open subgoals can be buried in the context window or pushed beyond it, failing to influence decisions when needed. We call this failure mode "behavioral state decay". We study memory as an active intervention mechanism rather than passive retrieval. A separate me

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that long-horizon agents don’t just need more memory—they need the right memory to be brought back at the right time. It introduces proactive memory as an active mechanism to prevent “behavioral state decay” when important task details get buried or lost in long trajectories.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of long-horizon decision-making where critical information such as prior attempts, task requirements, environment facts, and open subgoals becomes hard to access as the context grows.
method: Uses a separate memory agent to proactively identify decision-relevant state instead of relying only on passive retrieval.
Surfaces buried information from the expanding trajectory before it is needed, helping the action agent stay aligned with current goals.
Targets behavioral state decay by maintaining continuity of task context across long sequences of actions and observations.
infographic.impact: This matters because long-context agents often fail not from lack of information, but from failing to recall the right information at the right moment. Proactive memory can improve reliability, planning, and recovery in real-world long-horizon tasks.

title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
authors: Chuning Zhu, Eva Xu, Jose Barreiros, Krishnan Srinivasan, Paarth Shah
abstract: Human decision-making is highly flexible -- some actions are taken immediately; others require longer deliberation. Language models have exhibited a similar capacity for adaptive "reasoning." However, transferring this capability to continuous control policies has been challenging, as directly reasoning in language space may lack the granularity for spatial understanding and precise motions. In this work, we show that reasoning for control policies can emerge by organizing information in an auto

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that control policies can develop flexible, language-like reasoning by storing and organizing information in a latent "memory palace" rather than reasoning directly in text. This enables policies to adapt between quick actions and longer deliberation while remaining precise enough for continuous control.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of bringing adaptive reasoning to continuous control tasks, where direct language-space reasoning is often too coarse for spatial details and fine motor actions.
method: Represents control-relevant information in a latent structured space that supports deliberation before action.
Uses an autoregressive variational inference framework to model sequential reasoning for control.
Bridges high-level reasoning and low-level motion by learning latent steps that improve policy flexibility and precision.
infographic.impact: This matters for practitioners because it offers a path to more capable robotic and control agents that can decide when to act quickly versus when to think longer. It may improve robustness, adaptability, and interpretability in continuous decision-making systems.

title: MulTTiPop: A Multitrack Transcription Dataset for Pop Music
authors: Nathan Pruyne, Benjamin Stoler, William Chen, Chien-yu Huang, Shinji Watanabe
abstract: We present MulTTiPop, a dataset of pop music segments and their associated multitrack MIDI recordings for the evaluation of automatic music transcription models. MulTTiPop contains 572 segments of popular music totaling 3.5 hours of audio, and contains songs from diverse genres and decades from the 1930s to 2000s. To collect this dataset, we perform metadata-based matching on song segments from the Lakh MIDI and TheoryTab datasets, manually identify an anchor beat between the audio and MIDI, the

infographic.key_insight: MulTTiPop is a new benchmark dataset for evaluating automatic music transcription on real pop music, pairing audio segments with multitrack MIDI. It provides diverse, decade-spanning examples that make transcription evaluation more realistic and challenging.
infographic.problem_solved: Automatic music transcription models need high-quality, aligned audio-MIDI data for evaluation, but existing datasets are limited in scale, diversity, or alignment quality. This paper addresses the lack of a pop-music-focused multitrack transcription benchmark.
method: Collected 572 pop-music segments totaling 3.5 hours of audio.
Matched song segments from the Lakh MIDI and TheoryTab datasets using metadata-based alignment.
Manually identified an anchor beat to align audio and MIDI for accurate transcription evaluation.
infographic.impact: MulTTiPop gives researchers a more realistic testbed for evaluating transcription systems on varied pop music across decades and genres. This can improve benchmarking, error analysis, and model development for multitrack music transcription.

title: WaspMOT: A Benchmark for Long-Term Multi-Object Tracking of Trichogramma Wasps
authors: Tomasz Stanczyk, Yuan Gao, Hardik Agarwal, Seongroo Yoon, Tiantao Zhang
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) has achieved strong performance on benchmarks dominated by short video sequences. However, such datasets do not adequately evaluate long-term identity preservation, where objects must be tracked consistently over extended durations. We introduce WaspMOT, a benchmark designed to address this gap through long-duration tracking of Trichogramma wasps in controlled ecological experiments. The dataset contains 10 sequences of approximately 12,000 frames each (over 8 minutes

infographic.key_insight: WaspMOT introduces a new long-term multi-object tracking benchmark for ecological footage, targeting identity preservation over minutes-long sequences instead of short clips. It helps reveal whether MOT systems can remain consistent when tracking the same tiny animals for extended periods.
infographic.problem_solved: Most MOT benchmarks focus on short videos, which do not properly test long-term tracking and identity maintenance. This paper addresses the need for a dataset that evaluates sustained tracking in realistic, controlled biological experiments.
method: Collected WaspMOT: 10 long video sequences of Trichogramma wasps, each around 12,000 frames long (8+ minutes).
Designed the benchmark specifically for long-term multi-object tracking and identity preservation under controlled ecological conditions.
Provides a harder evaluation setting than standard short-sequence datasets, exposing failure cases such as drift, occlusion recovery, and ID switches over time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, WaspMOT offers a more realistic stress test for tracking models that need to operate reliably over long durations. It can drive the development and evaluation of tracking methods that are better suited for robotics, ecology, surveillance, and any application where identity consistency matters.

title: Enhancing In-context Panoramic Generation via Geometric-aware Pretraining
authors: Haoran Feng, Ruiyang Zhang, Longyi Zhang, Dizhe Zhang, Lu Qi
abstract: In this work, we present Canvas360, a two-stage framework for in-context panoramic generation that combines geometry-aware pretraining with downstream task-specific fine-tuning. To address the lack of large-scale, high-quality training data tailored to in-context panoramic tasks, we propose Canvas360Dataset, a collection of 1M high-quality paired panoramic samples for style transfer, inpainting, outpainting, and editing, enabling effective supervision across diverse in-context generation scenari

infographic.key_insight: Canvas360 improves in-context panoramic generation by pairing geometry-aware pretraining with task-specific fine-tuning. The key idea is that large, high-quality panoramic training data can teach models to handle style transfer, inpainting, outpainting, and editing more reliably.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper tackles the lack of large-scale, high-quality datasets and training strategies for in-context panoramic generation, where models must preserve 360° geometric consistency while performing diverse editing tasks.
method: Two-stage framework: geometry-aware pretraining followed by downstream task-specific fine-tuning.
Introduces Canvas360Dataset, a 1M-sample paired panoramic dataset covering style transfer, inpainting, outpainting, and editing.
Uses high-quality panoramic supervision to improve generalization across multiple in-context generation scenarios.
infographic.impact: This work gives practitioners a stronger foundation for building panoramic generation systems that are both more realistic and more controllable. It is especially useful for applications in virtual reality, 360° content editing, and immersive scene synthesis.

title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
authors: Xiao Fu, Yue Hu, Meida Chen, Peter Anthony Beerel, Barath Raghavan
abstract: Accurate 3D terrain maps are essential for emergency response when assessing wildfire hazards. However, wildfire-prone regions often span vast areas where conventional reconstruction methods underperform. Airborne LiDAR systems provide high-resolution terrain data, but they are expensive and infrequently updated. Image-based methods offer a lower-cost alternative, but struggle due to sparse visual features and limited image overlap. We propose a multi-modal reconstruction framework leveraging ou

infographic.key_insight: This paper proposes a large-scale terrain modeling approach designed for wildfire-prone regions where traditional 3D reconstruction methods struggle. The core idea is to combine multiple data sources to build accurate terrain maps more reliably and at larger geographic scales.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of reconstructing accurate 3D terrain over vast wildfire-prone landscapes, where airborne LiDAR is costly and infrequent, and image-only methods fail due to sparse features and low overlap.
method: Uses a multi-modal reconstruction framework to integrate complementary sources of terrain information.
Targets large-area mapping where standard image-based 3D reconstruction has poor coverage or accuracy.
Aims to produce updated terrain models that are more practical for emergency response and wildfire hazard assessment.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights how multi-modal geospatial modeling can overcome real-world data sparsity and scale limitations. It is especially relevant for building robust remote-sensing systems that support disaster response and environmental monitoring.

title: LongE2V: Long-Horizon Event-based Video Reconstruction, Prediction, and Frame Interpolation with Video Diffusion Models
authors: Cheng-De Fan, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu, Chen-Wei Chang, Chin-Yang Lin, Kun-Ru Wu
abstract: Recovering high-quality video from sparse event streams is a challenging task. Regression methods often blur textures, while existing generative models struggle with long-term stability. We propose LongE2V, a novel approach that leverages pre-trained video diffusion priors to jointly handle event-based video reconstruction, prediction, and frame interpolation. By fine-tuning a foundational video model, our approach achieves high data efficiency and superior perceptual quality. We introduce Autor

infographic.key_insight: LongE2V shows that a pre-trained video diffusion model can be adapted to event streams to produce sharper, more stable long-horizon video reconstruction and prediction than traditional regression-based methods. It unifies reconstruction, prediction, and frame interpolation in one generative framework.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of recovering high-quality video from sparse event data, especially over long time horizons where existing methods tend to blur details or drift in stability.
method: Fine-tunes a foundational video diffusion model to use event streams as conditioning input.
Jointly supports event-based video reconstruction, future frame prediction, and frame interpolation in a single model.
Improves data efficiency and perceptual quality by leveraging strong pre-trained diffusion priors instead of training from scratch.
infographic.impact: This matters because it offers a practical path to high-quality event-based video synthesis without requiring massive task-specific training data. For practitioners, it suggests diffusion priors can make sparse-sensing video systems more accurate, sharper, and more versatile.

title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
authors: Siddharth Damodharan, Radhika Gupta, Ali Alshami, Ryan Rabinowitz, Jugal Kalita
abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models, Large Language Models, and Multimodal Large Language Models have improved autonomous driving tasks such as scene understanding, decision making, trajectory prediction, and visual question answering. However, evaluating whether these models can reliably reason about safety-critical incidents remains challenging. To address this gap, we present AUTOPILOT-VQA, an incident-centric visual question answering benchmark for dashcam video understanding. The data

infographic.key_insight: AUTOPILOT-VQA introduces a benchmark focused on incident-centric dashcam understanding, making it easier to test whether vision-language models can reason about safety-critical driving events rather than just general scenes. The paper highlights a key gap: strong multimodal models still need rigorous evaluation on real-world driving incidents.

Frame evaluation around safety-relevant questions that require reasoning about what happened, why it matters, and what could happen next.
Use the benchmark to compare vision-language and multimodal models on incident understanding performance.
infographic.impact: This work gives researchers and practitioners a more realistic way to evaluate multimodal systems for autonomous driving and safety applications. It can help identify model weaknesses before deployment in high-stakes environments.

title: Accurate, Interdisciplinary and Transparent Structure-property Understanding with Deep Native Structural Reasoning
authors: Chen Tang, Yizhou Wang, Jianyu Wu, Lintao Wang, Shixiang Tang
abstract: Structure-property relationships are foundational to biology, chemistry and materials science, where function, reactivity and physical response emerge from spatial, chemical and periodic organization. Mechanistically explaining these relationships requires interpreting structural evidence through scientific principles and physical constraints, from stereochemistry and bonding to symmetry, energetics and periodic order. However, applying artificial intelligence to this process presents a joint ch

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces a deep native structural reasoning approach that aims to make AI predictions of structure-property relationships more accurate, interdisciplinary, and transparent. It emphasizes reasoning directly from structural evidence under scientific and physical constraints rather than relying on opaque pattern matching.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of explaining how structure determines properties across biology, chemistry, and materials science, where AI must account for stereochemistry, bonding, symmetry, energetics, and periodic order in a principled way.
method: Uses deep structural reasoning to interpret spatial, chemical, and periodic organization directly from input structures.
Integrates scientific principles and physical constraints into the prediction process to improve interpretability and reliability.
Aims to produce transparent explanations alongside property predictions, supporting interdisciplinary structure-property analysis.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a path toward models that are not only more accurate but also more trustworthy and scientifically grounded. It is especially relevant for domains where explanations matter as much as predictions.

title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis

title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
authors: Ying Chang, Jiahang Xu, Xuan Feng, Chenyuan Yang, Peng Cheng
abstract: The optimization of long-horizon agents increasingly relies on reflection-based mechanisms, where a large language model (LLM) acts as an optimizer to diagnose agent failures and improve agent policies. However, real execution traces are difficult to use directly for optimization: large trace collections are often redundant and heterogeneous, making optimization inefficient and prone to overfitting to low-value failures; meanwhile, each individual trajectory also contains many irrelevant steps,

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows that raw agent execution traces are too noisy to optimize directly, and that better agent improvement comes from extracting structurally meaningful failure patterns and root causes. In simple terms: compress many messy trajectories into a smaller set of high-value causal signals for reflection-based optimization.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of using long-horizon agent traces for optimization when traces are redundant, heterogeneous, and filled with irrelevant steps. These issues make LLM-based reflection inefficient and can lead to overfitting to low-value failures instead of learning actionable improvements.
method: Group and filter large collections of execution traces to reduce redundancy and focus on informative failures.
Analyze trajectories structurally to identify repeated patterns, key decision points, and failure modes rather than treating every trace equally.
Extract causal root causes from trajectories so the optimizer can target the true sources of agent failure and generate better policy updates.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, this can make agent debugging and improvement more sample-efficient, less noisy, and more robust. It helps LLM-based optimizers learn from the right failures instead of being distracted by irrelevant trace details.

title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
authors: Yair Feldman, Linxi Zhao, Nathan Godey, Dongyoung Go, Yilun Hua
abstract: Limited memory language models (LMLMs) externalize factual knowledge during pretraining to a knowledge base (KB), rather than memorizing it in their weights. During generation, the model then fetches knowledge from the KB as needed. This recently introduced paradigm provides multiple advantages, including knowledge control capabilities that remain beyond conventional LLMs. We propose continuous-query LMLM (CO-LMLM), where the KB pairs continuous keys with textual knowledge values, a significant

infographic.key_insight: Co-LMLM extends limited-memory language models by using continuous query keys to retrieve textual knowledge from an external knowledge base during generation. This preserves factual control while making knowledge access more flexible than discrete retrieval schemes.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of storing and using factual knowledge in language models without forcing it into model weights, while still allowing efficient, controllable retrieval at generation time.
method: Pairs continuous-valued keys with text-based knowledge values in an external knowledge base.
Uses the model's query representation to fetch relevant knowledge dynamically during generation.
Retains the LMLM paradigm of externalized knowledge to improve controllability and reduce reliance on parametric memory.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Co-LMLM offers a more controllable way to manage factual knowledge, making it easier to update, audit, and steer model behavior. This is especially useful for applications where knowledge freshness and governance matter.

title: MedPMC: A Systematic Framework for Scaling High-Fidelity Medical Multimodal Data for Foundation Models
authors: Hyunjae Kim, Dain Kim, Pan Xiao, Serina S. Applebaum, Younjoon Chung
abstract: Medicine is inherently multimodal, requiring clinicians to synthesize information across diverse data streams. Yet the development of multimodal foundation models is constrained by limited access to large-scale, high-quality clinical data. Although PubMed Central (PMC) offers a complementary source of expert-authored image-text data, existing PMC-derived resources remain limited in fidelity, reproducibility, and clinical validation. We introduce MedPMC, an automated, continuously updatable frame

infographic.key_insight: MedPMC proposes a systematic, automated way to turn PubMed Central into a scalable source of high-fidelity medical image-text data for foundation models. The key idea is to improve not just scale, but clinical fidelity, reproducibility, and validation in multimodal medical datasets.
infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the shortage of large, reliable, and clinically validated multimodal medical data needed to train foundation models. Existing PMC-based datasets are often hard to reproduce, low in fidelity, or insufficiently vetted for real clinical use.
method: Builds an automated framework to continuously collect and update medical multimodal data from PubMed Central.
Emphasizes data quality control, fidelity checking, and reproducibility to ensure the image-text pairs are clinically useful.
Creates a systematic pipeline designed to scale high-quality medical multimodal resources for foundation model development.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MedPMC offers a practical path to training stronger medical multimodal models with better data quality and less manual curation. This can improve robustness, trustworthiness, and downstream performance in clinical AI applications.

title: Scaling Mixture-of-Experts Video Pretraining for Embodied Intelligence
authors: Shuailei Ma, Jiaqi Liao, Xinyang Wang, Jingjing Wang, Chaoran Feng
abstract: Despite the recent promise in robot control, video generative models suffer from a domain mismatch due to their primary focus on content creation. For example, their design inherently prioritizes visual fidelity and creativity over computational efficiency and physical realism. In this work, we present LingBot-Video, a DiT-based video pretraining paradigm specifically tailored for embodied intelligence. From the architecture perspective, we adopt the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), instead of dense, f

infographic.key_insight: LingBot-Video adapts large-scale video pretraining for embodied intelligence by using a Mixture-of-Experts DiT design, aiming to improve both efficiency and physical relevance. The core idea is to move video models away from pure content generation and toward representations that better support robot control.
infographic.problem_solved: Traditional video generative models are optimized for visual quality and creativity, but this creates a domain mismatch for robotics and embodied AI, where physical realism, action understanding, and compute efficiency are more important.
method: Build a DiT-based video pretraining framework tailored for embodied intelligence.
Replace dense parameterization with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) to improve scaling and computational efficiency.
Pretrain on video data to learn motion-aware, action-relevant representations that transfer better to robot control tasks.
infographic.impact: This work offers a scalable path to turn general video models into more useful foundation models for robotics and embodied AI. For practitioners, it suggests a way to improve transfer to downstream control tasks while keeping training more efficient.

title: ALER-TI: Aligned Latent Embedding Retrieval for Time Series Imputation
authors: Xuan-Thong Truong, Trung-Kien Le, Tung Kieu, Thi-Thu Nguyen, Nhat-Hai Nguyen
abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced time series imputation, yet most existing architectures primarily rely on localized temporal context within the corrupted input sequence. This reliance can be limiting in real-world scenarios, where time series often exhibit non-stationary dynamics, weak temporal correlations, and infrequent patterns that are difficult to reconstruct from nearby observations alone. In this paper, we propose ALER-TI, Aligned Latent Embedding Retrieval for Time Series Imput

infographic.key_insight: ALER-TI improves time series imputation by retrieving useful latent patterns from aligned embeddings, instead of depending only on nearby corrupted observations. This helps reconstruct missing values when local context is weak, noisy, or non-stationary.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of imputing missing values in time series with weak temporal correlations, irregular patterns, and non-stationary behavior, where standard local-context-based deep models often fail.
method: Learn latent embeddings that capture richer time series representations beyond the raw observed neighborhood.
Retrieve aligned latent information from similar patterns to support reconstruction of missing segments.
Use the retrieved embedding context to guide imputation when local temporal clues are insufficient.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more robust imputation strategy for messy real-world time series such as sensor streams, healthcare signals, and industrial data. It can improve downstream forecasting, anomaly detection, and decision-making by producing more reliable completed sequences.

title: Infinite Worlds with Versatile Interactions
authors: Zelin Gao, Qiuyu Wang, Jiapeng Zhu, Jingye Chen, Zichen Liu
abstract: We present LingBot-World 2.0 (also known as LingBot-World-Infinity), an advanced iteration of LingBot-World featuring four distinct upgrades. (1) Our model achieves an unbounded interaction horizon while maintaining consistent output quality, benefiting from a carefully crafted causal pretraining paradigm. (2) Through distilling a real-time variant from the base model, our system guarantees rapid response time, sufficient to drive 720p video streams at 60 fps. (3) Compared to the previous versio

infographic.key_insight: LingBot-World 2.0 pushes AI world models toward open-ended interaction, combining unlimited interaction length with stable quality and real-time responsiveness. It also expands interaction versatility, making the system more practical for continuous, high-frame-rate environments.
infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of building world models that can interact for very long horizons without degrading output quality, while also running fast enough for real-time use in demanding visual settings like 720p video at 60 fps.
method: Uses a carefully designed causal pretraining paradigm to support unbounded interaction horizons while preserving consistency.
Distills a real-time variant from the base model to achieve low-latency inference suitable for live video generation/control.
Improves the previous LingBot-World system with four major upgrades, including broader interaction capabilities and stronger practical performance.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shows a path toward world models that are both scalable over long sessions and deployable in real-time applications. That makes them more useful for robotics, interactive agents, simulation, and live multimodal systems.

title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
authors: Jordan Painter, Dipankar Srirag, Adarsh Kappiyath, Diptesh Kanojia, Aditya Joshi
abstract: Large language models increasingly \emph{understand} dialectal English, yet still \emph{produce} only standard, US-leaning English, leaving dialectal generation, the harder half of the problem, largely unaddressed. We introduce \textbf{DiaLLM}, which continually pretrains three open-weight language model families on the International Corpus of English and applies implicit and explicit post-training paradigms, each combined with three model alignment strategies, giving the first controlled compar

infographic.key_insight: DiaLLM shows that language models can often understand dialectal English better than they can generate it, revealing a robustness-generation gap. The paper’s main contribution is a controlled setup to study and improve dialect adaptation across multiple model families and training strategies.
infographic.problem_solved: This paper addresses the mismatch between dialect understanding and dialect generation in large language models, especially their tendency to produce standard, US-leaning English even when dialectal input is understood.
method: Continual pretraining of three open-weight language model families on the International Corpus of English.
Comparison of implicit vs. explicit post-training paradigms for dialect adaptation.
Combination of each post-training paradigm with three different model alignment strategies to enable controlled analysis.
infographic.impact: For AI practitioners, this work provides a practical framework for evaluating and improving dialect-aware generation, not just comprehension. It is useful for building more linguistically inclusive systems that respond more naturally across English dialects.

title: Dual Latent Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Hongyu Qu, Jianzhe Gao, Xiaobin Hu, Shaohuan Yang, Xinlei Yu
abstract: Mainstream Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models predict actions primarily from the current observation under a Markovian assumption, thus struggling with long-horizon, temporally dependent tasks. Existing memory-augmented VLAs either expand the observation window or retrieve history from the memory bank as auxiliary policy-side context. However, they leave memory outside the native latent embedding space of VLA reasoning, preventing historical experience from being fluidly interleaved with multim

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that robotic VLAs need memory inside their latent reasoning space, not just as extra context. By introducing dual latent memory, the model can weave past experience into current decision-making more naturally for long-horizon tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard Vision-Language-Action models are mostly Markovian: they act from the current observation and struggle when tasks require remembering earlier steps, goals, or interactions over time. Existing memory methods often keep history outside the model’s core latent space, limiting seamless use of past experience.
method: Introduce a dual latent memory mechanism designed to support both short-term and long-term task dependencies.
Integrate historical experience directly into the VLA latent representation so reasoning over current and past context is more fluid.
Target robotic manipulation settings where actions depend on temporally extended, multi-step understanding.
infographic.impact: This could make robotic agents more reliable on complex manipulation tasks that unfold over many steps, such as rearranging objects or recovering from earlier mistakes. For practitioners, it offers a path toward memory-enabled policies that reason over time more effectively than purely observation-driven VLAs.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Calcification Classification in Mammography Across Multi-Site Datasets
authors: Xuan Liu, Derek L. Nguyen, Emily C. Barre, Jennifer Thomas, Thomas Lynch
abstract: Deep learning-based computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems have shown strong performance in breast cancer diagnosis, particularly for classification tasks in mammography. However, domain shifts across multi-site datasets remain a challenge, especially when models are applied to unseen domains. In this work, we proposed a calcification classification framework to improve malignant versus benign breast disease classification across multi-site mammography datasets. The framework consisted of two co

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows that unsupervised domain adaptation can help mammography models stay accurate when they are tested on data from hospitals or sites they have never seen before. The approach improves benign vs. malignant calcification classification by reducing the performance drop caused by multi-site dataset shifts.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the domain shift problem in mammography CAD systems, where models trained on one site often perform poorly on unseen sites due to differences in scanners, imaging protocols, and patient populations.
method: Builds a calcification classification framework for benign vs. malignant breast disease in multi-site mammography data.
Uses unsupervised domain adaptation to transfer knowledge from labeled source sites to unlabeled target sites.
Aims to learn domain-invariant features so the classifier generalizes better across institutions.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights a practical path toward more robust medical imaging models that generalize beyond a single dataset. It is especially relevant for deploying AI in real clinical settings where cross-site variability is unavoidable.

title: ELSA3D: Elastic Semantic Anchoring for Unified 3D Understanding and Generation
authors: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Onkar Susladkar, Yuanzhe Liu
abstract: Unified 3D foundation models aspire to generate 3D assets and reason about them in language within a single backbone, but their text-3D interaction remains largely implicit. Existing methods concatenate text and 3D tokens into a flat sequence and rely on self-attention, collapsing coarse structural cues and fine geometric details into one undifferentiated representation. We introduce ELSA3D, a unified 3D model that addresses this with elastic semantic anchoring, structuring language and geometri

infographic.key_insight: ELSA3D improves unified 3D understanding and generation by giving language a structured role in 3D reasoning, rather than flattening text and geometry into one undifferentiated token stream. Its elastic semantic anchoring helps preserve both coarse object structure and fine geometric detail.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper tackles the weakness of prior unified 3D foundation models, where text-3D interaction is implicit and flat self-attention collapses important structural cues and detailed geometry. This makes it harder to generate accurate 3D assets while also reasoning about them in language.
method: Introduces elastic semantic anchoring to explicitly structure interactions between language and 3D geometry.
Separates coarse semantic/structural cues from fine-grained geometric details instead of mixing everything into a single sequence.
Builds a unified backbone that supports both 3D generation and language-based understanding within the same model.
infographic.impact: This approach can make unified 3D foundation models more controllable, interpretable, and faithful to geometry. For practitioners, it suggests a better path toward models that can both create 3D assets and describe or reason about them reliably.

title: CAIRN: Cross-Room 3D Scene Understanding with Topology-Aware Large Multimodal Models
authors: He Liang, Chenyang Ma, Yiming Zhang, Sangyun Shin, Andrew Markham
abstract: Existing 3D scene-grounded Large Language Models (3D-LLMs) focus on answering questions grounded in simplified single-room 3D scenes, lacking the ability to reason over real-world household environments containing multiple interconnected rooms and diverse object categories. We introduce CAIRN, a topology-aware 3D-LLM for multi-room 3D scene understanding. CAIRN aligns transformer attention with scene hierarchy, giving the model explicit awareness of object-level relations and room-level connecti

infographic.key_insight: CAIRN extends 3D scene understanding from single rooms to realistic multi-room homes by making the model aware of scene topology, so it can reason over both object-level and room-level relationships. In simple terms, it helps a 3D multimodal model understand how spaces connect, not just what objects are present.
infographic.problem_solved: Most existing 3D-LLMs are limited to simplified single-room scenes and struggle with household environments made of multiple connected rooms, diverse objects, and hierarchical spatial relationships.
method: Introduces a topology-aware 3D-LLM designed for cross-room scene understanding in multi-room environments.
Aligns transformer attention with the scene hierarchy to explicitly model object-level relations and room-level connectivity.
Uses structured spatial reasoning so the model can answer questions grounded in realistic household layouts rather than isolated rooms.
infographic.impact: This work pushes 3D multimodal AI closer to real-world deployment in homes, robotics, and embodied assistants, where understanding connected spaces is essential. For practitioners, it offers a blueprint for adding topology and hierarchy to improve spatial reasoning beyond single-room benchmarks.

title: Vision as Unified Multimodal Generation
authors: Xiaoyang Han, Jianhua Li, Kewang Deng, Zukai Chen, Xuanke Shi
abstract: We formulate computer vision as unified multimodal generation, where heterogeneous visual tasks are expressed in the native text and image generation spaces of a unified multimodal model, without task-specific architectures. Under this formulation, SenseNova-Vision uses natural-language instructions and optional visual prompts to specify tasks, target regions or views, and decoding conventions, and generates responses as text for symbolic outputs, images for dense spatial predictions, or mixed t

infographic.key_insight: This paper reframes computer vision as a unified multimodal generation problem, where different vision tasks can be handled by the same model through text and image generation. Instead of building task-specific heads or architectures, one model can output text, images, or mixed outputs depending on the instruction.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the fragmentation of computer vision systems, where each task often needs its own specialized architecture, decoding strategy, or output format. The paper aims to make vision models more flexible, general, and easier to extend across heterogeneous tasks.
method: Uses a unified multimodal model, SenseNova-Vision, to express vision tasks in native text and image generation spaces.
Accepts natural-language instructions plus optional visual prompts to specify the task, target region, view, or decoding convention.
Generates different output types depending on the task: text for symbolic results, images for dense spatial predictions, or mixed outputs when needed.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this approach reduces the need for task-specific engineering and makes it easier to deploy one model across many vision applications. It also opens the door to more scalable, instruction-driven vision systems that can adapt to new tasks with less redesign.

title: Lift3D-VLA: Lifting VLA Models to 3D Geometry and Dynamics-Aware Manipulation
authors: Jiaming Liu, Qingpo Wuwu, Nuowei Han, Hao Chen, Zhuoyang Liu
abstract: Recently, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong generalization across diverse tasks. However, effective robotic manipulation in physical environments fundamentally requires geometric understanding and spatial reasoning. While some VLA approaches attempt to incorporate 3D information, they are constrained by limited data availability and geometric information loss in current 3D encoding pipelines, and fail to jointly capture 3D geometry and temporally structured actions in

infographic.key_insight: Lift3D-VLA aims to make VLA robots better at real-world manipulation by explicitly lifting 2D perception into 3D geometry and dynamics-aware action understanding. The core idea is that strong language-vision skills are not enough unless the model can reason about spatial structure and motion in the physical world.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between general-purpose VLA models and the geometric, temporal demands of robotic manipulation. Existing 3D-aware VLA methods are limited by scarce training data, information loss in 3D encoding pipelines, and weak coupling between 3D scene understanding and action dynamics.
method: Integrates 3D geometric cues into VLA modeling to preserve spatial structure needed for manipulation.
Learns dynamics-aware representations so the model can connect what it sees in 3D with how actions unfold over time.
Targets joint reasoning over geometry and temporally structured actions to improve manipulation in physical environments.
infographic.impact: This work is important for robotics and embodied AI because it points toward VLA systems that are more reliable in real-world settings, not just benchmark tasks. For practitioners, it suggests a path to better manipulation policies by combining spatial reasoning with action dynamics.

title: MonoIR-RS: Infrared Remote Sensing Vision-Language Learning with CLIP and VLM Adaptation
authors: Jiaju Han, Ma Yaqi, Yahui Chai, Xuemeng Sun, Xin Li
abstract: Infrared remote-sensing imagery captures intensity structure, object-background contrast, and illumination-invariant cues often invisible in RGB imagery. Yet, most remote-sensing vision-language resources and models focus on visible-band semantics, leaving infrared vision-language understanding underexplored. We introduce MonoIR-RS, a large-scale infrared remote-sensing vision-language dataset and benchmark that couples IR-aware data construction with CLIP-style contrastive adaptation and VLM in

infographic.key_insight: MonoIR-RS shows that infrared remote-sensing data can support effective vision-language learning when datasets and models are adapted beyond visible-band assumptions. The paper creates a new benchmark and uses CLIP-style and VLM adaptation to improve infrared understanding.
infographic.problem_solved: Most existing remote-sensing vision-language datasets and models are built around RGB/visible imagery, leaving infrared remote-sensing semantics underexplored. This paper addresses the lack of large-scale IR vision-language resources and methods tailored to IR-specific cues like object-background contrast and illumination invariance.
method: Builds MonoIR-RS, a large-scale infrared remote-sensing vision-language dataset and benchmark.
Constructs IR-aware training data to better reflect infrared scene characteristics and semantics.
Adapts CLIP-style contrastive learning and VLM components for infrared image-language alignment.
infographic.impact: This work gives practitioners a new benchmark for evaluating infrared vision-language systems and a stronger foundation for building models that work in non-visible sensing conditions. It is especially useful for remote sensing, surveillance, and multimodal AI applications where RGB-only methods are insufficient.

title: From RGB Generation to Dense Field Readout: Pixel-Space Dense Prediction with Text-to-Image Models
authors: Zanyi Wang, Xin Lin, Haodong Li, Dengyang Jiang, Yijiang Li
abstract: Large-scale text-to-image models are attractive backbones for dense prediction because RGB generation pretraining learns rich semantic, structural, and geometric priors. Existing generative and editing approaches reuse these priors by casting dense prediction as target generation: annotations such as depth, normals, alpha mattes, masks, and heatmaps are encoded into an RGB-trained VAE latent space and decoded back as image-like targets. We argue this inherits more of the generative output interf

infographic.key_insight: This paper argues that text-to-image models can do more than generate pictures: their learned RGB priors can be repurposed as strong backbones for dense prediction tasks. The key shift is from "generating targets" in image space to directly reading out dense fields in pixel space.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between using generative text-to-image models for dense prediction and the true goal of predicting structured outputs like depth, normals, masks, alpha mattes, and heatmaps. Existing methods often force these outputs through an image-like latent representation, which can limit accuracy and flexibility.
method: Reinterpret text-to-image models as pixel-space dense prediction backbones instead of pure RGB generators.
Replace target-generation-style decoding with a dense field readout mechanism that predicts structured outputs directly from learned visual features.
Leverage the semantic, geometric, and structural priors already embedded in large-scale RGB pretraining to improve dense prediction performance.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new way to reuse foundation generative models for vision tasks beyond synthesis. It could reduce the need for task-specific architectures and improve dense prediction quality by exploiting pretrained priors more directly.

title: DepthWeave-KV: Token-Adaptive Cross-Layer Residual Factorization for Long-Context KV Cache Compression
authors: Anna Cordoba, Adam Puente Tercero, Nerea Angulo Hijo, Mar Linares Tercero, Julia Barrientos
abstract: Long-context language model inference is increasingly limited by the memory bandwidth and capacity required to store key-value caches, yet existing compression methods often apply uniform budgets across layers or tokens and degrade retrieval when lexical cues and semantic states require different preservation. We introduce DepthWeave-KV, a token-adaptive cache compression method that factorizes key and value states across neighboring transformer layers using shared low-rank channel bases while r

infographic.key_insight: DepthWeave-KV makes long-context inference cheaper by compressing KV caches in a token-aware way, instead of forcing every token and layer to share the same memory budget. It preserves important retrieval signals by factorizing neighboring transformer-layer states with shared low-rank bases while adapting what gets kept per token.
infographic.problem_solved: Long-context language models are bottlenecked by the large memory and bandwidth cost of storing key-value (KV) caches. Existing compression methods often use uniform budgets across layers or tokens, which can hurt performance when different tokens need different amounts of lexical or semantic detail preserved.
method: Factorizes key and value states across neighboring transformer layers using shared low-rank channel bases.
Applies token-adaptive compression so important tokens can retain more information than less critical ones.
Targets KV cache reduction while trying to preserve retrieval quality for both lexical cues and semantic state.
infographic.impact: This approach can help practitioners run longer-context models more efficiently on limited hardware by reducing KV-cache memory pressure. It is especially relevant for production inference settings where latency, throughput, and context length all matter.

title: ProxyPose: 6-DoF Pose Tracking via Video-to-Video Translation
authors: Ruihang Zhang, Felix Taubner, Pooja Ravi, Kiriakos N. Kutulakos, David B. Lindell
abstract: Tracking the six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) pose of objects and surfaces from monocular video is a long-standing problem in computer vision. To tackle this problem, existing methods require inputs beyond the video itself-such as 3D models, depth maps, object masks, or task-specific learned features-and they struggle with textureless, transparent, reflective, or deformable surfaces. Here, we introduce ProxyPose, which recasts 6-DoF pose tracking as video-to-video translation. Given only a video an

infographic.key_insight: ProxyPose reframes 6-DoF pose tracking as a video-to-video translation problem, letting the model infer pose directly from monocular video without needing extra inputs like depth, masks, or 3D models. This makes pose tracking more practical for challenging real-world surfaces such as transparent, reflective, textureless, or deformable objects.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of tracking the full 6-DoF pose of objects and surfaces from a single video stream, especially when traditional methods fail without auxiliary 3D information or hand-crafted priors.
method: Transforms the pose-tracking task into video-to-video translation rather than explicit geometry estimation.
Uses only monocular video as input, avoiding reliance on depth maps, object masks, or 3D models.
Learns to map video observations to pose-relevant outputs in a way that is robust to visually difficult surface types.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ProxyPose suggests a simpler and more flexible path to pose tracking in settings where collecting 3D annotations or sensor data is expensive. It could improve deployment in robotics, AR/VR, and vision systems operating on hard-to-model objects.

title: Hierarchical Acoustic-Semantic Modeling: Modality Separation and Semantic Coherence for Full-Duplex SLMs
authors: Zhenyu Liu, Yunxin Li, Xuanyu Zhang, Qixun Teng, Shenyuan Jiang
abstract: Developing seamless, high-performance, native intelligent full-duplex Spoken Language Models (SLMs) remains a critical challenge and long-standing goal for the speech and NLP community. Despite notable progress, recent endeavors are fundamentally constrained by severe modality interference, which causes substantial knowledge degradation and compromises semantic integrity -- ultimately making full-duplex SLMs feel unnatural and unintelligent. In this paper, through an exhaustive fine-grained anal

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that full-duplex spoken language models fail mainly because speech and semantic processing interfere with each other. By separating acoustic and semantic pathways and enforcing semantic coherence, the model can sound more natural and stay more intelligible.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses modality interference in full-duplex SLMs, where overlapping acoustic and language signals degrade knowledge retention, semantic consistency, and overall conversational quality.
method: Hierarchical acoustic-semantic modeling to disentangle low-level speech cues from high-level meaning.
Modality separation mechanisms to reduce interference between acoustic and semantic representations.
Semantic coherence objectives to preserve natural, context-consistent responses in full-duplex interaction.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer path to building speech models that respond smoothly in real time without losing semantic quality. It is especially relevant for developing more natural voice assistants, conversational agents, and spoken dialogue systems.

title: Bridging Physical Reasoning and Task Generalization via Visual Action Outcome Reasoning Alignment
authors: Han-Jun Ko, Jr-Jen Chen, Haobo Yuan, Hsin-Ying Lee, Tiancheng Shen
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to generalize in interactive physical reasoning, particularly under unseen tasks and environments. Two key failure modes are prominent: hallucinated chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning that contradicts physical reality, and misalignment between the model's reasoning and actions. We present VAORA (Visual Action Outcome Reasoning Alignment), a novel reward design that directly addresses both issues. VAORA introduces two complementary rewards: Visual Alignment Re

infographic.key_insight: VAORA aligns a vision-language model’s reasoning with what actually happens after an action, helping it avoid physically impossible explanations and generalize better to new interactive tasks. In simple terms: it teaches the model to think and act in ways that stay grounded in real outcomes.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper tackles poor generalization in interactive physical reasoning, especially when models face unseen tasks or environments. It addresses two failure modes: hallucinated chain-of-thought reasoning that conflicts with physical reality, and a mismatch between the model’s reasoning process and the actions it chooses.
method: Introduces VAORA (Visual Action Outcome Reasoning Alignment), a reward design for interactive physical reasoning.
Uses two complementary rewards to align predicted reasoning with visual outcomes and action effects.
Optimizes the model so its chain-of-thought stays consistent with observed physical changes after actions are taken.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to improve VLM reliability in embodied and interactive settings where grounded reasoning matters. It can lead to agents that are more robust, more interpretable, and better able to transfer to new tasks and environments.

title: Graph Convolutional Attention: A Spectral Perspective on Graph Denoising and Diffusion
authors: Shervin Khalafi, Igor Krawczuk, Sergio Rozada, Charilaos Kanatsoulis, Antonio G Marques
abstract: Denoising graphs is a fundamental problem in graph learning and the core operation of graph diffusion models. Attention-based architectures like graph transformers have recently shown promise in denoising graphs. However, our principled understanding of attention-based graph denoising remains limited, making it unclear whether standard attention is the right mechanism for this task. Here we show that, under a denoising objective, linear attention is suboptimal and can only learn an average spect

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that, for graph denoising, standard linear attention is not well-suited and tends to learn only an averaged spectral response. A spectral viewpoint reveals when attention can truly denoise graphs and why more expressive mechanisms are needed for graph diffusion tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of denoising noisy graphs, which is a core step in graph learning and graph diffusion models. The work aims to clarify whether attention-based graph transformers are actually the right tool for reconstructing clean graph structure.
method: Analyze graph attention through a spectral lens to understand how it behaves as a denoiser.
Compare standard linear attention against denoising objectives to identify its limitations in learning graph frequency responses.
Derive principled insights for designing attention mechanisms that better match the needs of graph denoising and diffusion.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper helps explain why some graph transformer designs fail on denoising tasks and how to improve them. It provides a more principled foundation for building graph diffusion models and attention layers that are better aligned with signal processing on graphs.

title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini, Bruno Sanchez, Dominique Fouchez, Benjamin Racine, Maya Guy
abstract: Time-domain surveys generate many transient candidates, making Real-Bogus classification a critical step in automated discovery pipelines. Reliable labels are costly, while community labels can be noisy and survey-dependent. We aim to develop a Real-Bogus classification framework that can be trained without human-labeled data using injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data, remains robust under strong class contamination, and provides calibrated uncertainty quantification. We combine s

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows that Real-Bogus classifiers for time-domain astronomy can be trained without human labels by using injected transients and mostly bogus survey data. The result is an interpretable deep learning system that stays robust even when training data are heavily contaminated and can also report calibrated uncertainty.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of building reliable Real-Bogus classification models when expert labels are expensive, scarce, noisy, and survey-dependent, especially in the presence of strong class contamination.
method: Train a deep learning classifier without human-labeled examples by combining injected transients with bogus-dominated survey data.
Design the framework to remain robust under high levels of contamination in the training set.
Add uncertainty quantification so the model can indicate how confident it is in each prediction and support more trustworthy decisions.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical blueprint for label-free or weakly supervised classification in noisy real-world settings. It is especially valuable for scientific pipelines where interpretability, robustness, and calibrated confidence matter as much as accuracy.

title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
authors: Haozhe Wang, Weijia Feng, Jinpeng Yu, Che Liu, Ping Nie
abstract: Visual generators excel at rendering, but they confidently fabricate what they do not know. User requests are unbounded, evolving, and deeply long-tailed: new characters, trending entities, post-cutoff events, and more. This world-knowledge bottleneck is structural: generators are trained on fixed corpora, but the visual world is open-ended. We construct SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench, with 20,839 prompts spanning twelve failure categories and twenty-two domains, paired with a pre-executed mu

infographic.key_insight: Visual generators fail not because they cannot render images, but because their knowledge is fixed while the real world keeps changing. This paper proposes a search-based way to extend what visual agents can know and generate beyond their training cutoff.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the world-knowledge bottleneck in agentic visual generation: models are asked to create images involving new characters, trending entities, post-cutoff events, and other long-tailed concepts that were never in their training data, causing confident hallucinations.
method: Builds SearchGen-20K, a dataset of 20,839 prompts covering 12 failure categories and 22 domains.
Creates SearchGen-Bench to evaluate how well visual generation agents handle open-ended, knowledge-heavy requests.
Pairs prompts with pre-executed search information, enabling agents to retrieve missing world knowledge before generating visuals.
infographic.impact: For practitioners, this suggests a practical path to make image generation systems more reliable on real-world, evolving content. It is especially useful for building agents that must stay current without retraining on every new event or entity.

title: Guiding generative models to uncover diverse and novel crystals via reinforcement learning
authors: Hyunsoo Park, Aron Walsh
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 06 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01262-4

Park and Walsh introduce a reinforcement learning framework that could accelerate the discovery of new, thermodynamically stable and diverse crystalline materials with desired properties.

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows how reinforcement learning can steer generative models to produce crystalline materials that are not only novel and diverse, but also thermodynamically stable and property-targeted. In simple terms, it adds a feedback loop so the model learns to generate better crystals instead of just more crystals.
infographic.problem_solved: Traditional generative models for crystal design often struggle to balance novelty, diversity, and physical stability while still meeting desired material properties. This work addresses the challenge of guiding generation toward realistic, useful crystal candidates that are more likely to be experimentally viable.
method: Use a reinforcement learning framework to guide a generative model during crystal generation.
Define rewards that encourage thermodynamic stability, diversity, novelty, and target property fulfillment.
Iteratively update the model using feedback so it learns to sample better crystal structures over time.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates how RL can be used as a control mechanism for scientific generative models, especially when outputs must satisfy hard physical constraints. It is a useful template for designing reward-guided generation in materials discovery and other domains where validity and novelty must be balanced.

title: InFlux++: Real and Synthetic Data for Estimating Dynamic Camera Intrinsics
authors: Erich Liang, Caleb Kha-Uong, Chinmaya Saran, Sreemanti Dey, David W. Liu
abstract: Camera intrinsics are vital for recovering 3D structure from 2D video. However, most 3D algorithms assume fixed intrinsics throughout a video, an assumption that often fails for real-world in-the-wild videos. Consequently, estimating per-frame intrinsics from RGB images is critical for making 3D methods robust to videos with dynamic intrinsics. InFlux previously advanced this research direction by establishing the first real-world benchmark with per-frame ground truth intrinsics for dynamic intr

infographic.key_insight: InFlux++ extends the study of dynamic camera intrinsics by combining real-world and synthetic data to better estimate frame-by-frame camera parameters from RGB video. This helps 3D vision systems handle videos where camera zoom, focus, or other intrinsics change over time.
infographic.problem_solved: Most 3D reconstruction and video understanding methods assume camera intrinsics stay fixed across a video, which is often false in real-world footage. This paper addresses the challenge of estimating per-frame intrinsics for videos with dynamic camera settings.
method: Uses both real and synthetic data to train and evaluate dynamic intrinsic estimation.
Builds on the InFlux benchmark, which provides real-world per-frame ground-truth intrinsics for dynamic videos.
Focuses on predicting camera intrinsics directly from RGB frames to support downstream 3D methods.
infographic.impact: This matters for practitioners because more accurate intrinsics estimation can make 3D reconstruction, SLAM, and video-based geometry methods robust to in-the-wild videos. It reduces failure cases caused by the common but unrealistic assumption of fixed intrinsics.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
authors: Shiyuan Feng, Huan-ang Gao, Haohan Chi, Hanlin Wu, Zhilong Zhang
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is a powerful recipe for improving language-model reasoning, but it is expensive to repeat on every new strong model because the target model must generate many rollouts during training. As models scale, post-training itself becomes a bottleneck. We study a weak-to-strong alternative: run RL on a smaller model where rollouts are cheaper, then reuse what that RL run learned to improve a stronger target model. Directly distilling the post-RL we

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows that instead of running expensive reinforcement learning directly on a large target model, you can train a smaller model with RLVR and transfer that learned improvement to the stronger model through direct on-policy distillation. This creates a practical weak-to-strong path for boosting reasoning without repeating costly rollouts at full scale.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the high cost and scaling bottleneck of post-training large language models with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, where the target model must repeatedly generate many rollouts during training.
method: Run RLVR on a smaller, cheaper "weak" model to learn improved reasoning behavior.
Use direct on-policy distillation to transfer the post-RL behavior from the weak model to a stronger target model.
Reuse the learned signal from one RL run to avoid repeating expensive RL training on every new strong model.
infographic.impact: This matters because it reduces the compute and rollout cost of post-training while still improving a larger model's reasoning. For practitioners, it offers a more scalable recipe for upgrading strong models using cheaper training runs.

title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
authors: Jacky Kwok, Shulu Li, Pranav Atreya, Yuejiang Liu, Yixing Jiang
abstract: Scaling pre-training, post-training, and test-time compute have become the central paradigms for improving the capabilities of LLMs. In this work, we identify verification, the ability to determine the correctness of a solution, as a new scaling axis. To unlock this and demonstrate its effectiveness, we introduce LLM-as-a-Verifier, a general-purpose verification framework that provides fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without requiring additional training. Unlike standard LM judges that p

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that verification is a new scaling axis for improving LLMs: instead of only making models bigger or giving them more compute, we can make them better at checking whether solutions are correct. The proposed LLM-as-a-Verifier framework gives fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without extra training.
infographic.problem_solved: LLMs often generate plausible but incorrect outputs, and existing LM judges are usually too coarse to pinpoint exactly where a solution fails. This paper addresses the need for a general-purpose way to verify correctness and provide actionable feedback during task execution.
method: Introduce LLM-as-a-Verifier, a framework that evaluates solutions at a finer granularity than standard yes/no judging.
Provide feedback that can be used during agentic workflows to identify specific mistakes or weak steps.
Enable verification without requiring additional model training, making the approach practical and broadly applicable.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a new way to improve reliability and debugging in LLM-based systems. It can make agentic models easier to trust, inspect, and iterate on, especially in workflows where correctness matters.

title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
authors: Wenhao Li, Xueying Jiang, Quanhao Qian, Deli Zhao, Shijian Lu
abstract: Real-world robot deployment rarely maintains the training-stage camera setup, where cameras often experience repositioning or remounting depending on actual scenarios. Existing view-robust Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies tolerate such camera variations only when the camera extrinsics are explicitly provided, making them fragile and hard to use especially when view robustness is critical. We argue that the policy should not be told where the camera is, but rather figure it out by itself. To

infographic.key_insight: The paper argues that robot policies should not depend on being told the camera pose at test time. Instead, the model learns to infer view changes on its own, enabling robust action prediction even when cameras are moved or remounted.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the fragility of Vision-Language-Action policies under camera repositioning and remounting. Existing view-robust methods typically need explicit camera extrinsics, which limits practicality in real-world deployment.
method: Introduces a calibration-free VLA framework that handles changing camera viewpoints without requiring provided extrinsic parameters.
Learns to infer camera/view information internally so the policy can remain robust across different placements.
Targets real-world robot settings where camera setup is unstable and may vary after deployment.
infographic.impact: This makes VLA policies easier to deploy in real robots because practitioners no longer need precise camera calibration for every setup. It improves robustness in dynamic environments where camera positions cannot be guaranteed.

title: Deform360: A Massive Multi-view Visuotactile Dataset for Deformable World Models
authors: Hongyu Li, Wanjia Fu, Xiaoyan Cong, Zekun Li, Binghao Huang
abstract: Predicting object dynamics (i.e., world modeling) is a fundamental challenge for robotic manipulation, and modeling deformable objects presents a particularly difficult case due to their high-dimensional state spaces and complex material properties. While current world models approach this through two distinct paradigms: learning the dynamics over the 2D pixel space or more explicit 3D geometric space. A systematic understanding of their relative strengths and limitations remains elusive due to

infographic.key_insight: Deform360 introduces a large-scale multi-view visuotactile dataset to better evaluate and compare deformable world models. It helps clarify when 2D pixel-based models or 3D geometry-based models work better for predicting deformable object dynamics.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a systematic benchmark for studying how well current world models handle deformable objects, which are difficult to model because they have complex, high-dimensional, and material-dependent dynamics.
method: Builds Deform360, a massive multi-view dataset combining visual and tactile observations.
Targets deformable-world prediction tasks to compare 2D pixel-space and 3D geometric-space modeling approaches.
Provides an evaluation-focused resource for analyzing strengths and limitations of different world modeling paradigms.
infographic.impact: This matters because robotic manipulation of soft and deformable objects is a major real-world challenge. Practitioners get a stronger benchmark for testing model design choices and improving prediction accuracy in physically complex environments.

title: Principled approaches for extending neural architectures to function spaces for operator learning
authors: Julius Berner, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Jean Kossaifi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01267-z

Berner et al. show how to adapt popular neural networks into discretization-agnostic neural operators that learn from continuous scientific data, enabling scientific simulations that generalize more reliably across resolutions.

infographic.key_insight: The paper shows how to turn standard neural networks into discretization-agnostic neural operators that work directly with continuous function spaces. This makes learned scientific models more reliable when applied across different grid resolutions and simulation settings.
infographic.problem_solved: Many neural architectures are tied to the resolution of the training data, which makes them brittle when scientific simulations are represented on different meshes, grids, or discretizations. The paper addresses how to extend these models so they can learn operators over continuous data rather than fixed-size arrays.
method: Reformulate popular neural network architectures as neural operators that map between functions instead of finite-dimensional vectors.
Design principled extensions that preserve the original network’s useful inductive biases while making them agnostic to discretization.
Train on continuous scientific data so the model can generalize across resolutions and sampling schemes.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical path to building models that transfer better across simulation resolutions and scientific domains. It is especially useful for physics-informed learning, surrogate modeling, and numerical science workflows where discretization mismatch is a major limitation.

title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
authors: Hanlin Wang, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Wen Wang, Qingyan Bai
abstract: We present WorldDirector, a highly controllable video world model framework designed for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration. Unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, our framework explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. By leveraging an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera movements and subsequently employing these

infographic.key_insight: WorldDirector separates motion planning from image generation, letting a model control objects and camera paths independently. This enables persistent dynamic memory and freer viewpoint changes in video world simulation.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing world models often mix physical dynamics with rendering and depend on continuous visual input to keep motion going. This makes them hard to control, weak at long-term object persistence, and limited in exploring new viewpoints.
method: Use an LLM to orchestrate semantic motion, including 3D object trajectories and camera movements.
Decouple motion control from visual synthesis so dynamics can persist without constant frame-by-frame visual conditioning.
Generate videos/world simulations from the planned motions while supporting unrestricted viewpoint exploration.
infographic.impact: This makes world models more controllable, modular, and useful for interactive simulation, robotics, and content generation. Practitioners gain a way to design scenes with persistent objects and editable camera behavior.

In this paper, we advance this field through two primary contributions. (1) We introduce \textbf{DramaSR-532K}, a large-scale benchmark comprising 532K annotated dialogue lines across more than 900 unique characters, necessitating the integra

infographic.key_insight: A reasoning-capable LLM can substantially improve speaker recognition in long TV dramas by using storyline context instead of relying only on local utterances. The paper also introduces a large-scale benchmark that makes this hard task measurable at drama scale.

title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
authors: Yunhe Li, Hao Shi, Wenhao Liu, Mengzhe Ruan, Hanxu Hou
abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) has emerged as a practical method for training large language models (LLMs) to reason, where a single model acts as both the teacher and the student with different levels of information access. However, recent studies have found that the teacher's dense token-level supervision, conditioned on privileged information, can lead to overfitting to in-domain patterns, suppress exploration, and hurt cross-domain generalization, while also introducing a more fundamenta

infographic.key_insight: DemoPSD makes policy self-distillation more robust by reducing the harmful effects of overconfident teacher supervision. It uses disagreement between model signals to modulate when and how strongly the student should imitate the teacher.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses a core weakness of on-policy self-distillation for LLM reasoning: dense token-level teacher supervision can overfit to in-domain patterns, suppress exploration, and degrade cross-domain generalization.
method: Measures disagreement between teacher and student signals to estimate when supervision is reliable.
Modulates self-distillation strength based on that disagreement, rather than applying uniform dense imitation.
Preserves exploration by avoiding overly restrictive teacher guidance during uncertain or out-of-domain cases.
infographic.impact: This matters because it offers a practical way to train reasoning models that generalize better beyond their training distribution. For practitioners, it can improve robustness while keeping the simplicity of self-distillation.

title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
authors: Wentao Zhang, Liliana Hotsko, Woojeong Kim, Pengyu Nie, Stuart Shieber
abstract: Many everyday programming tasks resist clean rule-based implementation, such as alerting on important log lines, repairing malformed JSON, or ranking search results by intent, and are increasingly outsourced to large language model APIs at the cost of locality, reproducibility, and price. We propose fuzzy-function programming: compiling such a function from a natural-language specification into a compact, locally-executable neural artifact. We instantiate this paradigm with Program-as-Weights (P

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces "fuzzy-function programming": a way to compile natural-language behavior specifications into compact neural artifacts that run locally like software, but behave flexibly like LLMs. Its core idea is to replace many API-dependent, prompt-based tasks with reusable, reproducible program-as-weights models.
infographic.problem_solved: Many practical tasks—such as log filtering, JSON repair, and intent-based ranking—are hard to encode with rigid rules, yet relying on external LLM APIs can be expensive, non-local, and hard to reproduce.
method: Translate a natural-language specification of a task into a compact neural function.
Represent the function as weights rather than explicit source code, enabling local execution.
Target tasks that need fuzzy, approximate behavior where strict rule-based logic is brittle.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a middle ground between brittle handcrafted rules and costly API calls. It can improve latency, privacy, reproducibility, and deployment control for everyday language-heavy software tasks.
