title: HDR Video Generation via Latent Alignment with Logarithmic Encoding
authors: Naomi Ken Korem, Mohamed Oumoumad, Harel Cain, Matan Ben Yosef, Urska Jelercic
abstract: High dynamic range (HDR) imagery offers a rich and faithful representation of scene radiance, but remains challenging for generative models due to its mismatch with the bounded, perceptually compressed data on which these models are trained. A natural solution is to learn new representations for HDR, which introduces additional complexity and data requirements. In this work, we show that HDR generation can be achieved in a much simpler way by leveraging the strong visual priors already captured

infographic.key_insight: A simple logarithmic radiance encoding plus lightweight latent alignment lets existing generative models produce faithful HDR video without re-training large HDR-specific representations — leveraging pre-trained visual priors instead of learning HDR from scratch.

method: Apply a logarithmic encoding to HDR radiance so its dynamic range matches the statistics the pretrained generator expects.
Learn a compact latent alignment/mapping between encoded HDR frames and the generator's latent space (adapter network or alignment objective) rather than re-training full HDR representations.
Enforce temporal consistency in the latent domain for coherent HDR video output (temporal losses or latent smoothing) and decode back to HDR for evaluation and tone-mapped visualization.

title: SyncFix: Fixing 3D Reconstructions via Multi-View Synchronization
authors: Deming Li, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad
abstract: We present SyncFix, a framework that enforces cross-view consistency during the diffusion-based refinement of reconstructed scenes. SyncFix formulates refinement as a joint latent bridge matching problem, synchronizing distorted and clean representations across multiple views to fix the semantic and geometric inconsistencies. method: Formulate refinement as a joint latent bridge matching problem that couples distorted and clean representations across views.
Learn a joint conditional diffusion denoising process over multiple views so consistency is enforced throughout the entire denoising trajectory.
Train using only image pairs (data‑efficient) while applying the learned multi‑view synchronization to improve reconstructed scenes.

title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces
authors: Adam Stein, Davis Brown, Hamed Hassani, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong
abstract: To identify safety violations, auditors often search over large sets of agent traces. This search is difficult because failures are often rare, complex, and sometimes even adversarially hidden and only detectable when multiple traces are analyzed together. These challenges arise in diverse settings such as misuse campaigns, covert sabotage, reward hacking, and prompt injection. Existing approaches struggle here for several reasons. Per-trace judges miss failures that only become visible across t

infographic.key_insight: Failures that are rare, complex, or adversarially hidden often only become visible when multiple agent traces are analyzed together; by scoring and searching over sets of traces (not just individual ones), auditors can reliably surface these cross-trace safety violations.
infographic.problem_solved: Detecting safety violations in large collections of agent traces where failures are sparse, compositional, or intentionally concealed — situations where per-trace judges miss problems that only emerge across multiple executions.
method: Formulate cross-trace detection: evaluate candidate sets of traces with an aggregated failure score instead of per-trace labels.
Scalable search: use sampling, pruning, and targeted search heuristics to find small groups of traces that maximize the failure score across a huge trace corpus.
Robust validation: prioritize findings that are statistically or semantically robust to rare and adversarial patterns, and provide human-in-the-loop verification for high-risk cases.
infographic.impact: Enables auditors and ML teams to find hard-to-detect, multi-trace safety failures that would otherwise slip past per-trace checks, improving model auditing, risk assessment, and mitigation for deployed agents.

authors: WonJin Yoon, Kangyu Zhu, Ian Bulovic, Autumn Sehy, Yanjun Gao
abstract: With the recent progress of Large Language Models (LLMs), there is a growing interest in applying these models to solve complex and challenging problems. Modern LLMs, capable of processing long contexts and generating verbalized explanations, offer significant potential in addressing real-world applications. However, a critical hurdle in deploying LLMs for practical decision-making is their inability to provide reliable, quantitative probabilities. While task-specific fine-tuning of LLMs using t

infographic.key_insight: Fine-tuning large language models with a dual-head architecture yields jointly calibrated probability estimates and fluent verbalized explanations, enabling reliable, explainable decisions from a single model.
infographic.problem_solved: LLMs can generate natural explanations but lack reliable, quantitative probabilities for decision-making; the paper addresses how to produce both well-calibrated probabilities and coherent explanations from one fine-tuned model.
method: Dual-head fine-tuning: one head outputs a probabilistic classification distribution, the other generates a verbalized explanation.
Joint training objective that combines classification loss (with calibration-aware terms) and generative/explanation loss, aligning probability mass with explanation content.

Evaluation and calibration techniques (e.g., reliability/expected calibration error monitoring and dataset-specific explanation supervision) to improve and validate both uncertainty and explanation fidelity.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to deploy LLMs as decision-support tools that report trustworthy uncertainty and human-readable rationales, improving transparency and risk-aware automation.

title: LMMs Meet Object-Centric Vision: Understanding, Segmentation, Editing and Generation
authors: Yuqian Yuan, Wenqiao Zhang, Juekai Lin, Yu Zhong, Mingjian Gao
abstract: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) have achieved remarkable progress in general-purpose vision--language understanding, yet they remain limited in tasks requiring precise object-level grounding, fine-grained spatial reasoning, and controllable visual manipulation. In particular, existing systems often struggle to identify the correct instance, preserve object identity across interactions, and localize or modify designated regions with high precision. Object-centric vision provides a principled frame

infographic.key_insight: Integrating object-centric representations into Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) enables precise instance-level grounding, consistent object identity across interactions, and controllable region-level editing and generation in visual scenes.
infographic.problem_solved: LMMs often fail at fine-grained, object-level tasks: they misidentify instances, lose object identity across interactions, and cannot localize or modify designated regions with high precision. This work addresses those limits by combining object-centric vision with multimodal reasoning.
method: Augment LMM architecture with an object-centric module (e.g., slot/instance representations) that extracts explicit object-level tokens or masks from images.

Jointly train multimodal objectives spanning instance segmentation, referring-expression grounding, editing and conditional generation to align object tokens with language and visual manipulation operators.
Condition text-to-image and editing operations on object-level representations to enable precise localization, identity-preserving interactions, and controllable generation.
infographic.impact: Makes multimodal systems practical for tasks requiring precise object reasoning — e.g., interactive image editing, fine-grained VQA, robotics perception, and AR — by improving accuracy, controllability, and identity preservation at the object level.

title: Large Language Models Generate Harmful Content Using a Distinct, Unified Mechanism
authors: Hadas Orgad, Boyi Wei, Kaden Zheng, Martin Wattenberg, Peter Henderson
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) undergo alignment training to avoid harmful behaviors, yet the resulting safeguards remain brittle: jailbreaks routinely bypass them, and fine-tuning on narrow domains can induce ``emergent misalignment'' that generalizes broadly. Whether this brittleness reflects a fundamental lack of coherent internal organization for harmfulness remains unclear. Here we use targeted weight pruning as a causal intervention to probe the internal organization of harmfulness in LLMs.

infographic.key_insight: Harmful outputs in large language models arise from a coherent, localized mechanism in the model's weights; targeted weight pruning can causally reveal and disrupt that mechanism, showing harmfulness is structured rather than diffusely distributed.
infographic.problem_solved: Explains why alignment is brittle (jailbreaks, emergent misalignment) by probing the internal organization of harmfulness and demonstrating a unified, manipulable substrate for harmful behavior.
method: Use targeted weight pruning as a causal intervention to remove or weaken specific subsets of model weights.
Compare harmfulness (and standard capability benchmarks) before and after pruning to assess causal impact on outputs.
Locate and characterize the 'harmfulness mechanism' via ablation effects and diagnostic analyses of pruned weight regions.
infographic.impact: Provides a principled, causal diagnostic for alignment failures that enables more surgical mitigations and robustness evaluations — informing safer model editing, fine-tuning, and audit strategies.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of a transformer with a small localized region of weights highlighted and 'pruned' to illustrate the intervention.
Before/after bar chart showing reduction in harmful-response rate alongside preserved general-task performance.
Heatmap over model layers/parameters indicating localization and strength of the identified harmfulness mechanism.
Flowchart: intervention (pruning) → diagnostic readouts (harm vs capabilities) → targeted mitigation strategies.

title: Seeing is Believing: Robust Vision-Guided Cross-Modal Prompt Learning under Label Noise
authors: Zibin Geng, Xuefeng Jiang, Jia Li, Zheng Li, Tian Wen
abstract: Prompt learning is a parameter-efficient approach for vision-language models, yet its robustness under label noise is less investigated. Visual content contains richer and more reliable semantic information, which remains more robust under label noise. However, the prompt itself is highly susceptible to label noise. Motivated by this intuition, we propose VisPrompt, a lightweight and robust vision-guided prompt learning framework for noisy-label settings. Specifically, we exploit a cross-modal a

infographic.key_insight: Use reliable visual features to guide prompt learning so the learned prompts are robust to label noise. VisPrompt fuses cross-modal signals to prevent noisy labels from corrupting text prompt optimization.
infographic.problem_solved: Prompt tuning for vision-language models is highly sensitive to noisy training labels; this paper addresses how to make prompt learning robust when labels are corrupted or unreliable.
method: Introduce a lightweight vision-guided prompt learning framework that conditions prompt updates on visual features rather than relying solely on noisy labels.
Use cross-modal guidance (e.g., attention/affinity between image features and prompt tokens) to align prompt optimization with image semantics and reduce label-noise influence.
Design parameter-efficient modules and training objectives that regularize prompts with visual context, maintaining robustness without heavy extra modeling cost.
infographic.impact: Makes prompt learning practical on real-world datasets where labels are noisy, improving reliability of vision-language systems with minimal extra parameters—beneficial for deployment and few-shot learning scenarios.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: image encoder -> visual-guidance module -> prompt tokens -> text encoder/classifier (showing cross-modal links)
Before vs. after bar chart: prompt-only tuning accuracy under increasing label noise vs. VisPrompt robustness
Attention/heatmap visualization: how visual features influence specific prompt tokens (illustrating mitigation of noisy-label effects)

title: ANTIC: Adaptive Neural Temporal In-situ Compressor
authors: Sandeep S. Cranganore, Andrei Bodnar, Gianluca Galleti, Fabian Paischer, Johannes Brandstetter
abstract: The persistent storage requirements for high-resolution, spatiotemporally evolving fields governed by large-scale and high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) have reached the petabyte-to-exabyte scale. Transient simulations modeling Navier-Stokes equations, magnetohydrodynamics, plasma physics, or binary black hole mergers generate data volumes that are prohibitive for modern high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructures. To address this bottleneck, we introduce ANTIC (Adaptive

infographic.key_insight: ANTIC uses a neural, in-situ compressor that adapts compression fidelity over time to dramatically reduce storage for high-resolution, spatiotemporal PDE simulations while preserving scientifically relevant features.
infographic.problem_solved: Massive storage and I/O bottlenecks from petabyte-to-exabyte scale transient simulations (e.g., Navier–Stokes, MHD, plasma, black-hole mergers) that make long, high-resolution runs and post-hoc analysis impractical.
method: Neural latent-space compression (e.g., autoencoder-style model) trained or tuned to represent high-dimensional PDE fields compactly.
Adaptive temporal allocation: dynamically vary compression fidelity/bitrate across time steps to focus capacity on periods of complex dynamics.
In-situ integration with HPC simulation loops and error-aware reconstruction controls to meet scientific error tolerances while minimizing I/O.
infographic.impact: Enables orders-of-magnitude reduction in storage and I/O for large-scale simulations, making long-term, high-fidelity runs and downstream ML/analysis feasible on existing HPC resources.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing simulation → in‑situ ANTIC compressor → compressed archive → reconstruction/analysis.
Temporal fidelity chart: variable bitrate over time highlighting high-complexity windows preserved at higher fidelity.

title: Toward World Models for Epidemiology
authors: Zeeshan Memon, Yiqi Su, Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas, Walid Saad, Liang Zhao
abstract: World models have emerged as a unifying paradigm for learning latent dynamics, simulating counterfactual futures, and supporting planning under uncertainty. In this paper, we argue that computational epidemiology is a natural and underdeveloped setting for world models. This is because epidemic decision-making requires reasoning about latent disease burden, imperfect and policy-dependent surveillance signals, and intervention effects are mediated by adaptive human behavior. We introduce a concep

infographic.key_insight: World models—latent generative models that simulate dynamics and counterfactuals—can unify epidemiological state inference, policy-dependent observation modeling, and behavior-mediated intervention effects, enabling better planning under uncertainty.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the gap in computational epidemiology for jointly reasoning about unobserved disease burden, imperfect and policy-dependent surveillance signals, and how interventions interact with adaptive human behavior to affect outcomes.
method: Learn a latent-state world model that encodes hidden epidemic dynamics and ties them to noisy, policy-dependent surveillance observations.
Use the learned simulator to generate counterfactual futures under different interventions and behavioral responses for planning and evaluation.
Incorporate policy-conditioned observation models and behavior modules so interventions and surveillance adaptively influence simulated signals and outcomes.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical modeling paradigm to build more realistic, testable epidemiological simulators for decision support, bridging representation learning, causal counterfactuals, and policy-aware surveillance modeling.

title: Case-Grounded Evidence Verification: A Framework for Constructing Evidence-Sensitive Supervision
authors: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Mehdi Joodaki, Mahshad Lotfinia, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn
abstract: Evidence-grounded reasoning requires more than attaching retrieved text to a prediction: a model should make decisions that depend on whether the provided evidence supports the target claim. In practice, this often fails because supervision is weak, evidence is only loosely tied to the claim, and evaluation does not test evidence dependence directly. We introduce case-grounded evidence verification, a general framework in which a model receives a local case context, external evidence, and a stru

infographic.key_insight: Introducing "case-grounded evidence verification," a framework that forces models to condition decisions on provided evidence by pairing each decision with a local case context and evidence-sensitive supervision, revealing when models ignore supporting information.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses weak supervision and evaluation gaps where models make plausible predictions without actually depending on the supplied evidence, due to evidence being loosely tied to claims and tests not probing evidence dependence.
method: Formulate verification examples as triplets: local case context + external evidence + target claim, so the model must integrate context and evidence when predicting.
Create evidence-sensitive supervision signals (e.g., labels and targeted interventions/counterfactuals) that penalize predictions invariant to changes in evidence.
Design evaluation protocols that directly measure evidence dependence by testing model behavior under controlled evidence manipulations.
infographic.impact: Enables training and evaluation that reveal and reduce models' reliance on spurious cues, improving reliability, interpretability, and robustness of systems that must ground decisions in external evidence.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: inputs (case context, evidence, claim) → model → labeled decision, highlighting the enforced dependence on evidence.

title: Envisioning the Future, One Step at a Time
authors: Stefan Andreas Baumann, Jannik Wiese, Tommaso Martorella, Mahdi M. Kalayeh, Björn Ommer
abstract: Accurately anticipating how complex, diverse scenes will evolve requires models that represent uncertainty, simulate along extended interaction chains, and efficiently explore many plausible futures. Yet most existing approaches rely on dense video or latent-space prediction, expending substantial capacity on dense appearance rather than on the underlying sparse trajectories of points in the scene. This makes large-scale exploration of future hypotheses costly and limits performance when long-ho

infographic.key_insight: Predicting future scenes is more efficient and scalable when models focus on sparse, interaction-driven point trajectories and simulate futures step-by-step, enabling broad exploration of plausible long-horizon outcomes with explicit uncertainty.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the computational and representational burden of dense video prediction by shifting to sparse trajectory-based prediction, allowing efficient, uncertainty-aware exploration of many plausible long-term futures.
method: Represent scenes as sparse sets of salient points and model their trajectories instead of predicting dense pixel appearance.
Simulate futures iteratively along interaction chains (stepwise rollouts) to capture long-range dynamics without compounding dense errors.
Incorporate uncertainty-aware sampling or probabilistic outputs to generate diverse hypothesis sets while remaining computationally efficient.
infographic.impact: Enables scalable long-horizon forecasting and richer hypothesis generation for applications like robotics, planning, and autonomous systems, improving decision-making under uncertainty while reducing compute and memory costs.

title: Tango: Taming Visual Signals for Efficient Video Large Language Models
authors: Shukang Yin, Sirui Zhao, Hanchao Wang, Baozhi Jia, Xianquan Wang
abstract: Token pruning has emerged as a mainstream approach for developing efficient Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs). This work revisits and advances the two predominant token-pruning paradigms: attention-based selection and similarity-based clustering. Our study reveals two critical limitations in existing methods: (1) conventional top-k selection strategies fail to fully account for the attention distribution, which is often spatially multi-modal and long-tailed in magnitude; and (2) direct si

infographic.key_insight: Tango introduces a hybrid token-pruning strategy that explicitly accounts for multi-modal, long-tailed attention distributions and preserves rare but important visual signals, enabling much more efficient Video LLMs without sacrificing comprehension.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing token-pruning methods (top-k attention selection and similarity-based clustering) either neglect complex attention shapes or discard low-magnitude yet semantically important tokens, causing information loss and suboptimal efficiency-accuracy trade-offs in video-language models.
method: Attention-distribution-aware selection: replace naive top-k with adaptive thresholds and multi-modal peak detection so selection follows spatially multi-modal, long-tailed attention patterns.
Signal-preserving clustering: improve similarity-based merging by weighting clusters with attention-derived importance and preserving rare/high-value tokens via residual encoding.
Hybrid scheduler (Tango): combine the above into a lightweight, runtime-aware pruning pipeline that adaptively balances token sparsity and fidelity across frames.
infographic.impact: Practitioners can deploy Video LLMs that run faster and use less compute while maintaining understanding of temporally and spatially subtle visual cues—useful for real-time video analysis, multimodal agents, and resource-constrained deployments.

title: EgoTL: Egocentric Think-Aloud Chains for Long-Horizon Tasks
authors: Lulin Liu, Dayou Li, Yiqing Liang, Sicong Jiang, Hitesh Vijay
abstract: Large foundation models have made significant advances in embodied intelligence, enabling synthesis and reasoning over egocentric input for household tasks. However, VLM-based auto-labeling is often noisy because the primary data sources lack accurate human action labels, chain-of-thought (CoT), and spatial annotations; these errors are amplified during long-horizon spatial instruction following. These issues stem from insufficient coverage of minute-long, daily household planning tasks and from

infographic.key_insight: Aligning minute‑long egocentric video with synchronized human "think‑aloud" verbal chains provides rich action labels, chain‑of‑thought reasoning, and spatial cues that substantially reduce noisy auto‑labeling and improve long‑horizon instruction following.
infographic.problem_solved: VLM‑based auto‑labeling datasets lack accurate human action labels, chain‑of‑thought (CoT) transcripts, and spatial annotations, causing amplified errors when models must plan and follow multi‑step, spatially grounded household tasks.
method: Collect egocentric recordings of minute‑scale household tasks with synchronized think‑aloud speech capturing stepwise planning and spatial references.
Automatically align transcripts to video frames, extract action tokens and spatial cues, and apply denoising/verification to produce high‑quality supervision (EgoTL chains).
Finetune multimodal/vision‑language models on these aligned think‑aloud chains to improve temporal planning, spatial grounding, and long‑horizon instruction following.
infographic.impact: EgoTL gives practitioners a scalable way to inject human reasoning and spatial grounding into embodied datasets, improving long‑horizon task performance and reducing error propagation—beneficial for robotic instruction following, dataset curation, and VLM training.

title: VisionFoundry: Teaching VLMs Visual Perception with Synthetic Images
authors: Guanyu Zhou, Yida Yin, Wenhao Chai, Shengbang Tong, Xingyu Fu
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) still struggle with visual perception tasks such as spatial understanding and viewpoint recognition. One plausible contributing factor is that natural image datasets provide limited supervision for low-level visual skills. This motivates a practical question: can targeted synthetic supervision, generated from only a task keyword such as Depth Order, address these weaknesses? To investigate this question, we introduce VisionFoundry, a task-aware synthetic data genera

infographic.key_insight: Targeted, task-aware synthetic images generated from a simple keyword (e.g., “Depth Order”) can provide the missing low‑level supervision that helps vision–language models learn visual perception skills like spatial understanding and viewpoint recognition.
infographic.problem_solved: Vision–language models underperform on low‑level visual perception (spatial relations, depth/order, viewpoint) because natural image datasets provide limited targeted supervision; VisionFoundry asks whether synthetic, task-specific supervision can fill this gap.
method: Task-aware synthetic data generation: create images conditioned on a task keyword (e.g., Depth Order) to emphasize specific perceptual cues.
Produce aligned supervision (images + targeted annotations) tailored to the perceptual skill, then incorporate these examples into VLM training or fine‑tuning.
Evaluate gains on spatial and viewpoint benchmarks to verify that synthetic supervision improves the VLM’s low‑level visual abilities.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, low‑cost mechanism for practitioners to patch specific perceptual weaknesses in VLMs without large new natural datasets; enables focused improvements in multimodal systems for tasks requiring fine visual reasoning.

title: SIM1: Physics-Aligned Simulator as Zero-Shot Data Scaler in Deformable Worlds
authors: Yunsong Zhou, Hangxu Liu, Xuekun Jiang, Xing Shen, Yuanzhen Zhou
abstract: Robotic manipulation with deformable objects represents a data-intensive regime in embodied learning, where shape, contact, and topology co-evolve in ways that far exceed the variability of rigids. Although simulation promises relief from the cost of real-world data acquisition, prevailing sim-to-real pipelines remain rooted in rigid-body abstractions, producing mismatched geometry, fragile soft dynamics, and motion primitives poorly suited for cloth interaction. We posit that simulation fails n

infographic.key_insight: A physics-aligned simulator for deformable objects can act as a zero-shot data scaler: by generating diverse, physically plausible soft-body interactions, it enables policies trained only in simulation to transfer to real-world deformable manipulation without additional real data.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the sim-to-real gap for deformable-object manipulation caused by rigid-body-centric simulators, reducing the need for costly real-world data and brittle motion primitives.
method: Design a physics-aligned simulator that models shape, contact, and topology co-evolution for soft/deformable objects (e.g., cloth, soft bodies).
Use the simulator as a zero-shot data generator: produce diverse, physically plausible rollouts and motion primitives to train policies at scale without real data.
Align and validate simulator physics with real-world priors (calibration, constrained parameterization or lightweight domain alignment) to maximize zero-shot transferability.
infographic.impact: Enables large-scale, low-cost training for deformable manipulation tasks, improving robustness of learned controllers and accelerating deployment of soft-object robotics without extensive real-data collection.

title: Scal3R: Scalable Test-Time Training for Large-Scale 3D Reconstruction
authors: Tao Xie, Peishan Yang, Yudong Jin, Yingfeng Cai, Wei Yin
abstract: This paper addresses the task of large-scale 3D scene reconstruction from long video sequences. Recent feed-forward reconstruction models have shown promising results by directly regressing 3D geometry from RGB images without explicit 3D priors or geometric constraints. However, these methods often struggle to maintain reconstruction accuracy and consistency over long sequences due to limited memory capacity and the inability to effectively capture global contextual cues. In contrast, humans can

infographic.key_insight: Scal3R applies scalable test-time training to large-scale 3D reconstruction, allowing feed-forward models to adapt on-the-fly to long video sequences so they preserve geometric accuracy and cross-sequence consistency by capturing global contextual cues.
infographic.problem_solved: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models lose accuracy and consistency on long video sequences because of limited memory and insufficient mechanisms to aggregate global context; Scal3R addresses how to scale adaptation and context aggregation at test time.
method: Run lightweight test-time training during inference so the model incrementally adapts to incoming frames rather than relying on a single static forward pass.
Maintain a memory-efficient global context representation (compressed / hierarchical aggregation) that summarizes long-range scene information without unbounded memory growth.
Use incremental / sliding-window updates and consistency regularization to stabilize reconstructions across long sequences while keeping compute and memory manageable.
infographic.impact: Enables robust, consistent large-scale 3D reconstructions from long videos — important for mapping, robotics, AR/VR and any application requiring reliable scene geometry over extended captures. Practitioners get a practical route to scale test-time adaptation without prohibitive memory or compute.

title: GaussiAnimate: Reconstruct and Rig Animatable Categories with Level of Dynamics
authors: Jiaxin Wang, Dongxin Lyu, Zeyu Cai, Zhiyang Dou, Cheng Lin
abstract: Free-form bones, that conform closely to the surface, can effectively capture non-rigid deformations, but lack a kinematic structure necessary for intuitive control. Thus, we propose a Scaffold-Skin Rigging System, termed "Skelebones", with three key steps: (1) Bones: compress temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into free-form bones, approximating non-rigid surface deformations; (2) Skeleton: extract a Mean Curvature Skeleton from canonical Gaussians and refine it temporally, ensuring a c

infographic.key_insight: Convert temporally-consistent deformable Gaussian scaffolds into free-form bones plus a refined mean-curvature skeleton to produce intuitive, controllable rigs that preserve complex non‑rigid surface deformations.
infographic.problem_solved: Automatic creation of animatable, kinematically-structured rigs from category-level deformable reconstructions — bridging the gap between expressive surface representations (deformable Gaussians) and practical, controllable skeleton-based animation.
method: Compress temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into free-form 'skelebones' that approximate non-rigid surface deformation while remaining locally coherent.
Extract a Mean Curvature Skeleton from canonical Gaussians and temporally refine it to produce a stable kinematic backbone.
Assemble a Scaffold–Skin rig by binding the surface (skin) to the skelebones and expose per-bone 'level-of-dynamics' controls for varying animation complexity and fidelity.
infographic.impact: Enables scalable, category-level automatic rigging that keeps rich non-rigid detail while providing intuitive kinematic control — useful for faster animation pipelines, data generation, and downstream learning-based motion tasks.

title: OpenVLThinkerV2: A Generalist Multimodal Reasoning Model for Multi-domain Visual Tasks
authors: Wenbo Hu, Xin Chen, Yan Gao-Tian, Yihe Deng, Nanyun Peng
abstract: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has emerged as the de facto Reinforcement Learning (RL) objective driving recent advancements in Multimodal Large Language Models. However, extending this success to open-source multimodal generalist models remains heavily constrained by two primary challenges: the extreme variance in reward topologies across diverse visual tasks, and the inherent difficulty of balancing fine-grained perception with multi-step reasoning capabilities. To address these iss

infographic.key_insight: OpenVLThinkerV2 adapts Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to open-source multimodal models, stabilizing RL-driven fine-tuning across diverse visual tasks while preserving both fine-grained perception and multi-step reasoning.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes two core obstacles for open-source multimodal generalist models: (1) extreme variance in reward topologies across heterogeneous visual tasks, and (2) the trade-off between fine-grained visual perception and longer multi-step reasoning.
method: Adapt GRPO with task-/group-normalized rewards to reduce variance and make policy updates robust across heterogeneous visual tasks.
Modular perception–reasoning architecture and task-conditioned heads to retain fine visual detail while supporting compositional, multi-step reasoning.
Multi-domain training strategy (task grouping, curriculum, and shared representation learning) plus reward shaping to align objectives across tasks.
infographic.impact: Makes RL-based fine-tuning practical for open-source multimodal generalist models, enabling a single model to reliably handle many visual tasks and reducing the engineering cost of balancing perception and reasoning.

title: ETCH-X: Robustify Expressive Body Fitting to Clothed Humans with Composable Datasets
authors: Xiaoben Li, Jingyi Wu, Zeyu Cai, Yu Siyuan, Boqian Li
abstract: Human body fitting, which aligns parametric body models such as SMPL to raw 3D point clouds of clothed humans, serves as a crucial first step for downstream tasks like animation and texturing. An effective fitting method should be both locally expressive-capturing fine details such as hands and facial features-and globally robust to handle real-world challenges, including clothing dynamics, pose variations, and noisy or partial inputs. Existing approaches typically excel in only one aspect, lack

infographic.key_insight: Combining complementary datasets in a composable training and fitting pipeline enables a single body-fitting method that is both locally expressive (hands, face, fine geometry) and globally robust (clothing, pose variation, noise, partial scans).
infographic.problem_solved: Aligning parametric body models (e.g., SMPL) to raw 3D point clouds of clothed humans while preserving fine details and remaining robust to clothing, diverse poses, sensor noise, and incomplete scans.
method: Composable dataset assembly: curate and combine specialized datasets (hands, faces, clothed scans, diverse poses, noisy/partial captures) with stratified sampling to cover complementary failure modes.

Hybrid fitting pipeline: a modular approach that couples global robust optimization/prior with local high-resolution refinements (per-part or high-frequency detail modules) to capture fine geometry while staying stable.

Cross-dataset regularization & augmentation: train with dataset-aware losses, synthetic augmentations and consistency constraints to prevent overfitting and improve generalization to real-world clothed humans.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, generalizable body-fitting tool that reduces manual cleanup and improves downstream tasks (animation, texturing, avatar creation) by delivering more accurate and reliable fits on real, clothed scans.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: composable datasets feeding a two-stage fit (global robust fit → local high-detail refinement).

title: Learning to be uncertain before learning from data
authors: Takuya Isomura
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 09 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01205-z

Neural networks may be overconfident before they see real data. By briefly training on random noise, models can learn to be uncertain, leading to better calibration, improved identification of out-of-distribution inputs and thus more reliable predictions.

infographic.key_insight: Briefly pretraining neural networks on random noise teaches them to be uncertain before seeing real data, which improves calibration and out-of-distribution detection without major architecture changes.
infographic.problem_solved: Neural networks tend to be overconfident and poorly calibrated, especially on novel or out-of-distribution inputs; this method reduces overconfidence and makes predictive uncertainty more reliable.
method: Short pretraining phase on random noise so the model learns to produce high uncertainty priors.
Follow with standard training on real data (fine-tuning) so the model retains calibrated uncertainty while learning task signals.
Evaluate improvements in calibration (reliability diagrams, expected calibration error) and OOD detection (AUROC, false-positive rate) to validate gains.
infographic.impact: A simple, low-cost way to increase model reliability: better-calibrated confidences and improved OOD detection make deployment and risk-sensitive decisions safer and more trustworthy.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Noise pretraining → Fine-tuning on real data → Calibrated predictions
Before/after reliability diagrams or calibration curves showing reduced miscalibration
Histogram or density plot of predictive confidence on in-distribution vs OOD inputs
ROC/AUROC comparison for OOD detection: baseline vs noise-pretrained model

title: Brain-inspired warm-up training with random noise for uncertainty calibration
authors: Jeonghwan Cheon, Se-Bum Paik
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 09 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01215-x

Cheon and Paik show that overconfidence in deep neural networks arises from standard initialization practices, and that brief warm-up training with random noise improves uncertainty calibration and meta-cognitive recognition of unknown inputs.

infographic.key_insight: Standard parameter initialization drives deep networks toward overconfident predictions; a brief, early warm-up phase using random noise reverses this bias and yields better-calibrated uncertainties and improved recognition of unknown inputs.
infographic.problem_solved: Deep models are often overconfident and poorly calibrated, making them unreliable for decisions and unable to recognize out-of-distribution or novel inputs. The paper addresses the root cause (initialization-induced overconfidence) and provides a simple training fix.
method: Diagnose: show that common initialization practices push networks into overconfident regions of parameter space.
Intervention: add a short warm-up training phase at the start of learning where the model trains on random noise (no labels) to reshape early representations.
Outcome: after warm-up, standard supervised training yields significantly improved probability calibration and better meta-cognitive detection of unknown/OOD inputs.
infographic.impact: A low-cost, easy-to-add procedure that improves predictive uncertainty and OOD awareness without architectural changes — increasing reliability for downstream ML applications and safer deployment of models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side reliability diagrams (calibration curves) comparing standard training vs. noise warm-up
Schematic timeline showing: initialization → short noise warm-up → regular training
Distribution plots of predicted confidences (histograms) highlighting reduced overconfidence
Simple flowchart/icon set illustrating benefits: better calibration, improved OOD detection, minimal extra compute

title: Act Wisely: Cultivating Meta-Cognitive Tool Use in Agentic Multimodal Models
authors: Shilin Yan, Jintao Tong, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Yangyang Wang
abstract: The advent of agentic multimodal models has empowered systems to actively interact with external environments. However, current agents suffer from a profound meta-cognitive deficit: they struggle to arbitrate between leveraging internal knowledge and querying external utilities. Consequently, they frequently fall prey to blind tool invocation, resorting to reflexive tool execution even when queries are resolvable from the raw visual context. This pathological behavior precipitates severe latency

infographic.key_insight: Adding a lightweight meta-cognitive decision layer lets agentic multimodal models judge when to rely on internal perception/reasoning versus invoking external tools, greatly reducing unnecessary tool calls while preserving performance.
infographic.problem_solved: Agentic multimodal systems habitually over-invoke external tools (blind tool calls) even when answers are available from raw visual/text context, causing latency, cost, and brittle behavior; this work teaches agents to arbitrate tool use.
method: Introduce a meta-cognitive selector/gate that predicts necessity of tool invocation using signals such as model confidence, context features, and tool cost.
Train the selector with cost-aware objectives and mixed supervision (examples where tools are/aren't needed), plus self-reflection/fallback strategies to recover from mistaken abstentions.
Integrate the selector into the agent loop so the model can decide, reflect, and conditionally call tools with minimal changes to existing agent architectures.
infographic.impact: Makes agentic multimodal systems faster, cheaper, and more reliable by avoiding reflexive tool usage and enabling smarter, context-aware decisions about when to query external utilities—practical for deployed interactive AI.
visual_elements: Flowchart of agent loop: Perception → Meta-cognitive selector (confidence meter) → Decide: Internal answer vs Tool call → Response, showing the gating decision point.
Before/After bar chart comparing # of tool calls, average latency, and cost for baseline vs meta-cognitive agent.
Example interaction panel: a visual query with two annotated outcomes (internal solve vs unnecessary tool call) illustrating the selector's effect.

title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
authors: Haolei Xu, Haiwen Hong, Hongxing Li, Rui Zhou, Yang Zhang
abstract: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have achieved remarkable performance on vision-language tasks. However, we identify a puzzling phenomenon termed Seeing but Not Thinking: models accurately perceive image content yet fail in subsequent reasoning, while correctly solving identical problems presented as pure text. Through systematic analysis, we first verify that cross-modal semantic sharing exists in MoE architectures, ruling out semantic alignment failure as the sole explanation. We the

infographic.key_insight: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts models can perceive image content correctly yet fail to reason about it because the MoE routing mechanism gets 'distracted' by visual signals — not merely due to cross-modal semantic misalignment.
infographic.problem_solved: Diagnoses the puzzling 'Seeing but Not Thinking' failure mode in vision‑language MoE models and identifies routing distraction as a primary contributor to correct perception but faulty downstream reasoning.
method: Systematic empirical analysis comparing model behavior on identical problems presented as image+text versus text-only to isolate the failure mode.
Investigation of cross-modal semantic sharing and per-token expert activations to rule out simple semantic alignment failure and reveal routing patterns.

Characterization of 'routing distraction' — how visual tokens bias expert selection — and proposal of routing‑aware interventions (e.g., gating/regulation and expert re‑balancing) to mitigate the issue.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a concrete explanation and diagnostics for multimodal reasoning failures in MoE architectures, guiding improved routing designs and mitigation strategies to restore robust vision-language reasoning.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side example panel: same question as text-only vs image+text with model outputs illustrating 'correct' vs 'failed' reasoning.
Heatmap of MoE expert activations over tokens showing disproportionate attention to visual tokens (routing distraction).
Sankey/flow diagram of routing paths comparing 'distracted' vs 'focused' expert selection.

title: E-3DPSM: A State Machine for Event-Based Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
authors: Mayur Deshmukh, Hiroyasu Akada, Helge Rhodin, Christian Theobalt, Vladislav Golyanik
abstract: Event cameras offer multiple advantages in monocular egocentric 3D human pose estimation from head-mounted devices, such as millisecond temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and negligible motion blur. Existing methods effectively leverage these properties, but suffer from low 3D estimation accuracy, insufficient in many applications (e.g., immersive VR/AR). This is due to the design not being fully tailored towards event streams (e.g., their asynchronous and continuous nature), leading to hi

infographic.key_insight: E-3DPSM introduces a state-machine architecture that models the asynchronous, continuous nature of event-camera streams to produce substantially more accurate egocentric 3D human poses from head-mounted devices. By explicitly handling event timing and temporal states, it closes the accuracy gap required for immersive AR/VR applications.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing monocular egocentric 3D pose methods do not fully exploit the asynchronous, high-temporal-resolution structure of event-camera data, yielding insufficient 3D accuracy and unstable tracking for real-time immersive use.
method: State-machine driven processing that organizes event streams into meaningful temporal states (e.g., motion onset, steady motion, rest) to preserve asynchronous timing and reduce information loss.
Spatiotemporal feature extraction tailored to event data and a regression module that maps state-aware features to 3D joint positions with temporal/kinematic consistency constraints.
Training and evaluation strategy combining event-specific augmentations and losses to improve robustness to occlusions, fast motion, and varying illumination common in head-mounted setups.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical path to low-latency, high-accuracy egocentric 3D pose estimation using event cameras, enabling more responsive and immersive AR/VR experiences and informing future event-based perception models in robotics and HCI.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing event-camera input → state machine (temporal states) → spatiotemporal feature extractor → 3D pose output.

title: AVGen-Bench: A Task-Driven Benchmark for Multi-Granular Evaluation of Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
authors: Ziwei Zhou, Zeyuan Lai, Rui Wang, Yifan Yang, Zhen Xing
abstract: Text-to-Audio-Video (T2AV) generation is rapidly becoming a core interface for media creation, yet its evaluation remains fragmented. Existing benchmarks largely assess audio and video in isolation or rely on coarse embedding similarity, failing to capture the fine-grained joint correctness required by realistic prompts. We introduce AVGen-Bench, a task-driven benchmark for T2AV generation featuring high-quality prompts across 11 real-world categories. To support comprehensive assessment, we pro

infographic.key_insight: AVGen-Bench introduces a task-driven, multi-granular benchmark that evaluates text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation jointly across audio, visual, and temporal dimensions—capturing fine-grained correctness and synchronization that prior, embedding-based or isolated benchmarks miss.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses fragmented T2AV evaluation by providing a standardized suite of high-quality prompts and multi-level metrics to measure joint alignment, fidelity, and synchronization for realistic prompts across 11 real-world categories.
method: Curate a diverse set of high-quality, task-driven prompts spanning 11 real-world categories to stress different T2AV capabilities.

Define a multi-granular evaluation protocol combining automated metrics (e.g., audio fidelity, visual fidelity, cross-modal alignment, temporal synchronization) with targeted human judgments and per-task correctness checks.
Provide standardized benchmarking procedures, reference sets, and score aggregation so different models can be compared consistently on joint audio–video performance.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare and improve T2AV systems using fine-grained, task-aware metrics—accelerating development of models that produce coherent, synchronized audio and video from text prompts.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt → model → audio+video outputs → multi-granular metric computation (segment, event, scene levels).

title: When Numbers Speak: Aligning Textual Numerals and Visual Instances in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models
authors: Zhengyang Sun, Yu Chen, Xin Zhou, Xiaofan Li, Xiwu Chen
abstract: Text-to-video diffusion models have enabled open-ended video synthesis, but often struggle with generating the correct number of objects specified in a prompt. We introduce NUMINA , a training-free identify-then-guide framework for improved numerical alignment. NUMINA identifies prompt-layout inconsistencies by selecting discriminative self- and cross-attention heads to derive a countable latent layout. It then refines this layout conservatively and modulates cross-attention to guide regeneratio

infographic.key_insight: A training-free, identify-then-guide framework (NUMINA) detects attention-heads that encode object counts, derives a countable latent layout, and conservatively modulates cross-attention during generation to correct numeric mismatches between prompt and video.
infographic.problem_solved: Text-to-video diffusion models often fail to generate the correct number of object instances specified in prompts; NUMINA improves numerical alignment without additional model training.
method: Identify: select discriminative self- and cross-attention heads that reveal object-localization and counting signals to extract a latent, countable layout.
Refine: conservatively post-process the extracted layout to resolve ambiguities and stabilize object locations and counts.
Guide: modulate cross-attention maps during regeneration/denoising to nudge the model toward producing the specified number of visual instances (training-free).
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable, controllable text-to-video synthesis for prompts with numeric constraints, improving downstream editing, data generation, and evaluation without costly retraining.

title: Beyond Loss Values: Robust Dynamic Pruning via Loss Trajectory Alignment
authors: Huaiyuan Qin, Muli Yang, Gabriel James Goenawan, Kai Wang, Zheng Wang
abstract: Existing dynamic data pruning methods often fail under noisy-label settings, as they typically rely on per-sample loss as the ranking criterion. This could mistakenly lead to preserving noisy samples due to their high loss values, resulting in significant performance drop. To address this, we propose AlignPrune, a noise-robust module designed to enhance the reliability of dynamic pruning under label noise. Specifically, AlignPrune introduces the Dynamic Alignment Score (DAS), which is a loss-tra

infographic.key_insight: Instead of ranking samples by their instantaneous loss, AlignPrune scores examples by how their loss evolves over time (loss-trajectory alignment), enabling dynamic pruning that distinguishes true hard examples from noisy-label outliers.
infographic.problem_solved: Dynamic data pruning methods that rely on per-sample loss tend to retain noisy-label samples (which often exhibit high loss), degrading model performance under label noise; this work makes pruning robust to such noisy labels.
method: Introduce Dynamic Alignment Score (DAS): a metric that compares a sample's loss trajectory to expected/typical trajectories, downweighting or removing samples whose trajectories indicate label noise rather than genuine difficulty.
Integrate DAS as a lightweight, plug-and-play module into existing dynamic pruning pipelines to guide sample retention/removal decisions over training steps.
Operate on trajectory information (temporal loss patterns) rather than single-step loss values to reduce false preservation of noisy examples.
infographic.impact: Practitioners can apply dynamic pruning more safely in noisy-label scenarios, improving model generalization and compression decisions without manually cleaning labels; AlignPrune is a practical plug-in for robust, efficient training.
visual_elements: Line plot comparing loss trajectories: clean example (smooth/decaying) vs noisy-label example (persistently high or erratic) with DAS illustration.
Flowchart of training loop showing standard dynamic pruning vs AlignPrune-enhanced loop (DAS computation -> prune decision).

title: From Blobs to Spokes: High-Fidelity Surface Reconstruction via Oriented Gaussians
authors: Diego Gomez, Antoine Guédon, Nissim Maruani, Bingchen Gong, Maks Ovsjanikov
abstract:
3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has revolutionized fast novel view synthesis, yet its opacity-based formulation makes surface extraction fundamentally difficult. Unlike implicit methods built on Signed Distance Fields or occupancy, 3DGS lacks a global geometric field, forcing existing approaches to resort to heuristics such as TSDF fusion of blended depth maps.
  Inspired by the Objects as Volumes framework, we derive a principled occupancy field for Gaussian Splatting and show how it can be used t

infographic.key_insight: By deriving a principled occupancy field for oriented Gaussians, the paper converts 3D Gaussian Splatting from an opacity-driven renderer into a geometry-aware representation, enabling direct, high-fidelity surface extraction.
infographic.problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting lacks a global geometric field, making accurate surface reconstruction difficult and forcing heuristic workarounds (e.g., TSDF fusion of blended depth maps).
method: Formulate an occupancy probability field for oriented Gaussians (inspired by Objects as Volumes) that aggregates per-Gaussian contributions into a global geometry field.
Provide an analytical / differentiable mapping from Gaussian parameters to occupancy so the model yields consistent volumetric values rather than only opacity splats.
Extract surfaces from the occupancy field using standard iso-surface techniques (e.g., marching cubes), producing high-fidelity meshes without heuristic depth fusion.
infographic.impact: Transforms fast, view-synthesis-focused Gaussian Splatting into a practical tool for accurate surface reconstruction, bridging the gap between real-time rendering and geometry-centric tasks (e.g., modeling, AR/VR, robotics).

title: Distilling Photon-Counting CT into Routine Chest CT through Clinically Validated Degradation Modeling
authors: Junqi Liu, Xinze Zhou, Wenxuan Li, Scott Ye, Arkadiusz Sitek
abstract: Photon-counting CT (PCCT) provides superior image quality with higher spatial resolution and lower noise compared to conventional energy-integrating CT (EICT), but its limited clinical availability restricts large-scale research and clinical deployment. To bridge this gap, we propose SUMI, a simulated degradation-to-enhancement method that learns to reverse realistic acquisition artifacts in low-quality EICT by leveraging high-quality PCCT as reference. Our central insight is to explicitly model

infographic.key_insight: SUMI learns a realistic degradation model of conventional energy-integrating CT (EICT) from high-quality photon-counting CT (PCCT) and uses it to train an enhancement network that effectively converts routine chest CT scans to PCCT-like quality. This explicit simulation-to-restoration strategy enables training on paired data that mimic real-world EICT artifacts without requiring widespread PCCT availability.
infographic.problem_solved: Limited clinical availability of PCCT prevents large-scale research and clinical use of its superior image quality; current EICT scans suffer from lower resolution and higher noise, hindering downstream AI tasks and diagnosis.
method: Train a realistic degradation model that maps PCCT images to simulated EICT-like images by explicitly modeling acquisition artifacts (noise, blur, contrast changes).
Use the simulated degraded pairs to supervise an enhancement network (distillation) that restores routine EICT scans to PCCT-like image quality.
Validate the approach clinically to ensure restored images preserve diagnostic features and improve downstream tasks.
infographic.impact: Makes PCCT-level image quality accessible from routine chest CTs, enabling broader AI model development, improved diagnostic accuracy, and retrospective enhancement of existing datasets without requiring new hardware. Practitioners can train and evaluate models on higher-fidelity images at scale.

title: Region-Graph Optimal Transport Routing for Mixture-of-Experts Whole-Slide Image Classification
authors: Xin Tian, Jiuliu Lu, Ephraim Tsalik, Bart Wanders, Colleen Knoth
abstract: Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) is the dominant framework for gigapixel whole-slide image (WSI) classification in computational pathology. However, current MIL aggregators route all instances through a shared pathway, constraining their capacity to specialise across the pathological heterogeneity inherent in each slide. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) methods offer a natural remedy by partitioning instances across specialised expert subnetworks; yet unconstrained softmax routing may yield highly imbal

infographic.key_insight: Introducing a region-graph formulation with optimal transport routing lets a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) aggregator assign spatially coherent WSI regions to specialised experts, preventing imbalanced routing and improving classification and interpretability.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard MIL and MoE aggregators route all instances through shared or unconstrained softmax pathways, causing expert collapse, imbalanced workloads, and loss of spatial/contextual structure in gigapixel whole-slide image classification.
method: Construct a region-graph over WSI patches to encode local spatial relationships and reduce noisy per-instance routing.
Use an optimal-transport-based routing layer to assign region mass to experts under capacity and balance constraints, encouraging specialised, spatially coherent expert assignments.
Train end-to-end within the MIL framework so experts learn specialised features and the routing adapts to both task loss and load regularisation.
infographic.impact: Enables scalable, balanced MoE deployment for gigapixel pathology images with improved accuracy, interpretability, and resource efficiency—making specialised expert routing practical for real-world WSI pipelines.

title: SL-FAC: A Communication-Efficient Split Learning Framework with Frequency-Aware Compression
authors: Zehang Lin, Miao Yang, Haihan Zhu, Zheng Lin, Jianhao Huang
abstract: The growing complexity of neural networks hinders the deployment of distributed machine learning on resource-constrained devices. Split learning (SL) offers a promising solution by partitioning the large model and offloading the primary training workload from edge devices to an edge server. However, the increasing number of participating devices and model complexity leads to significant communication overhead from the transmission of smashed data (e.g., activations and gradients), which constitu

infographic.key_insight: SL-FAC applies frequency-aware compression to the smashed data (activations/gradients) in split learning, reducing communication volume substantially while preserving model accuracy and training stability.
infographic.problem_solved: High communication overhead in split learning caused by transmitting large smashed activations and gradients between many edge devices and the server, which prevents scalable deployment on bandwidth- and resource-constrained devices.
method: Transform smashed data into a frequency domain (e.g., FFT/DCT) and identify/retain the most informative frequency components.
Apply adaptive compression/quantization and selective transmission of low-importance high-frequency components, with lightweight reconstruction at the server.
Integrate the compression pipeline into split learning training to jointly optimize compression rate and task accuracy (low overhead for edge devices).
infographic.impact: Enables scalable, bandwidth-efficient split learning for edge devices and multi-client setups, making it practical to train large models across constrained networks with minimal accuracy trade-offs and improved privacy surface.

title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
authors: Yuechen Jiang, Enze Zhang, Md Mohsinul Kabir, Qianqian Xie, Stavroula Golfomitsou
abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have improved image captioning for cultural heritage. However, inferring structured cultural metadata (e.g., creator, origin, period) from visual input remains underexplored. We introduce a multi-category, cross-cultural benchmark for this task and evaluate VLMs using an LLM-as-Judge framework that measures semantic alignment with reference annotations. To assess cultural reasoning, we report exact-match, partial-match, and attribute-level accurac

infographic.key_insight: Appear2Meaning introduces a cross-cultural benchmark showing that structured cultural metadata (e.g., creator, origin, period) can be evaluated from images by combining VLM predictions with an LLM-as-Judge to measure semantic alignment with expert annotations.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the underexplored task of inferring structured, multi-attribute cultural metadata from images and providing a standardized, cross-cultural evaluation framework to quantify models' cultural reasoning.
method: Curate a multi-category, cross-cultural dataset of heritage images annotated with structured metadata (creator, origin, period, attributes).
Run diverse vision-language models to produce metadata predictions and use an LLM-as-Judge to semantically align model outputs with reference annotations.
Report complementary metrics (exact-match, partial-match, attribute-level accuracy) to capture fine-grained cultural reasoning performance.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a replicable benchmark and evaluation protocol to diagnose where VLMs fail or succeed on culturally sensitive metadata tasks, guiding model improvement and responsible deployment in cultural heritage applications.

title: Personalized RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models with Human Aligned Personalization
authors: Qiyao Ma, Dechen Gao, Rui Cai, Boqi Zhao, Hanchu Zhou
abstract: Pluralistic alignment has emerged as a critical frontier in the development of Large Language Models (LLMs), with reward models (RMs) serving as a central mechanism for capturing diverse human values. While benchmarks for general response quality are prevalent, evaluating how well reward models account for individual user preferences remains an open challenge. infographic.problem_solved: Existing RM evaluation focuses on overall response quality and population-level agreement, but lacks standardized tests for whether reward models honor diverse, individual user preferences—Personalized RewardBench fills this gap.
method: Assemble diverse user personas and preference-labeled comparisons (real or simulated) that reflect pluralistic human values.

title: TC-AE: Unlocking Token Capacity for Deep Compression Autoencoders
authors: Teng Li, Ziyuan Huang, Cong Chen, Yangfu Li, Yuanhuiyi Lyu
abstract: We propose TC-AE, a ViT-based architecture for deep compression autoencoders. Existing methods commonly increase the channel number of latent representations to maintain reconstruction quality under high compression ratios. However, this strategy often leads to latent representation collapse, which degrades generative performance. Instead of relying on increasingly complex architectures or multi-stage training schemes, TC-AE addresses this challenge from the perspective of the token space, the k

infographic.key_insight: Instead of widening latent channels to preserve quality at high compression, TC-AE unlocks representational capacity by operating in the token space of a ViT-based autoencoder, preventing latent collapse and maintaining reconstruction/generative fidelity with simpler models.
infographic.problem_solved: Latent representation collapse and degraded generative/reconstruction performance that arise when existing deep-compression AEs try to maintain quality by merely increasing latent channel counts under high compression ratios.
method: Design a ViT-based encoder–decoder that treats the bottleneck as a token space rather than a high-channel tensor.
Increase and utilize token capacity (more informative tokens or richer token interactions) to encode compressed latents instead of scaling channel width.
Introduce token-space operations/constraints that preserve diversity and prevent collapse, enabling stable training without multi-stage schemes or extreme architectural scaling.
infographic.impact: Enables more compact, stable deep-compression autoencoders that keep reconstruction and generative quality at high compression ratios while avoiding costly channel scaling or complicated training pipelines — useful for efficient storage, transmission, and generative tasks.

title: MoRight: Motion Control Done Right
authors: Shaowei Liu, Xuanchi Ren, Tianchang Shen, Huan Ling, Saurabh Gupta
abstract: Generating motion-controlled videos--where user-specified actions drive physically plausible scene dynamics under freely chosen viewpoints--demands two capabilities: (1) disentangled motion control, allowing users to separately control the object motion and adjust camera viewpoint; and (2) motion causality, ensuring that user-driven actions trigger coherent reactions from other objects rather than merely displacing pixels. Existing methods fall short on both fronts: they entangle camera and obje

infographic.key_insight: MoRight disentangles object motion from camera viewpoint and enforces motion causality, so user-specified actions trigger coherent physical reactions in the scene instead of merely displacing pixels.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing motion-controlled video models entangle camera and object motion and fail to produce causal, physically plausible interactions—users cannot independently control viewpoint and expect other objects to respond coherently to driven actions.
method: Disentangled representation: separate latent channels for object action control and camera viewpoint to enable independent manipulation.
Causal dynamics module: learns object–object interaction dynamics so user actions induce coherent reactions (not just pixel shifts).
Viewpoint-aware synthesis and multi-term training (reconstruction + causality-consistency + viewpoint-consistency) to produce physically plausible, controllable videos.
infographic.impact: Makes controllable video synthesis more reliable and useful for interactive applications (animation, simulation, robotics) by enabling independent viewpoint control and causally correct scene behavior—improving realism and downstream utility.

title: Fast Spatial Memory with Elastic Test-Time Training
authors: Ziqiao Ma, Xueyang Yu, Haoyu Zhen, Yuncong Yang, Joyce Chai
abstract: Large Chunk Test-Time Training (LaCT) has shown strong performance on long-context 3D reconstruction, but its fully plastic inference-time updates remain vulnerable to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting. As a result, LaCT is typically instantiated with a single large chunk spanning the full input sequence, falling short of the broader goal of handling arbitrarily long sequences in a single pass. We propose Elastic Test-Time Training inspired by elastic weight consolidation, that stabilizes

infographic.key_insight: Applying an elastic consolidation constraint to test-time training stabilizes inference-time updates for spatial memory, preventing catastrophic forgetting and enabling fast, chunked processing of arbitrarily long 3D sequences in a single pass.
infographic.problem_solved: LaCT's fully plastic inference updates overfit and forget when processing long inputs, forcing use of a single large chunk and preventing scalable single-pass handling of very long sequences.
method: Introduce Elastic Test-Time Training: add an elastic (EWC-style) regularizer during inference updates to anchor important weights and reduce forgetting.
Operate on smaller spatial chunks with a fast spatial memory module so the model can incrementally process long sequences while preserving previously learned information.
Use lightweight per-parameter importance estimates and a restricted optimization schedule to keep test-time updates both stable and computationally efficient.
infographic.impact: Makes test-time adaptation practical and robust for long-context 3D reconstruction and related tasks, allowing deployed models to adapt on-the-fly without catastrophic forgetting and with low latency.

title: Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning
authors: Roberto Vercellino, Jared Willard, Gustavo Campos, Weslley da Silva Pereira, Olivia Hull
abstract: The rapid growth of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced unprecedented computational demands, driving significant increases in the energy footprint of data centers. However, existing power consumption data is largely proprietary and reported at varying resolutions, creating challenges for estimating whole-facility energy use and planning infrastructure. In this work, we present a methodology that bridges this gap by linking high-resolution workload power measurements to whole-f

infographic.key_insight: High-resolution power profiles of generative AI workloads can be systematically mapped and scaled to whole-facility energy models, enabling accurate infrastructure planning without access to proprietary aggregated data.

method: Collect high-frequency power telemetry from AI compute (GPUs/accelerators) running representative generative workloads to build temporal power profiles.

title: In-Place Test-Time Training
authors: Guhao Feng, Shengjie Luo, Kai Hua, Ge Zhang, Di He
abstract: The static ``train then deploy" paradigm fundamentally limits Large Language Models (LLMs) from dynamically adapting their weights in response to continuous streams of new information inherent in real-world tasks. Test-Time Training (TTT) offers a compelling alternative by updating a subset of model parameters (fast weights) at inference time, yet its potential in the current LLM ecosystem is hindered by critical barriers including architectural incompatibility, computational inefficiency and mi

infographic.key_insight: In-Place Test-Time Training enables LLMs to adapt their weights during inference by performing lightweight, local parameter updates directly inside the deployed model, avoiding costly extra copies or offline retraining.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the limitations of the static "train-then-deploy" workflow and existing Test-Time Training approaches—namely architectural incompatibility with standard transformers, high compute/memory overhead, and misalignment between pretraining and on-the-fly adaptation needs.
method: Embed small, fast-weightable components into standard transformer blocks so parameter updates can be applied in-place (no full-model copies).
Use lightweight, local self-supervised losses at test time to drive quick updates of the fast weights with cheap update rules (low compute/memory footprint).
Train the model with an adaptation-aware objective so the network is prepared to benefit from in-place updates at inference (aligns pretraining and TTT behavior).
infographic.impact: Makes continuous, privacy-preserving personalization and robustness updates practical for deployed LLMs by enabling fast, low-cost adaptation at inference time—beneficial for on-device, low-latency, and streaming applications.

title: Claw-Eval: Toward Trustworthy Evaluation of Autonomous Agents
authors: Bowen Ye, Rang Li, Qibin Yang, Yuanxin Liu, Linli Yao
abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents executing multi-step workflows in real-world software environments. However, existing agent benchmarks suffer from three critical limitations: (1) trajectory-opaque grading that checks only final outputs, (2) underspecified safety and robustness evaluation, and (3) narrow modality coverage and interaction paradigms. We introduce Claw-Eval, an end-to-end evaluation suite addressing all three gaps. It comprises 300 human-verified

infographic.key_insight: Claw-Eval is an end-to-end benchmark that evaluates autonomous agents at the trajectory level (not just final outputs), while explicitly testing safety, robustness, and broader modality/interaction coverage using 300 human-verified scenarios.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing agent benchmarks miss errors that occur during multi-step execution, under-evaluate safety and robustness, and cover too few modalities or interaction styles—Claw-Eval fills these gaps.
method: Trajectory-aware grading: assess step-by-step agent behaviors and intermediate states rather than only terminal outputs.
Human-verified scenario suite: 300 curated cases spanning diverse tasks, modalities, and interaction paradigms to ensure realistic evaluation.
Explicit safety & robustness probes: targeted tests and metrics for failure modes, adversarial inputs, and environment perturbations.

title: PoM: A Linear-Time Replacement for Attention with the Polynomial Mixer
authors: David Picard, Nicolas Dufour, Lucas Degeorge, Arijit Ghosh, Davide Allegro
abstract: This paper introduces the Polynomial Mixer (PoM), a novel token mixing mechanism with linear complexity that serves as a drop-in replacement for self-attention. PoM aggregates input tokens into a compact representation through a learned polynomial function, from which each token retrieves contextual information. We prove that PoM satisfies the contextual mapping property, ensuring that transformers equipped with PoM remain universal sequence-to-sequence approximators. We replace standard self-at

infographic.key_insight: PoM (Polynomial Mixer) is a learned polynomial token-mixing module that compacts tokens into a small polynomial-based summary and lets each token retrieve context from that summary, achieving attention-like contextualization in linear time. It also satisfies a provable contextual mapping property, preserving the transformer's universality as a sequence-to-sequence approximator.
infographic.problem_solved: Replaces quadratic-cost self-attention with a linear-time token-mixing mechanism that retains expressive power while lowering compute and memory for long sequences.
method: Learn a polynomial function that aggregates input tokens into a compact representation (polynomial summary) rather than computing pairwise attention.
Provide a retrieval operation where each token extracts contextual information from the learned polynomial summary to update its representation.
Design PoM as a drop-in module for transformer layers, yielding O(N) complexity instead of O(N^2) for sequence length N while proving the contextual mapping (universality) property.
infographic.impact: Enables transformers to scale to much longer sequences with substantially reduced compute and memory overhead while preserving theoretical expressivity, making it practical for resource-constrained and large-context applications.

abstract: World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising direction for robot policy learning, as they can leverage powerful video backbones to model the future states. However, existing approaches often rely on separate action modules, or use action representations that are not pixel-grounded, making it difficult to fully exploit the pretrained knowledge of video models and limiting transfer across viewpoints and environments. In this work, we present Action Images, a unified world action model th

method: Introduce pixel-grounded action representations that are injected into a video backbone to generate future frames from multiple viewpoints.

title: Topological Characterization of Churn Flow and Unsupervised Correction to the Wu Flow-Regime Map in Small-Diameter Vertical Pipes
authors: Brady Koenig, Sushovan Majhi, Atish Mitra, Abigail Stein, Burt Todd
abstract: Churn flow-the chaotic, oscillatory regime in vertical two-phase flow-has lacked a quantitative mathematical definition for over $40$ years. We introduce the first topology-based characterization using Euler Characteristic Surfaces (ECS). infographic.key_insight: The paper provides the first quantitative, topology-based definition of churn flow by using Euler Characteristic Surfaces (ECS) and introduces an unsupervised Multiple Kernel Learning (MKL) method that fuses ECS-derived kernels to discover and correct flow regimes (including updates to the Wu flow‑regime map).
infographic.problem_solved: Churn flow—an oscillatory, chaotic vertical two‑phase regime—has lacked a precise mathematical characterization for decades; this work supplies a reproducible, data-driven definition and an automated method to discover and correct regime labels in small‑diameter vertical pipes.

Fuse kernels via unsupervised Multiple Kernel Learning to discover regimes and apply corrections to the Wu flow‑regime map.

title: Toward Consistent World Models with Multi-Token Prediction and Latent Semantic Enhancement
authors: Qimin Zhong, Hao Liao, Haiming Qin, Mingyang Zhou, Rui Mao
abstract: Whether Large Language Models (LLMs) develop coherent internal world models remains a core debate. infographic.key_insight: Training with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) introduces a gradient inductive bias that steers models toward coherent internal belief states; combining MTP with latent semantic enhancement yields more structured, semantically meaningful latent representations than conventional Next-Token Prediction (NTP).

title: Exclusive Unlearning
authors: Mutsumi Sasaki, Kouta Nakayama, Yusuke Miyao, Yohei Oseki, Masaru Isonuma
abstract: When introducing Large Language Models (LLMs) into industrial applications, such as healthcare and education, the risk of generating harmful content becomes a significant challenge. While existing machine unlearning methods can erase specific harmful knowledge and expressions, diverse harmful content makes comprehensive removal difficult. In this study, instead of individually listing targets for forgetting, we propose Exclusive Unlearning (EU), which aims for broad harm removal by extensively f

infographic.key_insight: Exclusive Unlearning (EU) enables broad removal of harmful knowledge and behaviors from LLMs without exhaustively listing every harmful instance, by training models to explicitly exclude harmful outputs while retaining useful capabilities.
