title: HaloProbe: Bayesian Detection and Mitigation of Object Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
authors: Reihaneh Zohrabi, Hosein Hasani, Akshita Gupta, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah, Anna Rohrbach
abstract: Large vision-language models can produce object hallucinations in image descriptions, highlighting the need for effective detection and mitigation strategies. Prior work commonly relies on the model's attention weights on visual tokens as a detection signal. infographic.key_insight: Coarse attention-based signals mislead hallucination detection because hidden confounders (like token position and object repetition) produce Simpson's paradox; a Bayesian probe that models these confounders and uncertainty yields reliable per-object hallucination probabilities and enables targeted mitigation.
infographic.problem_solved: Detecting and reducing object hallucinations in image captions generated by large vision-language models, overcoming unreliable attention-based heuristics.
method: Diagnose why attention-based detection fails by identifying confounders (token position, repetition) and demonstrating Simpson's paradox in coarse analyses.
Introduce HaloProbe: a Bayesian probe that estimates per-object hallucination probability while explicitly modeling confounders and predictive uncertainty.
Use the probe's probabilistic scores for mitigation (e.g., uncertainty-aware decoding or post-hoc correction/calibration) to reduce spurious object mentions.
infographic.impact: Provides a principled, uncertainty-aware tool to reliably flag and reduce object hallucinations, improving trustworthiness and safety of vision-language systems in downstream applications.

title: Generating Synthetic Doctor-Patient Conversations for Long-form Audio Summarization
authors: Yanis Labrak, David Grünert, Séverin Baroudi, Jiyun Chun, Pawel Cyrta
abstract: Long-context audio reasoning is underserved in both training data and evaluation. Existing benchmarks target short-context tasks, and the open-ended generation tasks most relevant to long-context reasoning pose well-known challenges for automatic evaluation. We propose a synthetic data generation pipeline designed to serve both as a training resource and as a controlled evaluation environment, and instantiate it for first-visit doctor-patient conversations with SOAP note generation as the task.

infographic.key_insight: A synthetic pipeline can produce realistic, long-form doctor–patient audio conversations and aligned SOAP-note targets, creating both a scalable training resource and a controlled evaluation suite for long-context audio summarization.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses scarcity of long-context audio training data and the lack of controlled benchmarks for evaluating open-ended summarization of extended clinical conversations.
method: Design templated clinical scenarios and behavioral variations to generate diverse first-visit doctor–patient dialogues.
Synthesize long-form audio and transcripts (controlled noise/turns) paired with reference SOAP notes to form train/eval splits.
Use the synthetic corpus as both a training dataset for models and a controllable evaluation environment for long-context summarization tasks.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a reproducible way to train and benchmark models on long-context audio reasoning, accelerating development of robust clinical summarization systems while preserving privacy and experimental control.

title: MMEmb-R1: Reasoning-Enhanced Multimodal Embedding with Pair-Aware Selection and Adaptive Control
authors: Yuchi Wang, Haiyang Yu, Weikang Bian, Jiefeng Long, Xiao Liang
abstract: MLLMs have been successfully applied to multimodal embedding tasks, yet their generative reasoning capabilities remain underutilized. Directly incorporating chain-of-thought reasoning into embedding learning introduces two fundamental challenges. First, structural misalignment between instance-level reasoning and pairwise contrastive supervision may lead to shortcut behavior, where the model merely learns the superficial format of reasoning. Second, reasoning is not universally beneficial for em

infographic.key_insight: MMEmb-R1 integrates generative chain-of-thought reasoning into multimodal embedding learning while preventing shortcut behavior by making reasoning use pair-aware and adaptively controlled, so reasoning helps only when it improves pairwise alignment.
infographic.problem_solved: Directly injecting reasoning into embedding training causes structural misalignment with pairwise contrastive objectives and can hurt performance because reasoning is not uniformly helpful across all sample pairs.
method: Pair-Aware Selection: selectively incorporate chain-of-thought reasoning for sample pairs where reasoning improves discriminative signals, avoiding noisy or irrelevant rationale for others.
Adaptive Control: learn a gating/weighting mechanism that modulates the influence of generated reasoning on the embedding objective on a per-pair basis.
Contrastive embedding training augmented with reasoning-enhanced representations to retain alignment with pairwise supervision while leveraging reasoning when beneficial.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to leverage large multimodal LLM reasoning capabilities without degrading contrastive embedding quality—improving robustness and retrieval/alignment performance in multimodal tasks where reasoning matters.

title: DiffHDR: Re-Exposing LDR Videos with Video Diffusion Models
authors: Zhengming Yu, Li Ma, Mingming He, Leo Isikdogan, Yuancheng Xu
abstract: Most digital videos are stored in 8-bit low dynamic range (LDR) formats, where much of the original high dynamic range (HDR) scene radiance is lost due to saturation and quantization. This loss of highlight and shadow detail precludes mapping accurate luminance to HDR displays and limits meaningful re-exposure in post-production workflows. Although techniques have been proposed to convert LDR images to HDR through dynamic range expansion, they struggle to restore realistic detail in the over- an

infographic.key_insight: DiffHDR leverages conditional video diffusion models to re-expose 8-bit LDR videos, hallucinating plausible highlight and shadow detail lost to saturation/quantization while preserving temporal consistency and enabling controllable exposure adjustments.
infographic.problem_solved: Converting ubiquitous 8-bit LDR videos into usable HDR for re-exposure and display—recovering realistic detail in clipped highlights and deep shadows and avoiding per-frame temporal artifacts that prior LDR→HDR expansion methods produce.
method: Train a conditional video diffusion model that maps LDR frames (plus optional target exposure) to HDR outputs.
Design spatio-temporal conditioning (video-aware U-Net / temporal attention) to enforce frame-to-frame consistency and reduce flicker.
Use exposure-aware conditioning and perceptual/temporal objectives to hallucinate plausible detail in saturated regions and support interactive re-exposure control.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical route to restore and re-expose archived or consumer LDR video for HDR displays and post-production workflows, improving visual quality and enabling downstream vision tasks that benefit from expanded dynamic range.

title: Early Stopping for Large Reasoning Models via Confidence Dynamics
authors: Parsa Hosseini, Sumit Nawathe, Mahdi Salmani, Meisam Razaviyayn, Soheil Feizi
abstract: Large reasoning models rely on long chain-of-thought generation to solve complex problems, but extended reasoning often incurs substantial computational cost and can even degrade performance due to overthinking. A key challenge is determining when the model should stop reasoning and produce the final answer. In this work, we study the confidence of intermediate answers during reasoning and observe two characteristic behaviors: correct reasoning trajectories often reach high-confidence answers ea

infographic.key_insight: Monitoring intermediate answer confidence during chain-of-thought reveals predictable dynamics: correct reasoning trajectories typically attain a high-confidence stable point early, enabling reliable early stopping to save compute and avoid overthinking.
infographic.problem_solved: Deciding when a large reasoning model should stop generating chains-of-thought so as to minimize inference cost and prevent accuracy degradation from overthinking.
method: Track per-step answer confidence scores (e.g., softmax probabilities or calibrated scores) throughout chain-of-thought generation.
Characterize confidence dynamics (peaks, plateaus, declines, variance) and derive simple heuristic or learned stopping rules that detect an 'early high-confidence' stable point.
Apply the stopping criterion at inference to terminate reasoning early and output the current answer; evaluate trade-offs between accuracy and compute across benchmarks.
infographic.impact: Makes long-chain-of-thought reasoning more efficient and robust—substantially reducing inference cost while often improving final accuracy by avoiding late-stage overthinking. Practical for deploying large reasoning models in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive settings.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: chain-of-thought steps with an overlaid confidence curve, highlighting the early high-confidence plateau and stop point.
Decision boundary graphic: confidence dynamics patterns (correct vs incorrect) with the early-stopping threshold illustrated.
Bar/line chart: compute cost (tokens or time) vs accuracy comparing full reasoning vs early-stopped runs.
Flowchart: simple runtime loop showing confidence monitoring, stop/continue decision, and final-answer extraction.

title: Rethinking Model Efficiency: Multi-Agent Inference with Large Models
authors: Sixun Dong, Juhua Hu, Steven Li, Wei Wen, Qi Qian
abstract: Most vision-language models (VLMs) apply a large language model (LLM) as the decoder, where the response tokens are generated sequentially through autoregression. Therefore, the number of output tokens can be the bottleneck of the end-to-end latency. However, different models may require vastly different numbers of output tokens to achieve comparable performance. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of the latency across different components of VLMs on simulated data. The experiment

infographic.key_insight: Autoregressive output length (number of response tokens) is a primary bottleneck for vision–language model latency; rethinking inference as a coordinated multi-agent process and adapting token budgets per model can unlock substantial efficiency gains.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between model capability and token-generation cost: VLM latency is often dominated by sequential LLM decoding, and different models require very different output-token counts to reach comparable performance—creating an opportunity to optimize end-to-end inference.
method: Comprehensive latency breakdown across VLM components (vision encoder, prompt processing, LLM decoding) using simulated workloads to identify where time is spent.

Introduce a multi-agent inference perspective: distribute decoding responsibilities among specialized/parallel agents and apply adaptive token budgets or early-exit strategies to reduce unnecessary autoregressive steps.
Analyze token-count vs. performance trade-offs across models to guide when to apply agent coordination, token-limiting, or model selection for deployment.
infographic.impact: Provides practical guidance for reducing inference latency and cost when deploying VLMs by focusing optimization on output-token generation and using multi-agent/adaptive decoding strategies—helpful for engineers building real-time or resource-constrained applications.
visual_elements: Stacked bar chart: latency breakdown per component (vision encoder | prompt prep | LLM decoding) to show decoding dominance
Scatter plot: number of output tokens vs. task performance for multiple VLMs, highlighting variability and diminishing returns

title: Beyond the Final Actor: Modeling the Dual Roles of Creator and Editor for Fine-Grained LLM-Generated Text Detection
authors: Yang Li, Qiang Sheng, Zhengjia Wang, Yehan Yang, Danding Wang
abstract: The misuse of large language models (LLMs) requires precise detection of synthetic text. Existing works mainly follow binary or ternary classification settings, which can only distinguish pure human/LLM text or collaborative text at best. This remains insufficient for the nuanced regulation, as the LLM-polished human text and humanized LLM text often trigger different policy consequences. In this paper, we explore fine-grained LLM-generated text detection under a rigorous four-class setting. To

infographic.key_insight: Modeling the dual roles of ‘creator’ and ‘editor’ enables a rigorous four-class detection that distinguishes pure human, pure LLM, human-created-but-LLM-edited, and LLM-created-but-human-edited text, revealing signals missed by standard binary/ternary detectors.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing detectors conflate different mixed-origin texts; the paper addresses the need for fine-grained identification of who authored vs who edited text to support nuanced regulation and policy decisions.
method: Define a rigorous four-class taxonomy (human, LLM, human→LLM edit, LLM→human edit) and curate evaluation data for these roles.
Develop a role-aware detection model that explicitly represents and disentangles creator vs editor signals to classify the four categories.
Design training objectives and evaluation metrics tailored to fine-grained detection and compare performance against binary/ternary baselines.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners with a more actionable detection tool for moderation, provenance, and compliance by differentiating LLM polishing from human rewrites. This supports targeted policy responses and improved forensic analysis of generated text.

title: TriAttention: Efficient Long Reasoning with Trigonometric KV Compression
authors: Weian Mao, Xi Lin, Wei Huang, Yuxin Xie, Tianfu Fu
abstract: Extended reasoning in large language models (LLMs) creates severe KV cache memory bottlenecks. Leading KV cache compression methods estimate KV importance using attention scores from recent post-RoPE queries. However, queries rotate with position during RoPE, making representative queries very few, leading to poor top-key selection and unstable reasoning. To avoid this issue, we turn to the pre-RoPE space, where we observe that Q and K vectors are highly concentrated around fixed non-zero center

infographic.key_insight: Operate in the pre-RoPE vector space—where Q/K vectors concentrate around a fixed non-zero center—and use a trigonometric compression of KV representations (TriAttention) to produce rotation-stable, highly compact KV caches for long-context reasoning.
infographic.problem_solved: KV cache memory bottlenecks and unstable top-key selection in extended LLM reasoning caused by RoPE-induced query rotation and poor importance estimation.
method: Analyze pre-RoPE Q/K statistics and identify a stable non-zero center that makes representations rotation-invariant compared to post-RoPE queries.
Apply trigonometric-based compression to encode KV pairs (angles/magnitudes or sin/cos components) so keys can be grouped and ranked reliably despite positional rotation.
Integrate compressed KV storage with attention retrieval to keep top keys accurately while drastically reducing memory footprint for long sequences.
infographic.impact: Enables more memory-efficient, stable long-range inference for LLMs, improving throughput and practicability of extended reasoning on existing hardware without sacrificing key-selection fidelity.

title: Analyzing Symbolic Properties for DRL Agents in Systems and Networking
authors: Mohammad Zangooei, Jannis Weil, Amr Rizk, Mina Tahmasbi Arashloo, Raouf Boutaba
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has shown remarkable performance on complex control problems in systems and networking, including adaptive video streaming, wireless resource management, and congestion control. For safe deployment, however, it is critical to reason about how agents behave across the range of system states they encounter in practice. Existing verification-based methods in this domain primarily focus on point properties, defined around fixed input states, which offer limited cove

infographic.key_insight: Introduce and analyze 'symbolic properties'—state-set predicates that capture behavioral guarantees of DRL agents across ranges of system states—allowing verification and reasoning beyond single input points. This yields broader, more practical assurances for DRL in systems and networking.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing verification approaches for DRL in systems and networking focus on pointwise properties (fixed inputs) and thus provide limited coverage; this paper addresses the challenge of specifying and checking richer, range-based properties that better reflect real-world state variability.
method: Formalize symbolic properties as predicates or constraints over sets of environment/system states that express safety, performance, or invariants for DRL agents.

Develop a verification/analysis workflow that checks these symbolic properties (via symbolic reasoning, over-approximation, or targeted testing) and produces counterexamples or certificates when a property fails.

Evaluate the approach on representative systems-and-networking tasks (e.g., adaptive streaming, wireless resource allocation, congestion control) to demonstrate improved coverage and actionable diagnostics.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners tools to specify meaningful, range-based guarantees for deployed DRL controllers, improving trust, safety, and diagnosability in critical networking and systems applications. It bridges the gap between formal verification and practical robustness testing for learned policies.

title: A Frame is Worth One Token: Efficient Generative World Modeling with Delta Tokens
authors: Tommie Kerssies, Gabriele Berton, Ju He, Qihang Yu, Wufei Ma
abstract: Anticipating diverse future states is a central challenge in video world modeling. Discriminative world models produce a deterministic prediction that implicitly averages over possible futures, while existing generative world models remain computationally expensive. Recent work demonstrates that predicting the future in the feature space of a vision foundation model (VFM), rather than a latent space optimized for pixel reconstruction, requires significantly fewer world model parameters. However,

infographic.key_insight: Represent video frames as single "delta tokens" in a vision foundation model feature space so a compact generative model can predict diverse future states with far fewer tokens and parameters.
infographic.problem_solved: Current generative world models are computationally expensive and discriminative models collapse to deterministic averages; this paper addresses the need for efficient, diverse video/world prediction with much lower token and model cost.
method: Encode frames into a pre-trained vision foundation model (VFM) feature space instead of pixel latents.
Compress temporal changes into lightweight "delta tokens"—one token per frame representing the feature-space change from the previous frame.
Train a compact generative model (e.g., transformer/autoregressive sampler) to predict sequences of delta tokens, then reconstruct future features/frames or feed them to downstream tasks.
infographic.impact: Enables fast, parameter-efficient generative world models that produce diverse future trajectories—useful for scaling video prediction, planning, and model-based RL in compute-constrained settings.

title: Vero: An Open RL Recipe for General Visual Reasoning
authors: Gabriel Sarch, Linrong Cai, Qunzhong Wang, Haoyang Wu, Danqi Chen
abstract: What does it take to build a visual reasoner that works across charts, science, spatial understanding, and open-ended tasks? The strongest vision-language models (VLMs) show such broad visual reasoning is within reach, but the recipe behind them remains unclear, locked behind proprietary reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines with non-public data. We introduce Vero, a family of fully open VLMs that matches or exceeds existing open-weight models across diverse visual reasoning tasks. We scale RL d

infographic.key_insight: Vero provides a fully open reinforcement-learning training recipe that produces vision–language models matching or exceeding other open-weight models on diverse visual reasoning tasks, demonstrating that strong, general visual reasoning can be achieved without proprietary pipelines or data.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of transparent, reproducible RL pipelines and non-public training data that have blocked the community from building competitive, general-purpose visual reasoners.
method: Design and release an end-to-end, open RL recipe for fine-tuning VLMs to improve visual reasoning and alignment.
Scale training across diverse visual reasoning domains (charts, science, spatial, open-ended tasks) using publicly available datasets and carefully constructed task mixes.
Provide benchmark-driven evaluation and open checkpoints/tools so results are reproducible and comparable to proprietary baselines.
infographic.impact: This work democratizes high-performance visual reasoning by giving practitioners a reproducible RL-based path to build and adapt competitive VLMs across many domains, accelerating research, deployment, and safe alignment work.

title: PointTPA: Dynamic Network Parameter Adaptation for 3D Scene Understanding
authors: Siyuan Liu, Chaoqun Zheng, Xin Zhou, Tianrui Feng, Dingkang Liang
abstract: Scene-level point cloud understanding remains challenging due to diverse geometries, imbalanced category distributions, and highly varied spatial layouts. Existing methods improve object-level performance but rely on static network parameters during inference, limiting their adaptability to dynamic scene data. We propose PointTPA, a Test-time Parameter Adaptation framework that generates input-aware network parameters for scene-level point clouds. PointTPA adopts a Serialization-based Neighborho

infographic.key_insight: PointTPA generates input-aware network parameters at test time so a single backbone can adapt dynamically to each scene-level point cloud, improving robustness to diverse geometries and layouts without retraining the whole model.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the limitation of static inference parameters for scene-level point clouds, addressing variability in geometry, class imbalance, and spatial layout that degrade performance when a network cannot adapt to each input.
method: Test-time Parameter Adaptation: a lightweight module predicts input-specific parameter deltas for a pretrained point-cloud backbone so the network adapts per scene at inference.
Serialization-based neighborhood encoding: local neighborhoods are serialized/encoded to capture scene structure and condition the parameter generator on local plus global context.
Plug-and-play design: the adapter is designed to be computationally efficient and inserted into existing segmentation/semantic backbones to update select layers online.
infographic.impact: Enables more robust, generalizable 3D scene understanding without costly retraining or per-dataset finetuning, making deployed systems better at handling real-world variability in point-cloud data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained backbone + test-time parameter generator feeding adapted weights into the backbone for a single input scene.

title: LoMa: Local Feature Matching Revisited
authors: David Nordström, Johan Edstedt, Georg Bökman, Jonathan Astermark, Anders Heyden
abstract: Local feature matching has long been a fundamental component of 3D vision systems such as Structure-from-Motion (SfM), yet progress has lagged behind the rapid advances of modern data-driven approaches. The newer approaches, such as feed-forward reconstruction models, have benefited extensively from scaling dataset sizes, whereas local feature matching models are still only trained on a few mid-sized datasets. In this paper, we revisit local feature matching from a data-driven perspective. In ou

infographic.key_insight: Revisiting local feature matching with a data-driven lens—scaling training data and standardizing evaluation—substantially improves matching accuracy and downstream 3D reconstruction, narrowing the gap with modern feed‑forward 3D models.
infographic.problem_solved: Local feature matching has stagnated due to small, fragmented training sets and inconsistent evaluation protocols; this work addresses the lack of large-scale data and rigorous benchmarks that prevent progress and fair comparison.
method: Assemble and scale diverse, task-focused datasets for local feature matching to unlock data-driven improvements.
Adapt training objectives and model design to leverage larger data (robust matching losses, contrastive/matching supervision, and architecture refinements).
Provide standardized evaluation and benchmarks across SfM and reconstruction tasks to measure real-world impact and comparability.
infographic.impact: Makes local feature matching more robust and competitive, improving SfM, localization and 3D reconstruction pipelines for practitioners; establishes a reproducible benchmark and training paradigm for future research.

title: Empowering Power Outage Prediction with Spatially Aware Hybrid Graph Neural Networks and Contrastive Learning
authors: Xuyang Shen, Zijie Pan, Diego Cerrai, Xinxuan Zhang, Christopher Colorio
abstract: Extreme weather events, such as severe storms, hurricanes, snowstorms, and ice storms, which are exacerbated by climate change, frequently cause widespread power outages. These outages halt industrial operations, impact communities, damage critical infrastructure, profoundly disrupt economies, and have far-reaching effects across various sectors. To mitigate these effects, the University of Connecticut and Eversource Energy Center have developed an outage prediction modeling (OPM) system to prov

infographic.key_insight: A spatially aware hybrid Graph Neural Network combined with contrastive pretraining significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of power outage prediction under extreme weather by learning richer, topology-informed representations.
infographic.problem_solved: Predicting weather-driven power outages across distributed electrical networks where spatial dependencies, noisy/missing labels, and multimodal inputs (weather, grid topology, assets) make reliable forecasting difficult.
method: Hybrid spatial GNN that models multi-scale grid topology and neighborhood interactions to capture spatial propagation of failures.
Temporal encoder (e.g., sequence model) integrated with the GNN to handle dynamic weather and time-varying load/asset states.
Contrastive learning pretraining on multimodal inputs (weather, historical outages, sensor/asset data) to produce robust, transferable node/region embeddings for downstream outage forecasting.
infographic.impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build more accurate, resilient infrastructure forecasting systems that leverage topology-aware representations and self-supervised learning—useful for transfer learning, operational decision support, and climate-resilience planning.

title: SpatialEdit: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Image Spatial Editing
authors: Yicheng Xiao, Wenhu Zhang, Lin Song, Yukang Chen, Wenbo Li
abstract: Image spatial editing performs geometry-driven transformations, allowing precise control over object layout and camera viewpoints. Current models are insufficient for fine-grained spatial manipulations, motivating a dedicated assessment suite. Our contributions are listed: (i) We introduce SpatialEdit-Bench, a complete benchmark that evaluates spatial editing by jointly measuring perceptual plausibility and geometric fidelity via viewpoint reconstruction and framing analysis. (ii) To address the

infographic.key_insight: SpatialEdit-Bench provides the first comprehensive benchmark that jointly measures perceptual plausibility and geometric fidelity for fine-grained image spatial editing, using viewpoint reconstruction and framing analysis to quantify how well edits preserve realistic appearance and correct geometry.
infographic.problem_solved: Current image-editing evaluations ignore or inadequately measure geometry—there was no standardized suite for assessing fine-grained, geometry-driven spatial edits (object layout and camera viewpoint changes). This benchmark fills that gap.
method: Curate SpatialEdit-Bench: a dataset of spatial-editing tasks with ground-truth viewpoints, framing annotations, and edited target images.
Define joint evaluation metrics: perceptual plausibility (e.g., realism / perceptual similarity) combined with geometric fidelity via viewpoint reconstruction and framing analysis.
Provide a standardized evaluation protocol and baseline model assessments to reveal trade-offs between visual realism and geometric accuracy.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare spatial-editing models along both visual and geometric axes, accelerating improvements for applications like AR, scene synthesis, and robotics that require precise layout and viewpoint control.

title: PINNs in PDE Constrained Optimal Control Problems: Direct vs Indirect Methods
authors: Zhen Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Alessandro Alla, Jerome Darbon, George Em Karniadakis
abstract: We study physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) as numerical tools for the optimal control of semilinear partial differential equations. We first recall the classical direct and indirect viewpoints for optimal control of PDEs, and then present two PINN formulations: a direct formulation based on minimizing the objective under the state constraint, and an indirect formulation based on the first-order optimality system. For a class of semilinear parabolic equations, we derive the state equation,

infographic.key_insight: The paper formulates and contrasts two PINN-based ways to solve PDE-constrained optimal control — a direct approach that enforces the state constraint inside the loss, and an indirect approach that enforces the first-order optimality (state + adjoint + control) system — and derives the governing state equation for a class of semilinear parabolic problems.
infographic.problem_solved: Provides a clear PINN-based framework for solving optimal control problems governed by semilinear PDEs, clarifying how to encode constraints and optimality conditions in neural-network training and comparing the two main formulations practitioners can use.
method: Recall classical direct vs indirect optimal-control viewpoints and translate each into a PINN loss formulation.
Direct PINN: minimize the control objective while imposing the PDE state constraint via PDE residual, boundary/initial, and data terms in the loss.

Indirect PINN: form a PINN that simultaneously enforces the state equation, the adjoint equation, and the optimality condition (first-order system) as residuals in a joint loss; derive the semilinear parabolic state equation used in analysis.
infographic.impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners principled guidance on implementing PINNs for PDE-constrained control, showing how to encode constraints and optimality conditions and helping choose between formulations based on enforceability, interpretability, and implementation complexity.

title: BAS: A Decision-Theoretic Approach to Evaluating Large Language Model Confidence
authors: Sean Wu, Fredrik K. Gustafsson, Edward Phillips, Boyan Gao, Anshul Thakur
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often produce confident but incorrect answers in settings where abstention would be safer. Standard evaluation protocols, however, require a response and do not account for how confidence should guide decisions under different risk preferences. To address this gap, we introduce the Behavioral Alignment Score (BAS), a decision-theoretic metric for evaluating how well LLM confidence supports abstention-aware decision making. BAS is derived from an explicit answer-or-ab

infographic.key_insight: BAS (Behavioral Alignment Score) is a decision-theoretic metric that quantifies how well an LLM's confidence supports correct answer-or-abstain decisions under different risk preferences, letting evaluation reflect the real costs of confident mistakes.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard benchmarks force a response and ignore abstention and user risk tolerance, so there is no principled way to evaluate whether model confidence actually helps make safer decisions.
method: Formulate an explicit answer-or-abstain decision problem with utilities/costs for correct answers, incorrect answers, and abstention.
Derive the Behavioral Alignment Score as the expected utility (or regret-relative) measure of model confidence-driven decisions across risk preferences and thresholds.
Compare BAS to baseline metrics (e.g., accuracy, calibration) to show when confidence leads to better abstention-aware behavior.
infographic.impact: BAS gives practitioners a practical, risk-aware way to rank models, set abstention thresholds, and deploy LLMs more safely by aligning confidence estimates with decision costs. It moves evaluation from pure accuracy toward actionable, context-sensitive metrics for real-world use.

title: Biologically Realistic Dynamics for Nonlinear Classification in CMOS+X Neurons
authors: Steven Louis, Hannah Bradley, Artem Litvinenko, Cody Trevillian, Darrin Hanna
abstract: Spiking neural networks encode information in spike timing and offer a pathway toward energy efficient artificial intelligence. However, a key challenge in spiking neural networks is realizing nonlinear and expressive computation in compact, energy-efficient hardware without relying on additional circuit complexity. In this work, we examine nonlinear computation in a CMOS+X spiking neuron implemented with a magnetic tunnel junction connected in series with an NMOS transistor. Circuit simulations

infographic.key_insight: A CMOS+X spiking neuron that pairs a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) in series with an NMOS transistor can produce biologically realistic, intrinsically nonlinear dynamics, enabling expressive classification without extra circuit overhead.
infographic.problem_solved: How to realize compact, energy-efficient nonlinear computation in spiking neurons for classification tasks without adding circuit complexity or large peripheral networks.
method: Design a CMOS+X neuron topology that integrates an MTJ device in series with an NMOS transistor to generate intrinsic nonlinear spiking dynamics.
Use circuit-level simulations to characterize voltage/current trajectories, spike timing, and nonlinear response regimes of the CMOS+X neuron.
Evaluate the neuron's ability to implement nonlinear decision boundaries for classification and compare trade-offs in compactness and energy relative to simpler spiking models.
infographic.impact: Provides a hardware-native route to richer neural computations in spiking systems, enabling more expressive, area- and energy-efficient neuromorphic accelerators for ML tasks without adding peripheral circuits.

title: CoME-VL: Scaling Complementary Multi-Encoder Vision-Language Learning
authors: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Xilin He, Imran Razzak, Hisham Cholakkal
abstract: Recent vision-language models (VLMs) typically rely on a single vision encoder trained with contrastive image-text objectives, such as CLIP-style pretraining. While contrastive encoders are effective for cross-modal alignment and retrieval, self-supervised visual encoders often capture richer dense semantics and exhibit stronger robustness on recognition and understanding tasks. In this work, we investigate how to scale the fusion of these complementary visual representations for vision-language

infographic.key_insight: Fusing complementary visual encoders — a contrastive image-text encoder (CLIP-style) and a self-supervised dense visual encoder — produces richer, more robust vision-language representations. The paper shows how to scale this multi-encoder fusion so VLMs gain both alignment/retrieval strengths and dense semantic understanding.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard VLMs typically use a single contrastive vision encoder, which is good for alignment and retrieval but misses dense semantics and robustness. The paper addresses how to combine and scale multiple complementary visual encoders so a single VLM benefits from both types of visual knowledge.
method: Dual (or multi-) encoder pipeline: retain a contrastive image-text encoder and a self-supervised/dense visual encoder operating in parallel to capture complementary signals.
Projection & fusion: map each encoder's features into a common representation space and aggregate them via a learnable fusion module so the text encoder can attend to combined visual semantics.

Unified training objectives: jointly optimize cross-modal alignment (contrastive) and complementary alignment or fusion losses to preserve retrieval strengths while injecting dense semantics and robustness.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical recipe to build VLMs that keep CLIP-style alignment while gaining richer dense understanding and robustness — improving performance across retrieval, recognition, and downstream multimodal tasks without discarding complementary visual encoders.

title: Multi-View Video Diffusion Policy: A 3D Spatio-Temporal-Aware Video Action Model
authors: Peiyan Li, Yixiang Chen, Yuan Xu, Jiabing Yang, Xiangnan Wu
abstract: Robotic manipulation requires understanding both the 3D spatial structure of the environment and its temporal evolution, yet most existing policies overlook one or both. They typically rely on 2D visual observations and backbones pretrained on static image--text pairs, resulting in high data requirements and limited understanding of environment dynamics. To address this, we introduce MV-VDP, a multi-view video diffusion policy that jointly models the 3D spatio-temporal state of the environment.

infographic.key_insight: MV-VDP uses a multi-view video diffusion policy to jointly model 3D spatial structure and temporal dynamics, enabling action generation that is aware of the environment's full spatio-temporal state.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing robotic policies often rely on 2D observations and image-pretrained backbones, missing 3D structure or temporal dynamics and demanding large amounts of data; MV-VDP addresses this by integrating multi-view inputs and temporal modeling into a single diffusion-based policy.
method: Condition a diffusion-based generative policy on synchronized multi-view video to capture multi-perspective spatial cues.
Learn a compact 3D spatio-temporal latent (implicit or voxel-aware) that encodes scene geometry and temporal evolution for downstream action generation.
Sample action or trajectory sequences by denoising in the learned latent space, training the policy end-to-end for robotic manipulation tasks.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable way to incorporate 3D and temporal context into action policies, improving sample efficiency and robustness for real-world robotic manipulation and dynamic scene reasoning.

title: A Tsetlin Machine-driven Intrusion Detection System for Next-Generation IoMT Security
authors: Rahul Jaiswal, Per-Arne Andersen, Linga Reddy Cenkeramaddi, Lei Jiao, Ole-Christoffer Granmo
abstract: The rapid adoption of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is transforming healthcare by enabling seamless connectivity among medical devices, systems, and services. However, it also introduces serious cybersecurity and patient safety concerns as attackers increasingly exploit new methods and emerging vulnerabilities to infiltrate IoMT networks. This paper proposes a novel Tsetlin Machine (TM)-based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) for detecting a wide range of cyberattacks targeting IoMT netwo

infographic.key_insight: A Tsetlin Machine (TM)-based IDS provides a lightweight, interpretable method to detect a wide range of cyberattacks in IoMT networks, enabling accurate detection with human-readable rules suitable for edge deployment.
infographic.problem_solved: Secures resource-constrained Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices and networks against evolving cyberattacks by offering an accurate, low-compute, and interpretable intrusion detection approach.
method: Design a TM-based classifier that learns propositional clauses from network/packet and flow features to distinguish normal vs. malicious IoMT traffic.
Train and evaluate the TM IDS on IoMT-relevant attack datasets and optimize for low latency and compute overhead for edge/medical-device deployment.
Produce human-readable rule outputs and an operational pipeline (feature extraction → TM inference → alerting + explainability) for forensic analysis and response.
infographic.impact: Offers AI/ML practitioners a practical, explainable alternative to heavyweight deep-learning IDS solutions, enabling deployment on constrained medical devices and easier investigation of detected incidents.

title: HyperCT: Low-Rank Hypernet for Unified Chest CT Analysis
authors: Fengbei Liu, Sunwoo Kwak, Hao Phung, Nusrat Binta Nizam, Ilan Richter
abstract: Non-contrast chest CTs offer a rich opportunity for both conventional pulmonary and opportunistic extra-pulmonary screening. While Multi-Task Learning (MTL) can unify these diverse tasks, standard hard-parameter sharing approaches are often suboptimal for modeling distinct pathologies. We propose HyperCT, a framework that dynamically adapts a Vision Transformer backbone via a Hypernetwork. To ensure computational efficiency, we integrate Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), allowing the model to regress

infographic.key_insight: HyperCT uses a hypernetwork to dynamically generate low-rank adapters (LoRA) that adapt a shared Vision Transformer for diverse chest CT tasks, achieving task-specific specialization with far fewer extra parameters than separate heads or full fine-tuning.
infographic.problem_solved: Unifies heterogeneous pulmonary and opportunistic extra-pulmonary chest CT tasks in a single model while avoiding the inefficiency and suboptimal sharing of standard hard-parameter multi-task approaches.
method: Use a Hypernetwork to regress task- and/or input-conditioned low-rank adapter weights that modify a frozen or shared Vision Transformer backbone.
Integrate Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to keep per-task parameter overhead and compute low while enabling task-specific modulation of representations.
Train the system in a multi-task setting so the shared backbone learns common features and the hypernet+LoRA provide efficient task specialization.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, parameter-efficient path to build one unified chest CT model that handles many screening and diagnostic tasks—reducing deployment complexity and enabling scalable clinical multi-task systems without sacrificing per-task performance.

title: The Eleventh NTIRE 2026 Efficient Super-Resolution Challenge Report
authors: Bin Ren, Hang Guo, Yan Shu, Jiaqi Ma, Ziteng Cui
abstract: This paper reviews the NTIRE 2026 challenge on efficient single-image super-resolution with a focus on the proposed solutions and results. The aim of this challenge is to devise a network that reduces one or several aspects, such as runtime, parameters, and FLOPs, while maintaining PSNR of around 26.90 dB on the DIV2K_LSDIR_valid dataset, and 26.99 dB on the DIV2K_LSDIR_test dataset. The challenge had 95 registered participants, and 15 teams made valid submissions. They gauge the state-of-the-ar

infographic.key_insight: The NTIRE 2026 Efficient SR challenge shows that carefully designed lightweight networks can substantially cut runtime, parameter count, and FLOPs while keeping PSNR near 26.9 dB on DIV2K_LSDIR benchmarks.
infographic.problem_solved: Designing single-image super-resolution models that balance high reconstruction quality with strict efficiency constraints (runtime, parameters, FLOPs) for practical deployment.
method: Organized a public challenge (95 registered, 15 valid submissions) to benchmark efficiency-focused SR designs on DIV2K_LSDIR_valid and DIV2K_LSDIR_test with target PSNR ≈ 26.90–26.99 dB.
Teams applied lightweight architectural choices (e.g., pruning, efficient blocks, mobile-friendly convolutions) and optimization/training tweaks to trade computation for minimal PSNR loss.
Systematic analysis and leaderboard comparisons highlighted practical trade-offs between PSNR, runtime, parameter count, and FLOPs.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical roadmap and empirical baselines for ML practitioners aiming to deploy SR on resource-constrained devices, and clarifies where efficiency gains are possible without sacrificing measurable quality.

title: VOSR: A Vision-Only Generative Model for Image Super-Resolution
authors: Rongyuan Wu, Lingchen Sun, Zhengqiang Zhang, Xiangtao Kong, Jixin Zhao
abstract: Most of the recent generative image super-resolution (SR) methods rely on adapting large text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models pretrained on web-scale text-image data. While effective, this paradigm starts from a generic T2I generator, despite that SR is fundamentally a low-resolution (LR) input-conditioned image restoration task. In this work, we investigate whether an SR model trained purely on visual data can rival T2I-based ones. To this end, we propose VOSR, a Vision-Only generative framewor

infographic.key_insight: VOSR shows that a super-resolution model trained solely on visual LR–HR data can match or rival generative SR methods that adapt large text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models, questioning the need for text-conditioned pretraining for SR.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces dependence on massive web-scale text–image pretraining and the mismatch between generic T2I generators and the LR-conditioned image restoration task, enabling SR models that are specialized, data-efficient, and free of text-conditioning biases.
method: Introduce a vision-only generative framework (VOSR) trained purely on visual LR–HR pairs rather than T2I-pretrained weights.
Condition the generative model directly on the low-resolution input so it learns restoration-specific priors tailored to SR.
Replace text-conditioning and large T2I adaptation with focused visual supervision to achieve comparable generative SR performance.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates a practical alternative to heavy T2I adaptation for SR, allowing practitioners to build more compact, targeted, and less biased super-resolution models that are easier to train and deploy in image-restoration pipelines.

To aid in these developments we introduce PR3DICTR: Platform for Research in 3D Image Classification and sTandardised tRaining. title: ProtoFlow: Mitigating Forgetting in Class-Incremental Remote Sensing Segmentation via Low-Curvature Prototype Flow
authors: Jiekai Wu, Rong Fu, Chuangqi Li, Zijian Zhang, Guangxin Wu
abstract: Remote sensing segmentation in real deployment is inherently continual: new semantic categories emerge, and acquisition conditions shift across seasons, cities, and sensors. Despite recent progress, many incremental approaches still treat training steps as isolated updates, which leaves representation drift and forgetting insufficiently controlled. We present ProtoFlow, a time-aware prototype dynamics framework that models class prototypes as trajectories and learns their evolution with an expli

infographic.key_insight: Model class prototypes as time-aware trajectories and learn a low-curvature prototype flow to constrain their evolution, which reduces representation drift and mitigates catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental remote sensing segmentation.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses forgetting and representation drift when segmentation models are updated incrementally with new classes and shifting acquisition conditions (seasons, cities, sensors).
method: Represent class prototypes as trajectories in feature space and track their temporal evolution across incremental steps.
Learn a prototype flow with a low-curvature regularizer and temporal-consistency objectives to enforce smooth, stable prototype transitions.
Integrate the prototype-flow module into class-incremental segmentation training to constrain representation drift and preserve prior knowledge.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical mechanism to retain prior segmentation knowledge while adapting to new classes and domain shifts, improving robustness and lowering maintenance cost for deployed remote sensing systems.

abstract: Cardiovascular modeling has rapidly advanced over the past few decades due to the rising needs for health tracking and early detection of cardiovascular diseases. While 1-D arterial models offer an attractive compromise between computational efficiency and solution fidelity, their application on large populations or for generating large \emph{in silico} cohorts remains challenging. Certain hemodynamic parameters like the terminal resistance/compliance, are difficult to clinically estimate and of

infographic.key_insight: A fast ML-based surrogate replaces computationally expensive 1-D arterial solvers to deliver personalized, real-time predictions of blood flow and hemodynamic indices, while estimating hard-to-measure parameters (e.g., terminal resistance/compliance). This enables rapid, population-scale or bedside hemodynamic analysis without sacrificing clinically relevant fidelity.

title: Reflective Context Learning: Studying the Optimization Primitives of Context Space
authors: Nikita Vassilyev, William Berrios, Ruowang Zhang, Bo Han, Douwe Kiela
abstract: Generally capable agents must learn from experience in ways that generalize across tasks and environments. The fundamental problems of learning, including credit assignment, overfitting, forgetting, local optima, and high-variance learning signals, persist whether the learned object lies in parameter space or context space. While these challenges are well understood in classical machine learning optimization, they remain underexplored in context space, leading current methods to be fragmented an

infographic.key_insight: Context-space learning suffers the same fundamental optimization pathologies as parameter-space learning; by identifying and formalizing core optimization primitives in context space, the paper introduces a reflective framework to analyze and mitigate those failures.
infographic.problem_solved: Brings order to a fragmented set of context-based techniques by addressing credit assignment, overfitting, forgetting, local optima, and high-variance learning signals in context space—problems that were previously underexplored compared to classical parameter optimization.
method: Formalize a set of optimization primitives for context-space updates (e.g., update operators, credit-assignment mechanisms, regularizers, and variance-reduction components).
Introduce a reflective learning framework that composes and tests these primitives to diagnose failure modes and guide design choices for context updates.
Empirically evaluate combinations of primitives across benchmarks/tasks to compare stability, generalization, and sample efficiency of context-space methods.
infographic.impact: Provides a principled toolkit for designing and diagnosing context-based learning (prompts, adapters, retrieval contexts, etc.), enabling more reliable, generalizable, and efficient use of context as a learning substrate in practical AI systems.

title: Reliability Gated Multi-Teacher Distillation for Low Resource Abstractive Summarization
authors: Dipto Sumit, Ankan Kumar Roy, Sadia Khair Rodela, Atia Haque Asha, Mourchona Afrin
abstract: We study multiteacher knowledge distillation for low resource abstractive summarization from a reliability aware perspective. We introduce EWAD (Entropy Weighted Agreement Aware Distillation), a token level mechanism that routes supervision between teacher distillation and gold supervision based on inter teacher agreement, and CPDP (Capacity Proportional Divergence Preservation), a geometric constraint on the student position relative to heterogeneous teachers. Across two Bangla datasets, 13 Ban

infographic.key_insight: Routing supervision by teacher agreement (EWAD) combined with a geometric capacity-preserving constraint (CPDP) lets a student model selectively learn from multiple heterogeneous teachers, improving reliability for low-resource abstractive summarization.
infographic.problem_solved: Low-resource abstractive summarization suffers from limited labeled data and noisy or conflicting signals from multiple teacher models. This work addresses how to distill multi-teacher supervision reliably so a compact student learns useful, consistent behavior rather than inheriting teacher disagreement.
method: EWAD (Entropy Weighted Agreement Aware Distillation): token-level routing that weights teacher vs. gold supervision based on inter-teacher agreement/entropy.
CPDP (Capacity Proportional Divergence Preservation): geometric constraint that positions the student relative to heterogeneous teachers to preserve useful divergences proportional to capacity.
Integrated multi-teacher distillation pipeline that combines agreement-aware supervision routing with capacity-aware student positioning, evaluated on Bangla summarization datasets.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, reliability-aware recipe for multi-teacher distillation that helps practitioners train smaller, more robust abstractive summarizers in low-resource languages or domains where teacher signals conflict or are noisy.

title: Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models
authors: Wancong Zhang, Basile Terver, Artem Zholus, Soham Chitnis, Harsh Sutaria
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) with learned world models has emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied control, particularly for its ability to generalize zero-shot when deployed in new environments. However, learned world models often struggle with long-horizon control due to the accumulation of prediction errors and the exponentially growing search space. In this work, we address these challenges by learning latent world models at multiple temporal scales and performing hierarchical plannin

infographic.key_insight: Learning latent world models at multiple temporal scales enables coarse-to-fine hierarchical planning in latent space, reducing prediction error accumulation and drastically shrinking the search space for long-horizon control.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of long-horizon model-based control where single-scale learned models accumulate prediction errors and face an exponentially large planning search space, limiting zero-shot generalization and practical deployment.
method: Train latent dynamics models at multiple temporal resolutions (e.g., fast short-horizon and slow long-horizon latent models) to capture both fine-grained control and abstract long-term structure.

Perform hierarchical planning: a high-level planner proposes coarse latent goals over long horizons using the slow model; a low-level MPC refines and executes short-horizon actions using the fast model.
Plan and optimize in latent space to reduce computational cost and mitigate prediction drift, enabling scalable, zero-shot-capable control in new environments.
infographic.impact: Makes long-horizon model-based control more reliable and scalable for embodied agents and robotics by combining abstraction with concrete short-term control—improving generalization and efficiency for practitioners building real-world planners.

title: ActionParty: Multi-Subject Action Binding in Generative Video Games
authors: Alexander Pondaven, Ziyi Wu, Igor Gilitschenski, Philip Torr, Sergey Tulyakov
abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion have enabled the development of "world models" capable of simulating interactive environments. However, these models are largely restricted to single-agent settings, failing to control multiple agents simultaneously in a scene. In this work, we tackle a fundamental issue of action binding in existing video diffusion models, which struggle to associate specific actions with their corresponding subjects. For this purpose, we propose ActionParty, an action control

infographic.key_insight: ActionParty introduces a mechanism to reliably bind per-subject actions to their corresponding agents in generative video models, enabling simultaneous, disentangled control of multiple characters in a scene. This closes a key gap in video diffusion world models that previously treated actions ambiguously across subjects.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing video diffusion/world models struggle to associate specific actions with the correct subject in multi-agent scenes, preventing reliable multi-subject control and producing mixed or misattributed behaviors.
method: Introduce ActionParty — an action-control module that conditions video generation on per-subject action inputs, explicitly linking action tokens to entity representations.

Use entity-aware attention mechanisms and/or subject-conditioned latent paths so each agent's action influences only its corresponding visual dynamics (e.g., per-subject masks or cross-attention linking).
Train with multi-subject interaction data and binding-aware objectives (e.g., contrastive or localization losses) to encourage disentangled action-to-subject mapping and robust multi-agent rollout.
infographic.impact: Enables precise, simultaneous control of multiple agents in generative video environments, improving realism and utility for game prototyping, multi-agent simulation, and interactive world modeling. Practitioners can build richer, controllable simulations and policies without per-frame manual editing.

title: Omni123: Exploring 3D Native Foundation Models with Limited 3D Data by Unifying Text to 2D and 3D Generation
authors: Chongjie Ye, Cheng Cao, Chuanyu Pan, Yiming Hao, Yihao Zhi
abstract: Recent multimodal large language models have achieved strong performance in unified text and image understanding and generation, yet extending such native capability to 3D remains challenging due to limited data. Compared to abundant 2D imagery, high-quality 3D assets are scarce, making 3D synthesis under-constrained. Existing methods often rely on indirect pipelines that edit in 2D and lift results into 3D via optimization, sacrificing geometric consistency. We present Omni123, a 3D-native foun

infographic.key_insight: Omni123 enables 3D-native foundation models to be trained despite scarce 3D data by unifying text→2D and text→3D generation in a shared framework, using abundant 2D supervision to bootstrap high-quality, geometry-consistent 3D synthesis.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of high-quality 3D assets and the under-constrained nature of text-to-3D generation; fixes reliance on indirect 2D-to-3D pipelines that produce inconsistent geometry by training a single 3D-native model with cross-modal supervision.
method: Unify text-to-image and text-to-3D generation within a shared model/latent space so 2D and 3D tasks provide mutual supervision.
Leverage abundant 2D data and pre-trained 2D generative models to distill visual knowledge into the 3D branch via cross-modal losses and multi-view consistency.
Use a 3D-native decoder/representation and synthetic renderings or limited real 3D assets to enforce geometric fidelity and reduce reliance on expensive 3D datasets.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to develop geometry-consistent text-to-3D systems with far less 3D data, accelerating downstream adoption in AR/VR, robotics, simulation, and content creation while lowering data collection cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing shared encoder, dual outputs (2D image branch and 3D branch), and cross-modal supervision arrows

title: Beyond Referring Expressions: Scenario Comprehension Visual Grounding
authors: Ruozhen He, Nisarg A. Shah, Qihua Dong, Zilin Xiao, Jaywon Koo
abstract: Existing visual grounding benchmarks primarily evaluate alignment between image regions and literal referring expressions, where models can often succeed by matching a prominent named category. We explore a complementary and more challenging setting of scenario-based visual grounding, where the target must be inferred from roles, intentions, and relational context rather than explicit naming. We introduce Referring Scenario Comprehension (RSC), a benchmark designed for this setting. The queries

infographic.key_insight: Standard visual grounding benchmarks reward literal category matching; this paper introduces scenario-based visual grounding (RSC), where targets must be inferred from roles, intentions and relations rather than explicit names, revealing a gap in model comprehension.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the limitation of existing grounding evaluations that let models succeed by matching prominent named categories, instead measuring the ability to infer referents from contextual roles, intentions and relational cues.
method: Introduce Referring Scenario Comprehension (RSC), a benchmark containing queries that require role-, intention- and relation-based inference rather than literal naming.
Define an evaluation protocol and metrics tailored to scenario comprehension to distinguish category-matching from true contextual reasoning.
Provide baseline experiments and analysis showing current models' failures and where scenario reasoning is required.
infographic.impact: RSC exposes weaknesses in current vision–language models and provides a targeted benchmark to drive development of models that understand roles, intentions and relations—important for robust scene understanding in robotics, assistive tech and multimodal reasoning.

title: Grounded Token Initialization for New Vocabulary in LMs for Generative Recommendation
authors: Daiwei Chen, Zhoutong Fu, Chengming Jiang, Haichao Zhang, Ran Zhou
abstract: Language models (LMs) are increasingly extended with new learnable vocabulary tokens for domain-specific tasks, such as Semantic-ID tokens in generative recommendation. The standard practice initializes these new tokens as the mean of existing vocabulary embeddings, then relies on supervised fine-tuning to learn their representations. We present a systematic analysis of this strategy: through spectral and geometric diagnostics, we show that mean initialization collapses all new tokens into a deg

infographic.key_insight: Initializing new vocabulary tokens as the mean of existing embeddings collapses them into a degenerate, low-variance space; grounding new-token initialization in semantically meaningful item/context embeddings preserves representational diversity and speeds learning for generative recommendation.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses poor and slow learning of newly added vocabulary tokens (e.g., Semantic-ID tokens) in LMs caused by naïve mean-of-vocabulary initialization that yields collapsed, uninformative embeddings.
method: Diagnose collapse using spectral and geometric analyses (eigenvalue spectra, PCA/variance, pairwise angles) to show mean initialization reduces embedding rank and diversity.

Introduce Grounded Token Initialization: seed new tokens with embeddings derived from external item features or context-conditioned encoders (rather than the vocabulary mean), optionally with normalization/orthogonalization to preserve variance.
Fine-tune the LM with these grounded initializations and compare convergence, embedding geometry, and downstream generative-recommendation metrics against standard initialization.
infographic.impact: Practitioners extending LMs with domain-specific tokens can achieve faster convergence, richer token representations, and better generative recommendation quality by using grounded initializations instead of mean-based ones.

title: No Single Best Model for Diversity: Learning a Router for Sample Diversity
authors: Yuhan Liu, Fangyuan Xu, Vishakh Padmakumar, Daphne Ippolito, Eunsol Choi
abstract: When posed with prompts that permit a large number of valid answers, comprehensively generating them is the first step towards satisfying a wide range of users. In this paper, we study methods to elicit a comprehensive set of valid responses. To evaluate this, we introduce \textbf{diversity coverage}, a metric that measures the total quality scores assigned to each \textbf{unique} answer in the predicted answer set relative to the best possible answer set with the same number of answers. Using t

infographic.key_insight: There is no single best generative model for producing a diverse set of valid answers; learning a lightweight router that selects which model or sampling strategy to use per prompt yields higher "diversity coverage" than relying on any single model.
infographic.problem_solved: Generative systems often miss many valid responses for prompts that admit many correct answers; existing evaluation and sampling methods don't prioritize covering unique, high-quality answers across outputs.
method: Define a new metric, diversity coverage, which measures total quality across unique answers relative to the optimal set of the same size.
Train a router that, given an input prompt, selects among multiple models or sampling configurations to maximize the diversity coverage of the produced answer set.
Combine outputs from heterogeneous models via the router and evaluate against baselines (single-model sampling, uniform mixtures) to show improved coverage.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way to generate more comprehensive, non-redundant answer sets for open-ended prompts, improving user satisfaction, dataset creation, and downstream evaluation. Enables practitioners to leverage model ensembles more effectively for diversity-sensitive tasks.

title: Generative World Renderer
authors: Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Jiaming Tan, Ruihan Yu, Yidan Zhang
abstract: Scaling generative inverse and forward rendering to real-world scenarios is bottlenecked by the limited realism and temporal coherence of existing synthetic datasets. To bridge this persistent domain gap, we introduce a large-scale, dynamic dataset curated from visually complex AAA games. Using a novel dual-screen stitched capture method, we extracted 4M continuous frames (720p/30 FPS) of synchronized RGB and five G-buffer channels across diverse scenes, visual effects, and environments, includi

infographic.key_insight: A large-scale, temporally coherent dataset captured from AAA games using a novel dual-screen stitched capture method enables realistic, synchronized RGB + G-buffer training data for scaling generative inverse and forward rendering to real-world scenarios.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing synthetic datasets lack realism and temporal coherence, limiting the performance and generalization of generative inverse/forward rendering methods in real-world settings.
method: Dual-screen stitched capture pipeline to record synchronized visuals from high-fidelity game engines.
Curated 4M continuous frames at 720p/30 FPS with RGB plus five G-buffer channels (e.g., depth, normals, albedo, material/lighting maps) across diverse scenes, effects, and dynamic interactions.
Dataset curation prioritizing temporal continuity and visual complexity to bridge the synthetic→real domain gap for training and evaluation.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a high-fidelity, temporally coherent training and evaluation resource that improves realism, temporal stability, and generalization of neural rendering, inverse rendering, and related pipelines—reducing reliance on costly real-world capture.

title: AdamFlow: Adam-based Wasserstein Gradient Flows for Surface Registration in Medical Imaging
authors: Qiang Ma, Qingjie Meng, Xin Hu, Yicheng Wu, Wenjia Bai
abstract: Surface registration plays an important role for anatomical shape analysis in medical imaging. Existing surface registration methods often face a trade-off between efficiency and robustness. Local point matching methods are computationally efficient, but vulnerable to noise and initialisation. Methods designed for global point set alignment tend to incur a high computational cost. To address the challenge, here we present a fast surface registration method, which formulates surface meshes as pro

infographic.key_insight: Framing surface meshes as probability measures and optimizing their Wasserstein gradient flow with an Adam-style optimizer (AdamFlow) yields fast, robust surface registration that balances speed and noise resilience.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between computational efficiency (local point matching) and robustness/global alignment (optimal-transport approaches) in medical surface registration.
method: Represent surface meshes as probability measures / weighted point clouds and define alignment via a Wasserstein (optimal transport) energy.
Derive a discretized Wasserstein gradient flow to evolve source surfaces toward targets while preserving global structure and robustness to noise.
Introduce an Adam-based solver (AdamFlow) to accelerate convergence, stabilize noisy gradients, and reduce runtime compared with standard gradient-flow solvers.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical registration method that is both fast and robust for anatomical shape analysis, enabling scalable preprocessing and improved downstream ML applications in medical imaging.

Schematic of Wasserstein mass transport between surfaces with arrows illustrating the gradient flow evolution.

Pipeline diagram: mesh → probability measure → Wasserstein gradient flow → AdamFlow optimizer → registered mesh.

title: EventHub: Data Factory for Generalizable Event-Based Stereo Networks without Active Sensors
authors: Luca Bartolomei, Fabio Tosi, Matteo Poggi, Stefano Mattoccia, Guillermo Gallego
abstract: We propose EventHub, a novel framework for training deep-event stereo networks without ground truth annotations from costly active sensors, relying instead on standard color images. From these images, we derive either proxy annotations and proxy events through state-of-the-art novel view synthesis techniques, or simply proxy annotations when images are already paired with event data. Using the training set generated by our data factory, we repurpose state-of-the-art stereo models from RGB litera

infographic.key_insight: EventHub is a "data factory" that enables training high-performance event-based stereo networks without costly active sensors by synthesizing proxy events and annotations from ordinary color image datasets. This lets existing RGB stereo models be repurposed for event data using scalable, inexpensive supervision.
infographic.problem_solved: Event-based stereo learning depends on expensive, hard-to-scale active sensors or dense ground truth; EventHub removes that dependency by generating training signals from standard color images, making event-stereo training practical and generalizable.
method: Generate training sets from color-image collections by producing proxy annotations and, when needed, proxy events using state-of-the-art novel view synthesis / rendering techniques or by using paired image+event data when available.
Use the synthesized proxy labels/events to supervise event-based stereo networks, allowing re-use of mature RGB stereo architectures adapted to event inputs.
Train and validate models on the generated dataset to achieve generalizable event-stereo performance without collecting active-sensor ground truth.
infographic.impact: EventHub drastically lowers the barrier to build and scale event-based stereo models by removing the need for active-sensor ground truth, enabling broader research, faster iteration, and easier domain transfer for neuromorphic and low-latency vision systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: color images -> novel view synthesis -> proxy events/annotations -> training stereo network
Before/after example: raw event input and resulting disparity map vs. baseline (with/without EventHub data)

title: Steerable Visual Representations
authors: Jona Ruthardt, Manu Gaur, Deva Ramanan, Makarand Tapaswi, Yuki M. Asano
abstract: Pretrained Vision Transformers (ViTs) such as DINOv2 and MAE provide generic image features that can be applied to a variety of downstream tasks such as retrieval, classification, and segmentation. However, such representations tend to focus on the most salient visual cues in the image, with no way to direct them toward less prominent concepts of interest. In contrast, Multimodal LLMs can be guided with textual prompts, but the resulting representations tend to be language-centric and lose their

infographic.key_insight: Pretrained ViT features can be 'steered' toward user-specified or less-salient concepts via lightweight directional adjustments in feature space, enabling targeted visual representations without full model retraining.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard pretrained ViTs emphasize the most salient cues and lack mechanisms to direct their attention toward less prominent or user-defined concepts; multimodal LLM guidance tends to be language-centric and can dilute pure visual specificity.
method: Define steering signals from text prompts or exemplar images and learn compact steering vectors/adapters that operate in pretrained ViT feature space (minimal or no fine-tuning of the backbone).
Apply steering via linear modulation or attention reweighting to shift representations toward desired concepts while preserving overall feature utility.
Train steering modules with contrastive or alignment objectives so steered features better serve downstream tasks like retrieval, classification, and segmentation.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a low-cost, flexible way to adapt general-purpose visual representations to focus on specific, possibly subtle concepts—improving performance on targeted retrieval and fine-grained tasks without expensive model re-training.
visual_elements: Side-by-side attention/saliency maps: original ViT attention vs. steered attention highlighting previously suppressed concepts.
Pipeline diagram: pretrained ViT -> steering vector/adapter insertion point -> steered features -> downstream head.

title: VOID: Video Object and Interaction Deletion
authors: Saman Motamed, William Harvey, Benjamin Klein, Luc Van Gool, Zhuoning Yuan
abstract: Existing video object removal methods excel at inpainting content "behind" the object and correcting appearance-level artifacts such as shadows and reflections. However, when the removed object has more significant interactions, such as collisions with other objects, current models fail to correct them and produce implausible results. We present VOID, a video object removal framework designed to perform physically-plausible inpainting in these complex scenarios. To train the model, we generate a

infographic.key_insight: VOID enables physically plausible video object removal by not only filling pixels behind removed objects but also correcting downstream interactions (e.g., collisions, pushed objects) so post-edit dynamics look realistic.
infographic.problem_solved: Current video object removal models handle appearance-level inpainting (background, shadows, reflections) but fail when the removed object caused physical interactions with other scene elements, producing implausible or inconsistent motion and geometry after removal.
method: Create paired training data that simulates object removals along with the resulting interaction effects (e.g., collisions, displacement) so the model learns how scenes should evolve after deletion.

Joint model that combines interaction-aware dynamics prediction (to infer how other objects should move or settle) with temporal, occlusion- and flow-aware video inpainting to produce consistent frames.
Train with losses enforcing temporal consistency, physical-plausibility (e.g., motion/occlusion constraints), and high-fidelity appearance reconstruction to reconcile dynamics and visual realism.
infographic.impact: VOID makes video editing and removal robust in realistic, dynamic scenes where objects interact—improving quality for special-effects, content creation, and dataset curation. Practitioners gain a tool to produce coherent temporal edits that respect physical scene behavior.
visual_elements: Before/after frame sequence highlighting a removed object and corrected interaction (e.g., object collision undone and displaced item returned to plausible position).
Schematic of training-data generation: original video → synthetic removal + simulated interaction outcome → paired supervision.

title: Stop Wandering: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation via Metacognitive Reasoning
authors: Xueying Li, Feng Lyu, Hao Wu, Mingliu Liu, Jia-Nan Liu
abstract: Training-free Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) agents powered by foundation models can follow instructions and explore 3D environments. However, existing approaches rely on greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory, leading to inefficient behaviors such as local oscillation and redundant revisiting. We argue that this stems from a lack of metacognitive capabilities: the agent cannot monitor its exploration progress, diagnose strategy failures, or adapt accordingly. To address this, we

infographic.key_insight: Equipping training-free VLN agents with lightweight metacognitive reasoning lets them monitor exploration, detect failure modes (e.g., loops or stalls), and adapt frontier selection, significantly reducing wandering and redundant revisits.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses inefficient exploration in vision-language navigation where greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory cause local oscillation, repeated revisits, and wasted steps—especially in zero-shot, foundation-model-driven agents.
method: Add a metacognitive module that estimates exploration progress and diagnoses failure modes (looping, stalling, low-information frontiers) without extra task-specific training.
Use adaptive frontier selection that deprioritizes recently unproductive regions and prioritizes informative goals inferred from instructions and progress signals.
Maintain an active spatial memory that marks visited/low-value areas and supports replanning and corrective actions to avoid redundant revisits.
infographic.impact: Improves efficiency and robustness of zero-shot VLN agents, reducing time, steps, and compute wasted on wandering—making foundation-model-driven navigation more practical for embodied AI and robotics deployments.
