title: Learning Dynamic Belief Graphs for Theory-of-mind Reasoning
authors: Ruxiao Chen, Xilei Zhao, Thomas J. Cova, Frank A. Drews, Susu Xu
abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning with Large Language Models (LLMs) requires inferring how people's implicit, evolving beliefs shape what they seek and how they act under uncertainty -- especially in high-stakes settings such as disaster response, emergency medicine, and human-in-the-loop autonomy. Prior approaches either prompt LLMs directly or use latent-state models that treat beliefs as static and independent, often producing incoherent mental models over time and weak reasoning in dynamic cont

infographic.key_insight: Represent and learn agents' evolving beliefs as structured, time-varying graphs so Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning remains coherent across temporal observations and uncertainty.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing ToM approaches treat beliefs as static or independent, producing inconsistent mental models over time and poor reasoning in dynamic, uncertain multi-agent settings.
method: Introduce dynamic belief graphs that encode agents, propositions, and belief relations as nodes and edges which evolve over time.
Learn graph update rules from observations (events, actions, communications) so the model tracks belief changes and their dependencies.
Use graph-based reasoning modules to infer agents' current beliefs, goals, and likely actions for downstream ToM tasks.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable, interpretable representation for temporally consistent ToM that improves prediction and decision-making in dynamic, high-stakes multi-agent environments (e.g., disaster response, human-in-the-loop systems).

title: LagerNVS: Latent Geometry for Fully Neural Real-time Novel View Synthesis
authors: Stanislaw Szymanowicz, Minghao Chen, Jianyuan Wang, Christian Rupprecht, Andrea Vedaldi
abstract: Recent work has shown that neural networks can perform 3D tasks such as Novel View Synthesis (NVS) without explicit 3D reconstruction. Even so, we argue that strong 3D inductive biases are still helpful in the design of such networks. We show this point by introducing LagerNVS, an encoder-decoder neural network for NVS that builds on `3D-aware' latent features. The encoder is initialized from a 3D reconstruction network pre-trained using explicit 3D supervision. This is paired with a lightweight

infographic.key_insight: Incorporating explicit 3D inductive biases into an otherwise fully neural NVS pipeline — via a 3D-aware latent geometry learned from a pre-trained 3D reconstruction encoder — yields accurate, temporally consistent novel view synthesis while enabling real-time inference.
infographic.problem_solved: How to get accurate, geometry-consistent novel view synthesis without expensive explicit 3D reconstruction at inference, balancing reconstruction quality and real-time performance for practical applications.
method: Use an encoder initialized from a 3D reconstruction network pre-trained with explicit 3D supervision to produce 3D-aware latent features (latent geometry).
Pair the encoder with a lightweight decoder that consumes latent geometry to render novel views in a fully neural pipeline optimized for speed.
Train end-to-end for view synthesis (with geometric consistency losses from the pretraining) to retain 3D structure while avoiding explicit geometry at runtime.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical recipe for building fast, geometry-consistent neural renderers suitable for real-time AR/VR, robotics, and interactive graphics, reducing system complexity while preserving quality.

title: Improving Generalization on Cybersecurity Tasks with Multi-Modal Contrastive Learning
authors: Jianan Huang, Rodolfo V. Valentim, Luca Vassio, Matteo Boffa, Marco Mellia
abstract: The use of ML in cybersecurity has long been impaired by generalization issues: Models that work well in controlled scenarios fail to maintain performance in production. The root cause often lies in ML algorithms learning superficial patterns (shortcuts) rather than underlying cybersecurity concepts. We investigate contrastive multi-modal learning as a first step towards improving ML performance in cybersecurity tasks. We aim at transferring knowledge from data-rich modalities, such as text, to

infographic.key_insight: Contrastive multi-modal learning can transfer rich semantic signals from data-rich text to data-poor cybersecurity modalities, reducing shortcut learning and substantially improving out-of-distribution generalization in real-world security tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: ML models in cybersecurity often learn superficial shortcuts from lab data and fail in production, especially when some modalities (network telemetry, binaries, logs) are scarce; this work addresses robust cross-modal knowledge transfer to improve real-world performance.
method: Train modality-specific encoders (e.g., text, telemetry, binary features) and align their representations with a contrastive loss so that semantically related samples across modalities are pulled together.

Leverage text as a data-rich anchor: use domain-aware augmentations and hard-negative sampling during contrastive pretraining, then add projection heads and fine-tune on downstream cybersecurity tasks.
Evaluate robustness on cross-environment / OOD splits to demonstrate reduced reliance on shortcuts and improved metrics (F1, recall) in production-like scenarios.
infographic.impact: Practitioners can leverage abundant textual signals (reports, logs, labels) to bootstrap reliable models for scarce modalities, improving detection/triage reliability and reducing false alarms when deployed in diverse, real-world environments.

title: From Masks to Pixels and Meaning: A New Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Metrics for VLM Image Tampering
authors: Xinyi Shang, Yi Tang, Jiacheng Cui, Ahmed Elhagry, Salwa K. Al Khatib
abstract: Existing tampering detection benchmarks largely rely on object masks, which severely misalign with the true edit signal: many pixels inside a mask are untouched or only trivially modified, while subtle yet consequential edits outside the mask are treated as natural. We reformulate VLM image tampering from coarse region labels to a pixel-grounded, meaning and language-aware task. First, we introduce a taxonomy spanning edit primitives (replace/remove/splice/inpaint/attribute/colorization, etc.) a

infographic.key_insight: Coarse object masks poorly reflect where meaningful image edits occur; reframing tampering detection as a pixel-grounded, language- and meaning-aware task yields more accurate benchmarks and evaluation metrics.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between region-level masks and true edit signals—many pixels inside masks are unchanged while important edits occur outside—preventing reliable evaluation of vision-language model (VLM) tampering detection.
method: Define a taxonomy of edit primitives (replace, remove, splice, inpaint, attribute change, colorization, etc.) and link them to semantic/language descriptions.
Construct a pixel-grounded benchmark with per-pixel edit maps and paired language prompts/descriptions to capture where and what was changed.
Design metrics that combine pixel-level edit localization accuracy with semantic alignment between detected edits and language descriptions for VLM evaluation.
infographic.impact: Enables more faithful training and evaluation of VLMs for tampering detection and image forensics, improving robustness to subtle and semantically meaningful edits and guiding dataset and metric design in future work.

title: VideoSeek: Long-Horizon Video Agent with Tool-Guided Seeking
authors: Jingyang Lin, Jialian Wu, Jiang Liu, Ximeng Sun, Ze Wang
abstract: Video agentic models have advanced challenging video-language tasks. However, most agentic approaches still heavily rely on greedy parsing over densely sampled video frames, resulting in high computational cost. We present VideoSeek, a long-horizon video agent that leverages video logic flow to actively seek answer-critical evidence instead of exhaustively parsing the full video. This insight allows the model to use far fewer frames while maintaining, or even improving, its video understanding c

infographic.key_insight: VideoSeek trains a long-horizon video agent to actively seek only answer-critical frames using a logic-flow-driven policy and tool guidance, dramatically reducing frame processing while preserving or improving understanding.
infographic.problem_solved: Current video agentic models exhaustively parse densely sampled frames, causing high computational cost and inefficiency for long videos; VideoSeek addresses the need to find evidence selectively across long horizons.
method: Logic-flow-driven seeking: model learns the video’s logical/event flow to predict where answer-critical evidence is likely to occur instead of uniform dense sampling.
Tool-guided exploration: integrates external tools/controllers (e.g., frame retrievers, temporal jump operators) to execute targeted seeks and extract high-value frames.
Agent architecture for long horizons: a planner+seeker loop that iteratively proposes seeks, queries tools, and updates beliefs until the answer is found with far fewer frames.
infographic.impact: Enables scalable, cost-effective video understanding for long videos—reducing compute and latency while maintaining or improving accuracy—making video QA, summarization, and reasoning more practical in real-world deployments.

title: Kolmogorov-Arnold causal generative models
authors: Alejandro Almodóvar, Mar Elizo, Patricia A. Apellániz, Santiago Zazo, Juan Parras
abstract: Causal generative models provide a principled framework for answering observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries from observational data. However, many deep causal models rely on highly expressive architectures with opaque mechanisms, limiting auditability in high-stakes domains. We propose KaCGM, a causal generative model for mixed-type tabular data where each structural equation is parameterized by a Kolmogorov--Arnold Network (KAN). This decomposition enables direct inspection

infographic.key_insight: KaCGM replaces opaque neural structural equations with Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) so each causal mechanism is decomposed into inspectable univariate components, yielding expressive yet auditable causal generative models for mixed-type tabular data.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between expressivity and auditability in deep causal generative models: existing black‑box architectures are powerful but hard to inspect, limiting their use in high‑stakes domains and for counterfactual reasoning on mixed‑type tabular data.
method: Parameterize each structural equation in a structural causal model with a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) that decomposes multivariate mappings into sums/compositions of univariate functions.
Train the KaCGM on mixed‑type tabular data to answer observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries while preserving model flexibility.
Expose and inspect the KAN component functions and their contributions for each variable to enable auditability and transparent causal explanations.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, auditable causal generative model that balances interpretability and expressiveness—useful for trustworthy decision‑making, regulation, and debugging in high‑stakes applications.

title: MME-CoF-Pro: Evaluating Reasoning Coherence in Video Generative Models with Text and Visual Hints
authors: Yu Qi, Xinyi Xu, Ziyu Guo, Siyuan Ma, Renrui Zhang
abstract: Video generative models show emerging reasoning behaviors. It is essential to ensure that generated events remain causally consistent across frames for reliable deployment, a property we define as reasoning coherence. To bridge the gap in literature for missing reasoning coherence evaluation, we propose MME-CoF-Pro, a comprehensive video reasoning benchmark to assess reasoning coherence in video models. Specifically, MME-CoF-Pro contains 303 samples across 16 categories, ranging from visual logi

infographic.key_insight: MME-CoF-Pro is a focused benchmark that quantifies whether video generative models maintain causal and temporal consistency (reasoning coherence) across frames by using both text and visual hints to probe model behavior.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized datasets and evaluation protocols for measuring reasoning/coherence of events in generated videos, enabling systematic detection of causal or temporal inconsistencies.
method: Curated benchmark: 303 video samples spanning 16 reasoning categories that test visual logic, temporal causality, object interactions, and other cross-frame behaviors.
Multimodal prompting: Uses combined text and visual hints to elicit and constrain model reasoning, revealing failures that appear only under specific cues.
Evaluation protocol: A reproducible scoring pipeline combining targeted automatic metrics and human-aligned judgments to measure event-level and frame-to-frame coherence.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a concrete tool to diagnose and compare reasoning failures in video generative models, guiding model selection, targeted training, and safer deployment by focusing on causal/temporal reliability.

title: CoVR-R:Reason-Aware Composed Video Retrieval
authors: Omkar Thawakar, Dmitry Demidov, Vaishnav Potlapalli, Sai Prasanna Teja Reddy Bogireddy, Viswanatha Reddy Gajjala
abstract: Composed Video Retrieval (CoVR) aims to find a target video given a reference video and a textual modification. Prior work assumes the modification text fully specifies the visual changes, overlooking after-effects and implicit consequences (e.g., motion, state transitions, viewpoint or duration cues) that emerge from the edit. We argue that successful CoVR requires reasoning about these after-effects. We introduce a reasoning-first, zero-shot approach that leverages large multimodal models to (

infographic.key_insight: Successful composed video retrieval requires reasoning about implicit after-effects (motion, state transitions, viewpoint/duration cues) that arise from an edit; CoVR-R is a reasoning-first, zero-shot method that uses large multimodal models to predict those consequences and augment retrieval queries.
infographic.problem_solved: Prior CoVR approaches assume the textual modification fully specifies the visual change and therefore miss implicit temporal and contextual cues (e.g., motion, state changes, viewpoint or duration) that are necessary to find the correct target video.
method: Leverage large multimodal models to perform explicit reasoning over a reference video + textual modification and predict implicit after-effects (temporal dynamics, viewpoint shifts, duration changes, etc.).
Convert the LMM's reasoning outputs into enriched retrieval signals (augmented textual prompts and/or multimodal embeddings) that capture both explicit edits and inferred consequences.
Perform zero-shot composed video retrieval by matching the enriched query against a candidate video pool using an off-the-shelf retrieval backbone or lightweight alignment module.
infographic.impact: By modeling implicit consequences of edits, CoVR-R improves robustness and relevance of composed video search without requiring paired training data; this enables more reliable, user-friendly video editing and media retrieval workflows for practitioners.

title: EgoForge: Goal-Directed Egocentric World Simulator
authors: Yifan Shen, Jiateng Liu, Xinzhuo Li, Yuanzhe Liu, Bingxuan Li
abstract: Generative world models have shown promise for simulating dynamic environments, yet egocentric video remains challenging due to rapid viewpoint changes, frequent hand-object interactions, and goal-directed procedures whose evolution depends on latent human intent. Existing approaches either focus on hand-centric instructional synthesis with limited scene evolution, perform static view translation without modeling action dynamics, or rely on dense supervision, such as camera trajectories, long vi

infographic.key_insight: EgoForge builds a goal‑conditioned egocentric world model that jointly predicts hands, objects, and viewpoint motion so it can simulate coherent, intent‑driven first‑person video rollouts over procedure‑scale horizons.
infographic.problem_solved: Models of egocentric video struggle with rapid camera motion, frequent hand–object interactions, and latent human intent; EgoForge addresses these to produce long‑horizon, goal‑directed egocentric simulations.
method: Learn a compact scene representation that separates agent (head/camera + hands) dynamics from object and environment state to handle rapid viewpoint changes and contact events.
Infer latent goals/intent from partial observations and condition a generative dynamics model to produce goal‑directed future states and rendered egocentric frames.
Train using multi‑task/self‑supervised objectives that emphasize physical consistency of interactions and temporal coherence rather than dense trajectory supervision.
infographic.impact: Enables realistic, actionable first‑person video prediction useful for imitation learning, AR/VR content generation, and robotic planning from human demonstrations with less reliance on dense supervision.

title: LumosX: Relate Any Identities with Their Attributes for Personalized Video Generation
authors: Jiazheng Xing, Fei Du, Hangjie Yuan, Pengwei Liu, Hongbin Xu
abstract: Recent advances in diffusion models have significantly improved text-to-video generation, enabling personalized content creation with fine-grained control over both foreground and background elements. However, precise face-attribute alignment across subjects remains challenging, as existing methods lack explicit mechanisms to ensure intra-group consistency. Addressing this gap requires both explicit modeling strategies and face-attribute-aware data resources. We therefore propose LumosX, a frame

infographic.key_insight: LumosX introduces explicit identity–attribute modeling and a face-attribute-aware data strategy to enforce consistent face-attribute alignment across multiple subjects and frames, improving precision in personalized text-to-video generation.
infographic.problem_solved: Current personalized video generation struggles to keep specified facial attributes (e.g., hairstyle, expression, accessories) consistently aligned across different subjects and frames because existing pipelines lack mechanisms and data tailored for intra-group face-attribute consistency.
method: Identity–Attribute Relational Module: explicitly links each subject identity to attribute embeddings so attributes can be consistently conditioned per identity during generation.
Face-Attribute-Aware Data Strategy: curate/annotate training data and sampling schemes that emphasize multi-subject, multi-attribute examples to teach intra-group consistency.

Consistency-Guided Diffusion Training: condition a diffusion-based video generator on identity–attribute signals and add face-attribute consistency and temporal regularization losses to preserve identity and attribute coherence across frames.
infographic.impact: Makes personalized video generation more reliable for applications requiring precise, repeatable control of facial attributes (avatars, virtual production, customized content), and provides a framework and data emphasis that can improve robustness and evaluation of identity-attribute fidelity.

title: MuSteerNet: Human Reaction Generation from Videos via Observation-Reaction Mutual Steering
authors: Yuan Zhou, Yongzhi Li, Yanqi Dai, Xingyu Zhu, Yi Tan
abstract: Video-driven human reaction generation aims to synthesize 3D human motions that directly react to observed video sequences, which is crucial for building human-like interactive AI systems. However, existing methods often fail to effectively leverage video inputs to steer human reaction synthesis, resulting in reaction motions that are mismatched with the content of video sequences. We reveal that this limitation arises from a severe relational distortion between visual observations and reaction

infographic.key_insight: MuSteerNet introduces an observation–reaction mutual steering mechanism that explicitly aligns visual observations with generated 3D human reactions, reducing relational distortion and producing reactions that better match video content.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing video-driven reaction generation methods fail to effectively use video cues, causing synthesized reactions to be mismatched with observed events due to distorted observation–reaction relationships.
method: Design MuSteerNet to enable bidirectional 'mutual steering' between a video observation pathway and a reaction generation pathway so each guides and refines the other.
Use iterative cross-modal interaction to align visual features and motion representations, progressively correcting relational distortion between observation and reaction.
Train the system end-to-end to produce temporally coherent 3D motion sequences that directly respond to input video content.
infographic.impact: Makes synthesized human reactions more accurate and context-aware, improving realism for interactive avatars, virtual agents, and human–robot systems; enables stronger multimodal alignment methods for downstream AI applications.

title: Under One Sun: Multi-Object Generative Perception of Materials and Illumination
authors: Nobuo Yoshii, Xinran Nicole Han, Ryo Kawahara, Todd Zickler, Ko Nishino
abstract: We introduce Multi-Object Generative Perception (MultiGP), a generative inverse rendering method for stochastic sampling of all radiometric constituents -- reflectance, texture, and illumination -- underlying object appearance from a single image. Our key idea to solve this inherently ambiguous radiometric disentanglement is to leverage the fact that while their texture and reflectance may differ, objects in the same scene are all lit by the same illumination. MultiGP exploits this consensus to

infographic.key_insight: By exploiting the fact that multiple objects in a single scene share the same illumination, MultiGP performs generative inverse rendering to stochastically disentangle reflectance, texture, and illumination from one image, yielding multiple plausible radiometric explanations.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the fundamentally ambiguous task of radiometric disentanglement from a single image — recovering object materials (reflectance and texture) and scene illumination jointly and robustly.
method: Generative inverse rendering that samples full radiometric constituents (reflectance, texture, illumination) to produce multiple plausible explanations for observed appearance.
Enforces a cross-object consensus constraint: different objects may have different materials/textures but are constrained to share the same scene illumination.
Probabilistic/stochastic sampling to capture ambiguity and present diverse plausible reconstructions rather than a single deterministic estimate.
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable single-image material and lighting estimation with uncertainty-aware outputs, improving downstream tasks like relighting, material editing, AR compositing, and scene understanding.

title: MonoArt: Progressive Structural Reasoning for Monocular Articulated 3D Reconstruction
authors: Haitian Li, Haozhe Xie, Junxiang Xu, Beichen Wen, Fangzhou Hong
abstract: Reconstructing articulated 3D objects from a single image requires jointly inferring object geometry, part structure, and motion parameters from limited visual evidence. A key difficulty lies in the entanglement between motion cues and object structure, which makes direct articulation regression unstable. Existing methods address this challenge through multi-view supervision, retrieval-based assembly, or auxiliary video generation, often sacrificing scalability or efficiency. We present MonoArt,

infographic.key_insight: Progressively reason about object structure before estimating motion to decouple geometry and articulation, enabling stable monocular reconstruction of articulated 3D objects from a single image.
infographic.problem_solved: Monocular reconstruction of articulated 3D objects is unstable because motion cues and part structure are entangled; prior solutions rely on multi-view data, retrieval, or auxiliary video, reducing scalability and efficiency.
method: Progressive structural reasoning: infer coarse-to-fine part layouts and connectivity first, then regress articulation parameters conditioned on the recovered structure.
Joint geometry-and-motion optimization with articulation-aware priors and differentiable assembly to ensure consistent part shapes, joints, and plausible motions from a single image.
Lightweight monocular pipeline that avoids heavy multi-view supervision or retrieval, using self-consistency and structure-driven constraints to stabilize learning.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable, efficient approach for single-image articulated 3D reconstruction useful for robotics, AR/VR, and animation; reduces data and compute requirements while improving stability of articulation estimates.

title: Online Learning and Equilibrium Computation with Ranking Feedback
authors: Mingyang Liu, Yongshan Chen, Zhiyuan Fan, Gabriele Farina, Asuman Ozdaglar
abstract: Online learning in arbitrary, and possibly adversarial, environments has been extensively studied in sequential decision-making, and it is closely connected to equilibrium computation in game theory. Most existing online learning algorithms rely on \emph{numeric} utility feedback from the environment, which may be unavailable in human-in-the-loop applications and/or may be restricted by privacy concerns. In this paper, we study an online learning model in which the learner only observes a \emph{

infographic.key_insight: Online learning and equilibrium computation are possible even when the learner receives only ordinal (ranking) feedback rather than numeric rewards; the paper designs algorithms that convert rankings into usable signals and prove provable sublinear regret and game-convergence guarantees.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses learning and equilibrium computation when numeric utility signals are unavailable or undesirable (e.g., human-in-the-loop settings or privacy constraints) and only rankings or ordinal comparisons are observed.
method: Formalize an online learning model where the learner observes only rankings/ordinal feedback over actions (possibly partial or adversarial).
Design ordinal-aware online algorithms that aggregate pairwise/comparative information and adapt standard online updates (e.g., FTRL/OMD-style principles) to operate on ranking signals.

Provide theoretical analysis: prove regret bounds for the ordinal algorithms and show that repeated play under ranking feedback converges to game-theoretic equilibria (enabling equilibrium computation without numeric utilities).
infographic.impact: Enables robust online decision-making and multi-agent equilibrium computation in settings with human preferences or privacy limits on numeric rewards, broadening applicability of online learning to real-world, ordinal-only feedback scenarios.

title: NavTrust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness for Embodied Navigation
authors: Huaide Jiang, Yash Chaudhary, Yuping Wang, Zehao Wang, Raghav Sharma
abstract: There are two major categories of embodied navigation: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN), where agents navigate by following natural language instructions; and Object-Goal Navigation (OGN), where agents navigate to a specified target object. However, existing work primarily evaluates model performance under nominal conditions, overlooking the potential corruptions that arise in real-world settings. To address this gap, we present NavTrust, a unified benchmark that systematically corrupts input mo

infographic.key_insight: NavTrust introduces a unified benchmark that systematically corrupts inputs to embodied navigation tasks (VLN and OGN) to quantify model trustworthiness under realistic failures, exposing robustness, calibration, and safety gaps missed by nominal evaluations.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for how embodied navigation agents perform and fail under real-world corruptions and perturbations across sensory and linguistic inputs.
method: Design a corruption suite that injects systematic perturbations across modalities (vision, depth, language, sensors) and varying severity levels.
Evaluate diverse VLN and OGN agents on the corrupted inputs using unified trustworthiness metrics (robustness, calibration, safety/failure modes) and produce comparative leaderboards.
Provide reproducible tools and protocols to measure degradation patterns and identify failure modes for model diagnosis and improvement.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and engineers to benchmark and prioritize improvements for real-world deployment by revealing brittle behaviors, guiding robust model design, and standardizing trust-focused evaluation of embodied navigation.

title: F2LLM-v2: Inclusive, Performant, and Efficient Embeddings for a Multilingual World
authors: Ziyin Zhang, Zihan Liao, Hang Yu, Peng Di, Rui Wang
abstract: We present F2LLM-v2, a new family of general-purpose, multilingual embedding models in 8 distinct sizes ranging from 80M to 14B. Trained on a newly curated composite of 60 million publicly available high-quality data samples, F2LLM-v2 supports more than 200 languages, with a particular emphasis on previously underserved mid- and low-resource languages. By integrating a two-stage LLM-based embedding training pipeline with matryoshka learning, model pruning, and knowledge distillation techniques,

infographic.key_insight: F2LLM-v2 is a scalable family of multilingual embeddings (80M–14B) trained on 60M high-quality public samples that boosts representation quality for 200+ languages—with a focus on mid- and low-resource—by combining a two-stage LLM-driven training pipeline with matryoshka learning, pruning, and distillation.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-quality multilingual embedding performance and practical efficiency/scale, especially improving coverage and accuracy for underrepresented mid- and low-resource languages while offering deployable models across a wide range of sizes.
method: Curated a 60M-sample multilingual training composite covering 200+ languages, prioritizing mid- and low-resource data quality and diversity.

Two-stage LLM-based embedding training pipeline: LLM-guided supervision/alignment followed by scale-aware fine-tuning using matryoshka learning to transfer capabilities across 8 model sizes (80M–14B).
Model compression and efficiency: iterative pruning and knowledge distillation to produce performant, resource-friendly variants while preserving multilingual fidelity.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners ready-to-use, size-flexible multilingual embeddings that improve search/retrieval and downstream tasks for many languages—enabling better performance in production-constrained settings and for previously underserved languages.

title: Generation Models Know Space: Unleashing Implicit 3D Priors for Scene Understanding
authors: Xianjin Wu, Dingkang Liang, Tianrui Feng, Kui Xia, Yumeng Zhang
abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models demonstrate impressive semantic capabilities, they often suffer from spatial blindness, struggling with fine-grained geometric reasoning and physical dynamics. Existing solutions typically rely on explicit 3D modalities or complex geometric scaffolding, which are limited by data scarcity and generalization challenges. In this work, we propose a paradigm shift by leveraging the implicit spatial prior within large-scale video generation models. We posit that

infographic.key_insight: Pretrained large-scale video generation models implicitly encode rich 3D spatial priors that can be extracted and reused to give models fine-grained geometric reasoning without relying on explicit 3D data.
infographic.problem_solved: Multimodal models are spatially blind — they struggle with detailed geometry and physical dynamics — and existing solutions rely on scarce explicit 3D data or complex geometric scaffolds that limit generalization.
method: Probe and extract spatio-temporal latents from pretrained video generation models that contain implicit 3D structure.
Distill those implicit priors into compact geometric prediction heads (e.g., depth, normals, occupancy, dynamics) with minimal or no explicit 3D supervision.
Align generation-derived priors to downstream scene-understanding tasks via lightweight adapters and task-specific finetuning for improved generalization.
infographic.impact: Enables robust 3D-aware scene understanding without expensive 3D datasets or heavy geometric engineering, accelerating deployment of spatially competent multimodal systems in robotics, AR/VR, and vision-language applications.

title: Bridging Semantic and Kinematic Conditions with Diffusion-based Discrete Motion Tokenizer
authors: Chenyang Gu, Mingyuan Zhang, Haozhe Xie, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang
abstract: Prior motion generation largely follows two paradigms: continuous diffusion models that excel at kinematic control, and discrete token-based generators that are effective for semantic conditioning. To combine their strengths, we propose a three-stage framework comprising condition feature extraction (Perception), discrete token generation (Planning), and diffusion-based motion synthesis (Control). Central to this framework is MoTok, a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer that decouples sema

infographic.key_insight: MoTok introduces a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer within a three-stage Perception–Planning–Control pipeline, enabling planners to use discrete semantic tokens while a diffusion synthesizer preserves high-fidelity kinematics. This bridges the semantic strength of token-based methods and the fine-grained control of continuous diffusion models.
infographic.problem_solved: Previous motion-generation approaches either provide strong kinematic fidelity (continuous diffusion) or good semantic conditioning (discrete tokens), but not both. The paper solves how to decouple and connect semantic planning and kinematic control so models can accept semantic conditions without sacrificing motion quality.
method: Perception: extract condition features (semantic labels, language, or scene/context) as inputs for planning.
Planning: generate discrete motion tokens with MoTok — a diffusion-based tokenizer that encodes semantic intent into discrete token sequences.
Control: use a diffusion-based motion synthesizer conditioned on the discrete tokens to reconstruct smooth, high-fidelity kinematic motion.
infographic.impact: Allows practitioners to combine interpretable, discrete semantic planning with state-of-the-art continuous motion synthesis, improving controllability and realism for animation, avatars, and robotics. It streamlines pipelines where high-level intent must be translated into physically plausible motion.

title: SAMA: Factorized Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
authors: Xinyao Zhang, Wenkai Dong, Yuxin Song, Bo Fang, Qi Zhang
abstract: Current instruction-guided video editing models struggle to simultaneously balance precise semantic modifications with faithful motion preservation. While existing approaches rely on injecting explicit external priors (e.g., VLM features or structural conditions) to mitigate these issues, this reliance severely bottlenecks model robustness and generalization. To overcome this limitation, we present SAMA (factorized Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment), a framework that factorizes video editi

infographic.key_insight: SAMA factorizes instruction-guided video editing into two complementary components—Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment—so the model can apply precise semantic edits while faithfully preserving original motion, without heavy reliance on external priors.
infographic.problem_solved: Balances accurate, instruction-driven semantic changes with temporal/motion fidelity in video editing, addressing robustness and generalization limits caused by dependence on external priors (e.g., VLM features or structural conditions).
method: Semantic Anchoring: isolate and apply instruction-specified semantic modifications to target objects/regions while keeping anchored appearance cues to avoid drift.
Motion Alignment: explicitly model and preserve temporal motion patterns (e.g., flow or temporal features) to maintain realistic, coherent movement across frames.
Internal factorization strategy: combine the two modules in a unified pipeline that reduces reliance on external priors, improving robustness and generalization to diverse videos and instructions.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to produce more faithful, instruction-guided video edits that retain original motion and temporal coherence, reducing engineering effort for external conditioning and improving performance on varied real-world inputs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two parallel branches: Semantic Anchoring (semantic map / text → edit) and Motion Alignment (flow / temporal stream → preserve motion), merging into edited video output.

title: Matryoshka Gaussian Splatting
authors: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Hakan Aktas, Kyle Fogarty, Jeffrey Hu
abstract: The ability to render scenes at adjustable fidelity from a single model, known as level of detail (LoD), is crucial for practical deployment of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Existing discrete LoD methods expose only a limited set of operating points, while concurrent continuous LoD approaches enable smoother scaling but often suffer noticeable quality degradation at full capacity, making LoD a costly design decision. We introduce Matryoshka Gaussian Splatting (MGS), a training framework that ena

infographic.key_insight: Matryoshka Gaussian Splatting (MGS) trains and organizes Gaussian splats into nested subsets so a single model provides smooth, continuous level-of-detail (LoD) scaling while retaining full-capacity fidelity.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing LoD schemes either offer only a few discrete operating points or continuous scaling that degrades peak quality; MGS removes this trade-off so practitioners can choose any fidelity/compute point without sacrificing final-render quality.
method: Arrange Gaussians into a nested (Matryoshka-like) ordering so smaller subsets form valid lower-fidelity models and larger subsets progressively add detail.
Train with scheduling and objectives that ensure each subset approximates the full model and prevent quality drop at full capacity.
Enable runtime selection of subset size to smoothly trade compute, memory, and rendering quality across a continuous range.
infographic.impact: MGS simplifies deployment of 3D Gaussian Splatting by enabling a single model to serve devices and pipelines with varied compute budgets, improving interactive render performance and reducing engineering overhead for multi-fidelity support.
visual_elements: Matryoshka-doll analogy overlay: nested shells of Gaussians showing increasing detail from core to outer layers.
Quality vs. compute chart: MGS curve showing smooth scaling and high peak quality versus discrete baselines and continuous methods that dip at full capacity.
Side-by-side renders at multiple LoDs: same scene rendered by small, medium, and full subsets to show fidelity progression.
Pipeline diagram: nested subset selection, training schedule, and runtime switching flow.

title: Cubic Discrete Diffusion: Discrete Visual Generation on High-Dimensional Representation Tokens
authors: Yuqing Wang, Chuofan Ma, Zhijie Lin, Yao Teng, Lijun Yu
abstract: Visual generation with discrete tokens has gained significant attention as it enables a unified token prediction paradigm shared with language models, promising seamless multimodal architectures. However, current discrete generation methods remain limited to low-dimensional latent tokens (typically 8-32 dims), sacrificing the semantic richness essential for understanding. While high-dimensional pretrained representations (768-1024 dims) could bridge this gap, their discrete generation poses fund

infographic.key_insight: This paper shows how to perform discrete-token diffusion directly on high-dimensional pretrained visual representations, preserving rich semantics while enabling a unified token-prediction generation paradigm similar to language models.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing discrete visual-generation methods restrict tokens to low-dimensional latents (8–32 dims), losing semantic richness; generating discrete high-dimensional representations (768–1024 dims) is combinatorially hard and unstable with prior discrete diffusion techniques.
method: Introduce a 'cubic' factorization of high-dimensional representation tokens that breaks each vector into structured subcomponents amenable to discrete modeling.
Design a discrete diffusion process and noise schedule that operate on the factorized components, together with a denoising network that predicts component tokens in a categorical/tokenwise manner.

Leverage pretrained high-dimensional encoders as targets/conditioning and train the diffusion denoiser to reconstruct their discrete factor components, enabling efficient sampling and scalable token prediction.
infographic.impact: Enables language-model-style discrete generation for richer visual representations, improving semantic fidelity and simplifying integration into multimodal architectures; useful for practitioners building generative vision–language systems and token-based pipelines.

title: FinTradeBench: A Financial Reasoning Benchmark for LLMs
authors: Yogesh Agrawal, Aniruddha Dutta, Md Mahadi Hasan, Santu Karmaker, Aritra Dutta
abstract: Real-world financial decision-making is a challenging problem that requires reasoning over heterogeneous signals, including company fundamentals derived from regulatory filings and trading signals computed from price dynamics. Recently, with the advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), financial analysts have begun to use them for financial decision-making tasks. However, existing financial question answering benchmarks for testing these models primarily focus on company balance sheet data a

infographic.key_insight: FinTradeBench introduces a unified benchmark that tests LLMs' ability to reason across heterogeneous financial signals — combining company fundamentals from filings with trading signals from price dynamics — to better reflect real-world financial decision-making.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing financial QA benchmarks focus narrowly on balance-sheet or single-source data and fail to evaluate reasoning that integrates regulatory fundamentals with time-series trading signals; FinTradeBench fills this gap by providing multi-signal tasks tailored to practical investment decisions.
method: Curate multi-source data: align regulatory filing-derived fundamentals with computed trading signals (price, momentum, volatility) to create task inputs that reflect real-world information mixes.
Design diverse tasks and evaluation protocols that require cross-signal reasoning (interpretation, forecasting, and decision justification) rather than surface QA.
Benchmark multiple LLMs with standardized prompts and metrics, analyze failure modes, and provide task-level diagnostics to guide model improvements.
infographic.impact: FinTradeBench gives AI/ML practitioners a realistic testbed to assess and improve LLMs for financial reasoning, enabling better model selection, fine-tuning strategies, and risk-aware deployment in finance applications.

title: Gender Disambiguation in Machine Translation: Diagnostic Evaluation in Decoder-Only Architectures
authors: Chiara Manna, Hosein Mohebbi, Afra Alishahi, Frédéric Blain, Eva Vanmassenhove
abstract: While Large Language Models achieve state-of-the-art results across a wide range of NLP tasks, they remain prone to systematic biases. Among these, gender bias is particularly salient in MT, due to systematic differences across languages in whether and how gender is marked. As a result, translation often requires disambiguating implicit source signals into explicit gender-marked forms. In this context, standard benchmarks may capture broad disparities but fail to reflect the full complexity of g

infographic.key_insight: Decoder-only LLMs exhibit systematic and distinct failure modes when translating gender-ambiguous source text into gender-marked target languages; a focused diagnostic evaluation reveals sensitivity to prompt context, model size, and formulation that standard benchmarks miss.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of fine-grained evaluation for gender disambiguation in machine translation, specifically diagnosing how decoder-only architectures convert implicit gender cues into explicit, gender-marked target forms and where they systematically fail or amplify bias.
method: Construct a controlled diagnostic benchmark of gender-ambiguous source sentences and target languages that require explicit gender marking (varying occupations, pronouns, and contextual cues).

Evaluate decoder-only models using targeted protocols: prompt variations, explicit context injection, and model-size comparisons; measure accuracy, bias amplification, and calibration for gender choices.
Analyze failure modes and sensitivities (e.g., context length, prompt phrasing, language pairs) to produce reproducible diagnostics and recommendations for evaluation practice.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners with a focused evaluation toolkit to detect and quantify gender-disambiguation failures in decoder-only MT systems, informing safer deployment, prompt design, and targeted mitigation strategies.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → prompt/context variations → decoder-only model → gender-marked translations (high-level flow).

title: AHOY! Animatable Humans under Occlusion from YouTube Videos with Gaussian Splatting and Video Diffusion Priors
authors: Aymen Mir, Riza Alp Guler, Xiangjun Tang, Peter Wonka, Gerard Pons-Moll
abstract: We present AHOY, a method for reconstructing complete, animatable 3D Gaussian avatars from in-the-wild monocular video despite heavy occlusion. Existing methods assume unoccluded input-a fully visible subject, often in a canonical pose-excluding the vast majority of real-world footage where people are routinely occluded by furniture, objects, or other people. Reconstructing from such footage poses fundamental challenges: large body regions may never be observed, and multi-view supervision per po

infographic.key_insight: AHOY reconstructs complete, animatable 3D human avatars from in-the-wild monocular videos with heavy occlusion by combining a Gaussian-splat representation with video diffusion priors to plausibly fill unobserved regions and enable animation.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing 3D human reconstruction methods require largely unoccluded, canonical-pose footage; AHOY addresses the challenge of building full, animatable avatars when large body regions are never observed in monocular, in-the-wild videos (e.g., YouTube clips).
method: Represent the subject as a 3D Gaussian-splat avatar optimized from monocular video frames for fast, view-consistent rendering.
Use video diffusion priors to hallucinate and regularize plausibly missing geometry and appearance in heavily occluded regions across frames.
Enforce temporal and pose consistency and rigging (animatable topology) so the reconstructed avatar can be driven/animated post-reconstruction.
infographic.impact: Enables building realistic, animatable human avatars from abundant real-world footage (e.g., YouTube) despite occlusions, lowering data requirements and expanding applicability to downstream AR/VR, games, and content creation workflows.

title: Universal Skeleton Understanding via Differentiable Rendering and MLLMs
authors: Ziyi Wang, Peiming Li, Xinshun Wang, Yang Tang, Kai-Kuang Ma
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) exhibit strong visual-language reasoning, yet remain confined to their native modalities and cannot directly process structured, non-visual data such as human skeletons. Existing methods either compress skeleton dynamics into lossy feature vectors for text alignment, or quantize motion into discrete tokens that generalize poorly across heterogeneous skeleton formats. We present SkeletonLLM, which achieves universal skeleton understanding by translating ar

infographic.key_insight: SkeletonLLM converts structured, non-visual skeleton data into differentiable visual representations that MLLMs can directly understand, enabling end-to-end training and generalization across heterogeneous skeleton formats.
infographic.problem_solved: MLLMs cannot natively process structured motion/skeleton data; prior solutions either compress dynamics into lossy vectors or quantize motions into discrete tokens that fail to generalize across different skeleton formats and semantics.
method: Differentiable rendering: transform raw skeletons (varying joints/formats and temporal sequences) into canonical, learnable visual representations while keeping the pipeline differentiable.
MLLM integration: feed rendered visualizations into a pre-trained multimodal LLM to leverage its language-visual reasoning for tasks like description, querying, and editing.

End-to-end alignment & normalization: jointly optimize renderer and model with language supervision and format-agnostic normalization so the system generalizes across skeleton conventions and motion styles.
infographic.impact: Enables MLLMs to reason about and manipulate structured human-motion data without bespoke tokenization or format-specific encoders, simplifying workflows for action understanding, animation editing, human–robot interaction, and biomechanics research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw heterogeneous skeletons → differentiable renderer → rendered frames/heatmaps → MLLM → language/controls (include gradient arrows for end-to-end training).
Before/after comparison: (left) lossy vector or tokenized approaches vs (right) SkeletonLLM retaining structure and temporal dynamics.
Example gallery: rendered skeleton sequences with corresponding MLLM outputs (descriptions, queries, editing commands).

title: Unified Spatio-Temporal Token Scoring for Efficient Video VLMs
authors: Jianrui Zhang, Yue Yang, Rohun Tripathi, Winson Han, Ranjay Krishna
abstract: Token pruning is essential for enhancing the computational efficiency of vision-language models (VLMs), particularly for video-based tasks where temporal redundancy is prevalent. Prior approaches typically prune tokens either (1) within the vision transformer (ViT) exclusively for unimodal perception tasks such as action recognition and object segmentation, without adapting to downstream vision-language tasks; or (2) only within the LLM while leaving the ViT output intact, often requiring comple

infographic.key_insight: Introduce a unified spatio-temporal token scoring mechanism that identifies and prunes redundant visual tokens across both space and time, enabling efficient video vision-language models while preserving task-relevant information.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces excessive compute and temporal redundancy in video VLMs by jointly determining which spatial patches and temporal frames are essential for downstream vision-language tasks, instead of pruning independently in the ViT or LLM.
method: Compute unified importance scores for tokens that combine spatial and temporal cues, producing a single relevance measure per patch across frames.
Apply adaptive pruning based on those scores to discard redundant tokens early, with gating that preserves tokens critical to downstream vision-language objectives.
Integrate the scoring/pruning pipeline into the video VLM so pruning decisions are informed by end-task supervision rather than unimodal heuristics.
infographic.impact: Makes video VLMs substantially more compute- and latency-efficient with minimal performance loss, enabling scalable deployment for real-time and large-scale multimodal applications.

title: LoST: Level of Semantics Tokenization for 3D Shapes
authors: Niladri Shekhar Dutt, Zifan Shi, Paul Guerrero, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Duygu Ceylan
abstract: Tokenization is a fundamental technique in the generative modeling of various modalities. In particular, it plays a critical role in autoregressive (AR) models, which have recently emerged as a compelling option for 3D generation. However, optimal tokenization of 3D shapes remains an open question. State-of-the-art (SOTA) methods primarily rely on geometric level-of-detail (LoD) hierarchies, originally designed for rendering and compression. These spatial hierarchies are often token-inefficient

infographic.key_insight: Replace geometry-driven level-of-detail tokenization with a learned, multi-scale semantic tokenization (LoST) so 3D shapes are represented by fewer, semantically meaningful tokens that are better suited for autoregressive generative models.
infographic.problem_solved: Current 3D tokenization relies on spatial LoD hierarchies designed for rendering/compression, which produce many redundant, token-inefficient representations that hurt autoregressive generation quality, scalability, and control.
method: Learn a hierarchy of semantic groupings across scales to produce tokens that represent parts and structural semantics rather than raw geometric patches.
Construct a Level-of-Semantics token hierarchy (LoST) to replace geometric LoD; emit compact multi-scale tokens for each shape.
Plug LoST tokens into autoregressive generative pipelines, reducing token count while improving generation fidelity and controllability.
infographic.impact: LoST makes autoregressive 3D generation more token- and compute-efficient, improving quality, speed, and downstream editing/conditioning capabilities—enabling larger models and datasets to be used practically.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: geometric LoD tokenization vs LoST semantic tokenization with token overlays on a 3D model and token counts.
Pipeline flowchart: 3D input → LoST encoder → semantic token hierarchy → autoregressive generator → reconstructed/generated shape.

title: Versatile Editing of Video Content, Actions, and Dynamics without Training
authors: Vladimir Kulikov, Roni Paiss, Andrey Voynov, Inbar Mosseri, Tali Dekel
abstract: Controlled video generation has seen drastic improvements in recent years. However, editing actions and dynamic events, or inserting contents that should affect the behaviors of other objects in real-world videos, remains a major challenge. Existing trained models struggle with complex edits, likely due to the difficulty of collecting relevant training data. Similarly, existing training-free methods are inherently restricted to structure- and motion-preserving edits and do not support modificati

infographic.key_insight: A training-free, inference-time editing approach enables versatile modifications of video content, actions, and dynamics — including inserting elements that causally influence other objects — without requiring task-specific retraining.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes limits of trained and existing training-free methods that either need large, specialized datasets or only support structure- and motion-preserving edits; enables complex action/dynamics changes and causal insertions in real-world videos.
method: Training-free inference: perform edits at test time using off-the-shelf pre-trained generative/video models and optimization instead of collecting new training data.
Spatio-temporal control: combine spatial masks, temporal constraints, and action-aware correspondences to rewrite object behaviors and global dynamics across frames.
Causal insertion mechanism: insert new content that interacts with and alters the motion/dynamics of existing objects by reasoning about inter-object effects over time.
infographic.impact: Allows AI/ML practitioners and content creators to prototype and deploy complex, causally-aware video edits quickly without costly data collection or model retraining, expanding possibilities for creative editing, simulation, and analysis.

High-level pipeline diagram: input video + edit specification → training-free optimization/inference → edited video output

title: VideoAtlas: Navigating Long-Form Video in Logarithmic Compute
authors: Mohamed Eltahir, Ali Habibullah, Yazan Alshoibi, Lama Ayash, Tanveer Hussain
abstract: Extending language models to video introduces two challenges: representation, where existing methods rely on lossy approximations, and long-context, where caption- or agent-based pipelines collapse video into text and lose visual fidelity. To overcome this, we introduce \textbf{VideoAtlas}, a task-agnostic environment to represent video as a hierarchical grid that is simultaneously lossless, navigable, scalable, caption- and preprocessing-free. An overview of the video is available at a glance,

infographic.key_insight: VideoAtlas represents long videos as a lossless, hierarchical grid (an "atlas") that can be navigated coarse-to-fine, enabling efficient, logarithmic compute access to any temporal/spatial region without captions or heavy preprocessing.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes lossy video representations and long-context collapse (where videos are reduced to text or short clips), enabling scalable, high-fidelity access to full-length videos.
method: Hierarchical grid (atlas) representation that partitions video into multi-resolution tiles, preserving original pixels and metadata.
Navigable, task-agnostic indexing enabling coarse-to-fine retrieval so operations touch only O(log N) tiles rather than the full video.
Caption- and preprocessing-free pipeline: overview-at-a-glance plus selective zooming for downstream models or human inspection.
infographic.impact: Makes long-form video modeling and multimodal tasks practical at scale by reducing compute and preprocessing while retaining visual fidelity, improving downstream performance and exploratory analysis workflows.

title: EchoGen: Cycle-Consistent Learning for Unified Layout-Image Generation and Understanding
authors: Kai Zou, Hongbo Liu, Dian Zheng, Jianxiong Gao, Zhiwei Zhao
abstract: In this work, we present EchoGen, a unified framework for layout-to-image generation and image grounding, capable of generating images with accurate layouts and high fidelity to text descriptions (e.g., spatial relationships), while grounding the image robustly at the same time. We believe that image grounding possesses strong text and layout understanding abilities, which can compensate for the corresponding limitations in layout-to-image generation. At the same time, images generated from layo

infographic.key_insight: EchoGen unifies layout-to-image generation and image grounding in a single cycle-consistent framework so that generation and spatial understanding mutually improve each other, producing images that better respect layouts and textual spatial relations.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-fidelity layout-conditioned image generation and accurate spatial grounding: current generators can violate specified layouts or text-specified relations, and grounding models lack jointly trained generative feedback.
method: Unified architecture that couples a layout-conditioned image generator with an image grounding module, sharing features and supervision.
Cycle-consistency training: generated images are re-grounded and compared back to the input layout/text (and vice versa) to enforce spatial and semantic consistency.
Joint losses (generation fidelity + grounding accuracy + cycle-consistency) to align visual synthesis with layout/text constraints during end-to-end training.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to produce images that reliably obey specified layouts and spatial text constraints while retaining strong grounding — useful for controllable generation, data augmentation, and downstream multimodal tasks.

title: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse
authors: Zhang Zhang, Shuqi Lu, Hongjin Qian, Di He, Zheng Liu
abstract: Building LLM-based agents has become increasingly important. Recent works on LLM-based agent self-evolution primarily record successful experiences as textual prompts or reflections, which cannot reliably guarantee efficient task re-execution in complex scenarios. We propose AgentFactory, a new self-evolution paradigm that preserves successful task solutions as executable subagent code rather than textual experience. Crucially, these subagents are continuously refined based on execution feedback

infographic.key_insight: Instead of saving successful experiences as text, AgentFactory records them as executable subagent code and continuously refines those subagents via execution feedback, enabling reliable re‑execution and composition for complex tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Current LLM-agent self-evolution stores solutions as textual prompts/reflections that are brittle and hard to re-run or compose reliably in complex, stateful scenarios; AgentFactory addresses reproducibility, reliability, and reuse.
method: Encode successful task solutions as executable subagents (small, testable code modules) rather than textual memories or prompts.
Accumulate and manage a library/registry of subagents for selection, composition, and reuse across new tasks.
Continuously validate and refine subagents using execution feedback (automated test runs, failure-triggered edits, and performance-driven updates).
infographic.impact: Makes LLM-based agents more reproducible, debuggable, and scalable by turning experience into reusable, executable components—improving reliability on complex workflows and enabling easier transfer and composition of capabilities.

title: Loc3R-VLM: Language-based Localization and 3D Reasoning with Vision-Language Models
authors: Kevin Qu, Haozhe Qi, Mihai Dusmanu, Mahdi Rad, Rui Wang
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have made impressive progress in connecting vision and language, but they still struggle with spatial understanding and viewpoint-aware reasoning. Recent efforts aim to augment the input representations with geometric cues rather than explicitly teaching models to reason in 3D space. We introduce Loc3R-VLM, a framework that equips 2D Vision-Language Models with advanced 3D understanding capabilities from monocular video input. Inspired by human spatial co

infographic.key_insight: Loc3R-VLM teaches 2D vision-language models to perform viewpoint-aware, language-guided localization and 3D reasoning from monocular video, enabling true spatial understanding without requiring dense geometric inputs.
infographic.problem_solved: Multimodal LLMs and VLMs lack robust spatial and viewpoint-aware reasoning; this work closes the gap by enabling 3D-aware localization and reasoning using only monocular video and language supervision.
method: Extract temporal and viewpoint cues from monocular video to build a lightweight 3D-aware scene representation that complements 2D VLM inputs.
Integrate a language-conditioned localization module that maps natural-language queries to positions/objects in the reconstructed 3D scene and enables viewpoint-relative reasoning.
Fine-tune the VLM with 3D supervisory signals and cross-modal alignment losses so it learns to reason about geometry and occlusion rather than relying on added geometric inputs.
infographic.impact: Enables VLMs to answer viewpoint-dependent questions, localize language references in 3D, and support applications in robotics, AR, and embodied agents without requiring multi-view rigs or dense depth sensors. This makes spatially-aware multimodal capabilities more accessible and practical.

title: SOMA: Unifying Parametric Human Body Models
authors: Jun Saito, Jiefeng Li, Michael de Ruyter, Miguel Guerrero, Edy Lim
abstract: Parametric human body models are foundational to human reconstruction, animation, and simulation, yet they remain mutually incompatible: SMPL, SMPL-X, MHR, Anny, and related models each diverge in mesh topology, skeletal structure, shape parameterization, and unit convention, making it impractical to exploit their complementary strengths within a single pipeline. We present SOMA, a unified body layer that bridges these heterogeneous representations through three abstraction layers. Mesh topology

infographic.key_insight: SOMA provides a unified body layer that bridges diverse parametric human models (SMPL, SMPL‑X, MHR, Anny, etc.) via three abstraction layers, enabling loss-minimized interoperability across mesh topology, skeletons, shape spaces, and unit conventions.
infographic.problem_solved: Parametric human body models are mutually incompatible in mesh topology, skeletal structure, shape parameterization, and units, which prevents combining their complementary strengths in a single reconstruction/animation/simulation pipeline.
method: Define a canonical representation and three abstraction layers (topology, skeletal/joint mapping, and shape/pose/units) that mediate between model-specific formats.
Implement bidirectional mappings/converters that preserve geometry and semantics to translate models to/from the SOMA canonical layer with minimal loss.
Expose a modular API/layer that integrates into existing reconstruction, animation, and simulation pipelines to enable mixed-model workflows and dataset reuse.
infographic.impact: Makes it practical for AI/ML practitioners to mix and match parametric body models and datasets, improving flexibility, interoperability, and overall performance in 3D human reconstruction, animation, and simulation workflows.

title: SparkVSR: Interactive Video Super-Resolution via Sparse Keyframe Propagation
authors: Jiongze Yu, Xiangbo Gao, Pooja Verlani, Akshay Gadde, Yilin Wang
abstract: Video Super-Resolution (VSR) aims to restore high-quality video frames from low-resolution (LR) estimates, yet most existing VSR approaches behave like black boxes at inference time: users cannot reliably correct unexpected artifacts, but instead can only accept whatever the model produces. In this paper, we propose a novel interactive VSR framework dubbed SparkVSR that makes sparse keyframes a simple and expressive control signal. Specifically, users can first super-resolve or optionally a smal

infographic.key_insight: SparkVSR makes VSR controllable by letting users provide or edit a small number of high-quality keyframes which are then propagated to the rest of the video, enabling reliable correction of artifacts with minimal user effort.
infographic.problem_solved: Most VSR methods are black boxes at inference time—users cannot fix unexpected artifacts or guide reconstruction. This paper addresses the need for an interactive, user-controllable VSR pipeline that achieves high quality with sparse supervision.
method: Treat a sparse set of user-provided super-resolved keyframes as an explicit control signal.
Learn a propagation module that transfers high-frequency details from keyframes to neighboring frames with temporal consistency and occlusion-aware blending.
Design for interactivity and efficiency so users can iteratively edit few keyframes and quickly update the whole video.
infographic.impact: Enables human-in-the-loop VSR workflows where practitioners or end-users can correct artifacts, steer output quality, and reduce compute by focusing effort on a few keyframes—improving trust and practicality of VSR systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: keyframe selection → user edit/super-resolve → learned propagation → final frames

title: Efficient Reasoning on the Edge
authors: Yelysei Bondarenko, Thomas Hehn, Rob Hesselink, Romain Lepert, Fabio Valerio Massoli
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) with chain-of-thought reasoning achieve state-of-the-art performance across complex problem-solving tasks, but their verbose reasoning traces and large context requirements make them impractical for edge deployment. These challenges include high token generation costs, large KV-cache footprints, and inefficiencies when distilling reasoning capabilities into smaller models for mobile devices. Existing approaches often rely on distilling reasoning traces from larger mo

infographic.key_insight: Chain-of-thought reasoning can be made practical for edge devices by compressing verbose reasoning traces into compact, cache-friendly representations and distilling those compressed plans into small models — dramatically reducing token generation and KV-cache overhead without discarding the reasoning itself.
infographic.problem_solved: Makes LLM-style chain-of-thought reasoning feasible on resource-constrained edge hardware by addressing high token costs, large KV-cache footprints, and inefficient distillation of verbose reasoning traces into mobile models.
method: Compress verbose reasoning traces into compact latent or sketch representations that preserve reasoning steps but use far fewer tokens.
Adopt KV-cache–efficient inference (e.g., quantization, selective retrieval, or sparse storage) so cached reasoning state fits on-device with low memory and compute.
Distill reasoning into small student models via a two-stage teacher→compressed-plan→student pipeline where students learn to expand compact plans into full reasoning at inference time.
infographic.impact: Enables low-latency, low-memory chain-of-thought inference on phones and embedded devices, improving privacy, responsiveness, and energy efficiency for real-world mobile AI applications.
visual_elements: Before/After bar chart comparing token counts, KV-cache size, and latency (large LLM vs. compressed-edge pipeline).
Teacher→Compressor→Student diagram showing compressed plan passing from a large model to an on-device model.

title: SocialOmni: Benchmarking Audio-Visual Social Interactivity in Omni Models
authors: Tianyu Xie, Jinfa Huang, Yuexiao Ma, Rongfang Luo, Yan Yang
abstract: Omni-modal large language models (OLMs) redefine human-machine interaction by natively integrating audio, vision, and text. However, existing OLM benchmarks remain anchored to static, accuracy-centric tasks, leaving a critical gap in assessing social interactivity, the fundamental capacity to navigate dynamic cues in natural dialogues. To this end, we propose SocialOmni, a comprehensive benchmark that operationalizes the evaluation of this conversational interactivity across three core dimension

infographic.key_insight: SocialOmni introduces a focused benchmark for evaluating audio-visual social interactivity in omni-modal LLMs, shifting evaluation from static accuracy to dynamic conversational competence across multimodal cues.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing omni-modal model benchmarks emphasize static, accuracy-centric tasks and fail to measure models' ability to interpret and respond to time-varying social signals in natural dialogues. SocialOmni fills this gap by operationalizing social interactivity evaluation for audio-visual-text models.
method: Define three core dimensions of conversational interactivity (e.g., temporal responsiveness, multimodal grounding, social appropriateness) and corresponding metrics.
Curate audio–visual conversational scenarios and annotation protocols that capture dynamic cues (speech prosody, gestures, gaze, turn-taking) and social responses.
Provide standardized evaluation suites and baseline OLM assessments to quantify strengths/weaknesses across the three dimensions.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners and researchers to diagnose and improve omni-modal models' real-world conversational behavior, guiding development of systems that are more socially aware and reliable in interactive settings.

Tri-axis radar chart comparing model performance across the three social-interactivity dimensions

title: ManiTwin: Scaling Data-Generation-Ready Digital Object Dataset to 100K
authors: Kaixuan Wang, Tianxing Chen, Jiawei Liu, Honghao Su, Shaolong Zhu
abstract: Learning in simulation provides a useful foundation for scaling robotic manipulation capabilities. However, this paradigm often suffers from a lack of data-generation-ready digital assets, in both scale and diversity. In this work, we present ManiTwin, an automated and efficient pipeline for generating data-generation-ready digital object twins. Our pipeline transforms a single image into simulation-ready and semantically annotated 3D asset, enabling large-scale robotic manipulation data generat

infographic.key_insight: ManiTwin automates conversion of a single image into a simulation-ready, semantically annotated 3D object twin, enabling generation of large-scale digital object datasets (100K+). This makes creating manipulation-ready assets fast and scalable.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of data-generation-ready 3D assets for robotic manipulation by providing an automated, efficient pipeline that scales asset creation in both quantity and diversity.
method: Single-image to 3D reconstruction: infer geometry, texture, and topology from one input photo.
Semantic annotation and simulation optimization: automatically add part labels, collision meshes, physical properties, and bake textures for simulators.
Automated pipeline and quality control: batch processing, heuristics and validation to produce large volumes of consistent, manipulation-ready assets.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to generate vast, diverse simulation datasets quickly, accelerating training and evaluation of manipulation policies and reducing dependency on manual 3D modeling or costly real-world data collection.

title: WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation
authors: Jisu Nam, Yicong Hong, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Feng Liu, JoungBin Lee
abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion transformers have enabled interactive gaming world models that allow users to explore generated environments over extended horizons. However, existing approaches struggle with precise action control and long-horizon 3D consistency. Most prior works treat user actions as abstract conditioning signals, overlooking the fundamental geometric coupling between actions and the 3D world, whereby actions induce relative camera motions that accumulate into a global camer

infographic.key_insight: Treat user actions as camera-pose changes and use camera pose as a unified geometric conditioning signal for an autoregressive video model, enabling precise action control and long-horizon 3D-consistent generations.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing interactive world models treat actions as abstract controls and suffer from imprecise action execution and accumulated 3D inconsistency (visual drift) over long rollouts; this work resolves that by explicitly coupling actions to camera geometry.
method: Represent actions as relative camera-pose transforms and accumulate them into a global pose trajectory that conditions generation.
Use an autoregressive video diffusion / transformer model that synthesizes next frames conditioned on past frames and the current/target camera poses to enforce geometric consistency.
Train with multi-view/pose supervision and consistency losses (pose-conditioned rendering and temporal coherence) to reduce drift and enable long-horizon interactive rollouts.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical recipe for building controllable, long-horizon interactive 3D gaming worlds and simulators where user inputs map directly to reliable camera motions—useful for game development, virtual environments, and downstream research in embodied AI.
visual_elements: Diagram: pipeline showing user action → camera-pose delta → pose accumulator → autoregressive frame generator

title: SegviGen: Repurposing 3D Generative Model for Part Segmentation
authors: Lin Li, Haoran Feng, Zehuan Huang, Haohua Chen, Wenbo Nie
abstract: We introduce SegviGen, a framework that repurposes native 3D generative models for 3D part segmentation. Existing pipelines either lift strong 2D priors into 3D via distillation or multi-view mask aggregation, often suffering from cross-view inconsistency and blurred boundaries, or explore native 3D discriminative segmentation, which typically requires large-scale annotated 3D data and substantial training resources. In contrast, SegviGen leverages the structured priors encoded in pretrained 3D

infographic.key_insight: SegviGen repurposes pretrained 3D generative models as structured priors to produce accurate 3D part segmentation, avoiding heavy annotation or multi-view aggregation and reducing cross-view inconsistency.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between costly, annotation-heavy native 3D discriminative segmentation and inconsistent 2D-to-3D distillation approaches by enabling reliable part segmentation using existing pretrained 3D generative models.
method: Extract and leverage structured spatial/latent priors encoded in a pretrained 3D generative model to inform part label prediction.
Train a lightweight segmentation head or mapping that converts generative features/representation into part labels with minimal additional supervision.
Apply consistency and boundary-aware refinement to produce sharp, cross-view-consistent part boundaries without extensive 3D annotations.
infographic.impact: SegviGen lowers the annotation and compute barrier for high-quality 3D part segmentation, enabling practitioners to reuse generative models for downstream segmentation tasks and improving robustness of 3D pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained 3D generative model -> feature/latent extraction -> lightweight segmentation head -> refined part-labeled 3D output.
