title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
authors: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Qingxiu Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang
abstract: The prevailing paradigm for improving large language models relies on offline training with human annotations or simulated environments, leaving the rich experience accumulated during real-world deployment entirely unexploited. We propose Online Experiential Learning (OEL), a framework that enables language models to continuously improve from their own deployment experience. OEL operates in two stages: first, transferable experiential knowledge is extracted and accumulated from interaction traje

infographic.key_insight: Online Experiential Learning (OEL) lets language models continuously improve by extracting and reusing knowledge from their real-world deployment interactions, turning lived experience into reusable training signal.
infographic.problem_solved: Traditional LM improvement relies on offline human annotations or simulated data and ignores the rich, actionable experience collected during deployment; OEL unlocks that untapped stream for ongoing model improvement and adaptation.
method: Extract transferable experiential knowledge from interaction trajectories (logs of prompts, model actions, user feedback) in an online fashion.
Accumulate and compress experiences into a persistent, queryable store (experience buffer or distilled corpus) that captures recurring patterns and corrective signals.

Use the accumulated experience to adapt the model online via lightweight updates (e.g., continual fine-tuning, experience-conditioned prompts, or retrieval-augmented generation) while preserving stability.
infographic.impact: Enables LMs to self-improve from deployment, reducing reliance on costly human annotation and simulated environments, and improving robustness, personalization, and long-term performance in real-world settings.

title: Demystifing Video Reasoning
authors: Ruisi Wang, Zhongang Cai, Fanyi Pu, Junxiang Xu, Wanqi Yin
abstract: Recent advances in video generation have revealed an unexpected phenomenon: diffusion-based video models exhibit non-trivial reasoning capabilities. Prior work attributes this to a Chain-of-Frames (CoF) mechanism, where reasoning is assumed to unfold sequentially across video frames. In this work, we challenge this assumption and uncover a fundamentally different mechanism. We show that reasoning in video models instead primarily emerges along the diffusion denoising steps. Through qualitative a

infographic.key_insight: Reasoning in diffusion-based video models emerges primarily along the diffusion denoising steps (the denoising trajectory), not as a sequential Chain-of-Frames across time; intervening in the denoising process disrupts reasoning more than intervening across frames.
infographic.problem_solved: Clarifies the mechanism behind surprising reasoning abilities in video diffusion models by disproving the prevailing Chain-of-Frames hypothesis and identifying the true locus of reasoning, enabling better analysis and targeted model design.
method: Design interventions and probes that selectively perturb denoising steps versus frame-wise information to trace where reasoning signals form.
Compare qualitative and quantitative metrics (e.g., task performance, attention/latent activations) under step-wise and frame-wise ablations to test CoF vs denoising hypotheses.
Visualize denoising trajectories and perform controlled experiments (freeze/perturb steps, alter noise schedules) to demonstrate causality of denoising dynamics for reasoning.
infographic.impact: Reorients research and engineering efforts toward the denoising process as the key target for interpretability, diagnostics, and architecture improvements in video diffusion models, leading to more effective debugging and design strategies.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: Chain-of-Frames (temporal chain) vs Denoising-Steps (stepwise reasoning) to illustrate contrasting hypotheses

title: LLMs displaying less cognitive bias are not necessarily better decision makers
authors: Vittoria Dentella, Marco Marelli, Luca Rinaldi
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 17 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01208-w

Large language models (LLMs) include not only social stereotypes but also cognitive biases. As researchers work to identify, characterize and rectify these biases, we encourage the scientific community to recognize that, although often seen as errors, cognitive biases can also reflect functional, context-specific adaptations in reason

infographic.key_insight: Reducing measurable cognitive bias in LLMs does not automatically lead to better decision-making; some biases can be functional, context-dependent adaptations that support useful reasoning.
infographic.problem_solved: Challenges the assumption that bias removal is always beneficial by investigating the relationship between cognitive biases in LLMs and downstream decision quality, highlighting trade-offs and context-specific effects.
method: Empirical evaluation comparing LLMs' measured cognitive-bias levels with their decision-making performance across varied tasks and contexts.
Qualitative and quantitative analysis identifying cases where bias-like heuristics improve or impair decisions.
Discussion of implications for debiasing interventions and evaluation protocols emphasizing task-specific outcomes.
infographic.impact: Prompts AI/ML practitioners to move beyond blanket debiasing: assess how bias interventions affect real-world decision quality and design context-aware evaluation metrics before deploying changes.

title: Long-Horizon Traffic Forecasting via Incident-Aware Conformal Spatio-Temporal Transformers
authors: Mayur Patil, Qadeer Ahmed, Shawn Midlam-Mohler, Stephanie Marik, Allen Sheldon
abstract: Reliable multi-horizon traffic forecasting is challenging because network conditions are stochastic, incident disruptions are intermittent, and effective spatial dependencies vary across time-of-day patterns. This study is conducted on the Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) traffic count data and corresponding ODOT crash records. This work utilizes a Spatio-Temporal Transformer (STT) model with Adaptive Conformal Prediction (ACP) to produce multi-horizon forecasts with calibrated uncertain

infographic.key_insight: Combining an incident-aware Spatio-Temporal Transformer with Adaptive Conformal Prediction yields accurate, calibrated multi-horizon traffic forecasts that remain robust to intermittent incidents and time-varying spatial dependencies.
infographic.problem_solved: Produces reliable long-horizon traffic forecasts under stochastic network conditions and intermittent incidents while providing calibrated uncertainty estimates for safer decision-making.
method: Spatio-Temporal Transformer (STT) that models dynamic spatial dependencies and temporal patterns from ODOT traffic counts.
Incident-awareness: fuse crash/incident records as external inputs to capture disruption effects on flows.
Adaptive Conformal Prediction (ACP) applied to STT outputs to produce calibrated prediction intervals across multiple forecast horizons.
infographic.impact: Enables ML practitioners and transportation operators to deploy uncertainty-aware, long-horizon traffic forecasting models that improve reliability, risk assessment, and operational decision-making under disruptive events.

title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 17 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01200-4

Guo et al. train a Mamba-based language model for molecule generation and find that data augmentation and experience replay can enable the efficient generation of property-optimized small molecules.

infographic.key_insight: A Mamba-based generative language model combined with data augmentation and an experience-replay memory yields sample-efficient generation of property-optimized small molecules, cutting the need for large labeled datasets or many expensive evaluations.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the data and evaluation burden in molecular generative design by improving sample efficiency and steering generation toward molecules with desired properties despite limited training examples.
method: Fine-tune a Mamba-based language model to generate SMILES/chemical strings for small molecules.
Apply targeted data augmentation to expand the effective training set and diversify candidate molecules.
Use experience replay / a memory buffer to store high-quality candidates and bias subsequent generation toward property-optimized molecules (memory manipulation).
infographic.impact: Enables faster, cheaper iterative design cycles in drug discovery and materials screening by lowering dependency on large datasets and costly property evaluations; practical for ML teams building generative chemistry pipelines.

title: The case for stakeholder-driven AI auditing in automatic speech recognition
authors: Mona Sloane, Hilke Schellmann, Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Allison Koenecke
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 16 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01207-x

The case for stakeholder-driven AI auditing in automatic speech recognition

infographic.key_insight: Auditing automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems is most effective when driven by the people affected: a stakeholder-centered audit uncovers real-world harms and priorities that purely technical tests miss, leading to more actionable, equitable evaluations.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the gap between standard benchmark evaluations and the lived needs and harms experienced by diverse ASR users — including dialects, accents, disability-related speech, and contextual misuse — by making audits inclusive, contextualized, and actionable.
method: Define and engage diverse stakeholders (end users, affected communities, domain experts, deployers) to co-design audit goals and success criteria.

Combine quantitative disaggregated testing (accuracy/error analyses by demographic, dialect, environment) with qualitative methods (interviews, contextual harm assessments) to surface harms and priorities.
Produce transparent, repeatable audit protocols and remediation cycles (reporting, policy recommendations, iterative model or data changes) tied to stakeholder-defined metrics.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical roadmap to evaluate ASR beyond aggregate metrics, improving fairness, reliability, compliance, and user trust by centering those who experience system failures.

title: Towards Generalizable Robotic Manipulation in Dynamic Environments
authors: Heng Fang, Shangru Li, Shuhan Wang, Xuanyang Xi, Dingkang Liang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel in static manipulation but struggle in dynamic environments with moving targets. This performance gap primarily stems from a scarcity of dynamic manipulation datasets and the reliance of mainstream VLAs on single-frame observations, restricting their spatiotemporal reasoning capabilities. To address this, we introduce DOMINO, a large-scale dataset and benchmark for generalizable dynamic manipulation, featuring 35 tasks with hierarchical complexities, ove

infographic.key_insight: Introducing DOMINO, a large-scale dataset and benchmark that enables spatiotemporal learning for Vision–Language–Action models, showing that multi-frame temporal reasoning is essential for robust robotic manipulation in dynamic, moving-target environments.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of dynamic manipulation data and the limitation of single-frame VLA models, which prevents generalization to tasks with moving objects and changing scenes.
method: Curate DOMINO: 35 manipulation tasks with hierarchical difficulty levels and diverse dynamic scenarios to train and evaluate models.
Move beyond single-frame inputs by framing problems as spatiotemporal sequences (multi-frame / video inputs) for action grounding.
Provide a standardized benchmark and baseline evaluations to measure generalization and temporal reasoning performance.
infographic.impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to develop and benchmark models that generalize to real-world, time-varying manipulation tasks, accelerating progress in robust robot behavior under dynamic conditions.

title: Look Before Acting: Enhancing Vision Foundation Representations for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Yulin Luo, Hao Chen, Zhuangzhe Wu, Bowen Sui, Jiaming Liu
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, in which reliable action prediction critically depends on accurately interpreting and integrating visual observations conditioned on language instructions. Although recent works have sought to enhance the visual capabilities of VLA models, most approaches treat the LLM backbone as a black box, providing limited insight into how visual information is grounded into action generation. Therefo

infographic.key_insight: Pre-grounding and enhancing vision foundation representations — i.e., "looking" and encoding action-relevant visual features before language-driven decoding — significantly improves action prediction reliability in Vision‑Language‑Action models.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between generic visual features and action generation by ensuring visual information is explicitly represented and aligned for downstream language-conditioned robot actions, reducing misgrounding and failure modes in VLA systems.
method: Introduce a "Look Before Acting" stage that produces action-centric visual representations from foundation vision encoders prior to LLM decoding.
Align and adapt these visual features to the language/action space (lightweight adapters or fine‑tuning) so the LLM receives grounded, task-relevant signals rather than raw visual embeddings.
Use targeted supervision (e.g., affordance/goal signals, attention maps, or contrastive alignment) to emphasize spatial/temporal cues important for manipulation and decision-making.
infographic.impact: Makes VLA models more reliable and interpretable for robotic manipulation by improving how visual evidence is presented to language backbones, enabling safer and more accurate action planning with lower data/fine‑tuning cost.

title: Mixture-of-Depths Attention
authors: Lianghui Zhu, Yuxin Fang, Bencheng Liao, Shijie Wang, Tianheng Cheng
abstract: Scaling depth is a key driver for large language models (LLMs). Yet, as LLMs become deeper, they often suffer from signal degradation: informative features formed in shallow layers are gradually diluted by repeated residual updates, making them harder to recover in deeper layers. We introduce mixture-of-depths attention (MoDA), a mechanism that allows each attention head to attend to sequence KV pairs at the current layer and depth KV pairs from preceding layers. We further describe a hardware-e

infographic.key_insight: Mixture-of-Depths Attention (MoDA) lets attention heads read KV pairs from the current layer and from previous layers, preserving informative shallow-layer signals so they aren't lost as models get deeper.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses signal degradation in very deep LLMs, where features formed in early layers are progressively diluted by repeated residual updates and become hard to recover in later layers.
method: Per-head mixture mechanism: each attention head attends to both current-layer KV pairs and depth KV pairs from preceding layers.
Learned or parameterized mixing across depths so heads can select/use the most informative layer-wise representations.
Design and optimizations for a hardware-efficient implementation to limit added compute and memory overhead.
infographic.impact: Enables deeper transformer models to retain and reuse early-layer features, improving scalability and robustness of deep LLMs while keeping computational costs manageable for practitioners.

title: OpenSeeker: Democratizing Frontier Search Agents by Fully Open-Sourcing Training Data
authors: Yuwen Du, Rui Ye, Shuo Tang, Xinyu Zhu, Yijun Lu
abstract: Deep search capabilities have become an indispensable competency for frontier Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet the development of high-performance search agents remains dominated by industrial giants due to a lack of transparent, high-quality training data. This persistent data scarcity has fundamentally hindered the progress of the broader research community in developing and innovating within this domain. To bridge this gap, we introduce OpenSeeker, the first fully open-source search age

infographic.key_insight: OpenSeeker fully open-sources the training data, tooling, and baselines needed to build frontier search-capable LLM agents, removing the primary data barrier that has kept this capability inside a few companies.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of transparent, high-quality training data and reproducible pipelines for training search agents, which has limited academic and community innovation in search-enabled LLM agents.
method: Curate and release a large, structured dataset of search interactions (queries, retrieval traces, tool calls, and agent reasoning) designed for training search agents.
Provide standardized annotation schemas, training/fine-tuning recipes, and evaluation benchmarks to enable reproducible model development.
Open-source baseline agent implementations and the end-to-end pipeline under a permissive license to encourage community adoption and extension.
infographic.impact: By democratizing access to the data and code required to train search agents, OpenSeeker enables researchers and practitioners to reproduce, improve, and compete with industrial systems—accelerating innovation and lowering barriers to entry.

title: Fast SAM 3D Body: Accelerating SAM 3D Body for Real-Time Full-Body Human Mesh Recovery
authors: Timing Yang, Sicheng He, Hongyi Jing, Jiawei Yang, Zhijian Liu
abstract: SAM 3D Body (3DB) achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in monocular 3D human mesh recovery, yet its inference latency of several seconds per image precludes real-time application. We present Fast SAM 3D Body, a training-free acceleration framework that reformulates the 3DB inference pathway to achieve interactive rates. By decoupling serial spatial dependencies and applying architecture-aware pruning, we enable parallelized multi-crop feature extraction and streamlined transformer decoding. Moreov

infographic.key_insight: Reformulating SAM 3D Body's inference pathway—removing serial spatial dependencies and applying architecture-aware pruning—enables a training-free speedup that brings full-body 3D mesh recovery to interactive (real-time) rates without retraining.
infographic.problem_solved: SAM 3D Body achieves top accuracy but requires several seconds per image, making it impractical for real-time applications like AR/VR, live animation, and interactive HCI.
method: Training-free inference pathway reformulation to avoid costly retraining.
Decouple serial spatial dependencies and parallelize multi-crop feature extraction for concurrent processing.
Apply architecture-aware pruning and streamline transformer decoding to cut compute while preserving accuracy.
infographic.impact: Makes state-of-the-art monocular full-body mesh recovery usable in real-time systems, reducing latency and compute needs so practitioners can deploy interactive human understanding on edge and interactive platforms.

title: Code-A1: Adversarial Evolving of Code LLM and Test LLM via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Aozhe Wang, Yuchen Yan, Nan Zhou, Zhengxi Lu, Weiming Lu
abstract: Reinforcement learning for code generation relies on verifiable rewards from unit test pass rates. Yet high-quality test suites are scarce, existing datasets offer limited coverage, and static rewards fail to adapt as models improve. Recent self-play methods unify code and test generation in a single model, but face a inherent dilemma: white-box access leads to self-collusion where the model produces trivial tests for easy rewards, yet black-box restriction yields generic tests that miss impleme

infographic.key_insight: Train two separate LLMs — a Code LLM and a Test LLM — in an adversarial, co-evolving reinforcement learning loop so tests become progressively harder and code generation becomes more robust, avoiding trivial test generation or generic low-coverage suites.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses brittle RL rewards for code generation caused by scarce/high-quality unit tests and the self-collusion dilemma of single-model self-play (trivial tests from white‑box access vs. generic weak tests under black‑box constraints).
method: Adversarial co-evolution: alternate/update a Test LLM that generates unit tests and a Code LLM that attempts to solve them, forming a competitive training loop.

Reinforcement learning with dynamic rewards: use execution-based signals (test pass/fail, coverage, difficulty) and diversity/hardness bonuses to adapt rewards as models improve and prevent trivialization.

Population/curriculum and access control: maintain evolving model populations or constrained interfaces (graded white/gray/black-box) to reduce self-collusion and encourage generalizable test/code behaviors.
infographic.impact: Delivers stronger, automatically generated test suites and more robust code LLMs by replacing static, scarce rewards with an adaptive adversarial signal — improving RL training quality and real-world reliability of code generation systems.

title: Predicting and interpreting cell-type-specific drug responses in the small-data regime using inductive priors
authors: Reem Alsulami, Robert Lehmann, Sumeer A. Khan, Vincenzo Lagani, Alberto Maillo
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 16 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01202-2

Alsulami et al. present PrePR-CT, a computational approach that predicts how different cell types respond to drug-like compounds using limited data. By integrating biological networks with machine learning, it improves accuracy, interpretability and efficiency in early drug discovery.

infographic.key_insight: PrePR-CT injects biological network knowledge as inductive priors into machine-learning models to accurately predict cell-type-specific drug responses from very limited data, yielding more interpretable and data-efficient predictions for early drug discovery.

method: Encode biological knowledge (pathways / interaction networks) as inductive priors that bias model learning toward biologically plausible patterns.

title: Tri-Prompting: Video Diffusion with Unified Control over Scene, Subject, and Motion
authors: Zhenghong Zhou, Xiaohang Zhan, Zhiqin Chen, Soo Ye Kim, Nanxuan Zhao
abstract: Recent video diffusion models have made remarkable strides in visual quality, yet precise, fine-grained control remains a key bottleneck that limits practical customizability for content creation. For AI video creators, three forms of control are crucial: (i) scene composition, (ii) multi-view consistent subject customization, and (iii) camera-pose or object-motion adjustment. Existing methods typically handle these dimensions in isolation, with limited support for multi-view subject synthesis a

infographic.key_insight: Tri-Prompting introduces a unified conditioning scheme that simultaneously controls scene composition, multi-view-consistent subject appearance, and camera/object motion in video diffusion, enabling fine-grained coordinated edits from three complementary prompts.
infographic.problem_solved: Provides precise, joint control over scene layout, personalized multi-view subject synthesis, and motion/camera pose in video generation—tasks previously handled separately or with limited consistency.
method: Tri-prompt design: separate but jointly-applied prompts for Scene, Subject, and Motion to decompose control signals.
Cross-view subject conditioning: enforce multi-view consistency for personalized subjects via view-aware conditioning or feature-alignment across frames.
Motion & pose guidance: integrate camera-pose or object-motion cues into the diffusion denoising process to produce temporally coherent, controllable motion.
infographic.impact: Enables AI creators and ML practitioners to generate highly-customizable videos with coordinated scene, subject, and motion control, improving usability for content creation, animation, and personalized media synthesis.

title: HorizonMath: Measuring AI Progress Toward Mathematical Discovery with Automatic Verification
authors: Erik Y. Wang, Sumeet Motwani, James V. Roggeveen, Eliot Hodges, Dulhan Jayalath
abstract: Can AI make progress on important, unsolved mathematical problems? Large language models are now capable of sophisticated mathematical and scientific reasoning, but whether they can perform novel research is still widely debated and underexplored. We introduce HorizonMath, a benchmark of over 100 predominantly unsolved problems spanning 8 domains in computational and applied mathematics, paired with an open-source evaluation framework for automated verification. Our benchmark targets a class of

infographic.key_insight: HorizonMath shows that language models can be evaluated on novel, research-like mathematical problems by pairing a large benchmark of mostly-unsolved problems with an automated verification framework, enabling objective measurement of discovery-oriented capabilities.
infographic.problem_solved: Lack of standardized, verifiable benchmarks for assessing whether AI models can make progress on important, predominantly unsolved problems in computational and applied mathematics.
method: Curate a benchmark of 100+ predominantly unsolved problems spanning 8 domains in computational and applied math.
Provide an open-source evaluation pipeline that automatically verifies model outputs using computational checks and formal/numeric verification tools.
Run and analyze model attempts to generate solutions, using the verifier to classify correct/partial/incorrect results and produce reproducible evidence.
infographic.impact: Enables rigorous, reproducible measurement of AI progress toward mathematical discovery and gives practitioners a toolset to benchmark, debug, and improve models on research-grade tasks. title: AC-Foley: Reference-Audio-Guided Video-to-Audio Synthesis with Acoustic Transfer
authors: Pengjun Fang, Yingqing He, Yazhou Xing, Qifeng Chen, Ser-Nam Lim
abstract: Existing video-to-audio (V2A) generation methods predominantly rely on text prompts alongside visual information to synthesize audio. However, two critical bottlenecks persist: semantic granularity gaps in training data, such as conflating acoustically distinct sounds under coarse labels, and textual ambiguity in describing micro-acoustic features. These bottlenecks make it difficult to perform fine-grained sound synthesis using text-controlled modes. To address these limitations, we propose AC-

infographic.key_insight: AC-Foley uses a reference-audio-guided acoustic transfer module to inject micro-acoustic textures from an exemplar audio into video-to-audio generation, enabling fine-grained sound synthesis beyond coarse text labels and ambiguous prompts.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing V2A methods rely on text + visuals and suffer from semantic-granularity gaps (different acoustics collapsed under coarse labels) and textual ambiguity for micro-acoustic features, making it hard to synthesize detailed, controllable sounds. AC-Foley addresses these limitations by conditioning generation on reference audio rather than relying solely on text.
method: Reference-audio encoder: extract timbre/texture and micro-acoustic features from an exemplar audio clip to serve as a conditioning signal.
Acoustic transfer module: align and inject the extracted acoustic features into the V2A generator while preserving event semantics from video frames (disentangles semantic event vs. acoustic style).
Training strategy: paired video-audio supervision (plus contrastive/augmentation losses) to learn robust cross-modal alignment and allow style transfer across different semantic categories.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to produce more realistic, controllable foley and environmental sounds for video by transferring acoustic style from examples rather than relying on limited text descriptions. This improves fidelity and user controllability in multimodal audio generation pipelines.

title: From Passive Observer to Active Critic: Reinforcement Learning Elicits Process Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Yibin Liu, Yaxing Lyu, Daqi Gao, Zhixuan Liang, Weiliang Tang
abstract: Accurate process supervision remains a critical challenge for long-horizon robotic manipulation. A primary bottleneck is that current video MLLMs, trained primarily under a Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) paradigm, function as passive "Observers" that recognize ongoing events rather than evaluating the current state relative to the final task goal. In this paper, we introduce PRIMO R1 (Process Reasoning Induced Monitoring), a 7B framework that transforms video MLLMs into active "Critics". We levera

infographic.key_insight: Reinforcement learning can turn video MLLMs from passive 'Observers' into active 'Critics' that evaluate process progress relative to a final goal, enabling explicit process reasoning for long‑horizon robotic manipulation tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses poor process supervision in long‑horizon robotic manipulation: SFT‑trained video models recognize events but cannot judge whether the current state is on track to achieve the final task goal.
method: PRIMO R1: a 7B video‑MLLM framework designed to produce critic‑style evaluations rather than passive descriptions.
Use reinforcement learning objectives (instead of only SFT) to elicit process reasoning and train the model to score/evaluate intermediate states against task goals.
Integrate video inputs with critic feedback to monitor progress, flag deviations, and inform corrective actions during manipulation.
infographic.impact: Enables models that provide actionable, goal‑aware supervision for long‑horizon robotic tasks—improving monitoring, failure detection, and closed‑loop recovery—making deployment of more robust manipulation systems practical.

title: HSImul3R: Physics-in-the-Loop Reconstruction of Simulation-Ready Human-Scene Interactions
authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Fangzhou Hong, Long Zhuo, Zhaoxi Chen
abstract: We present HSImul3R, a unified framework for simulation-ready 3D reconstruction of human-scene interactions (HSI) from casual captures, including sparse-view images and monocular videos. Existing methods suffer from a perception-simulation gap: visually plausible reconstructions often violate physical constraints, leading to instability in physics engines and failure in embodied AI applications. To bridge this gap, we introduce a physically-grounded bi-directional optimization pipeline that trea

infographic.key_insight: HSImul3R closes the perception–simulation gap by integrating physics directly into the 3D reconstruction loop, producing human–scene interaction outputs that are both visually accurate and stable in physics engines.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing HSI reconstruction methods produce visually plausible results that often violate physical constraints, causing instability or failure when used in simulators and embodied AI tasks—HSImul3R makes casual captures (sparse views, monocular video) simulation-ready.
method: Physically-grounded bi-directional optimization: alternate perception updates with physics-based corrections to enforce contact, collision, and dynamic consistency.
Unified pipeline for casual captures: jointly optimize human pose, scene geometry, contacts, and physical parameters from sparse-view images or monocular video.
Physics-in-the-loop validation: run candidate reconstructions in a physics engine during optimization to reject/adjust physically implausible solutions.
infographic.impact: Enables reliable, simulator-ready HSI reconstructions from everyday captures, improving downstream tasks in robotics, virtual agents, and AR/VR by ensuring interactions are physically valid and stable.

title: PhysMoDPO: Physically-Plausible Humanoid Motion with Preference Optimization
authors: Yangsong Zhang, Anujith Muraleedharan, Rikhat Akizhanov, Abdul Ahad Butt, Gül Varol
abstract: Recent progress in text-conditioned human motion generation has been largely driven by diffusion models trained on large-scale human motion data. Building on this progress, recent methods attempt to transfer such models for character animation and real robot control by applying a Whole-Body Controller (WBC) that converts diffusion-generated motions into executable trajectories. While WBC trajectories become compliant with physics, they may expose substantial deviations from original motion. To a

infographic.key_insight: PhysMoDPO closes the gap between diffusion-based text-to-motion models and physically-executable humanoid trajectories by optimizing generated motions with a learned preference objective that trades off fidelity and physical plausibility.
infographic.problem_solved: Diffusion-generated motions look realistic but often become unrealistic or unstable after conversion to robot/executable trajectories by Whole-Body Controllers (WBCs); the paper addresses how to modify generated motions so they remain faithful to the original intent while being physically feasible under WBCs.
method: Start from text-conditioned diffusion motion samples and convert them to executable trajectories via a Whole-Body Controller to expose physical mismatches.
Train a learned preference model that scores motions by a balance of fidelity to the original generation and compliance with physics/WBC outcomes.
Optimize the generated motion samples (PhysMoDPO) using preference-guided updates so final trajectories remain stylistically faithful while being physically plausible and executable.
infographic.impact: Enables reliable transfer of high-quality generative motion models to character animation and real robot control by producing motions that survive controller constraints—reducing manual retuning and improving realism in deployment.

title: Developing and evaluating a chatbot to support maternal health care
authors: Smriti Jha, Vidhi Jain, Jianyu Xu, Grace Liu, Sowmya Ramesh
abstract:

However, deploying such systems is technically challenging: user queries are short, underspecified, and code-mixed across languages, answers require regional context-specific grounding, and partial or missing symptom context makes safe routing decisions difficult.

title: Towards Spatio-Temporal World Scene Graph Generation from Monocular Videos
authors: Rohith Peddi, Saurabh, Shravan Shanmugam, Likhitha Pallapothula, Yu Xiang
abstract: Spatio-temporal scene graphs provide a principled representation for modeling evolving object interactions, yet existing methods remain fundamentally frame-centric: they reason only about currently visible objects, discard entities upon occlusion, and operate in 2D. To address this, we first introduce ActionGenome4D, a dataset that upgrades Action Genome videos into 4D scenes via feed-forward 3D reconstruction, world-frame oriented bounding boxes for every object involved in actions, and dense r

infographic.key_insight: Representing object interactions in a persistent 3D world-frame (4D: 3D + time) from monocular video enables scene graphs that reason through occlusions and over time, rather than being limited to single 2D frames.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing scene-graph methods are frame-centric: they operate in 2D, drop objects when occluded, and cannot model persistent, world-referenced interactions across time. This work provides a dataset and approach to build spatio‑temporal, world‑centric scene graphs from monocular video.
method: ActionGenome4D dataset: upgrade Action Genome videos into 4D scenes via feed‑forward 3D reconstruction and world‑frame oriented bounding boxes and dense relational annotations for all action objects.
World‑centric scene graph generation: infer object locations and relations in a fixed world frame across time (3D + temporal links), enabling object permanence and occlusion handling.
Temporal and 3D-aware relation modeling: aggregate temporal cues and 3D geometry (tracking, poses, world transforms) to predict spatio‑temporal edges and evolving interactions.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners with a benchmark and methods to build persistent, 3D-aware scene graphs from ordinary monocular video — useful for robotics, AR/VR, long-horizon video understanding, and any system needing durable scene reasoning across occlusions and time.

title: MXNorm: Reusing MXFP block scales for efficient tensor normalisation
authors: Callum McLean, Luke Y. Prince, Alexandre Payot, Paul Balança, Carlo Luschi
abstract: Matrix multiplication performance has long been the major bottleneck to scaling deep learning workloads, which has stimulated the design of new accelerators that use increasingly low-precision number formats. However, improvements in matrix multiplication performance have far outstripped improvements in performance on reductions and elementwise computations, which are still being performed in higher precision. In this work, we propose MXNorm, a drop-in replacement for RMSNorm that estimates the

infographic.key_insight: MXNorm reuses block-scale metadata produced by MXFP-style low-precision matrix-multiply units to approximate RMSNorm statistics, enabling tensor normalisation without expensive high-precision reductions or extra elementwise passes.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the performance and precision mismatch between highly-optimized low-precision matrix multiplication and slower, higher-precision reductions/elementwise ops used for normalization, which limit throughput on modern accelerators.
method: Intercept and reuse MXFP block scale factors emitted during low-precision matmul to approximate per-block second-moment / RMS statistics.
Compute normalization using those reused scales (and minimal extra correction) in lower precision, avoiding full-precision global reductions and elementwise passes.
Provide a drop-in replacement for RMSNorm that preserves compatibility with existing models while shifting the reduction workload onto already-available MXFP metadata.
infographic.impact: Enables faster and more hardware-efficient model training/inference on accelerators that use low-precision formats by removing a key software bottleneck (reductions/elementwise ops), improving throughput and energy efficiency with minimal model changes.

title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection In Instruction Tuning For Large Language Models
authors: Xin Chen, Junchao Wu, Shu Yang, Runzhe Zhan, Zeyu Wu
abstract: Instruction Tuning (IT) has been proven to be an effective approach to unlock the powerful capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Recent studies indicate that excessive IT data can degrade LLMs performance, while carefully selecting a small subset of high-quality IT data can significantly enhance their capabilities. Therefore, identifying the most efficient subset data from the IT dataset to effectively develop either specific or general abilities in LLMs has become a critical challenge.

infographic.key_insight: Measuring example-level neuron activation patterns identifies small, high‑impact instruction examples; training on these neuron‑aware subsets improves or preserves LLM capabilities while avoiding degradation from excessive instruction data.
infographic.problem_solved: Instruction tuning with large, uncurated datasets can hurt or waste compute; the paper solves how to pick a compact, effective subset of instruction data that builds specific or general abilities without performance loss.
method: Record neuron activation signatures for candidate instruction examples using a pretrained LLM backbone (or probe neurons linked to target behaviors).
Score and rank examples by neuron‑aware criteria (e.g., activation alignment, information gain, or diversity over important neurons) to select a compact subset.
Fine‑tune the LLM on the selected subset and validate improvements on targeted tasks and general benchmarks.
infographic.impact: Enables more efficient, targeted instruction tuning—reducing compute and data while improving or maintaining model capability—useful for practitioners aiming to build specialized skills or cost‑effective generalists.

title: DiT-IC: Aligned Diffusion Transformer for Efficient Image Compression
authors: Junqi Shi, Ming Lu, Xingchen Li, Anle Ke, Ruiqi Zhang
abstract: Diffusion-based image compression has recently shown outstanding perceptual fidelity, yet its practicality is hindered by prohibitive sampling overhead and high memory usage. Most existing diffusion codecs employ U-Net architectures, where hierarchical downsampling forces diffusion to operate in shallow latent spaces (typically with only 8x spatial downscaling), resulting in excessive computation. In contrast, conventional VAE-based codecs work in much deeper latent domains (16x - 64x downscaled

infographic.key_insight: DiT-IC replaces costly U-Net diffusion backbones with an aligned Diffusion Transformer that lets diffusion operate in much deeper latent spaces (e.g., 16x–64x downscaling), dramatically cutting computation and memory while keeping diffusion-quality reconstructions.
infographic.problem_solved: Diffusion-based image codecs deliver superior perceptual quality but are impractical due to heavy sampling overhead and high memory use caused by shallow-latent U-Net designs; this work makes diffusion compression efficient and scalable.
method: Design an aligned Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone that is compatible with deep latent spaces used by VAE-style codecs, avoiding U-Net hierarchical constraints.
Shift diffusion operations into much more compressed latent domains (16x–64x spatial downscaling) to reduce per-sample compute and memory footprints.

Introduce alignment mechanisms between encoder/quantizer and the transformer diffusion process (e.g., positional/patch-aware embeddings and attention-aware quantization) so high perceptual fidelity is preserved despite deeper compression.
infographic.impact: Enables practical deployment of diffusion-based image compression by reducing runtime and memory cost without sacrificing perceptual quality—useful for ML systems that need high-fidelity compression under resource limits.

title: Semantic Invariance in Agentic AI
authors: I. de Zarzà, J. de Curtò, Jordi Cabot, Pietro Manzoni, Carlos T. Calafate
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly serve as autonomous reasoning agents in decision support, scientific problem-solving, and multi-agent coordination systems. However, deploying LLM agents in consequential applications requires assurance that their reasoning remains stable under semantically equivalent input variations, a property we term semantic invariance.Standard benchmark evaluations, which assess accuracy on fixed, canonical problem formulations, fail to capture this critical reliab

infographic.key_insight: LLM-based agents must produce stable, consistent reasoning when faced with semantically equivalent input variations; the paper defines and operationalizes this property—"semantic invariance"—and shows that standard fixed-form benchmarks miss these reliability failures.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the gap in assurance that agentic LLMs reason consistently under paraphrases and other semantics-preserving input changes, revealing that canonical benchmark evaluations underrate brittleness in real-world, variable inputs.
method: Define the semantic invariance property and propose an evaluation protocol that measures consistency of agent outputs across semantically equivalent input perturbations.

Construct a suite of controlled semantic-preserving transformations (e.g., paraphrases, reordering, context framing) and apply them to agentic tasks (decision support, scientific reasoning, multi-agent coordination).
Introduce an invariance score/metric to quantify output stability and compare model behaviours to identify failure modes and mitigation opportunities.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners with a practical way to detect and quantify brittle reasoning in agentic LLMs, enabling more reliable deployment in high-stakes settings and guiding robust model design and evaluation.

title: Visual-ERM: Reward Modeling for Visual Equivalence
authors: Ziyu Liu, Shengyuan Ding, Xinyu Fang, Xuanlang Dai, Penghui Yang
abstract: Vision-to-code tasks require models to reconstruct structured visual inputs, such as charts, tables, and SVGs, into executable or structured representations with high visual fidelity. While recent Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) achieve strong results via supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning remains challenging due to misaligned reward signals. Existing rewards either rely on textual rules or coarse visual embedding similarity, both of which fail to capture fine-grained visual dis

infographic.key_insight: Train a learned reward that measures visual equivalence between a model's rendered output and the target visual, enabling reinforcement learning to directly optimize visual fidelity for vision-to-code tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing RL rewards for vision-to-code are misaligned: rule-based or coarse embedding similarities fail to capture fine-grained visual differences needed to reconstruct charts, tables, and SVGs accurately.
method: Learn a visual-equivalence reward model that scores how well a generated, rendered output matches the target visual at fine granularity.
Use the learned reward to fine-tune LVLMs with reinforcement learning (policy optimization), replacing coarse or handcrafted rewards.
Design the reward training to exploit rendered comparisons and dense visual features so small structural or styling errors are penalized appropriately.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way to align RL objectives with visual fidelity, improving the correctness and usability of models that generate executable visual representations (e.g., chart/table/SVG code). This helps practitioners deploy LVLMs that produce visually accurate, runnable outputs.

title: Representation Learning for Spatiotemporal Physical Systems
authors: Helen Qu, Rudy Morel, Michael McCabe, Alberto Bietti, François Lanusse
abstract: Machine learning approaches to spatiotemporal physical systems have primarily focused on next-frame prediction, with the goal of learning an accurate emulator for the system's evolution in time. However, these emulators are computationally expensive to train and are subject to performance pitfalls, such as compounding errors during autoregressive rollout. In this work, we take a different perspective and look at scientific tasks further downstream of predicting the next frame, such as estimation

infographic.key_insight: Instead of training heavy next-frame emulators, learning compact, task-oriented representations of spatiotemporal physical systems yields more efficient, robust solutions for downstream scientific tasks and avoids compounding autoregressive errors.
infographic.problem_solved: Current ML workflows focus on next-frame prediction that are costly to train and prone to error accumulation during autoregressive rollouts, making them suboptimal for downstream estimation and analysis tasks in scientific applications.
method: Learn compact latent representations from spatiotemporal data that are explicitly optimized for downstream scientific tasks (e.g., parameter estimation, forecasting of aggregate quantities) rather than pixel-wise next-frame accuracy.
Model short-horizon or latent dynamics in representation space to capture relevant temporal structure without requiring long autoregressive rollouts.
Incorporate task-aligned losses and physics-aware inductive biases to improve robustness, interpretability, and generalization while reducing computational cost.
infographic.impact: This shift reduces training and inference cost, mitigates rollout-induced error accumulation, and delivers representations better suited for scientific analysis, enabling faster and more reliable workflows for AI-driven physical modeling.

title: Towards Faithful Multimodal Concept Bottleneck Models
authors: Pierre Moreau, Emeline Pineau Ferrand, Yann Choho, Benjamin Wong, Annabelle Blangero
abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) are interpretable models that route predictions through a layer of human-interpretable concepts. While widely studied in vision and, more recently, in NLP, CBMs remain largely unexplored in multimodal settings. For their explanations to be faithful, CBMs must satisfy two conditions: concepts must be properly detected, and concept representations must encode only their intended semantics, without smuggling extraneous task-relevant or inter-concept information into

infographic.key_insight: Extends Concept Bottleneck Models to multimodal inputs and identifies two necessary conditions for faithful explanations: reliable concept detection and concept representations that encode only their intended semantics (no information "smuggling"). The paper proposes ways to enforce and measure these properties in multimodal CBMs.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the challenge that, in multimodal models, concept-based explanations can be unfaithful because concepts may be undetected or leak task-relevant or cross-concept information, undermining interpretability and trust.
method: Formalize faithfulness for multimodal CBMs via two criteria: concept detectability and representation purity (no smuggling of extraneous info).
Introduce training objectives, regularizers and evaluation metrics to enforce and quantify concept purity and accurate detection across modalities.
Build multimodal CBM architectures (modality-specific encoders → shared concept bottleneck → task head) and empirically compare faithfulness to standard baselines.
infographic.impact: Gives practitioners practical diagnostics and training tools to build interpretable multimodal systems whose concept-level explanations are more trustworthy, aiding model debugging, compliance, and human-AI collaboration.

title: OmniStream: Mastering Perception, Reconstruction and Action in Continuous Streams
authors: Yibin Yan, Jilan Xu, Shangzhe Di, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie
abstract: Modern visual agents require representations that are general, causal, and physically structured to operate in real-time streaming environments. However, current vision foundation models remain fragmented, specializing narrowly in image semantic perception, offline temporal modeling, or spatial geometry. This paper introduces OmniStream, a unified streaming visual backbone that effectively perceives, reconstructs, and acts from diverse visual inputs. By incorporating causal spatiotemporal attent

infographic.key_insight: OmniStream unifies perception, reconstruction and action in a single streaming visual backbone by applying causal spatiotemporal and geometry-aware processing, enabling real-time, physically grounded understanding from continuous visual inputs.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges fragmented visual foundations (static image perception, offline temporal models, and separate geometry modules) to deliver a single model that operates causally and continuously for real-time embodied tasks.
method: Causal spatiotemporal attention: process incoming frames in a streaming, low-latency manner that preserves temporal causality for online decision-making.
Unified representation: fuse semantic perception, implicit/explicit 3D reconstruction, and action-ready features in one backbone with task-specific heads.
Efficiency and memory design: streaming buffer and sparse attention/compute mechanisms to keep inference real-time while supporting long-range temporal context.
infographic.impact: Simplifies pipelines for embodied agents and robotics by providing a single, real-time backbone that generalizes across perception, 3D reconstruction and control — improving responsiveness and deployment practicality.

title: EndoCoT: Scaling Endogenous Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Diffusion Models
authors: Xuanlang Dai, Yujie Zhou, Long Xing, Jiazi Bu, Xilin Wei
abstract: Recently, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely integrated into diffusion frameworks primarily as text encoders to tackle complex tasks such as spatial reasoning. However, this paradigm suffers from two critical limitations: (i) MLLMs text encoder exhibits insufficient reasoning depth. Single-step encoding fails to activate the Chain-of-Thought process, which is essential for MLLMs to provide accurate guidance for complex tasks. (ii) The guidance remains invariant during the

infographic.key_insight: EndoCoT endogenizes Chain-of-Thought (CoT) inside diffusion models so the multimodal LLM provides iterative, evolving reasoning guidance during generation rather than a single static encoding.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses two bottlenecks in MLLM+diffusion pipelines: (1) shallow, single-step text encoding that fails to trigger CoT reasoning, and (2) invariant guidance across diffusion steps that cannot adapt to intermediate visual-linguistic states.
method: Embed an internal CoT loop into the diffusion sampling process so the MLLM produces multi-step reasoning updates that condition subsequent denoising steps.
Introduce a lightweight interface (adapter/prompts) between the diffusion latent states and the MLLM to enable iterative querying and conditional refinement without full model re-run.
Train with consistency and alignment objectives that encourage coherent, stepwise explanations and stable guidance across diffusion iterations, allowing scalable application to larger MLLMs.
infographic.impact: Enables more accurate and interpretable multimodal reasoning for complex tasks (e.g., spatial planning, compositional instructions) by turning static text guidance into a dynamic, self-refining signal—improving generation quality and trustworthiness for practitioners.

title: SciMDR: Benchmarking and Advancing Scientific Multimodal Document Reasoning
authors: Ziyu Chen, Yilun Zhao, Chengye Wang, Rilyn Han, Manasi Patwardhan
abstract: Constructing scientific multimodal document reasoning datasets for foundation model training involves an inherent trade-off among scale, faithfulness, and realism. To address this challenge, we introduce the synthesize-and-reground framework, a two-stage pipeline comprising: (1) Claim-Centric QA Synthesis, which generates faithful, isolated QA pairs and reasoning on focused segments, and (2) Document-Scale Regrounding, which programmatically re-embeds these pairs into full-document tasks to ensu

infographic.key_insight: A two-stage "synthesize-and-reground" pipeline creates faithful, scalable QA pairs from focused document segments and programmatically re-embeds them into full-document tasks, reconciling the trade-off between scale, faithfulness, and realism for scientific multimodal reasoning datasets.
infographic.problem_solved: How to build large-scale, realistic, and faithful scientific multimodal document reasoning datasets for training foundation models without sacrificing fidelity or contextual realism.
method: Claim-Centric QA Synthesis: generate faithful, isolated QA pairs and stepwise reasoning focused on specific claims or local segments.
Document-Scale Regrounding: programmatically re-embed the isolated QA pairs into full-document tasks to restore context, coherence, and document-level challenges.
End-to-end pipeline design that balances dataset scale with faithfulness and realism for multimodal scientific documents (text + figures/tables).
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to produce large, realistic training data for multimodal foundation models that preserve factual grounding and document-level context, improving scientific document understanding and downstream reasoning performance.

title: The Latent Color Subspace: Emergent Order in High-Dimensional Chaos
authors: Mateusz Pach, Jessica Bader, Quentin Bouniot, Serge Belongie, Zeynep Akata
abstract: Text-to-image generation models have advanced rapidly, yet achieving fine-grained control over generated images remains difficult, largely due to limited understanding of how semantic information is encoded. We develop an interpretation of the color representation in the Variational Autoencoder latent space of FLUX.1 [Dev], revealing a structure reflecting Hue, Saturation, and Lightness. We verify our Latent Color Subspace (LCS) interpretation by demonstrating that it can both predict and explic

infographic.key_insight: A distinct Latent Color Subspace (LCS) emerges inside the FLUX.1 VAE latent space that aligns with Hue, Saturation and Lightness, enabling predictable, interpretable color control via simple latent operations.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the opacity of how color is encoded in high-dimensional generative models, enabling fine-grained, controllable color manipulation and interpretation in text-to-image pipelines.
method: Analyze the FLUX.1 VAE latent space to identify a low-dimensional subspace correlated with color attributes (H, S, L).

title: DVD: Deterministic Video Depth Estimation with Generative Priors
authors: Hongfei Zhang, Harold Haodong Chen, Chenfei Liao, Jing He, Zixin Zhang
abstract: Existing video depth estimation faces a fundamental trade-off: generative models suffer from stochastic geometric hallucinations and scale drift, while discriminative models demand massive labeled datasets to resolve semantic ambiguities. To break this impasse, we present DVD, the first framework to deterministically adapt pre-trained video diffusion models into single-pass depth regressors. Specifically, DVD features three core designs: (i) repurposing the diffusion timestep as a structural anc

infographic.key_insight: DVD deterministically adapts pre-trained video diffusion models into single-pass depth regressors by repurposing diffusion timesteps as structural anchors and using generative priors to resolve geometric ambiguity without stochastic hallucinations or scale drift.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off in video depth estimation where generative models produce stochastic geometry and scale drift while discriminative models require massive labeled data to disambiguate semantics.
method: Deterministic conversion of pre-trained video diffusion models into a single-pass depth regression pipeline (no iterative sampling).
Repurpose the diffusion timestep as a structural anchor to encode coarse-to-fine geometry and stabilize scale across frames.
Leverage generative priors from the pre-trained diffusion model to resolve semantic ambiguities and enforce temporal consistency without stochastic hallucinations.

title: GRADE: Benchmarking Discipline-Informed Reasoning in Image Editing
authors: Mingxin Liu, Ziqian Fan, Zhaokai Wang, Leyao Gu, Zirun Zhu
abstract: Unified multimodal models target joint understanding, reasoning, and generation, but current image editing benchmarks are largely confined to natural images and shallow commonsense reasoning, offering limited assessment of this capability under structured, domain-specific constraints. In this work, we introduce GRADE, the first benchmark to assess discipline-informed knowledge and reasoning in image editing. GRADE comprises 520 carefully curated samples across 10 academic domains, spanning from

infographic.key_insight: GRADE is the first benchmark that measures discipline-informed knowledge and reasoning in image editing, revealing that current multimodal models struggle with domain-specific, constraint-driven edits beyond commonsense scenarios.

method: Curate 520 high-quality editing examples across 10 academic domains (e.g., chemistry, medicine, engineering) that require discipline-specific constraints and rationale.

title: Video Streaming Thinking: VideoLLMs Can Watch and Think Simultaneously
authors: Yiran Guan, Liang Yin, Dingkang Liang, Jianzhong Ju, Zhenbo Luo
abstract: Online Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) play a critical role in supporting responsive, real-time interaction. Existing methods focus on streaming perception, lacking a synchronized logical reasoning stream. However, directly applying test-time scaling methods incurs unacceptable response latency. To address this trade-off, we propose Video Streaming Thinking (VST), a novel paradigm for streaming video understanding. It supports a thinking while watching mechanism, which activates reasonin

infographic.key_insight: Video Streaming Thinking (VST) enables VideoLLMs to 'think while watching' by running a synchronized reasoning stream alongside a fast perception stream, reducing response latency while preserving coherent logical inference.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between low-latency streaming perception and synchronized, high-quality reasoning in online VideoLLMs, avoiding the unacceptable delay caused by naive test-time scaling.
method: Dual-stream architecture: a fast perception stream ingests video frames continuously while a parallel reasoning (thinking) stream processes accumulated context at a controllable cadence.
Asynchronous, event-driven scheduling: selectively activate reasoning steps (or scale compute) based on perceptual cues, reducing unnecessary computation and end-to-end delay.

Incremental context fusion and memory compression: continuously align and summarize incoming visual information so the reasoning stream accesses up-to-date, compact context without waiting for full-frame batches.

title: EVATok: Adaptive Length Video Tokenization for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Generation
authors: Tianwei Xiong, Jun Hao Liew, Zilong Huang, Zhijie Lin, Jiashi Feng
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video generative models rely on video tokenizers that compress pixels into discrete token sequences. The length of these token sequences is crucial for balancing reconstruction quality against downstream generation computational cost. Traditional video tokenizers apply a uniform token assignment across temporal blocks of different videos, often wasting tokens on simple, static, or repetitive segments while underserving dynamic or complex ones. To address this inefficiency, we

infographic.key_insight: EVATok adaptively assigns variable-length discrete token sequences across a video's temporal blocks, allocating more tokens to dynamic/complex segments and fewer to static/repetitive ones, thereby preserving reconstruction quality while reducing autoregressive generation cost.
infographic.problem_solved: Fixed-rate video tokenizers waste tokens on simple frames and underrepresent complex ones, forcing a trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and generation efficiency for autoregressive video models.
method: Learn a per-block complexity estimator that predicts token budget based on motion/visual complexity and content redundancy.
Use a variable-length tokenization pipeline (e.g., adaptive VQ/VAE or entropy-constrained quantization) that emits more discrete tokens for high-complexity blocks and fewer for low-complexity blocks.
Train end-to-end with reconstruction + budget/bitrate regularization and integrate the adaptive tokens into standard autoregressive generators for efficient sampling.
infographic.impact: Practitioners can substantially cut computation and sampling latency of autoregressive video generation without sacrificing visual quality, enabling more scalable training and deployment of high-fidelity video models.

title: DreamVideo-Omni: Omni-Motion Controlled Multi-Subject Video Customization with Latent Identity Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yujie Wei, Xinyu Liu, Shiwei Zhang, Hangjie Yuan, Jinbo Xing
abstract: While large-scale diffusion models have revolutionized video synthesis, achieving precise control over both multi-subject identity and multi-granularity motion remains a significant challenge. Recent attempts to bridge this gap often suffer from limited motion granularity, control ambiguity, and identity degradation, leading to suboptimal performance on identity preservation and motion control. In this work, we present DreamVideo-Omni, a unified framework enabling harmonious multi-subject custom

infographic.key_insight: DreamVideo-Omni unifies precise, multi-granularity motion control and strong multi-subject identity preservation by introducing latent identity reinforcement learning inside a diffusion-based video customization pipeline.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses identity degradation, motion-control ambiguity, and limited motion granularity in multi-subject video synthesis, enabling faithful identity retention and fine-to-coarse motion control for multiple subjects simultaneously.
method: Omni-motion control module that supports multi-granularity motion signals (pose, trajectory, and high-level motion prompts) and routes them per subject within a single framework.
Latent Identity Reinforcement Learning: a reinforcement signal in latent space that explicitly rewards identity preservation during diffusion-based video customization to prevent identity drift.
Integrated multi-subject conditioning and fusion strategies to resolve cross-subject interference and maintain coherent interactions while generating temporally consistent videos.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to generate customizable multi-person videos with stronger identity fidelity and precise motion specification, improving downstream tasks like avatar creation, virtual production, and personalized content generation.

title: Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training
authors: Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Jiawei Chi, Yimo Cai, Yi-Hsin Hung
abstract: Humans perceive and understand real-world spaces through a stream of visual observations. Therefore, the ability to streamingly maintain and update spatial evidence from potentially unbounded video streams is essential for spatial intelligence. The core challenge is not simply longer context windows but how spatial information is selected, organized, and retained over time. In this paper, we propose Spatial-TTT towards streaming visual-based spatial intelligence with test-time training (TTT), wh

infographic.key_insight: Spatial-TTT applies test-time training to streaming video so a model can continuously adapt, selectively store, and organize spatial evidence—enabling persistent spatial intelligence from unbounded visual streams.
infographic.problem_solved: How to maintain, update, and compress spatial information from potentially unbounded video streams—selecting, organizing, and retaining relevant spatial cues over time rather than merely increasing context window length.
method: Streaming spatial memory that incrementally accumulates and prunes visual evidence to form a persistent spatial representation.
Online test-time training (self-supervised) that adapts model parameters on incoming frames to align perception with the current environment.
Lightweight selection and update rules that preserve key geometry/semantics while enabling continuous operation without full offline retraining.
infographic.impact: Enables systems (robots, AR/VR, mapping) to maintain robust, long-term spatial understanding by adapting on-the-fly to new environments; reduces reliance on large offline datasets and periodic retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: live video stream → TTT adaptation block → streaming spatial memory → downstream task (e.g., mapping/localization)

title: Attend Before Attention: Efficient and Scalable Video Understanding via Autoregressive Gazing
authors: Baifeng Shi, Stephanie Fu, Long Lian, Hanrong Ye, David Eigen
abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced general-purpose video understanding but struggle with long, high-resolution videos -- they process every pixel equally in their vision transformers (ViTs) or LLMs despite significant spatiotemporal redundancy. We introduce AutoGaze, a lightweight module that removes redundant patches before processed by a ViT or an MLLM. Trained with next-token prediction and reinforcement learning, AutoGaze autoregressively selects a minimal set of multi-s

infographic.key_insight: AutoGaze autoregressively 'gazes' to select only the most informative spatiotemporal patches before they reach a ViT or MLLM, removing redundancy and dramatically cutting computation for long, high‑resolution videos.
infographic.problem_solved: Current MLLMs and ViTs treat every pixel/frame region equally, causing excessive compute and memory use on long, high‑resolution videos with large spatiotemporal redundancy; AutoGaze addresses this inefficiency by pre‑filtering irrelevant patches.
method: Lightweight AutoGaze module placed upstream of a ViT/MLLM that autoregressively selects a minimal set of multi‑scale spatiotemporal patches (gazes) per step.
Training combines next‑token prediction with reinforcement learning to balance task accuracy and the cost of selecting patches, learning where to look over time.
Selected patches are forwarded to the backbone model (ViT/MLLM) while redundant patches are skipped, enabling plug‑and‑play integration with existing video models.
infographic.impact: Makes large multimodal video models far more compute‑ and memory‑efficient, enabling scalable long‑form and high‑resolution video understanding in research and production settings while reducing inference cost.

title: MM-CondChain: A Programmatically Verified Benchmark for Visually Grounded Deep Compositional Reasoning
authors: Haozhan Shen, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Shuaiqi Lu, Xiaojun Tang
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to carry out visual workflows such as navigating GUIs, where the next step depends on verified visual compositional conditions (e.g., "if a permission dialog appears and the color of the interface is green, click Allow") and the process may branch or terminate early. Yet this capability remains under-evaluated: existing benchmarks focus on shallow-compositions or independent-constraints rather than deeply chained compositional condit

infographic.key_insight: MM-CondChain introduces a programmatically verified benchmark that tests MLLMs on deeply chained, visually grounded conditional workflows — including branching and early termination — revealing gaps not captured by prior shallow-composition benchmarks.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing multimodal benchmarks focus on shallow compositions or independent constraints and fail to evaluate the ability of models to verify and follow long, conditional visual workflows (e.g., GUI tasks) where decisions depend on chained visual conditions and execution may branch or stop early.
method: Design a dataset of procedurally generated multimodal scenarios that require chained, compositional visual conditions and action decisions (branching and termination).
Employ a programmatic verifier / execution engine to simulate ground-truth workflow execution and automatically validate model outputs against expected conditional branches and end states.
Benchmark multiple MLLMs with metrics that measure correctness across chain depth, branching complexity, and termination accuracy to surface failure modes.
infographic.impact: Provides a reliable, reproducible way to measure and improve MLLMs' ability to perform real-world visual workflows that require precise conditional reasoning, aiding safer and more robust deployment in GUI automation and other multimodal decision-making systems.

title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
authors: Tao Zhong, Yixun Hu, Dongzhe Zheng, Aditya Sood, Christine Allen-Blanchette
abstract: We propose Neural Field Thermal Tomography (NeFTY), a differentiable physics framework for the quantitative 3D reconstruction of material properties from transient surface temperature measurements. While traditional thermography relies on pixel-wise 1D approximations that neglect lateral diffusion, and soft-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often fail in transient diffusion scenarios due to gradient stiffness, NeFTY parameterizes the 3D diffusivity field as a continuous neural

infographic.key_insight: NeFTY uses a continuous neural field as a differentiable 3D diffusivity representation coupled to a physics-aware forward model, enabling end-to-end gradient-based reconstruction of internal material properties from transient surface temperature measurements. This overcomes limitations of 1D pixel-wise thermography and fragile PINN formulations in transient diffusion settings.
infographic.problem_solved: Converts sparse, time-resolved surface thermography data into accurate quantitative 3D maps of thermal diffusivity by accounting for lateral heat diffusion and enabling stable inversion of transient diffusion PDEs.
method: Represent the 3D thermal diffusivity field as a continuous neural field (coordinate-to-property mapping) instead of per-pixel 1D models.
Couple the neural field with a differentiable transient heat-diffusion forward model so simulated surface temperatures are fully differentiable w.r.t. the neural parameters.
Perform end-to-end gradient-based inversion from measured transient surface temperature sequences to recover the underlying 3D material property distribution.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, ML-native pipeline for quantitative non-destructive evaluation that leverages neural fields and differentiable physics — useful for researchers tackling PDE-constrained inverse problems, improved defect detection, and material characterization workflows.

title: Too Vivid to Be Real? Benchmarking and Calibrating Generative Color Fidelity
authors: Zhengyao Fang, Zexi Jia, Yijia Zhong, Pengcheng Luo, Jinchao Zhang
abstract: Recent advances in text-to-image (T2I) generation have greatly improved visual quality, yet producing images that appear visually authentic to real-world photography remains challenging. This is partly due to biases in existing evaluation paradigms: human ratings and preference-trained metrics often favor visually vivid images with exaggerated saturation and contrast, which make generations often too vivid to be real even when prompted for realistic-style images. To address this issue, we presen

infographic.key_insight: Existing T2I evaluation (human ratings and preference-trained metrics) biases models toward overly vivid, oversaturated outputs; calibrating both benchmarks and model outputs for color fidelity yields generations that better match real-world photographic color distributions.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch where evaluation signals and model training encourage exaggerated saturation/contrast, causing 'too vivid to be real' images even under realism prompts and masking true color fidelity issues.
method: Construct a color-fidelity benchmark pairing real photographs with realism prompts and annotations that emphasize photographic color accuracy rather than subjective vividness.
Introduce objective color-fidelity measures (e.g., perceptual color distance and distribution divergence) and recalibrate preference-trained metrics to penalize unrealistic saturation/contrast.

Provide a calibration procedure (post-hoc score scaling or simple color-correction module) to adjust generative outputs or metric scores so model preferences align with photographic color distributions.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably evaluate and tune generative models for photographic realism (not just visual vividness), reducing over-saturation artifacts and improving trustworthiness of T2I outputs in applications requiring authentic colors.

title: GroundCount: Grounding Vision-Language Models with Object Detection for Mitigating Counting Hallucinations
authors: Boyuan Chen, Minghao Shao, Siddharth Garg, Ramesh Karri, Muhammad Shafique
abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit persistent hallucinations in counting tasks, with accuracy substantially lower than other visual reasoning tasks (excluding sentiment). This phenomenon persists even in state-of-the-art reasoning-capable VLMs. Conversely, CNN-based object detection models (ODMs) such as YOLO excel at spatial localization and instance counting with minimal computational overhead. We propose GroundCount, a framework that augments VLMs with explicit spatial grounding from ODMs

infographic.key_insight: GroundCount reduces counting hallucinations in vision–language models by explicitly grounding them with object detections (bounding boxes + instance counts), combining the localization strengths of detectors with the reasoning strengths of VLMs.
infographic.problem_solved: VLMs frequently hallucinate numeric answers in counting tasks (low counting accuracy despite strong visual reasoning elsewhere); GroundCount addresses unreliable counting by injecting explicit, detector-derived spatial and instance information into the VLM pipeline.
method: Run a lightweight object detector (e.g., YOLO) to produce bounding boxes, class labels, and instance counts for an input image.
Integrate detector outputs into the VLM via grounding tokens/adapter layers or prompt augmentation so the model conditions on explicit spatial instances when answering count queries.
Aggregate detector-backed evidence (e.g., filter/merge detections, consensus counting) while preserving the VLM for higher-level reasoning — minimal compute overhead, improved numerical fidelity.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, low-overhead way to make VLM outputs more reliable for counting and instance-level queries, enabling safer and more accurate use in VQA, inventory, robotics, and scene understanding workloads.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image → object detector (boxes) → GroundCount fusion → VLM answer (highlight grounding flow)
