title: DynVLA: Learning World Dynamics for Action Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
authors: Shuyao Shang, Bing Zhan, Yunfei Yan, Yuqi Wang, Yingyan Li
abstract: We propose DynVLA, a driving VLA model that introduces a new CoT paradigm termed Dynamics CoT. DynVLA forecasts compact world dynamics before action generation, enabling more informed and physically grounded decision-making. To obtain compact dynamics representations, DynVLA introduces a Dynamics Tokenizer that compresses future evolution into a small set of dynamics tokens. Considering the rich environment dynamics in interaction-intensive driving scenarios, DynVLA decouples ego-centric and env

infographic.key_insight: DynVLA first forecasts a compact, tokenized representation of future world dynamics (Dynamics CoT) before generating driving actions, enabling more physically grounded and interaction-aware decisions.
infographic.problem_solved: Making safe, interpretable action decisions in interaction-heavy autonomous driving is hard when future scene evolution is not explicitly modeled or is too high-dimensional for efficient reasoning.
method: Introduce Dynamics CoT: perform chain-of-thought style reasoning over predicted future dynamics prior to action generation.
Dynamics Tokenizer: compress future scene evolution into a small set of compact dynamics tokens that summarize physically relevant changes.
Decouple ego-centric and environment dynamics so the model can reason about self-motion and surrounding-agent behaviors separately and then fuse them for action selection.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable way to inject explicit, low-dimensional world dynamics into driving decision modules, improving physical plausibility, interpretability, and robustness for autonomous driving systems.

title: Federated Learning-driven Beam Management in LEO 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Maria Lamprini Bartsioka, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Athanasios D. Panagopoulos, Dimitra I. Kaklamani, Iakovos S. Venieris
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) require efficient beam management under dynamic propagation conditions. This work investigates Federated Learning (FL)-based beam selection in LEO satellite constellations, where orbital planes operate as distributed learners through the utilization of High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS). Two models, a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and a Graph Neural Network (GNN), are evaluated using realistic channel and beamforming data. Results demonstr

infographic.key_insight: Federated learning across LEO orbital planes using HAPS as aggregators enables efficient, privacy-preserving beam selection; topology-aware GNNs can better capture spatial relationships and often outperform MLPs in dynamic NTN conditions.
infographic.problem_solved: Efficient beam management in LEO Non-Terrestrial Networks under rapidly changing propagation and strict inter-node communication/privacy constraints, avoiding costly centralized data collection.
method: Model orbital planes as distributed learners and use High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS) for federated aggregation to limit raw-data transfer.
Train and compare two local models — an MLP baseline and a Graph Neural Network (GNN) that encodes spatial/topological relations — using realistic channel and beamforming datasets.
Evaluate trade-offs in selection accuracy, communication overhead, and adaptability to LEO mobility and propagation dynamics.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable, communication-efficient approach for 6G NTN beam management that preserves data locality; ML practitioners can adopt FL+GNN designs to improve topology-aware decisions while reducing central coordination and data-sharing requirements.

title: Does AI See like Art Historians? Interpreting How Vision Language Models Recognize Artistic Style
authors: Marvin Limpijankit, Milad Alshomary, Yassin Oulad Daoud, Amith Ananthram, Tim Trombley
abstract: VLMs have become increasingly proficient at a range of computer vision tasks, such as visual question answering and object detection. This includes increasingly strong capabilities in the domain of art, from analyzing artwork to generation of art. In an interdisciplinary collaboration between computer scientists and art historians, we characterize the mechanisms underlying VLMs' ability to predict artistic style and assess the extent to which they align with the criteria art historians use to re

infographic.key_insight: Vision-language models can predict artistic style using a mix of visual and textual cues, but their internal criteria only partially align with how art historians reason about style—revealing both meaningful overlaps and systematic differences.
infographic.problem_solved: Clarifies what cues VLMs use to recognize artistic style and assesses whether those cues correspond to art-historical criteria, addressing the interpretability gap between model predictions and humanities expertise.
method: Apply interpretability tools (attention/grad maps, concept probing) to VLMs to identify visual and textual features driving style predictions.
Compare model-derived cues against art-historical annotations and criteria via collaboration with art historians to evaluate alignment and divergence.
Quantify and visualize sources of agreement and bias (e.g., color, texture, composition, metadata) to explain when and why models succeed or fail.
infographic.impact: Helps practitioners build more transparent, reliable multimodal systems for cultural heritage and fine-grained visual tasks, and guides dataset curation and model evaluation by surfacing domain-specific failure modes.

title: RCTs & Human Uplift Studies: Methodological Challenges and Practical Solutions for Frontier AI Evaluation
authors: Patricia Paskov, Kevin Wei, Shen Zhou Hong, Dan Bateyko, Xavier Roberts-Gaal
abstract: Human uplift studies - or studies that measure AI effects on human performance relative to a status quo, typically using randomized controlled trial (RCT) methodology - are increasingly used to inform deployment, governance, and safety decisions for frontier AI systems. While the methods underlying these studies are well-established, their interaction with the distinctive properties of frontier AI systems remains underexamined, particularly when results are used to inform high-stakes decisions.

infographic.key_insight: Established RCT methods are still useful for measuring AI-driven human uplift, but frontier AI systems systematically violate key RCT assumptions (e.g., non‑stationarity, interference, scale, adaptivity). The paper maps those failure modes and offers concrete design, analysis, and governance fixes so RCTs yield reliable, high‑stakes evidence.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the gap between traditional RCT practice and the distinctive properties of frontier AI systems that can bias or invalidate human uplift studies, preventing misleading conclusions in deployment and governance decisions.
method: Systematically diagnose how frontier-AI properties (non‑stationarity, emergent behavior, interference/contagion, heterogeneity, scale) conflict with core RCT assumptions.

Propose practical adjustments for study design and analysis (e.g., pre-registration, stratification and blocking, interference-aware designs, sequential monitoring, robust estimands, simulation-based power checks) plus operational safety/privacy controls.
Provide actionable guidance: checklists, templates, and governance processes to link study results to high‑stakes deployment decisions safely.
infographic.impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and evaluators concise, implementable methods to run and interpret human uplift RCTs for frontier systems, reducing the risk of erroneous policy or deployment decisions and improving evidence quality.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side diagram: standard RCT assumptions vs frontier AI violations (icons for non‑stationarity, interference, scale).

title: A benchmarking framework for embodied neuromorphic agents
authors: Giulia D’Angelo, Jens E. Pedersen, Taimoor Hassan, Matteo Cianchetti, Josh Bongard
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01197-w

Combining soft robotics with neuromorphic engineering is a promising approach in embodied intelligence. Giulia d’Angelo et al. contribute to progress in this field by developing a framework for benchmarking neuromorphic controllers on soft robotic platforms.

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces a standardized benchmarking framework that lets researchers evaluate and compare neuromorphic controllers on soft robotic platforms, enabling reproducible, hardware-aware assessments of embodied intelligence.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized, reproducible benchmarks for neuromorphic controllers in soft robotics—fragmented evaluation protocols, inconsistent metrics (energy, latency, robustness), and poor comparability across simulators and hardware.
method: Define task suite and metrics tailored to embodied neuromorphic agents (e.g., energy use, latency, control robustness, adaptability).
Provide an integrated pipeline combining simulation and real-world hardware interfaces for soft robots and neuromorphic processors.
Deliver an open-source evaluation suite and reference controllers to enable reproducible experiments and fair comparisons.
infographic.impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a practical way to measure controller performance across energy, speed, and robustness trade-offs, accelerating reproducible research and informed co-design of neuromorphic algorithms and soft bodies.

title: V2M-Zero: Zero-Pair Time-Aligned Video-to-Music Generation
authors: Yan-Bo Lin, Jonah Casebeer, Long Mai, Aniruddha Mahapatra, Gedas Bertasius
abstract: Generating music that temporally aligns with video events is challenging for existing text-to-music models, which lack fine-grained temporal control. We introduce V2M-Zero, a zero-pair video-to-music generation approach that outputs time-aligned music for video. Our method is motivated by a key observation: temporal synchronization requires matching when and how much change occurs, not what changes. While musical and visual events differ semantically, they exhibit shared temporal structure that

infographic.key_insight: Temporal synchronization between video and music can be achieved by matching when and how much change occurs (temporal structure) rather than trying to map semantic content across modalities.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing text-to-music and cross-modal generators lack fine-grained temporal control and cannot produce music that is time-aligned to video events without paired training data; V2M-Zero enables zero-pair, time-aligned video-to-music generation.
method: Extract modality-agnostic temporal-change representations from video (motion/scene-change signals) and music (onset/intensity patterns).
Learn a zero-pair alignment that matches temporal change patterns across modalities, focusing on 'when' and 'how much' change rather than semantic correspondence.
Condition a music synthesis module with the aligned temporal-control signal to generate time-aligned audio for the input video.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way to generate synchronized music for arbitrary videos without paired datasets, enabling scalable multimodal content creation and refined temporal control for audio-visual generation tasks.

title: FRIEND: Federated Learning for Joint Optimization of multi-RIS Configuration and Eavesdropper Intelligent Detection in B5G Networks
authors: Maria Lamprini A. Bartsioka, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Anastasios K. Papazafeiropoulos, Maria A. Seimeni, Dimitra I. Kaklamani
abstract: As wireless systems evolve toward Beyond 5G (B5G), the adoption of cell-free (CF) millimeter-wave (mmWave) architectures combined with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) is emerging as a key enabler for ultra-reliable, high-capacity, scalable, and secure Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) communications. However, safeguarding these complex and distributed environments against eavesdropping remains a critical challenge, particularly when conventional security mechanisms struggle to overc

infographic.key_insight: FRIEND uses federated learning to jointly optimize multi‑RIS configurations and intelligent eavesdropper detection across distributed B5G cell‑free mmWave nodes, improving secrecy and detection without centralizing raw data.
infographic.problem_solved: Securing distributed CF mmWave B5G/IIoT networks with multiple RIS elements against passive and active eavesdroppers while avoiding centralized data collection and scaling to many edge nodes; conventional centralized or isolated approaches struggle with privacy, latency, and coordination.
method: Design a federated learning pipeline (FRIEND) where edge nodes (APs/RIS controllers/UEs) locally train detection and configuration models and share model updates for privacy‑preserving aggregation.

Joint optimization loop that alternates between learned eavesdropper detection and multi‑RIS configuration (beamforming/profile selection) to maximize secrecy metrics and detection accuracy under realistic mmWave/CF channels.

Lightweight communication and aggregation strategies tailored for IIoT/B5G constraints, plus performance evaluation via simulations comparing secrecy rate and detection error against baseline centralized and non‑cooperative schemes.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates a practical, privacy‑aware way to apply federated ML to physical‑layer security and multi‑agent control in next‑generation wireless systems, giving AI/ML practitioners a blueprint for distributed model design and evaluation in edge wireless environments.

title: Factorized Neural Implicit DMD for Parametric Dynamics
authors: Siyuan Chen, Zhecheng Wang, Yixin Chen, Yue Chang, Peter Yichen Chen
abstract: A data-driven, model-free approach to modeling the temporal evolution of physical systems mitigates the need for explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Even when physical priors such as partial differential equations are available, such systems often reside in high-dimensional state spaces and exhibit nonlinear dynamics, making traditional numerical solvers computationally expensive and ill-suited for real-time analysis and control. Consider the problem of learning a parametric flow of a

infographic.key_insight: The paper combines neural implicit representations with a factorized Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) to learn compact, parametric flows: spatial modes are represented implicitly while parameter- and time-dependence are separated and propagated linearly in a learned latent DMD space. This yields accurate, efficient predictions across parameter variations without needing explicit governing equations.
infographic.problem_solved: How to build fast, low-dimensional, data-driven models that generalize across continuous parameter changes for high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems where traditional solvers or fixed reduced bases fail.
method: Learn neural implicit representations of system state (continuous spatial field) conditioned on parameters and time.
Factorize the representation into shared spatial modes and parameter/time-dependent coefficients.
Apply a learned DMD/linear operator in the coefficient (latent) space to propagate dynamics and enable interpolation/extrapolation across parameters.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a scalable, physics-agnostic reduced-order modeling tool for real-time prediction, control, and parameter studies of complex dynamical systems, reducing compute cost while retaining accuracy over parameter variations.

title: Agentar-Fin-OCR
authors: Siyi Qian, Xiongfei Bai, Bingtao Fu, Yichen Lu, Gaoyang Zhang
abstract: In this paper, we propose Agentar-Fin-OCR, a document parsing system tailored to financial-domain documents, transforming ultra-long financial PDFs into semantically consistent, highly accurate, structured outputs with auditing-grade provenance. To address finance-specific challenges such as complex layouts, cross-page structural discontinuities, and cell-level referencing capability, Agentar-Fin-OCR combines (1) a Cross-page Contents Consolidation algorithm to restore continuity across pages an

infographic.key_insight: Agentar-Fin-OCR converts ultra-long, complex financial PDFs into semantically consistent, audited structured outputs by restoring cross-page continuity and enabling cell-level references, yielding high accuracy suitable for regulated finance workflows.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses finance-specific document parsing challenges: complex multi-column and table layouts, structural discontinuities across pages, loss of cell-level relationships, and the need for audit-grade provenance in extraction results.
method: Cross-page Contents Consolidation: algorithmically stitch and restore logical continuity of fragmented elements (tables, captions, footnotes) that span pages.
Layout-aware OCR + table reconstruction: combine spatial/layout features with text recognition to recover table cells and explicit cell-level references and relationships.
Provenance & validation layer: emit structured outputs with precise source pointers (page/coordinate), confidence scores, and audit traces for downstream verification.
infographic.impact: Makes extraction from long, heterogeneous financial documents reliable and auditable, reducing manual cleanup and enabling safer downstream ML/analytics, compliance checks, and model training on high-quality structured data.

title: Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration for General-Purpose Dexterous Manipulation
authors: Zixuan Liu, Ruoyi Qiao, Chenrui Tie, Xuanwei Liu, Yunfan Lou
abstract: Deep Reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved remarkable success in domains with well-defined reward structures, such as Atari games and locomotion. In contrast, dexterous manipulation lacks general-purpose reward formulations and typically depends on task-specific, handcrafted priors to guide hand-object interactions. We propose Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration (CCGE), a general exploration method designed for general-purpose dexterous manipulation tasks. CCGE represents contact state as th

infographic.key_insight: CCGE introduces an intrinsic exploration signal based on contact coverage that encourages a dexterous hand to discover diverse, meaningful hand–object contact modes, enabling general-purpose manipulation without task-specific reward engineering.
infographic.problem_solved: Dexterous manipulation suffers from sparse or ill-defined rewards and relies on handcrafted priors to shape hand–object interactions; CCGE addresses poor exploration and the lack of a general-purpose reward for discovering useful contact behaviors.
method: Represent contact state as a compact descriptor (e.g., contact map / contact patch set / contact graph) that summarizes which hand surfaces touch object surfaces.
Maintain a coverage memory / novelty estimator over contact descriptors and compute an intrinsic reward that increases when the agent generates previously under-covered contact states.
Integrate the intrinsic contact-coverage reward with standard DRL algorithms so agents learn diverse, transferable manipulation strategies without task-specific shaping.
infographic.impact: CCGE reduces the need for task-specific reward design and improves exploration and sample efficiency in sparse-reward dexterous tasks, making it easier for practitioners to train general-purpose manipulation skills transferable across objects and tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensor input → contact descriptor extraction → coverage memory → intrinsic reward → RL agent loop.

title: Understanding the Use of a Large Language Model-Powered Guide to Make Virtual Reality Accessible for Blind and Low Vision People
authors: Jazmin Collins, Sharon Y Lin, Tianqi Liu, Andrea Stevenson Won, Shiri Azenkot
abstract: As social virtual reality (VR) grows more popular, addressing accessibility for blind and low vision (BLV) users is increasingly critical. Researchers have proposed an AI "sighted guide" to help users navigate VR and answer their questions, but it has not been studied with users. To address this gap, we developed a large language model (LLM)-powered guide and studied its use with 16 BLV participants in virtual environments with confederates posing as other users. We found that when alone, partic

infographic.key_insight: An LLM-powered “sighted guide” can meaningfully support blind and low vision (BLV) users to navigate and ask questions in social VR, but its usefulness depends on social context, accuracy, and trust-related concerns uncovered in a 16-participant study.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of practical, user-evaluated solutions for making social VR navigation and in-situ information access accessible to BLV people.
method: Built an LLM-powered guide agent that provides navigation help and answers user queries inside social VR environments.
Conducted a mixed-methods user study with 16 BLV participants interacting in VR while confederates posed as other users to simulate social scenarios.
Collected behavioral data and qualitative feedback to evaluate usability, perceived usefulness, trust, and social acceptability.
infographic.impact: Provides concrete evidence and design lessons for deploying LLM agents in accessibility-sensitive, social VR settings — highlighting the need to handle accuracy, personalization, multimodal cues, and social dynamics when building accessible AI features.

title: When Learning Rates Go Wrong: Early Structural Signals in PPO Actor-Critic
authors: Alberto Fernández-Hernández, Cristian Pérez-Corral, Jose I. Mestre, Manuel F. Dolz, Jose Duato
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning systems are highly sensitive to the learning rate (LR), and selecting stable and performant training runs often requires extensive hyperparameter search. In Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) actor--critic methods, small LR values lead to slow convergence, whereas large LR values may induce instability or collapse. We analyse this phenomenon from the behavior of the hidden neurons in the network using the Overfitting-Underfitting Indicator (OUI), a metric that quantif

infographic.key_insight: Early structural signals in hidden neurons, captured by the Overfitting-Underfitting Indicator (OUI), reliably predict whether a PPO actor–critic run with a given learning rate will converge, collapse, or underfit—often within the initial training steps—enabling early intervention.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses PPO's extreme sensitivity to learning rate and the expensive, time-consuming hyperparameter search by providing an early indicator of run stability and eventual performance.
method: Compute the Overfitting–Underfitting Indicator (OUI) from hidden neuron activations during the first training epochs of PPO actor–critic runs.
Correlate OUI trajectories across a range of learning rates with long-term outcomes (convergence, collapse, slow learning) to identify reproducible structural signatures.
Use the early OUI signal to classify runs as stable/unstable and propose interventions (early stop, LR reduction or increase, or reinitialization) to avoid wasted compute.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to detect unstable or doomed PPO runs early, reducing wasted compute and accelerating hyperparameter tuning; improves reliability of RL training by informing learning-rate choices and automated interventions.
visual_elements: Timeline plot: early OUI trajectory (first epochs) overlaid with final return to show predictive power.
Heatmap: hidden-neuron activation patterns across different learning rates, highlighting structural differences for collapse vs successful runs.
Scatter plot: learning rate vs final performance colored by early OUI classification (stable / underfitting / collapsing).
Flowchart: suggested workflow — measure OUI early → classify run → apply intervention (stop / adjust LR / continue).

title: Adaptive Clinical-Aware Latent Diffusion for Multimodal Brain Image Generation and Missing Modality Imputation
authors: Rong Zhou, Houliang Zhou, Yao Su, Brian Y. Chen, Yu Zhang
abstract: Multimodal neuroimaging provides complementary insights for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis, yet clinical datasets frequently suffer from missing modalities. We propose ACADiff, a framework that synthesizes missing brain imaging modalities through adaptive clinical-aware diffusion. ACADiff learns mappings between incomplete multimodal observations and target modalities by progressively denoising latent representations while attending to available imaging data and clinical metadata. The framework e

infographic.key_insight: ACADiff uses clinical-aware latent diffusion to synthesize missing brain imaging modalities by progressively denoising latent representations conditioned on available scans and patient metadata, producing clinically coherent imputations with high fidelity.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the missing-modality problem in multimodal neuroimaging datasets (common in Alzheimer's research) by generating plausible, clinically consistent images for absent modalities so subjects need not be discarded and downstream models can use more complete data.
method: Latent diffusion in a compressed representation to efficiently generate high-quality imaging modalities.
Adaptive conditioning that attends to available imaging modalities and clinical metadata (e.g., age, diagnosis, cognitive scores) during progressive denoising.
Joint training with reconstruction/modality-consistency and clinical-aware losses to ensure realistic and diagnostically relevant imputations.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way for ML practitioners to recover missing medical imaging modalities, improving dataset completeness and robustness of downstream diagnostic models while leveraging clinical context for more reliable syntheses.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (available scans + clinical metadata) → latent encoder → conditioned diffusion denoising → decoded synthesized modality.
Denoising timeline: sequence of latent-space steps showing coarse-to-fine image refinement.

title: ReCoSplat: Autoregressive Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting Using Render-and-Compare
authors: Freeman Cheng, Botao Ye, Xueting Li, Junqi You, Fangneng Zhan
abstract: Online novel view synthesis remains challenging, requiring robust scene reconstruction from sequential, often unposed, observations. We present ReCoSplat, an autoregressive feed-forward Gaussian Splatting model supporting posed or unposed inputs, with or without camera intrinsics. While assembling local Gaussians using camera poses scales better than canonical-space prediction, it creates a dilemma during training: using ground-truth poses ensures stability but causes a distribution mismatch whe

infographic.key_insight: ReCoSplat combines an autoregressive, feed‑forward Gaussian splatting representation with a render‑and‑compare training strategy to enable robust online novel‑view synthesis from sequential posed or unposed observations, even when camera intrinsics are unknown. This closes the gap between stable training with ground‑truth poses and realistic inference with predicted poses.
infographic.problem_solved: Online novel‑view synthesis from sequential, often unposed and low‑quality observations — addressing scalability and the train/test distribution mismatch caused by training with ground‑truth poses but deploying with predicted/unknown poses and intrinsics.
method: Autoregressive feed‑forward Gaussian Splatting: assemble local Gaussians per incoming view (scales better than canonical‑space prediction and supports online updates).

Render‑and‑compare training objective: render predicted assemblies and compare to observations to align training with inference, mitigating distribution mismatch between ground‑truth and predicted poses.
Flexible input handling: supports posed or unposed inputs and operates with or without known camera intrinsics, enabling deployment in streaming/robotic settings.
infographic.impact: Makes real‑time, scalable novel‑view synthesis more robust to unposed and imperfect input streams, reducing reliance on accurate camera metadata and enabling practical deployment in robotics, AR/VR and online reconstruction pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sequential/autoregressive assembly of local Gaussians vs canonical‑space prediction (highlighting scalability).
Render‑and‑compare schematic: predicted render vs observed image with error signal back to Gaussian assembly and pose predictions.
Qualitative comparisons: novel‑view renderings for posed vs unposed inputs and with/without intrinsics.

title: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition
authors: Lucas Prieto, Edward Stevinson, Melih Barsbey, Tolga Birdal, Pedro A. M. Mediano
abstract: A central idea in mechanistic interpretability is that neural networks represent more features than they have dimensions, arranging them in superposition to form an over-complete basis. This framing has been influential, motivating dictionary learning approaches such as sparse autoencoders. However, superposition has mostly been studied in idealized settings where features are sparse and uncorrelated. In these settings, superposition is typically understood as introducing interference that must

infographic.key_insight: Correlations in the data—not just sparsity or idealized independence—determine how models hide features in superposition; data statistics shape a predictable geometry of overlapping feature vectors rather than random interference.
infographic.problem_solved: Explains how and why neural networks arrange more features than dimensions (superposition) on realistic, correlated datasets, resolving the gap between idealized theory and practical representations.
method: Analytical framework that links data second-order statistics (covariance/correlations) to the geometric arrangement of learned feature vectors.
Controlled experiments on synthetic and real datasets to measure how changing correlation structure alters feature overlap, alignment, and interference.
Quantitative visualizations and metrics that map data correlation matrices to observable feature-geometry patterns in trained models.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners and interpretability researchers with a principled way to predict and diagnose feature superposition from dataset statistics, improving model analysis, compression, and feature decoding strategies.
visual_elements: Schematic comparing orthogonal vs. superposed feature vectors in high-dimensional space, annotated to show correlation-driven clustering/alignment.
Paired heatmaps: data correlation matrix vs. learned feature overlap matrix to show one-to-one structural relationships.
Line/bar charts showing how varying correlation strength changes interference, feature sparsity, and task performance.
Flow diagram: data statistics → theoretical prediction of geometry → empirical measurement on models.

title: PathMem: Toward Cognition-Aligned Memory Transformation for Pathology MLLMs
authors: Jinyue Li, Yuci Liang, Qiankun Li, Xinheng Lyu, Jiayu Qian
abstract: Computational pathology demands both visual pattern recognition and dynamic integration of structured domain knowledge, including taxonomy, grading criteria, and clinical evidence. In practice, diagnostic reasoning requires linking morphological evidence with formal diagnostic and grading criteria. Although multimodal large language models (MLLMs) demonstrate strong vision language reasoning capabilities, they lack explicit mechanisms for structured knowledge integration and interpretable memory

infographic.key_insight: PathMem adds a cognition-aligned memory transformation to pathology MLLMs so they can explicitly encode and retrieve structured domain knowledge (taxonomy, grading, clinical evidence) and link it to visual findings, producing more interpretable diagnostic reasoning.
infographic.problem_solved: MLLMs for computational pathology lack mechanisms to integrate formal, structured medical knowledge and to produce traceable, interpretable memory traces that link morphological evidence to diagnostic and grading criteria.
method: Introduce a cognition-aligned memory transformation module that encodes taxonomy, grading rules, and clinical evidence as structured, queryable memory representations.
Link visual features extracted from pathology images to memory nodes for dynamic retrieval and alignment with diagnostic criteria during reasoning.
Provide interpretable read/write traces so the MLLM’s diagnostic steps can be inspected and mapped back to formal criteria and evidence.
infographic.impact: Enables pathology MLLMs to produce diagnoses that are better aligned with clinical protocols and easier to audit, improving trust, reproducibility, and practical deployment in clinical workflows.

title: Think Before You Lie: How Reasoning Improves Honesty
authors: Ann Yuan, Asma Ghandeharioun, Carter Blum, Alicia Machado, Jessica Hoffmann
abstract: While existing evaluations of large language models (LLMs) measure deception rates, the underlying conditions that give rise to deceptive behavior are poorly understood. We investigate this question using a novel dataset of realistic moral trade-offs where honesty incurs variable costs. Contrary to humans, who tend to become less honest given time to deliberate (Capraro, 2017; Capraro et al., 2019), we find that reasoning consistently increases honesty across scales and for several LLM families.

infographic.key_insight: Prompting LLMs to 'think' (i.e., elicit reasoning) makes them more honest — across model sizes and families — a reversal of the pattern observed in human subjects where deliberation can increase dishonesty.
infographic.problem_solved: Clarifies when and why LLMs behave deceptively by isolating the effect of deliberative reasoning on honesty using controlled moral trade-offs with variable costs.
method: Constructed a novel dataset of realistic moral trade-offs where honesty carries different costs to the model/agent.
Evaluated multiple LLM families and scales, comparing baseline (shallow) responses vs. reasoning-elicited responses (e.g., chain-of-thought prompts).
Measured honesty rates as a function of cost and model type to quantify how reasoning changes deceptive behavior.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates a practical intervention — encouraging explicit reasoning — that reduces deception in LLMs, informing safer prompting and evaluation practices for practitioners and alignment researchers.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing honesty rates with vs. without reasoning across several model families and sizes.
Schematic/example of a moral trade-off prompt showing the honesty cost and the expected truthful vs. deceptive responses.
Line plot of honesty rate as a function of honesty 'cost' (cost–honesty curve) to show sensitivity.
Flow diagram contrasting baseline prompting vs. reasoning-eliciting prompting and their downstream honesty outcomes.

title: From Semantics to Pixels: Coarse-to-Fine Masked Autoencoders for Hierarchical Visual Understanding
authors: Wenzhao Xiang, Yue Wu, Hongyang Yu, Feng Gao, Fan Yang
abstract: Self-supervised visual pre-training methods face an inherent tension: contrastive learning (CL) captures global semantics but loses fine-grained detail, while masked image modeling (MIM) preserves local textures but suffers from "attention drift" due to semantically-agnostic random masking. We propose C2FMAE, a coarse-to-fine masked autoencoder that resolves this tension by explicitly learning hierarchical visual representations across three data granularities: semantic masks (scene-level), inst

infographic.key_insight: C2FMAE resolves the trade-off between global semantics and local textures by learning hierarchical visual representations with a coarse-to-fine masked autoencoder that moves from scene-level semantic masks to fine pixel reconstruction.
infographic.problem_solved: Self-supervised visual pretraining methods either capture global semantics (contrastive learning) or local textures (masked image modeling); random masking in MIM causes attention drift and fails to preserve semantics. This paper addresses how to jointly learn both levels without semantic-agnostic masking.
method: Generate semantically-aware coarse masks (scene-level) and progressively refine to instance-level and pixel/patch-level masks for masking and reconstruction.
Train a masked autoencoder in a coarse-to-fine curriculum so the model first captures global structure and then recovers instance details and local textures.
Use multi-granularity reconstruction objectives (and/or auxiliary semantic consistency losses) to align global semantics with fine-grained pixel prediction and reduce attention drift.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical pretraining strategy that preserves both high-level semantics and low-level details, improving transfer performance on downstream vision tasks (classification, detection, segmentation) and making representations more robust and interpretable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing coarse-to-fine masking stages (scene → instance → pixel) and the corresponding encoder/decoder flow
Before/after attention maps or reconstruction examples illustrating reduced attention drift and improved detail recovery
Bar chart comparing downstream task performance (e.g., linear probe, detection, segmentation) against CL and standard MIM baselines

title: CREATE: Testing LLMs for Associative Creativity
authors: Manya Wadhwa, Tiasa Singha Roy, Harvey Lederman, Junyi Jessy Li, Greg Durrett
abstract: A key component of creativity is associative reasoning: the ability to draw novel yet meaningful connections between concepts. We introduce CREATE, a benchmark designed to evaluate models' capacity for creative associative reasoning. CREATE requires models to generate sets of paths connecting concepts in a model's parametric knowledge. Paths should have high specificity (distinctiveness and closeness of the concept connection) and high diversity (dissimilarity from other paths), and models are s

infographic.key_insight: CREATE is a benchmark that measures LLMs' associative creativity by asking models to generate sets of concept-connecting paths and scoring them for both specificity (how distinct and meaningful each connection is) and diversity (how different the paths are from one another).
infographic.problem_solved: Provides a principled way to evaluate creative associative reasoning in language models, addressing the gap where models produce generic or repetitive links and where existing benchmarks don't quantify novelty vs. meaningfulness.
method: Define a path-generation task: given concepts, models must produce multiple paths that connect them using their parametric knowledge.
Introduce complementary metrics—specificity (distinctiveness and closeness of connections) and diversity (dissimilarity across paths)—to score sets of paths rather than single outputs.
Establish an evaluation protocol to compare models' associative reasoning capabilities and surface strengths/failure modes.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to benchmark and improve LLMs' ability to form novel yet relevant associations, guiding model development, prompt design, and evaluation for creative reasoning tasks.

Scatterplot or 2D chart with axes Specificity vs Diversity to illustrate model tradeoffs and clustering of model behaviors.

title: No Image, No Problem: End-to-End Multi-Task Cardiac Analysis from Undersampled k-Space
authors: Yundi Zhang, Sevgi Gokce Kafali, Niklas Bubeck, Daniel Rueckert, Jiazhen Pan
abstract: Conventional clinical CMR pipelines rely on a sequential "reconstruct-then-analyze" paradigm, forcing an ill-posed intermediate step that introduces avoidable artifacts and information bottlenecks. This creates a fundamental mathematical paradox: it attempts to recover high-dimensional pixel arrays (i.e., images) from undersampled k-space, rather than directly extracting the low-dimensional physiological labels actually required for diagnosis. To unlock the direct diagnostic potential of k-space

infographic.key_insight: The paper demonstrates that clinical cardiac labels can be predicted directly from undersampled MRI k-space in an end-to-end, multi-task model, removing the need for an intermediate image reconstruction step and avoiding its artifacts and information bottleneck.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses the ill-posed reconstruct-then-analyze paradigm that forces recovery of full images from undersampled k-space, which introduces artifacts and wastes capacity when the clinical goal is low-dimensional diagnostic labels.
method: Train an end-to-end neural architecture that maps undersampled k-space inputs to multiple cardiac tasks (e.g., segmentation, quantification, diagnosis) without producing intermediate images.
Use a shared k-space encoder and task-specific decoders with a joint multi-task loss so representations are tuned for clinical targets rather than image fidelity.
Incorporate MRI physics constraints (e.g., data-consistency layers or sampling-aware modules) to respect k-space structure while learning task-driven features.
infographic.impact: This approach shortens and stabilizes the clinical pipeline, reducing latency and artifact-driven errors while enabling task-optimized acquisition and models — a practical blueprint for task-first medical AI systems working directly from raw sensor data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: undersampled k-space → shared encoder → multiple task heads (segmentation, volumes, diagnosis) vs traditional reconstruct-then-analyze flow.
Before/after comparison: artifacts introduced by reconstruction vs clean, accurate task outputs from direct k-space inference.

title: SignalMC-MED: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Biosignal Foundation Models on Single-Lead ECG and PPG
authors: Fredrik K. Gustafsson, Xiao Gu, Mattia Carletti, Patitapaban Palo, David W. Eyre
abstract: Recent biosignal foundation models (FMs) have demonstrated promising performance across diverse clinical prediction tasks, yet systematic evaluation on long-duration multimodal data remains limited. We introduce SignalMC-MED, a benchmark for evaluating biosignal FMs on synchronized single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) data. Derived from the MC-MED dataset, SignalMC-MED comprises 22,256 visits with 10-minute overlapping ECG and PPG signals, and includes 20 clinically r

infographic.key_insight: SignalMC-MED is a standardized multimodal benchmark that enables rigorous evaluation of biosignal foundation models on synchronized, long-duration single-lead ECG and PPG recordings, revealing model strengths and failure modes on clinically relevant tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of systematic, long-duration multimodal evaluation for biosignal foundation models by providing a large, synchronized ECG+PPG benchmark derived from MC-MED (22,256 visits with 10-minute overlapping signals).

title: ER-Pose: Rethinking Keypoint-Driven Representation Learning for Real-Time Human Pose Estimation
authors: Nanjun Li, Pinqi Cheng, Zean Liu, Minghe Tian, Xuanyin Wang
abstract: Single-stage multi-person pose estimation aims to jointly perform human localization and keypoint prediction within a unified framework, offering advantages in inference efficiency and architectural simplicity. Consequently, multi-scale real-time detection architectures, such as YOLO-like models, are widely adopted for real-time pose estimation. However, these approaches typically inherit a box-driven modeling paradigm from object detection, in which pose estimation is implicitly constrained by

infographic.key_insight: ER-Pose replaces the conventional box-driven paradigm with a keypoint-driven representation learning strategy, enabling single-stage real-time pose models to learn spatial relationships among keypoints directly and thus improve accuracy without sacrificing speed.
infographic.problem_solved: Single-stage multi-person pose methods often inherit object-detection box-centric constraints that limit keypoint learning, assignment, and multi-scale fusion—this work addresses the resulting accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for real-time systems.
method: Decouple pose learning from bounding-box supervision by designing keypoint-centric representations and targets that emphasize spatial relations among joints.
Integrate the keypoint representation into a YOLO-like single-stage detection backbone with a dedicated keypoint decoding branch and multi-scale feature fusion for real-time inference.
Use tailored training objectives and assignment strategies that prioritize precise keypoint localization and robust multi-person separation in crowded scenes.
infographic.impact: Offers a practical route to more accurate and robust real-time multi-person pose estimation while keeping the simplicity and speed of single-stage detectors—useful for mobile/edge deployment, robotics, and live analytics.

title: How Far Can Unsupervised RLVR Scale LLM Training?
authors: Bingxiang He, Yuxin Zuo, Zeyuan Liu, Shangziqi Zhao, Zixuan Fu
abstract: Unsupervised reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (URLVR) offers a pathway to scale LLM training beyond the supervision bottleneck by deriving rewards without ground truth labels. Recent works leverage model intrinsic signals, showing promising early gains, yet their potential and limitations remain unclear. In this work, we revisit URLVR and provide a comprehensive analysis spanning taxonomy, theory and extensive experiments. We first classify URLVR methods into intrinsic versus exter

infographic.key_insight: Unsupervised RL with verifiable rewards (URLVR) can meaningfully scale LLM training beyond labeled supervision by using model-intrinsic signals, but its benefits are constrained by reward quality and scaling trade-offs—this work maps those limits and gives practical guidelines.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the supervision bottleneck in RL-based LLM fine‑tuning (e.g., RLHF) by deriving verifiable rewards without ground-truth labels and quantifying when and how such rewards reliably improve model performance.
method: Taxonomy: categorize URLVR approaches into intrinsic (model-derived signals) versus extrinsic verifiable rewards and characterize their properties.
Theory: develop analytical bounds on reward verifiability, signal-to-noise, and their impact on policy/value updates and scaling behavior.
Experiments: large-scale empirical evaluation across model sizes, tasks, and reward designs to measure gains, failure modes, and provide practical recipes.
infographic.impact: Equips researchers and engineers with rigorous criteria and empirical evidence to decide when unsupervised verifiable rewards can replace or complement human labels—enabling more scalable, cost‑effective LLM training while clarifying limitations to avoid wasted effort.
visual_elements: Taxonomy diagram: intrinsic vs extrinsic URLVR methods, with examples and pros/cons per branch.

title: Agentic Critical Training
authors: Weize Liu, Minghui Liu, Sy-Tuyen Ho, Souradip Chakraborty, Xiyao Wang
abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) as autonomous agents often begins with imitation learning, but it only teaches agents what to do without understanding why: agents never contrast successful actions against suboptimal alternatives and thus lack awareness of action quality. Recent approaches attempt to address this by introducing self-reflection supervision derived from contrasts between expert and alternative actions. However, the training paradigm fundamentally remains imitation learning: t

infographic.key_insight: Agentic Critical Training shifts agent learning from pure imitation to contrastive self-critique: agents are trained not only to copy expert actions but to generate, compare, and learn from suboptimal alternatives so they understand why actions succeed or fail.
infographic.problem_solved: Imitation learning teaches what to do but not why; agents lack awareness of action quality because they never contrast expert decisions with plausible alternatives, leading to brittle or suboptimal autonomous behavior.
method: Have the agent produce candidate actions (expert-like and alternative/suboptimal options) during training and collect pairwise comparisons.
Introduce a critic/contrastive supervision signal that scores and ranks alternatives so the agent learns to prefer high-quality actions and explain their advantage.
Train the policy with a contrastive or ranking objective that combines imitation of good actions with explicit penalties for suboptimal alternatives, closing the gap between 'what' and 'why'.
infographic.impact: By giving agents an explicit sense of action quality, this approach improves robustness, decision transparency, and downstream performance for autonomous LLM agents—especially in tasks requiring long-horizon planning or error recovery.

authors: Ben Rank, Hardik Bhatnagar, Ameya Prabhu, Shira Eisenberg, Karina Nguyen
abstract: AI agents have become surprisingly proficient at software engineering over the past year, largely due to improvements in reasoning capabilities. This raises a deeper question: can these systems extend their capabilities to automate AI research itself? In this paper, we explore post-training, the critical phase that turns base LLMs into useful assistants. We introduce PostTrainBench to benchmark how well LLM agents can perform post-training autonomously under bounded compute constraints (10 hours

infographic.key_insight: PostTrainBench introduces a focused benchmark showing that LLM agents can autonomously perform many post-training tasks within bounded compute (e.g., a 10-hour budget), exposing which steps are reliably automatable and where human oversight remains necessary.
infographic.problem_solved: Evaluates whether and how LLM-based agents can automate the post-training phase that converts base models into usable assistants, under realistic time and compute constraints.
method: Design PostTrainBench: a modular task suite that represents typical post-training steps (data preparation, tuning/optimization, evaluation, deployment checks) with fixed compute/time budgets.
Run agentic LLMs that plan, use tools, and schedule operations to attempt end-to-end post-training workflows within the 10-hour constraint, logging outcomes, resource use, and decisions.
Analyze performance, failure modes, and task-level automability to identify where agents succeed, fail, or require human intervention.

title: Talking Together: Synthesizing Co-Located 3D Conversations from Audio
authors: Mengyi Shan, Shouchieh Chang, Ziqian Bai, Shichen Liu, Yinda Zhang
abstract: We tackle the challenging task of generating complete 3D facial animations for two interacting, co-located participants from a mixed audio stream. While existing methods often produce disembodied "talking heads" akin to a video conference call, our work is the first to explicitly model the dynamic 3D spatial relationship -- including relative position, orientation, and mutual gaze -- that is crucial for realistic in-person dialogues. Our system synthesizes the full performance of both individual

infographic.key_insight: This paper presents the first system that synthesizes synchronized, full 3D facial animations for two co-located speakers from a single mixed audio stream by explicitly modeling their relative 3D spatial relationship (position, orientation, mutual gaze).
infographic.problem_solved: Generates realistic in-person multi-speaker 3D conversations from mixed audio—moving beyond disembodied 'talking heads' by resolving who speaks when and how speakers orient, look, and react to each other in space.
method: Separate and attribute mixed audio to individual participants (speaker diarization/voice separation) and extract conversational cues (turns, prosody).
Predict per-speaker 3D head pose, facial expression, and gaze conditioned on the separated audio plus a learned interaction module that models relative position/orientation and mutual gaze dynamics.
Render synchronized 3D performances for both participants in a shared spatial scene, ensuring temporal consistency and cross-participant responses.
infographic.impact: Enables realistic multi-person avatars for AR/VR, telepresence, social robotics, and human behavior research by producing spatially coherent, interactive 3D conversations from audio alone—improving realism and social signal fidelity over single-head methods.

title: CAST: Modeling Visual State Transitions for Consistent Video Retrieval
authors: Yanqing Liu, Yingcheng Liu, Fanghong Dong, Budianto Budianto, Cihang Xie
abstract: As video content creation shifts toward long-form narratives, composing short clips into coherent storylines becomes increasingly important. However, prevailing retrieval formulations remain context-agnostic at inference time, prioritizing local semantic alignment while neglecting state and identity consistency. To address this structural limitation, we formalize the task of Consistent Video Retrieval (CVR) and introduce a diagnostic benchmark spanning YouCook2, COIN, and CrossTask. We propose C

infographic.key_insight: Modeling visual state transitions between clips enables retrieval that preserves object/actor identity and temporal consistency, not just local semantic match. CAST frames retrieval as a consistency-aware problem and operationalizes it for long-form, multi-clip storylines.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing video retrieval methods match clips based on local semantic similarity and ignore state/identity continuity, causing incoherent multi-clip results; this work formalizes Consistent Video Retrieval (CVR) and provides tools to benchmark and improve consistency.
method: Formalize the Consistent Video Retrieval (CVR) task and build a diagnostic benchmark spanning YouCook2, COIN, and CrossTask to evaluate state and identity consistency across retrieved clip sequences.
Introduce CAST, a model that explicitly represents visual state transitions between clips so retrieval decisions account for how objects/actors evolve over time rather than only per-clip semantics.
Train with transition-aware objectives and consistency constraints that encourage retrieved sequences to maintain identity and plausible state progressions.
infographic.impact: By shifting retrieval from context-agnostic matching to transition-aware selection, CAST enables more coherent multi-clip storylines—useful for video editing, summarization, and downstream multimodal reasoning in long-form video applications.

title: OfficeQA Pro: An Enterprise Benchmark for End-to-End Grounded Reasoning
authors: Krista Opsahl-Ong, Arnav Singhvi, Jasmine Collins, Ivan Zhou, Cindy Wang
abstract: We introduce OfficeQA Pro, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on grounded, multi-document reasoning over a large and heterogeneous document corpus. The corpus consists of U.S. Treasury Bulletins spanning nearly 100 years, comprising 89,000 pages and over 26 million numerical values. OfficeQA Pro consists of 133 questions that require precise document parsing, retrieval, and analytical reasoning across both unstructured text and tabular data. Frontier LLMs including Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, an

infographic.key_insight: OfficeQA Pro provides a high-fidelity, enterprise-scale benchmark that stresses end-to-end grounded reasoning across 89,000 pages of heterogeneous documents and tables, forcing models to combine precise retrieval, parsing, and numeric analysis across long historical records.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of realistic benchmarks for multi-document, numeric- and table-heavy grounded reasoning needed for enterprise tasks like auditing, compliance, and financial analysis.
method: Curate a large corpus of U.S. Treasury Bulletins (~89k pages, >26M numerical values) spanning ~100 years to represent heterogeneous, real-world enterprise documents.
Design 133 targeted questions that require document-level retrieval, fine-grained parsing of unstructured text and tabular data, and multi-step analytical reasoning across documents.
Evaluate end-to-end agent performance (retrieval → parsing → answer + evidence) to reveal capability gaps in frontier LLMs on precise, grounded tasks.

title: CoCo: Code as CoT for Text-to-Image Preview and Rare Concept Generation
authors: Haodong Li, Chunmei Qing, Huanyu Zhang, Dongzhi Jiang, Yihang Zou
abstract: Recent advancements in Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) have significantly advanced text-to-image (T2I) generation, particularly through the integration of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. However, existing CoT-based T2I methods largely rely on abstract natural-language planning, which lacks the precision required for complex spatial layouts, structured visual elements, and dense textual content. In this work, we propose CoCo (Code-as-CoT), a code-driven reasoning framework that represents the

infographic.key_insight: Representing Chain-of-Thought as executable code (Code-as-CoT) gives text-to-image systems precise, structured planning that can be rendered into previews and used to generate rare or complex visual concepts more reliably.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the imprecision of natural-language planning in CoT for T2I, which struggles with complex spatial layouts, structured visual elements, and dense textual content.
method: Encode reasoning/planning as executable code (e.g., SVG/HTML/canvas-like scripts or scene descriptions) instead of abstract natural language.
Render the code into a visual preview that conditions a unified multimodal generator, enabling iterative refinement and tighter layout control.
Leverage the explicit code-to-visual mapping to inject and compose rare concepts and structured content more accurately during generation.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to add precise layout control, reproducibility, and better handling of rare/structured concepts to T2I pipelines, improving fidelity for design, OCR-heavy scenes, and compositional tasks.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Gaussian Avatars: Improving Expression Generalization
authors: Matan Levy, Gavriel Habib, Issar Tzachor, Dvir Samuel, Rami Ben-Ari
abstract: Template-free animatable head avatars can achieve high visual fidelity by learning expression-dependent facial deformation directly from a subject's capture, avoiding parametric face templates and hand-designed blendshape spaces. However, since learned deformation is supervised only by the expressions observed for a single identity, these models suffer from limited expression coverage and often struggle when driven by motions that deviate from the training distribution. We introduce RAF (Retriev

infographic.key_insight: Augmenting a single-subject, template-free avatar with a retrieval mechanism from a multi-subject expression library and Gaussian-based deformation primitives lets the model synthesize realistic, previously unseen expressions without needing a parametric face template.
infographic.problem_solved: Template-free animatable head avatars trained on one identity usually overfit to observed expressions and fail to generalize to out-of-distribution motions; this work addresses limited expression coverage and poor driveability for unseen expressions.
method: Create a cross-subject expression library and represent local facial deformations with learnable Gaussian primitives (the "Gaussian avatars").
At inference time retrieve nearest expression priors from the library and fuse their Gaussian deformation fields with the subject-specific model (RAF = Retrieval-Augmented Framework).
Train the system end-to-end with reconstruction and retrieval-consistency objectives so retrieved priors improve generalization without overriding identity-specific detail.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way to expand expression coverage of high-fidelity, template-free avatars using reusable priors—reducing capture requirements and improving robustness when driving avatars with novel or extreme expressions.

title: Impermanent: A Live Benchmark for Temporal Generalization in Time Series Forecasting
authors: Azul Garza, Renée Rosillo, Rodrigo Mendoza-Smith, David Salinas, Andrew Robert Williams
abstract: Recent advances in time-series forecasting increasingly rely on pre-trained foundation-style models. While these models often claim broad generalization, existing evaluation protocols provide limited evidence. Indeed, most current benchmarks use static train-test splits that can easily lead to contamination as foundation models can inadvertently train on test data or perform model selection using test scores, which can inflate performance. We introduce Impermanent, a live benchmark that evaluate

infographic.key_insight: Impermanent introduces a live, continuously updated benchmark that measures how well time-series forecasting models truly generalize across time, avoiding inflated scores from static train-test splits and test-set contamination.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing static benchmarks allow inadvertent contamination and optimistic evaluation of foundation-style forecasting models, giving poor evidence of real-world temporal generalization and robustness to distribution drift.
method: Live evaluation protocol: run models on periodically refreshed, strictly held-out future windows rather than fixed train/test splits to simulate real deployment.
Contamination controls: dataset versioning, submission rules, and isolation of test periods to prevent pretraining or model-selection on future data.

Transparent leaderboard & metrics: continuously updated public leaderboard that tracks performance over time and across drifts, emphasizing temporal generalization metrics (e.g., performance decay, robustness to regime change).
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners and researchers with a realistic, contamination-resistant way to compare forecasting models and foundation models over time, improving trust in reported gains and guiding model selection for deployment under temporal drift.

title: HiAR: Efficient Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Hierarchical Denoising
authors: Kai Zou, Dian Zheng, Hongbo Liu, Tiankai Hang, Bin Liu
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) diffusion offers a promising framework for generating videos of theoretically infinite length. However, a major challenge is maintaining temporal continuity while preventing the progressive quality degradation caused by error accumulation. To ensure continuity, existing methods typically condition on highly denoised contexts; yet, this practice propagates prediction errors with high certainty, thereby exacerbating degradation. In this paper, we argue that a highly clean conte

infographic.key_insight: HiAR prevents progressive quality degradation in autoregressive long-video diffusion by preserving calibrated uncertainty in context through hierarchical denoising, enabling temporally continuous generation over long horizons.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces error accumulation and loss of temporal continuity in autoregressive (AR) diffusion video generation, which otherwise degrades quality as generation proceeds.
method: Hierarchical denoising: condition generation on multi-level (noisy → clean) context representations to avoid overconfident propagation of past prediction errors.
Autoregressive long-video pipeline: generate video segments sequentially while exchanging hierarchical context to maintain temporal consistency across long horizons.
Efficiency-oriented design: structured conditioning and denoising schedule that balances sampling cost with robustness to accumulated errors.
infographic.impact: Enables more stable, longer-duration video synthesis with diffusion-based AR models, making generative video systems more practical for long-form content, simulations, and downstream tasks that require temporal coherence.

title: FVG-PT: Adaptive Foreground View-Guided Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
authors: Haoyang Li, Liang Wang, Siyu Zhou, Jiacheng Sun, Jing Jiang
abstract: CLIP-based prompt tuning enables pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to efficiently adapt to downstream tasks. Although existing studies have made significant progress, they pay limited attention to changes in the internal attention representations of VLMs during the tuning process. In this paper, we attribute the failure modes of prompt tuning predictions to shifts in foreground attention of the visual encoder, and propose Foreground View-Guided Prompt Tuning (FVG-PT), an adaptive plug-and

infographic.key_insight: Prompt tuning failures in CLIP-style VLMs are largely caused by shifts in the visual encoder's foreground attention; FVG-PT adaptively extracts and aligns foreground attention to guide prompt updates, stabilizing and improving downstream performance.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing prompt tuning methods ignore internal attention shifts in the visual encoder, leading to inconsistent or degraded predictions when foreground attention drifts during adaptation; this work addresses unstable transfer and poor robustness caused by unaligned visual attention.
method: Diagnose attention shift: analyze how foreground attention maps change during prompt tuning and correlate shifts with prediction errors.
Foreground View-Guided module: extract image-specific foreground attention views and use them to condition prompt representations (attention-guided prompt generation or re-weighting).
Adaptive alignment and loss: incorporate an attention-alignment objective and a lightweight, plug-and-play prompt adapter that adjusts prompts per image or batch to preserve correct foreground focus.
infographic.impact: FVG-PT improves transfer accuracy, robustness, and interpretability of CLIP-based prompt tuning with minimal overhead, making prompt adaptation more reliable for real-world downstream tasks and low-data regimes.

abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for financial analysis and investment research, yet systematic evaluation of their financial reasoning capabilities remains limited. title: Fly360: Omnidirectional Obstacle Avoidance within Drone View
authors: Xiangkai Zhang, Dizhe Zhang, WenZhuo Cao, Zhaoliang Wan, Yingjie Niu
abstract: Obstacle avoidance in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), as a fundamental capability, has gained increasing attention with the growing focus on spatial intelligence. However, current obstacle-avoidance methods mainly depend on limited field-of-view sensors and are ill-suited for UAV scenarios which require full-spatial awareness when the movement direction differs from the UAV's heading. This limitation motivates us to explore omnidirectional obstacle avoidance for panoramic drones with full-view

infographic.key_insight: By leveraging panoramic (full-view) sensing and a view-aligned planning/controller, Fly360 enables reliable obstacle avoidance even when a drone’s movement direction differs from its heading, closing the gap left by narrow field-of-view systems.

Use a view-aligned planning/controller that outputs safe motion commands for arbitrary travel directions, trained and validated in sim/real scenarios to minimize collisions.

abstract: Orofacial clefts are among the most common congenital craniofacial abnormalities, yet accurate prenatal detection remains challenging due to the scarcity of experienced specialists and the relative rarity of the condition. title: Boosting deep Reinforcement Learning using pretraining with Logical Options
authors: Zihan Ye, Phil Chau, Raban Emunds, Jannis Blüml, Cedric Derstroff
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning agents are often misaligned, as they over-exploit early reward signals. Recently, several symbolic approaches have addressed these challenges by encoding sparse objectives along with aligned plans. However, purely symbolic architectures are complex to scale and difficult to apply to continuous settings. Hence, we propose a hybrid approach, inspired by humans' ability to acquire new skills. We use a two-stage framework that injects symbolic structure into neural-based

infographic.key_insight: Pretraining neural policies with symbolic "logical options" injects structured, aligned behavior that reduces over-exploitation of early rewards and improves downstream deep RL performance in sparse/continuous tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses misalignment and poor sample efficiency in deep RL where agents exploit early dense signals and struggle with sparse objectives or scaling purely symbolic planners to continuous domains.
method: Two-stage hybrid pipeline: (1) derive symbolic logical options (structured subgoals/subpolicies) and use them to pretrain neural modules, (2) fine-tune the pretrained policy end-to-end with standard deep RL in the target environment.

authors: Alejandra Perez, Anita Rau, Lee White, Busisiwe Mlambo, Chinedu Nwoye
abstract: Surgeons don't just see -- they interpret. abstract: Understanding how neural networks transform inputs into outputs is crucial for interpreting and manipulating their behavior. title: Accelerating Text-to-Video Generation with Calibrated Sparse Attention
authors: Shai Yehezkel, Shahar Yadin, Noam Elata, Yaron Ostrovsky-Berman, Bahjat Kawar
abstract: Recent diffusion models enable high-quality video generation, but suffer from slow runtimes. The large transformer-based backbones used in these models are bottlenecked by spatiotemporal attention. In this paper, we identify that a significant fraction of token-to-token connections consistently yield negligible scores across various inputs, and their patterns often repeat across queries. Thus, the attention computation in these cases can be skipped with little to no effect on the result. This ob

infographic.key_insight: A large fraction of token-to-token attention scores in video diffusion transformers are consistently negligible and often repeatable across queries, so the model can safely skip those attention computations with careful calibration to retain output quality.
infographic.problem_solved: Text-to-video diffusion models produce high-quality results but run slowly because spatiotemporal attention across many tokens is computationally expensive. The paper reduces wasted attention computation to speed up generation.
method: Analyze attention matrices to identify token-to-token connections that consistently yield near-zero scores and find repeating sparsity patterns across queries.
Construct calibrated sparse attention masks (e.g., per-layer/head thresholds or lightweight gating) that skip low-impact attention computations while controlling for fidelity loss.
Integrate the sparse attention mechanism into transformer backbones of text-to-video diffusion models to reduce runtime without degrading perceptual/video quality.
infographic.impact: Practitioners can generate videos faster and cheaper by avoiding redundant attention work, enabling higher throughput, lower latency, or larger-resolution video synthesis with the same hardware. The technique is applicable to other large spatiotemporal transformers beyond text-to-video.

title: EdgeDAM: Real-time Object Tracking for Mobile Devices
authors: Syed Muhammad Raza, Syed Murtaza Hussain Abidi, Khawar Islam, Muhammad Ibrahim, Ajmal Saeed Mian
abstract: Single-object tracking (SOT) on edge devices is a critical computer vision task, requiring accurate and continuous target localization across video frames under occlusion, distractor interference, and fast motion. However, recent state-of-the-art distractor-aware memory mechanisms are largely built on segmentation-based trackers and rely on mask prediction and attention-driven memory updates, which introduce substantial computational overhead and limit real-time deployment on resource-constraine

infographic.key_insight: EdgeDAM introduces a distractor-aware memory design that removes heavy segmentation and attention-driven mask prediction, enabling accurate single-object tracking with much lower compute so it can run in real time on mobile/edge devices.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-accuracy distractor-aware SOT methods (which are segmentation- and attention-heavy) and the compute/latency constraints of resource-limited mobile devices, enabling robust tracking under occlusion, distractors, and fast motion.
method: Proposes EdgeDAM, a lightweight distractor-aware memory architecture tailored for edge inference that avoids costly mask prediction and attention updates.
Applies compact feature encoding and efficient memory-update rules to maintain target identity across frames while minimizing computation and memory footprint.
Optimizes model components and inference flow for low-latency deployment on mobile CPUs/NPUs without sacrificing tracking robustness.
infographic.impact: Makes state-of-the-art distractor-aware single-object tracking feasible on mobile and embedded platforms, unlocking real-time applications in AR, robotics, and on-device surveillance where latency and energy are critical.

title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
authors: Ted Zadouri, Markus Hoehnerbach, Jay Shah, Timmy Liu, Vijay Thakkar
abstract: Attention, as a core layer of the ubiquitous Transformer architecture, is the bottleneck for large language models and long-context applications. While FlashAttention-3 optimized attention for Hopper GPUs through asynchronous execution and warp specialization, it primarily targets the H100 architecture. The AI industry has rapidly transitioned to deploying Blackwell-based systems such as the B200 and GB200, which exhibit fundamentally different performance characteristics due to asymmetric hardw

infographic.key_insight: Co-designing the attention algorithm with kernel-level pipelining tuned for asymmetric compute/memory characteristics (e.g., Blackwell B200/GB200) recovers lost efficiency from Hopper-optimized implementations, yielding substantially higher throughput and memory efficiency for long‑context attention.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing FlashAttention optimizations targeted H100-like (Hopper) hardware and underperform on Blackwell-class GPUs because their compute vs. memory bandwidth tradeoffs are different. This causes suboptimal utilization, higher memory traffic, and worse latency/throughput for large‑context LLM workloads.
method: Algorithm reorganization: tile- and chunk-based attention orderings that reduce memory traffic and enable streaming of Q/K/V blocks rather than full-buffering.
Kernel pipelining: staggered, stage-wise kernels with double-buffering and overlapped compute+DMA to hide memory latency and match the pipeline depth to hardware asymmetry.
Hardware-aware autotuning: select tile sizes, pipeline depth, and precision strategies per device (B200/GB200) to balance compute utilization against memory bandwidth constraints.
infographic.impact: Makes attention kernels faster and more memory-efficient on modern Blackwell systems, improving throughput and latency for training and inference of large-context LLMs and lowering operational cost for deployments.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic comparing Hopper vs Blackwell hardware asymmetry (compute vs memory bandwidth) and the resulting utilization gap.
Pipeline timeline (swimlane) showing overlapping stages: load Q/K/V → compute partial attention → reduce/accumulate → write, illustrating double-buffering.

title: RoboPocket: Improve Robot Policies Instantly with Your Phone
authors: Junjie Fang, Wendi Chen, Han Xue, Fangyuan Zhou, Tian Le
abstract: Scaling imitation learning is fundamentally constrained by the efficiency of data collection. While handheld interfaces have emerged as a scalable solution for in-the-wild data acquisition, they predominantly operate in an open-loop manner: operators blindly collect demonstrations without knowing the underlying policy's weaknesses, leading to inefficient coverage of critical state distributions. Conversely, interactive methods like DAgger effectively address covariate shift but rely on physical

infographic.key_insight: A smartphone becomes an interactive, closed-loop tool for collecting targeted corrective demonstrations and instantly improving robot policies, closing the gap between scalable handheld data collection and on-policy correction.
infographic.problem_solved: Handheld open-loop demonstrations miss critical failure states and waste labeling effort, while interactive on-robot correction (e.g., DAgger) is costly and hard to scale; this work enables efficient, scalable corrective supervision without needing constant physical interventions.
method: A phone-based interactive interface that presents robot behavior and lets users provide corrective inputs or relabel critical moments.
Active selection of states where the current policy is uncertain or likely to fail, focusing demonstrations on high-value regions of the state distribution.
A low-latency update pipeline that incorporates corrections and fine-tunes or adapts the policy immediately so improvements are realized 'instantly.'
infographic.impact: Makes imitation learning more data- and time-efficient by enabling non-expert, in-the-wild users to rapidly fix policy failures; reduces covariate shift and accelerates deployment of robust robot behaviors.

title: Beyond Scattered Acceptance: Fast and Coherent Inference for DLMs via Longest Stable Prefixes
authors: Pengxiang Li, Joey Tsai, Hongwei Xue, Kunyu Shi, Shilin Yan
abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) promise highly parallel text generation, yet their practical inference speed is often bottlenecked by suboptimal decoding schedulers. Standard approaches rely on 'scattered acceptance'-committing high confidence tokens at disjoint positions throughout the sequence. This approach inadvertently fractures the Key-Value (KV) cache, destroys memory locality, and forces the model into costly, repeated repairs across unstable token boundaries. To resolve this, we presen

infographic.key_insight: Commit contiguous, longest stable prefixes (LSP) instead of scattered high‑confidence tokens to preserve KV cache locality and avoid repeated repairs, enabling much faster and more coherent DLM inference.
infographic.problem_solved: Diffusion Language Models suffer from 'scattered acceptance' that fractures the KV cache, destroys memory locality, and forces costly repeated recomputation and local repairs during decoding — this paper fixes the decoding scheduler to eliminate those inefficiencies.
method: Detect token stability across diffusion iterations and compute the longest contiguous prefix that is stable (Longest Stable Prefix, LSP).
Commit the LSP incrementally so the KV cache can be updated and reused in-place, avoiding random writes/reads that fragment memory locality.
Schedule parallel generation only on the remaining unstable suffix and perform targeted, efficient repairs when instability appears, minimizing recomputation.
infographic.impact: Faster, more memory-efficient DLM decoding with improved output coherence and reduced latency — directly beneficial for hardware accelerators and large-scale deployment of diffusion-based text models.

Flowchart of the LSP scheduler: stability detection → commit prefix → parallel suffix decoding → targeted repair
