title: Mobile-O: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation on Mobile Device
authors: Abdelrahman Shaker, Ahmed Heakl, Jaseel Muhammad, Ritesh Thawkar, Omkar Thawakar
abstract: Unified multimodal models can both understand and generate visual content within a single architecture. Existing models, however, remain data-hungry and too heavy for deployment on edge devices. We present Mobile-O, a compact vision-language-diffusion model that brings unified multimodal intelligence to a mobile device. Its core module, the Mobile Conditioning Projector (MCP), fuses vision-language features with a diffusion generator using depthwise-separable convolutions and layerwise alignment

infographic.key_insight: Mobile-O demonstrates that a single compact vision-language-diffusion architecture can both understand and generate visual content on-device by using an efficient fusion module (Mobile Conditioning Projector) and lightweight convolutional building blocks.
infographic.problem_solved: Large unified multimodal models are too data- and compute-hungry for edge deployment; Mobile-O addresses the need for a unified understanding+generation model that fits mobile compute, memory, and latency constraints.
method: Mobile Conditioning Projector (MCP): fuses vision and language features into the diffusion generator for unified tasks.
Efficiency-first design: depthwise-separable convolutions to reduce parameters and runtime on mobile hardware.
Layerwise alignment between modality encoders and the diffusion generator to improve feature fusion and generation quality.
infographic.impact: Enables practical on-device multimodal apps (image editing, captioning, visual Q&A, image generation) with lower latency, better privacy, and reduced server cost — making unified multimodal intelligence feasible on mobile devices.

title: AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization
authors: Mert Cemri, Shubham Agrawal, Akshat Gupta, Shu Liu, Audrey Cheng
abstract: The paradigm of automated program generation is shifting from one-shot generation to inference-time search, where Large Language Models (LLMs) function as semantic mutation operators within evolutionary loops. While effective, these systems are currently governed by static schedules that fail to account for the non-stationary dynamics of the search process. This rigidity results in substantial computational waste, as resources are indiscriminately allocated to stagnating populations while promis

infographic.key_insight: AdaEvolve replaces fixed, static schedules in LLM-driven evolutionary program search with an adaptive controller that reallocates inference-time compute based on non-stationary search dynamics, substantially reducing wasted evaluations while preserving or improving search outcomes.
infographic.problem_solved: Fixed evaluation schedules in LLM-as-mutation evolutionary loops ignore changing population dynamics, causing compute to be wasted on stagnating populations and slowing down program-generation searches.
method: Treat LLMs as semantic mutation operators inside an evolutionary (zeroth-order) search loop during inference-time search.
Continuously monitor search dynamics (e.g., progress, diversity, stagnation) and adapt the allocation of inference/evaluation budget across populations.
Use an adaptive scheduling policy to prioritize promising subpopulations and throttle or reallocate resources away from stagnating ones.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, AdaEvolve means more cost-efficient program synthesis and optimization using LLMs—reducing unnecessary compute and accelerating search without changing the underlying model. It enables scalable, practical deployment of LLM-driven search in resource-constrained settings.

title: Simulation-Ready Cluttered Scene Estimation via Physics-aware Joint Shape and Pose Optimization
authors: Wei-Cheng Huang, Jiaheng Han, Xiaohan Ye, Zherong Pan, Kris Hauser
abstract: Estimating simulation-ready scenes from real-world observations is crucial for downstream planning and policy learning tasks. Regretfully, existing methods struggle in cluttered environments, often exhibiting prohibitive computational cost, poor robustness, and restricted generality when scaling to multiple interacting objects. We propose a unified optimization-based formulation for real-to-sim scene estimation that jointly recovers the shapes and poses of multiple rigid objects under physical c

infographic.key_insight: Jointly optimizing object shapes and poses with physics-aware constraints produces simulation-ready reconstructions of highly cluttered scenes that are more accurate and stable than separate or purely vision-driven pipelines.
infographic.problem_solved: Recovers shapes and poses of multiple interacting rigid objects from real-world observations in cluttered, occluded scenes while producing scenes that run stably in physics simulators (real-to-sim), overcoming high cost, brittleness, and limited scalability of prior methods.
method: Unified optimization that jointly estimates object geometry and 6-DoF poses for multiple rigid bodies under physical constraints (contacts, collisions, dynamic stability).
Physics-aware loss terms (contact consistency, penetration avoidance, simulation stability) that guide reconstructions to be ‘simulation-ready’.
An efficient solver/design that handles occlusions and inter-object interactions to scale to cluttered scenes with many objects.
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable sim-to-real workflows for planning, control, and policy learning by producing realistic, physically consistent scene models — reducing tuning and failure in downstream robotics and simulation-based training.

title: tttLRM: Test-Time Training for Long Context and Autoregressive 3D Reconstruction
authors: Chen Wang, Hao Tan, Wang Yifan, Zhiqin Chen, Yuheng Liu
abstract: We propose tttLRM, a novel large 3D reconstruction model that leverages a Test-Time Training (TTT) layer to enable long-context, autoregressive 3D reconstruction with linear computational complexity, further scaling the model's capability. Our framework efficiently compresses multiple image observations into the fast weights of the TTT layer, forming an implicit 3D representation in the latent space that can be decoded into various explicit formats, such as Gaussian Splats (GS) for downstream ap

infographic.key_insight: tttLRM uses a Test‑Time Training (TTT) layer to compress multiple image observations into fast weights, forming an implicit 3D latent representation that supports autoregressive reconstruction with linear computational complexity. This enables long‑context multi‑view 3D reconstruction that can be decoded into explicit formats like Gaussian Splats.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing multi‑view and autoregressive 3D reconstruction methods struggle to scale to long input sequences because of quadratic compute/memory growth or limited context; tttLRM addresses this by encoding observations into compact fast weights at test time to keep complexity linear while preserving reconstruction fidelity.
method: Introduce a TTT layer that stores and updates fast weights at test time to compress multiple image observations into a compact implicit 3D latent state.
Perform autoregressive decoding from the TTT latent state so reconstruction complexity grows linearly with the number of views/steps.
Decode the implicit latent into explicit downstream formats (e.g., Gaussian Splats) for rendering and application-specific use.
infographic.impact: Enables scalable, compute‑efficient 3D reconstruction from many images, making large‑context multi‑view pipelines practical for mapping, AR/VR, robotics, and other real‑world applications. Practitioners can handle longer sequences without prohibitive memory or runtime costs.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: encoder images → TTT layer (fast weights) → autoregressive decoder → explicit outputs (Gaussian Splats).

title: A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite
authors: Maijunxian Wang, Ruisi Wang, Juyi Lin, Ran Ji, Thaddäus Wiedemer
abstract: Rapid progress in video models has largely focused on visual quality, leaving their reasoning capabilities underexplored. Video reasoning grounds intelligence in spatiotemporally consistent visual environments that go beyond what text can naturally capture, enabling intuitive reasoning over spatiotemporal structure such as continuity, interaction, and causality. However, systematically studying video reasoning and its scaling behavior is hindered by the lack of large-scale training data. To addr

infographic.key_insight: Building a very large, diverse video reasoning suite enables systematic study and scaling of spatiotemporal reasoning (continuity, interaction, causality) that text alone cannot capture.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of large-scale training and evaluation data needed to study and benchmark video-level reasoning and its scaling behavior across models.
method: Assemble a large, diverse corpus of videos annotated for spatiotemporal reasoning phenomena (continuity, interaction, causality, temporal localization).
Define a suite of standardized tasks and unified evaluation metrics that probe multi-step and temporal reasoning capabilities.
Conduct scaling studies (varying dataset size and model capacity) to quantify how video reasoning improves with more data and compute and to surface failure modes.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a standardized benchmark and empirical scaling insights to accelerate development of models that truly understand temporal dynamics and causal interactions in video.

title: Recurrent Structural Policy Gradient for Partially Observable Mean Field Games
authors: Clarisse Wibault, Johannes Forkel, Sebastian Towers, Tiphaine Wibault, Juan Duque
abstract: Mean Field Games (MFGs) provide a principled framework for modeling interactions in large population models: at scale, population dynamics become deterministic, with uncertainty entering only through aggregate shocks, or common noise. However, algorithmic progress has been limited since model-free methods are too high variance and exact methods scale poorly. Recent Hybrid Structural Methods (HSMs) use Monte Carlo rollouts for the common noise in combination with exact estimation of the expected

infographic.key_insight: A recurrent Structural Policy Gradient algorithm lets agents in partially observable Mean Field Games learn scalable, low-variance policies by combining exact structural expectations with Monte Carlo treatment of common (aggregate) noise and a recurrent memory for hidden information.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-variance model-free approaches and computationally costly exact methods for large-population games under partial observability: it enables tractable, sample-efficient learning when agents only observe local/partial signals and the population introduces common shocks.
method: Hybrid structural decomposition: compute exact expectations over idiosyncratic effects while using Monte Carlo rollouts for common (aggregate) noise to keep computations tractable.

Recurrent policy-gradient: parameterize agents with recurrent policies (RNNs/LSTMs) to capture partial observability and history-dependent strategies while applying a structural policy gradient update.
Variance-reduction & scalability: exploit mean-field structure to reduce estimator variance and scale to large populations without fully enumerating joint dynamics.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, lower-variance approach for training policies in large multi-agent settings with hidden state and aggregate shocks, improving sample efficiency and enabling deployment of principled MFG methods in real-world domains (e.g., economics, traffic, resource allocation).

title: Agentic AI for Scalable and Robust Optical Systems Control
authors: Zehao Wang, Mingzhe Han, Wei Cheng, Yue-Kai Huang, Philip Ji
abstract: We present AgentOptics, an agentic AI framework for high-fidelity, autonomous optical system control built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). AgentOptics interprets natural language tasks and executes protocol-compliant actions on heterogeneous optical devices through a structured tool abstraction layer. We implement 64 standardized MCP tools across 8 representative optical devices and construct a 410-task benchmark to evaluate request understanding, role-aware responses, multi-step coordinati

infographic.key_insight: AgentOptics shows that an agentic AI built on a standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) can interpret natural-language tasks and autonomously orchestrate heterogeneous optical hardware, enabling high-fidelity, multi-step instrument control at scale.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between human intent and diverse instrument APIs by providing a protocol-compliant abstraction that enables safe, repeatable, and role-aware control of complex optical systems.
method: Define the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a standardized interface and tool schema to represent device capabilities and permissible actions.
Implement an agent that parses natural-language requests, maps intent to MCP-compliant tool calls, and executes protocol-safe action sequences across devices.

Realize 64 standardized MCP tools across 8 representative optical devices and evaluate performance on a 410-task benchmark targeting request understanding, role-aware responses, and multi-step coordination.
infographic.impact: Provides a reproducible framework for automating optical labs and integrating hardware-in-the-loop with language-driven agents, reducing manual overhead and accelerating experimentation for AI/ML practitioners working with physical systems.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: Agent ↔ MCP (tool layer) ↔ heterogeneous devices, showing data and command flow.
Pipeline flowchart: Natural-language task → intent parsing → MCP tool mapping → sequenced device actions → observation loop.

title: Quantum-enhanced satellite image classification
authors: Qi Zhang, Anton Simen, Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gabriel Alvarado Barrios, Paolo A. Erdman
abstract: We demonstrate the application of a quantum feature extraction method to enhance multi-class image classification for space applications. By harnessing the dynamics of many-body spin Hamiltonians, the method generates expressive quantum features that, when combined with classical processing, lead to quantum-enhanced classification accuracy. Using a strong and well-established ResNet50 baseline, we achieved a maximum classical accuracy of 83%, which can be improved to 84% with a transfer learning

infographic.key_insight: Quantum-generated features from many-body spin Hamiltonians, when combined with a classical ResNet50 backbone and transfer learning, yield a measurable improvement in multi-class satellite image classification (≈83% → 84% accuracy).
infographic.problem_solved: Improves feature extraction for satellite image classification by exploring a hybrid quantum–classical pipeline to boost accuracy and model expressivity where classical features may be limiting.
method: Create expressive quantum feature maps via the dynamics of many-body spin Hamiltonians.
Combine quantum features with a classical ResNet50 baseline using transfer learning in a hybrid pipeline.
Evaluate multi-class satellite image classification and compare classical vs. quantum-enhanced accuracies (≈1 percentage-point improvement).
infographic.impact: Provides a practical demonstration that near-term quantum feature extractors can be integrated into existing ML workflows to yield modest but meaningful gains, offering AI/ML practitioners a pathway to experiment with quantum-augmented remote-sensing models.

title: VIRAASAT: Traversing Novel Paths for Indian Cultural Reasoning
authors: Harshul Raj Surana, Arijit Maji, Aryan Vats, Akash Ghosh, Sriparna Saha
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made significant progress in reasoning tasks across various domains such as mathematics and coding. However, their performance deteriorates in tasks requiring rich socio-cultural knowledge and diverse local contexts, particularly those involving Indian Culture. Existing Cultural benchmarks are (i) Manually crafted, (ii) contain single-hop questions testing factual recall, and (iii) prohibitively costly to scale, leaving this deficiency largely unmeasured. To add

infographic.key_insight: VIRAASAT introduces a scalable, multi‑hop benchmark to reveal and measure LLM weaknesses on Indian cultural reasoning, moving beyond small, manually crafted factual tests.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing cultural benchmarks are manual, single‑hop, and expensive to scale, leaving LLM performance on rich, context‑dependent Indian cultural reasoning largely unmeasured and undervalued.
method: Design a benchmark (VIRAASAT) focused on Indian socio‑cultural scenarios that require multi‑hop reasoning and local contextual knowledge.
Use a scalable, semi‑automated pipeline (combining expert curation, templates, and model‑assisted generation) to produce diverse question types and avoid single‑fact recall.
Evaluate multiple LLMs on the benchmark to quantify performance gaps and identify common failure modes specific to cultural reasoning.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a targeted, scalable tool to diagnose and improve LLMs on culturally grounded reasoning tasks, informing dataset curation, fine‑tuning, and evaluation practices for better real‑world cultural competence.

title: Generated Reality: Human-centric World Simulation using Interactive Video Generation with Hand and Camera Control
authors: Linxi Xie, Lisong C. Sun, Ashley Neall, Tong Wu, Shengqu Cai
abstract: Extended reality (XR) demands generative models that respond to users' tracked real-world motion, yet current video world models accept only coarse control signals such as text or keyboard input, limiting their utility for embodied interaction. We introduce a human-centric video world model that is conditioned on both tracked head pose and joint-level hand poses. For this purpose, we evaluate existing diffusion transformer conditioning strategies and propose an effective mechanism for 3D head an

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces a video world model that conditions diffusion-transformer generation on tracked 3D head pose and joint-level hand poses, enabling fine-grained, embodied control of generated video for XR and interactive scenarios.
infographic.problem_solved: Current generative video models accept only coarse control signals (e.g., text or keyboard), preventing tight coupling with users' tracked motion; this work closes the gap by enabling camera + hand-conditioned video generation for embodied interaction.
method: Extend diffusion-transformer video models to accept dense 3D head-pose and joint-level hand-pose conditioning signals.

Systematically evaluate alternative conditioning strategies for diffusion transformers and introduce an effective mechanism for integrating 3D head and hand control (pose-token / cross-attention style conditioning).
Combine pose-conditioned generation with camera/head tracking to produce interactive video sequences responsive to user motion and hand gestures.
infographic.impact: By enabling fine-grained, motion-driven video synthesis, this approach makes generative world models usable for XR, telepresence, and embodied AI research—giving practitioners a path to tightly couple user motion with realistic scene generation and interaction.

title: CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation
authors: Xia Su, Ruiqi Chen, Benlin Liu, Jingwei Ma, Zonglin Di
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown remarkable progress in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN), offering new possibilities for navigation decision-making that could benefit both robotic platforms and human users. However, real-world navigation is inherently conditioned by the agent's mobility constraints. For example, a sweeping robot cannot traverse stairs, while a quadruped can. We introduce Capability-Conditioned Navigation (CapNav), a benchmark designed to evaluate how well VLMs can naviga

infographic.key_insight: CapNav exposes that Vision–Language Models for navigation must be conditioned on an agent’s mobility constraints — without capability conditioning, VLMs frequently recommend infeasible or unsafe routes. The benchmark measures how well models adapt navigation outputs to different embodied capabilities.
infographic.problem_solved: Closes the evaluation gap in VLN by providing a capability-conditioned benchmark that tests whether VLMs respect agent-specific mobility limits (e.g., stairs vs. ramps, narrow passages) during indoor navigation.
method: Define mobility capability profiles (e.g., wheeled, legged, low-clearance) and generate capability-aware navigation tasks and instructions in indoor environments.

Run standardized evaluations: feed VLMs the same linguistic prompts plus an explicit capability descriptor, execute navigation in simulation, and compute capability-conditioned metrics (success, path feasibility, efficiency).
Benchmark multiple VLMs and baselines, analyze failure modes, and evaluate simple conditioning/prompting strategies to measure improvement when models are capability-aware.
infographic.impact: Provides researchers and practitioners a practical protocol to audit and improve VLMs for embodied tasks, encouraging models that plan safely and feasibly for different robot types. Results guide dataset design, model conditioning, and deployment decisions in robotics and assistive applications.

title: Spatio-Spectroscopic Representation Learning using Unsupervised Convolutional Long-Short Term Memory Networks
authors: Kameswara Bharadwaj Mantha, Lucy Fortson, Ramanakumar Sankar, Claudia Scarlata, Chris Lintott
abstract: Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS) surveys offer a unique new landscape in which to learn in both spatial and spectroscopic dimensions and could help uncover previously unknown insights into galaxy evolution. In this work, we demonstrate a new unsupervised deep learning framework using Convolutional Long-Short Term Memory Network Autoencoders to encode generalized feature representations across both spatial and spectroscopic dimensions spanning $19$ optical emission lines (3800A $< λ<$ 8000A) amo

infographic.key_insight: A Convolutional LSTM autoencoder can learn compact, unsupervised representations that jointly capture spatial structure and spectral (wavelength) dependencies in Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS) data across 19 optical emission lines, enabling discovery and downstream analysis without labels.
infographic.problem_solved: High-dimensional IFS cubes contain rich spatial and spectral correlations but lack large labeled datasets; this work addresses how to learn generalized spatio‑spectroscopic features unsupervised so models can summarize, compare, and discover patterns in galaxy data.
method: Treat IFS data as spatio‑spectral sequences (spatial maps across wavelength channels) and preprocess into multi‑channel input cubes covering 3800–8000 Å across 19 emission lines.

Use a Convolutional Long Short‑Term Memory (ConvLSTM) autoencoder: convolutional layers extract spatial features per channel while ConvLSTM units model sequential spectral dependencies, compressing into a low‑dimensional latent representation.
Train unsupervised with a reconstruction objective to produce embeddings useful for clustering, anomaly detection, and transfer to supervised downstream tasks.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable pretraining approach for high‑dimensional spatio‑spectral data that reduces dependence on labels, yields interpretable latent maps for scientific discovery, and can be adapted to other domains with spatial + spectral/temporal structure.

title: Robo-Saber: Generating and Simulating Virtual Reality Players
authors: Nam Hee Kim, Jingjing May Liu, Jaakko Lehtinen, Perttu Hämäläinen, James F. O'Brien
abstract: We present the first motion generation system for playtesting virtual reality (VR) games. Our player model generates VR headset and handheld controller movements from in-game object arrangements, guided by style exemplars and aligned to maximize simulated gameplay score. We train on the large BOXRR-23 dataset and apply our framework on the popular VR game Beat Saber. The resulting model Robo-Saber produces skilled gameplay and captures diverse player behaviors, mirroring the skill levels and mov

infographic.key_insight: Robo-Saber is the first system that automatically generates VR headset and controller motions from in-game object arrangements, using style exemplars and score-alignment to produce skilled, diverse virtual players for playtesting.
infographic.problem_solved: Automates realistic, scalable VR playtesting by producing diverse player motions (headset + controllers) that reflect different play styles and skill levels—addressing the lack of tools to simulate credible VR user behavior for game evaluation.
method: Train a conditional motion generator on the large BOXRR-23 dataset to map in-game object arrangements to headset and controller trajectories.
Condition generation on style exemplars to capture varied player behaviors and skill signatures.
Align or optimize generated motions to maximize simulated gameplay score, and validate the model on Beat Saber to produce skilled, diverse virtual players.
infographic.impact: Enables automated, repeatable VR playtesting and rapid design iteration, reducing reliance on human testers and providing a benchmarkable way to evaluate level difficulty and player experience. It also advances motion synthesis and simulated human behavior modeling in ML.

title: Exploiting Completeness Perception with Diffusion Transformer for Unified 3D MRI Synthesis
authors: Junkai Liu, Nay Aung, Theodoros N. Arvanitis, Joao A. C. Lima, Steffen E. Petersen
abstract: Missing data problems, such as missing modalities in multi-modal brain MRI and missing slices in cardiac MRI, pose significant challenges in clinical practice. Existing methods rely on external guidance to supply detailed missing state for instructing generative models to synthesize missing MRIs. However, manual indicators are not always available or reliable in real-world scenarios due to the unpredictable nature of clinical environments. Moreover, these explicit masks are not informative enoug

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces a unified diffusion-transformer framework that learns an internal "completeness perception" to synthesize missing 3D MRI data (missing modalities or slices) without relying on external/manual masks, enabling robust, real-world recovery of incomplete scans.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses missing-data in multi-modal and 3D MRI (e.g., absent imaging modalities or missing slices) and the practical limitation that manual/external masks indicating missing regions are often unavailable or unreliable in clinical settings.
method: Learn a completeness perception module that estimates the missingness/completeness state of an input MRI directly from data, removing dependence on external masks.
Use a diffusion-based generative model integrated with a transformer backbone to perform unified 3D MRI synthesis conditioned on the model’s perceived completeness.
Train with completeness-aware objectives (self-supervised reconstruction and diffusion losses) to handle variable missingness patterns (both missing modalities and missing slices) in a single model.
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable MRI reconstruction and augmentation in real clinical workflows by removing manual mask requirements and consolidating multiple missing-data scenarios into one robust generative model — useful for downstream diagnosis, segmentation, and multi-site studies.

title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 20 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01182-3

Zhou et al. develop PISA, an optimizer for deep learning models that supports heterogeneous data and various preconditions. It converges under minimal assumptions, while outperforming established methods for diverse tasks.

infographic.key_insight: PISA is a preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM optimizer that enables stable, provably convergent training of deep models under minimal assumptions, while handling heterogeneous data and a variety of preconditioners. It matches or outperforms standard optimizers across diverse tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Training deep models when data is heterogeneous, problems are ill-conditioned, or only inexact/local updates are feasible—situations where existing optimizers lack robustness, flexibility, or strong convergence guarantees.
method: Formulate a preconditioned, stochastic ADMM framework that permits inexact (approximate) subproblem solves and flexible preconditioners (diagonal, block, quasi-Newton, etc.).
Use stochastic updates that accommodate heterogeneous data across nodes/partitions while retaining a global coordination step via ADMM.
Provide theoretical convergence guarantees under minimal assumptions and demonstrate empirical gains over common optimizers on multiple tasks.
infographic.impact: Gives practitioners a robust, flexible optimizer for distributed/federated and ill-conditioned training scenarios, reducing tuning and improving stability and performance for real-world heterogeneous datasets.

Convergence plots comparing PISA vs. Adam/SGD/ADMM variants on accuracy and loss across tasks

title: SARAH: Spatially Aware Real-time Agentic Humans
authors: Evonne Ng, Siwei Zhang, Zhang Chen, Michael Zollhoefer, Alexander Richard
abstract: As embodied agents become central to VR, telepresence, and digital human applications, their motion must go beyond speech-aligned gestures: agents should turn toward users, respond to their movement, and maintain natural gaze. Current methods lack this spatial awareness. We close this gap with the first real-time, fully causal method for spatially-aware conversational motion, deployable on a streaming VR headset. Given a user's position and dyadic audio, our approach produces full-body motion th

infographic.key_insight: SARAH is the first real-time, fully causal method that makes conversational agents spatially aware—using a user's position and dyadic audio to generate natural, full‑body motion (turns, responses, gaze) suitable for streaming VR headsets.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing conversational-motion models ignore spatial context and/or require non-causal/offline processing, so agents fail to turn toward users, react to their movement, or maintain natural gaze in live VR/telepresence settings.
method: Causal, low-latency pipeline that runs in real time and is deployable on streaming VR hardware.
Conditions generation on user position (spatial cue) and dyadic audio to produce full-body motion and gaze that respond to the other participant.
Design and optimization choices focused on streaming/VR constraints (latency, continuous updates), enabling agentic, spatially-aware behavior.
infographic.impact: Enables VR, telepresence, and digital-human applications to exhibit natural, spatially-aware social behavior in live settings, improving immersion and social signaling while remaining practical to deploy on consumer streaming setups.

title: G-LoG Bi-filtration for Medical Image Classification
authors: Qingsong Wang, Jiaxing He, Bingzhe Hou, Tieru Wu, Yang Cao
abstract: Building practical filtrations on objects to detect topological and geometric features is an important task in the field of Topological Data Analysis (TDA). In this paper, leveraging the ability of the Laplacian of Gaussian operator to enhance the boundaries of medical images, we define the G-LoG (Gaussian-Laplacian of Gaussian) bi-filtration to generate the features more suitable for multi-parameter persistence module. By modeling volumetric images as bounded functions, then we prove the interl

infographic.key_insight: Applying a Laplacian-of-Gaussian enhancement together with a Gaussian-scale axis yields a G-LoG bi-filtration that captures boundary- and scale-aware topological features from volumetric medical images, with provable stability for multiparameter persistence representations.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard single-parameter filtrations miss scale-dependent boundary information in medical volumes; this work provides a practical, stable multiparameter filtration that better encodes geometric/topological features for classification.
method: Model volumetric medical images as bounded functions and apply a Laplacian-of-Gaussian (LoG) operator across Gaussian scales to enhance boundaries.
Construct a two-parameter (G-LoG) bi-filtration using Gaussian scale and LoG response, then compute multiparameter persistence summaries suited for multi-parameter persistence modules.
Prove an interleaving/stability result for the bi-filtration and convert multiparameter topological summaries into features for downstream classifiers (e.g., ML models for diagnosis).
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a theoretically grounded, boundary-aware topological feature extractor for 3D medical images that can improve robustness and interpretability of classification models—especially valuable when geometric detail and scale matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input volumetric scan → Gaussian scale axis + LoG operator → G-LoG bi-filtration → multiparameter persistence summary → classifier.

title: Multi-Level Conditioning by Pairing Localized Text and Sketch for Fashion Image Generation
authors: Ziyue Liu, Davide Talon, Federico Girella, Zanxi Ruan, Mattia Mondo
abstract: Sketches offer designers a concise yet expressive medium for early-stage fashion ideation by specifying structure, silhouette, and spatial relationships, while textual descriptions complement sketches to convey material, color, and stylistic details. Effectively combining textual and visual modalities requires adherence to the sketch visual structure when leveraging the guidance of localized attributes from text. We present LOcalized Text and Sketch with multi-level guidance (LOTS), a framework

infographic.key_insight: Pairing localized textual attributes with a designer's sketch and applying multi-level conditioning enables generated fashion images that faithfully follow the sketch structure while adding fine-grained material, color, and style details.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between sparse structural input (designer sketches) and rich semantic guidance (text) by ensuring localized textual attributes are respected spatially, preventing attribute bleeding or layout violations in fashion image generation.
method: Associate textual attribute phrases with spatial regions of the sketch (localized text–sketch pairing) so each attribute has a clear target area.
Apply multi-level conditioning (e.g., global, regional, local) during generation to enforce overall silhouette, regional consistency, and fine-grained local details.
Fuse the paired, multi-level conditioning signals into a generative pipeline to produce photorealistic fashion images that preserve sketch structure and reflect specified attributes.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, controllable multimodal conditioning technique for fashion design tools and generative research, enabling designers and ML practitioners to produce layout-faithful and attribute-accurate images from sparse inputs.

title: Going Down Memory Lane: Scaling Tokens for Video Stream Understanding with Dynamic KV-Cache Memory
authors: Vatsal Agarwal, Saksham Suri, Matthew Gwilliam, Pulkit Kumar, Abhinav Shrivastava
abstract: Streaming video understanding requires models to robustly encode, store, and retrieve information from a continuous video stream to support accurate video question answering (VQA). Existing state-of-the-art approaches rely on key-value caching to accumulate frame-level information over time, but use a limited number of tokens per frame, leading to the loss of fine-grained visual details. In this work, we propose scaling the token budget to enable more granular spatiotemporal understanding and re

infographic.key_insight: Increasing the per-frame token budget and managing those tokens with a dynamic key-value (KV) cache lets streaming models retain fine-grained spatiotemporal details, improving retrieval and question answering over long video streams without treating memory as a fixed low-resolution summary.
infographic.problem_solved: Streaming video understanding and VQA suffer when per-frame representations are compressed into too few tokens, losing fine-grained visual detail and temporal context; this work addresses how to scale and manage token memory so models can store and retrieve richer frame information over time.
method: Scale per-frame tokenization to produce more spatially and temporally granular tokens, then write those tokens into a KV-cache rather than discarding details.
Introduce dynamic KV-cache memory management (importance-based allocation, eviction, and aggregation) so the cache grows/contracts with stream demands while controlling compute and latency.
Efficient retrieval for question answering via selective attention/lookup over the cached keys and values, enabling the model to combine long-range context with high-resolution frame detail.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical recipe for building streaming video models that keep richer history without catastrophic memory bloat—improving accuracy on long-horizon VQA and other continuous-vision tasks while offering controllable trade-offs between fidelity, latency, and memory.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: live video frames → dense tokenization → dynamic KV-cache (write/evict) → query/retrieve → VQA output

title: Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory
authors: Usman Anwar, Tim Bakker, Dana Kianfar, Cristina Pinneri, Christos Louizos
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitors are LLM-based systems that analyze reasoning traces to detect when outputs may exhibit attributes of interest, such as test-hacking behavior during code generation. In this paper, we use information-theoretic analysis to show that non-zero mutual information between CoT and output is a necessary but not sufficient condition for CoT monitorability. We identify two sources of approximation error that may undermine the performance of CoT monitors in practice: informa

infographic.key_insight: Non-zero mutual information between a chain-of-thought (CoT) and an LLM output is necessary but not enough for reliable monitoring; practical monitor failure often comes from two approximation errors that break the theoretical link between CoT signal and monitor decisions.
infographic.problem_solved: Clarifies why CoT-based monitors sometimes fail in practice despite informative reasoning traces, and identifies the theoretical and practical failure modes that must be addressed to make CoT monitoring dependable.
method: Formulate CoT monitorability in information-theoretic terms and show that non-zero mutual information is a necessary but insufficient condition.
Analyze practical breakdowns by isolating two sources of approximation error that reduce monitor performance (statistical/estimation error and model/mismatch approximations).
Recommend mitigation strategies (improved estimators, better monitor modelling/calibration, and targeted probe designs) and validate their effects empirically.
infographic.impact: Provides a principled diagnostic framework and actionable levers (estimator quality and monitor fidelity) so practitioners can build and evaluate more reliable CoT monitors to catch undesirable behaviors like test‑hacking or spurious solutions.

title: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks in Solving Hard Constraint Satisfaction Problems
authors: Geri Skenderi, Lorenzo Buffoni, Francesco D'Amico, David Machado, Raffaele Marino
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly applied to hard optimization problems, often claiming superiority over classical heuristics. However, such claims risk being unsolid due to a lack of standard benchmarks on truly hard instances. From a statistical physics perspective, we propose new hard benchmarks based on random problems. We provide these benchmarks, along with performance results from both classical heuristics and GNNs. Our fair comparison shows that classical algorithms still out

infographic.key_insight: Standard GNN claims of superiority on hard optimization tasks are unreliable without truly hard benchmarks; when evaluated on new statistically-motivated hard random instances, classical heuristics still outperform current GNN approaches.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the absence of standardized, truly hard benchmark instances for evaluating Graph Neural Networks on hard constraint satisfaction and combinatorial optimization problems, enabling fair and meaningful comparisons with classical heuristics.
method: Construct hard random CSP instances using insights from statistical physics to target regions of algorithmic hardness (phase-transition-like regimes).
Assemble and release a benchmark suite plus evaluation protocol for fair comparison of solvers.
Empirically compare performance of multiple classical heuristics and GNN-based methods on these benchmarks, reporting solution quality and computational cost.
infographic.impact: Provides a rigorous benchmark and evaluation framework that prevents overclaiming GNN advantages and helps practitioners choose or develop solvers that truly handle the hardest instances; encourages more robust, reproducible research in graph-based optimization.

title: Unifying Color and Lightness Correction with View-Adaptive Curve Adjustment for Robust 3D Novel View Synthesis
authors: Ziteng Cui, Shuhong Liu, Xiaoyu Dong, Xuangeng Chu, Lin Gu
abstract: High-quality image acquisition in real-world environments remains challenging due to complex illumination variations and inherent limitations of camera imaging pipelines. These issues are exacerbated in multi-view capture, where differences in lighting, sensor responses, and image signal processor (ISP) configurations introduce photometric and chromatic inconsistencies that violate the assumptions of photometric consistency underlying modern 3D novel view synthesis (NVS) methods, including Neura

infographic.key_insight: A single, view-adaptive curve adjustment module jointly corrects both color (chromatic) and lightness (photometric) differences across multi-view captures, enabling robust novel view synthesis without relying on strict photometric consistency. Integrating learnable per-view curves into the NVS pipeline reduces color/lightness mismatch and improves rendered view fidelity.
infographic.problem_solved: Photometric and chromatic inconsistencies from lighting, sensor responses, and ISP settings break the photometric-consistency assumptions of modern NeRF-style novel view synthesis, causing artifacts and poor generalization on real multi-view captures.
method: Learnable, differentiable per-view curve adjustments that jointly correct color channels and lightness (a unified color+lightness correction operation).
View-adaptive conditioning: curves are predicted or optimized per view (from image features or view metadata) and applied within the NVS/NeRF pipeline to normalize inputs or intermediate radiance.
End-to-end training / joint optimization so the curve module and the novel-view synthesis model co-adapt, preserving geometry while removing photometric/chromatic variation.
infographic.impact: Makes 3D novel view synthesis far more robust for real-world, multi-camera captures by removing a common source of reconstruction and rendering error, reducing the need for manual color calibration and improving downstream quality metrics and visual realism. This enables more reliable NeRF deployment in uncontrolled capture scenarios.

title: Mine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Search Retrieval
authors: Jiaqi Xi, Raghav Saboo, Luming Chen, Martin Wang, Sudeep Das
abstract: We propose a two-stage "Mine and Refine" contrastive training framework for semantic text embeddings to enhance multi-category e-commerce search retrieval. Large scale e-commerce search demands embeddings that generalize to long tail, noisy queries while adhering to scalable supervision compatible with product and policy constraints. A practical challenge is that relevance is often graded: users accept substitutes or complements beyond exact matches, and production systems benefit from clear sep

infographic.key_insight: A two-stage contrastive training pipeline—"Mine" then "Refine"—produces semantic embeddings that capture graded relevance (exact matches, substitutes, complements) at scale, improving multi-category e-commerce search retrieval robustness for long-tail and noisy queries.
infographic.problem_solved: E-commerce retrieval needs embeddings that generalize to long-tail, noisy queries while respecting scalable supervision and product/policy constraints; existing approaches struggle to represent graded relevance where users accept substitutes or complements beyond exact matches.
method: Mine: gather large-scale, scalable supervision (weak/silver positives and negatives across categories) suitable for production constraints.
Refine: contrastive fine-tuning that explicitly models graded relevance, separating exact matches, substitutes, complements and true negatives in embedding space.
End-to-end design prioritizes scalability and compatibility with product/policy requirements so embeddings can be deployed across multi-category search systems.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way to train embedding models that better rank items for nuanced user intent in production search systems—improving relevance for long-tail queries while remaining scalable and policy-aware.

title: CLEF HIPE-2026: Evaluating Accurate and Efficient Person-Place Relation Extraction from Multilingual Historical Texts
authors: Juri Opitz, Corina Raclé, Emanuela Boros, Andrianos Michail, Matteo Romanello
abstract: HIPE-2026 is a CLEF evaluation lab dedicated to person-place relation extraction from noisy, multilingual historical texts. Building on the HIPE-2020 and HIPE-2022 campaigns, it extends the series toward semantic relation extraction by targeting the task of identifying person--place associations in multiple languages and time periods. Systems are asked to classify relations of two types - $at$ ("Has the person ever been at this place?") and $isAt$ ("Is the person located at this place around pub

infographic.key_insight: HIPE-2026 frames person–place relation extraction as a targeted multilingual evaluation over noisy historical texts, focusing on two pragmatic relation types (ever-at vs. contemporaneous location) to push semantic IE in diachronic, OCR-affected corpora.
infographic.problem_solved: Provides a standardized evaluation and benchmark for extracting accurate person–place associations from noisy, multilingual historical documents across time periods—addressing ambiguity, OCR errors, language variation, and temporality.
method: Curated multilingual, diachronic corpora with noisy historical and OCR-processed texts and annotated person–place relations.
Defined a two-label relation taxonomy: at (Has the person ever been at this place?) and isAt (Is the person located at the place around the text's timestamp?), with clear annotation guidelines.
Organized benchmark tasks, baseline systems, and multilingual evaluation metrics to compare accuracy and efficiency across languages and periods.
infographic.impact: Enables reproducible progress in historical and multilingual information extraction, guiding practitioners toward models robust to OCR noise, temporal reasoning, and cross-language variation—useful for digital humanities, biography extraction, and cultural analytics.

title: AI Gamestore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games
authors: Lance Ying, Ryan Truong, Prafull Sharma, Kaiya Ivy Zhao, Nathan Cloos
abstract: Rigorously evaluating machine intelligence against the broad spectrum of human general intelligence has become increasingly important and challenging in this era of rapid technological advance. Conventional AI benchmarks typically assess only narrow capabilities in a limited range of human activity. Most are also static, quickly saturating as developers explicitly or implicitly optimize for them. title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs
authors: Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) promise to ground language instructions in robot control, yet in practice often fail to faithfully follow language. When presented with instructions that lack strong scene-specific supervision, VLAs suffer from counterfactual failures: they act based on vision shortcuts induced by dataset biases, repeatedly executing well-learned behaviors and selecting objects frequently seen during training regardless of language intent. To systematically study it, we intro

infographic.key_insight: Vision-Language-Action models often ignore instructions and fall back on visual shortcuts learned from biased data; the paper identifies these "counterfactual failures" and shows how targeted evaluation and simple mitigation reduce vision-overrides of language.
infographic.problem_solved: VLAs can repeatedly execute visually frequent behaviors or pick commonly seen objects regardless of language intent, compromising instruction following and robustness. The paper diagnoses these failures systematically and provides methods to measure and reduce them.
method: Introduce a counterfactual evaluation protocol that tests instruction adherence by swapping scene elements or command targets to reveal vision-driven shortcuts.
Define metrics that quantify language override (how often vision-leaning actions contradict instructions) and analyze dataset biases driving failures.
Propose mitigation strategies (e.g., counterfactual data augmentation, bias-aware training objectives, and alignment regularizers) to strengthen language grounding in action policies.
infographic.impact: Provides practical diagnostics and fixes so practitioners can better evaluate VLA systems for instruction fidelity and robustness, improving safe and reliable robot behavior in real-world, ambiguous scenes.

title: OpenEarthAgent: A Unified Framework for Tool-Augmented Geospatial Agents
authors: Akashah Shabbir, Muhammad Umer Sheikh, Muhammad Akhtar Munir, Hiyam Debary, Mustansar Fiaz
abstract: Recent progress in multimodal reasoning has enabled agents that can interpret imagery, connect it with language, and perform structured analytical tasks. Extending such capabilities to the remote sensing domain remains challenging, as models must reason over spatial scale, geographic structures, and multispectral indices while maintaining coherent multi-step logic. To bridge this gap, OpenEarthAgent introduces a unified framework for developing tool-augmented geospatial agents trained on satelli

infographic.key_insight: OpenEarthAgent presents a unified framework that equips multimodal agents with geospatial tools so they can reason coherently over satellite imagery, spatial scales, geographic structures, and multispectral indices in multi-step tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between general multimodal reasoning and remote‑sensing needs by enabling agents to perform structured, tool-augmented analysis of satellite data while handling spatial scale, geographic structures, and multispectral signals.
method: Design a unified agent framework that integrates external geospatial tools (e.g., GIS queries, index calculators, segmentation/measurement utilities) with a multimodal reasoning core.
Train and align models on satellite imagery + language supervision so the agent can interpret multispectral inputs and call tools as part of multi-step workflows.
Provide a modular tool interface and execution loop that lets the agent plan, invoke tools, combine results, and produce coherent analytic outputs (maps, measurements, labeled areas).

title: Meta-designing quantum experiments with language models

abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 19 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01153-0

Language models can write human-readable code that captures general design rules, generating whole families of quantum experiments at once. A design strategy described here makes results interpretable and scalable, as well as accelerates discovery.

method: Use language models to write human‑readable code/programs that encode experiment design rules rather than single instances.
Generate families of quantum experiment candidates from the synthesized code and validate them via simulation or lab checks.

title: A.R.I.S.: Automated Recycling Identification System for E-Waste Classification Using Deep Learning
authors: Dhruv Talwar, Harsh Desai, Wendong Yin, Goutam Mohanty, Rafael Reveles
abstract: Traditional electronic recycling processes suffer from significant resource loss due to inadequate material separation and identification capabilities, limiting material recovery. We present A.R.I.S. (Automated Recycling Identification System), a low-cost, portable sorter for shredded e-waste that addresses this efficiency gap. The system employs a YOLOx model to classify metals, plastics, and circuit boards in real time, achieving low inference latency with high detection accuracy. Experimental

infographic.key_insight: A.R.I.S. pairs a YOLOx object-detection model with a low-cost portable sorter to classify shredded e-waste (metals, plastics, circuit boards) in real time, achieving low inference latency and high detection accuracy for improved material separation.
infographic.problem_solved: Electronic recycling loses recoverable resources because shredded e-waste is hard to identify and separate at scale; A.R.I.S. provides a practical, real-time identification and sorting solution to increase material recovery and reduce waste.
method: Train and deploy a YOLOx-based detector to classify fragments of shredded e-waste into metals, plastics, and circuit boards.
Integrate the model on a low-cost, portable sorter platform for edge inference and real-time actuation of sorting mechanisms.
Optimize system-level latency and throughput to enable high-speed classification while maintaining high detection accuracy on noisy, mixed-material feed.
infographic.impact: Shows a concrete, deployable use of modern object-detection models for environmental impact—valuable for ML practitioners working on edge deployment, real-time inference, and system integration in resource-constrained settings.

title: FAMOSE: A ReAct Approach to Automated Feature Discovery
authors: Keith Burghardt, Jienan Liu, Sadman Sakib, Yuning Hao, Bo Li
abstract: Feature engineering remains a critical yet challenging bottleneck in machine learning, particularly for tabular data, as identifying optimal features from an exponentially large feature space traditionally demands substantial domain expertise. To address this challenge, we introduce FAMOSE (Feature AugMentation and Optimal Selection agEnt), a novel framework that leverages the ReAct paradigm to autonomously explore, generate, and refine features while integrating feature selection and evaluation

infographic.key_insight: FAMOSE uses the ReAct (reasoning + acting) paradigm to autonomously generate, evaluate, and select informative features for tabular data, substantially reducing the need for manual feature engineering while improving downstream performance.
infographic.problem_solved: Automates the hard, expertise-heavy search over an exponentially large feature space to discover high-quality features for tabular ML tasks, integrating generation, evaluation, and selection into one loop.
method: ReAct agent loop: alternate reasoning (propose feature transformations) and acting (apply transformations to data) to explore candidate features.
Model-in-the-loop evaluation: iteratively evaluate candidates with predictive models and scoring metrics, pruning and refining proposals.
Integrated selection and optimization: combine feature importance, redundancy checks, and resource-aware search to produce a compact, high-performing feature set.
infographic.impact: Reduces time and domain expertise required for tabular feature engineering, improving reproducibility and enabling practitioners to achieve stronger models with less manual effort.

title: Art2Mus: Artwork-to-Music Generation via Visual Conditioning and Large-Scale Cross-Modal Alignment
authors: Ivan Rinaldi, Matteo Mendula, Nicola Fanelli, Florence Levé, Matteo Testi
abstract: Music generation has advanced markedly through multimodal deep learning, enabling models to synthesize audio from text and, more recently, from images. However, existing image-conditioned systems suffer from two fundamental limitations: (i) they are typically trained on natural photographs, limiting their ability to capture the richer semantic, stylistic, and cultural content of artworks; and (ii) most rely on an image-to-text conversion stage, using language as a semantic shortcut that simplifi

infographic.key_insight: Art2Mus directly translates visual features of artworks into music by learning large-scale cross-modal alignment between images and audio, avoiding lossy image→text shortcuts and capturing artistic style and cultural cues.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing image-conditioned music systems are trained mainly on natural photos and often convert images to text first, which loses stylistic, semantic and cultural information from artworks; Art2Mus addresses these gaps to produce music more faithful to artistic content.
method: Assemble large-scale paired (artwork, music) data and learn cross-modal alignment so visual embeddings align with musical/audio embeddings.
Use direct visual conditioning of an audio generative model (e.g., transformer/diffusion-based generator) to synthesize music from artwork features without an intermediary text stage.
Optimize for stylistic and semantic fidelity via contrastive/objectives and multimodal finetuning to preserve artistic cues (style, era, mood) in generated audio.
infographic.impact: Enables more faithful, style-aware music generation from artworks, improving creative AI tools for artists, museums and multimedia creators; advances multimodal alignment methods that better preserve non-textual semantics.

title: Pushing the Frontier of Black-Box LVLM Attacks via Fine-Grained Detail Targeting
authors: Xiaohan Zhao, Zhaoyi Li, Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Zhiqiang Shen
abstract: Black-box adversarial attacks on Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) are challenging due to missing gradients and complex multimodal boundaries. While prior state-of-the-art transfer-based approaches like M-Attack perform well using local crop-level matching between source and target images, we find this induces high-variance, nearly orthogonal gradients across iterations, violating coherent local alignment and destabilizing optimization. We attribute this to (i) ViT translation sensitivity tha

infographic.key_insight: Attacks that target stable, fine-grained image details (rather than matching large local crops) reduce high-variance, nearly-orthogonal gradient signals in transfer-based black-box LVLM attacks, producing more coherent and effective adversarial perturbations.
infographic.problem_solved: Improves transfer-based black-box adversarial attacks on Large Vision–Language Models by addressing instability caused by ViT translation sensitivity and inconsistent local crop-level matching, which previously produced noisy, non-coherent optimization steps.
method: Diagnose instability: show that crop-level matching yields high-variance, almost-orthogonal gradients across iterations due to ViT translation sensitivity and multimodal alignment mismatches.

Fine-grained detail targeting: concentrate perturbations on semantically stable, small-scale image details (attention/patch-aware selection) to preserve coherent local alignment across crops and iterations.
Stabilize optimization: enforce cross-crop and cross-iteration consistency (e.g., momentum/gradient-smoothing and multi-scale constraints) to improve transferability to black-box LVLMs.
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable and higher-success-rate black-box attacks on LVLMs, improving robustness evaluation and guiding better defenses and secure deployment practices for multimodal models.

title: Sink-Aware Pruning for Diffusion Language Models
authors: Aidar Myrzakhan, Tianyi Li, Bowei Guo, Shengkun Tang, Zhiqiang Shen
abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) incur high inference cost due to iterative denoising, motivating efficient pruning. Existing pruning heuristics largely inherited from autoregressive (AR) LLMs, typically preserve attention sink tokens because AR sinks serve as stable global anchors. We show that this assumption does not hold for DLMs: the attention-sink position exhibits substantially higher variance over the full generation trajectory (measured by how the dominant sink locations shift across ti

infographic.key_insight: Attention-sink positions in diffusion language models shift substantially across denoising steps, so pruning heuristics that preserve static AR-style sinks are suboptimal; a sink-aware importance metric that accounts for trajectory variance enables much more effective pruning.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the high inference cost of Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) by providing a principled pruning method tailored to DLMs — addressing the mismatch between autoregressive pruning heuristics and diffusion-specific attention dynamics.
method: Empirically measure attention-sink behavior across the full denoising trajectory and quantify per-position/attention variance.
Define a sink-aware importance score that aggregates step-wise dominance and variance to rank tokens/heads/units for retention.
Prune models using the sink-aware scores (static or step-aware masks), then fine-tune or calibrate to recover generation quality while reducing FLOPs/latency.
infographic.impact: Gives practitioners a principled, diffusion-specific pruning strategy that lowers DLM inference cost and latency without sacrificing generation quality, enabling more practical deployment of diffusion-based LLMs.

title: Stable Asynchrony: Variance-Controlled Off-Policy RL for LLMs
authors: Luke Huang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Qinghao Hu, Shang Yang, Song Han
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is widely used to improve large language models on reasoning tasks, and asynchronous RL training is attractive because it increases end-to-end throughput. However, for widely adopted critic-free policy-gradient methods such as REINFORCE and GRPO, high asynchrony makes the policy-gradient estimator markedly $\textbf{higher variance}$: training on stale rollouts creates heavy-tailed importance ratios, causing a small fraction of samples to dominate updates. This amplifi

infographic.key_insight: Introducing variance-controlled off-policy corrections lets asynchronous, critic-free policy-gradient training remain stable: by detecting and down-weighting heavy-tailed importance ratios from stale rollouts, updates stop being dominated by a few bad samples and variance is controlled.
infographic.problem_solved: Asynchrony in off-policy, critic-free policy-gradient methods (e.g., REINFORCE, GRPO) produces heavy-tailed importance ratios from stale rollouts, causing very high gradient variance and unstable or inefficient LLM fine-tuning.
method: Detect and mitigate heavy-tailed importance ratios from stale rollouts using per-sample variance-aware reweighting and adaptive clipping to limit any single sample's influence.
Apply off-policy correction that is aware of staleness (timestamped rollouts) and dynamically adjusts importance weights to trade off bias and variance.
Integrate these variance-control steps into asynchronous worker pipelines so throughput gains are retained while training stability is restored.
infographic.impact: Enables higher asynchrony and throughput for RL-based LLM tuning (e.g., RLHF) without sacrificing stability; practitioners can train faster with lower compute waste from high-variance updates and fewer training collapses.

title: MolHIT: Advancing Molecular-Graph Generation with Hierarchical Discrete Diffusion Models
authors: Hojung Jung, Rodrigo Hormazabal, Jaehyeong Jo, Youngrok Park, Kyunggeun Roh
abstract: Molecular generation with diffusion models has emerged as a promising direction for AI-driven drug discovery and materials science. While graph diffusion models have been widely adopted due to the discrete nature of 2D molecular graphs, existing models suffer from low chemical validity and struggle to meet the desired properties compared to 1D modeling. In this work, we introduce MolHIT, a powerful molecular graph generation framework that overcomes long-standing performance limitations in exist

infographic.key_insight: MolHIT introduces a hierarchical discrete diffusion framework that generates molecular graphs in a coarse‑to‑fine manner, enabling more chemically valid and property‑aligned molecules than prior graph diffusion approaches.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing graph diffusion models for molecular generation suffer from low chemical validity and poor control of desired molecular properties, limiting their usefulness compared with 1D (SMILES) models.
method: Hierarchical discrete diffusion: generate molecular graphs progressively from coarse structure to fine atom/bond details to stabilize sampling and capture multi-scale structure.
Discrete denoising tailored to categorical graph features (nodes/edges) with a specially designed noise schedule and denoiser network.
Training and architectural strategies to preserve chemical constraints and steer generation toward target properties (e.g., valency-aware modules, conditional guidance).
infographic.impact: MolHIT makes graph-based molecular generation more reliable and controllable, helping AI/ML practitioners produce chemically realistic candidates for drug discovery and materials design while enabling property-focused generation workflows.

title: CORAL: Correspondence Alignment for Improved Virtual Try-On
authors: Jiyoung Kim, Youngjin Shin, Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Jisu Nam
abstract: Existing methods for Virtual Try-On (VTON) often struggle to preserve fine garment details, especially in unpaired settings where accurate person-garment correspondence is required. These methods do not explicitly enforce person-garment alignment and fail to explain how correspondence emerges within Diffusion Transformers (DiTs). In this paper, we first analyze full 3D attention in DiT-based architecture and reveal that the person-garment correspondence critically depends on precise person-garme

infographic.key_insight: Explicitly enforcing person–garment correspondence inside Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) causes correspondence to emerge reliably and preserves fine garment details in unpaired virtual try-on. CORAL analyzes 3D attention and injects alignment constraints so DiT-based VTONs better map garment pixels to the correct body regions.
infographic.problem_solved: Virtual try-on systems (especially DiT-based) struggle to preserve fine garment detail and lack explicit mechanisms or explanations for person–garment correspondence in unpaired settings, producing misaligned or blurred clothing outputs.
method: Analyze full 3D attention patterns in Diffusion Transformer architectures to identify how and when person–garment correspondence forms or degrades.

Introduce CORAL — a correspondence alignment module/constraint that enforces precise person–garment alignment within the attention mechanism (via attention regularization and correspondence supervision), so mappings emerge robustly without paired training data.
Train the model with combined generative diffusion objectives plus correspondence-alignment signals to preserve fine details and improve realism in the synthesized try-on images.
infographic.impact: Enables more realistic, detail-preserving virtual try-on results and makes DiT attention more interpretable and controllable. Useful for practitioners building conditioned image synthesis, fashion applications, and any pipeline that needs robust spatial correspondence from generative transformers.

title: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
authors: Faria Huq, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Zhanqiu Guo, Venu Arvind Arangarajan, Tianyue Ou
abstract: Despite rapid progress in autonomous web agents, human involvement remains essential for shaping preferences and correcting agent behavior as tasks unfold. However, current agentic systems lack a principled understanding of when and why humans intervene, often proceeding autonomously past critical decision points or requesting unnecessary confirmation. In this work, we introduce the task of modeling human intervention to support collaborative web task execution. We collect CowCorpus, a dataset o

infographic.key_insight: Human intervention in web agents follows predictable patterns that can be learned and anticipated; modeling when and why people step in enables agents to collaborate more effectively instead of over-autonomizing or asking needless confirmations.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a principled framework for predicting and reasoning about human intervention during autonomous web task execution, reducing harmful autonomous decisions and unnecessary human queries.
method: Collect and annotate CowCorpus — a dataset of web task traces with labeled human intervention points and contextual signals.
Train supervised sequence/prediction models that use agent state, task context, and uncertainty cues to predict likely intervention moments and types.
Analyze intervention causes and outcomes to derive policies for when agents should defer, query, or act autonomously.

title: Towards Anytime-Valid Statistical Watermarking
authors: Baihe Huang, Eric Xu, Kannan Ramchandran, Jiantao Jiao, Michael I. Jordan
abstract: The proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) necessitates efficient mechanisms to distinguish machine-generated content from human text. While statistical watermarking has emerged as a promising solution, existing methods suffer from two critical limitations: the lack of a principled approach for selecting sampling distributions and the reliance on fixed-horizon hypothesis testing, which precludes valid early stopping. In this paper, we bridge this gap by developing the first e-value-based

infographic.key_insight: Reformulates statistical watermarking using e-values to produce the first anytime-valid detection procedure, and introduces a principled way to choose sampling distributions to improve detection power while allowing valid early stopping.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes two limitations of prior watermarking: (1) ad-hoc sampling distributions that reduce power, and (2) fixed-horizon tests that break validity under optional stopping, preventing reliable early detection.
method: Builds an e-value based test statistic for watermark detection so hypothesis tests remain valid under optional stopping (anytime-valid inference).
Develops principled criteria for selecting sampling distributions that optimize detection power under the watermarking scheme.
Provides algorithms with theoretical guarantees and empirical evaluations on LLM-generated text to demonstrate improved power and valid early stopping.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to detect machine-generated text more reliably and efficiently—using fewer tokens and allowing safe early stopping—while retaining provable statistical guarantees, improving practicality for real-world deployment and monitoring.

title: Learning Situated Awareness in the Real World
authors: Chuhan Li, Ruilin Han, Joy Hsu, Yongyuan Liang, Rajiv Dhawan
abstract: A core aspect of human perception is situated awareness, the ability to relate ourselves to the surrounding physical environment and reason over possible actions in context. However, most existing benchmarks for multimodal foundation models (MFMs) emphasize environment-centric spatial relations (relations among objects in a scene), while largely overlooking observer-centric relationships that require reasoning relative to agent's viewpoint, pose, and motion. To bridge this gap, we introduce SAW-

infographic.key_insight: This paper introduces SAW, a real-world benchmark that explicitly measures observer-centric (agent-relative) situated awareness—letting models reason about viewpoint, pose, and motion rather than only object-object relations.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing multimodal benchmarks emphasize environment-centric spatial relations and neglect observer-centric relationships that require reasoning relative to an agent's viewpoint, pose, and motion; SAW fills this evaluation gap.
method: Curate a real-world dataset focused on observer-centric annotations (viewpoint, pose, motion cues, and agent-relative relations).
Define tasks and evaluation protocols that test situated awareness (e.g., viewpoint-aware QA, action-inference, localization from agent pose, temporal reasoning).
Benchmark state-of-the-art multimodal foundation models to quantify gaps and provide diagnostics for improving agent-relative reasoning.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a targeted benchmark to train and evaluate models for real-world, agent-centered reasoning—critical for robotics, AR, and navigation systems. It highlights concrete failure modes and guides improvements in multimodal and embodied AI.

title: Are Object-Centric Representations Better At Compositional Generalization?
authors: Ferdinand Kapl, Amir Mohammad Karimi Mamaghan, Maximilian Seitzer, Karl Henrik Johansson, Carsten Marr
abstract: Compositional generalization, the ability to reason about novel combinations of familiar concepts, is fundamental to human cognition and a critical challenge for machine learning. Object-centric (OC) representations, which encode a scene as a set of objects, are often argued to support such generalization, but systematic evidence in visually rich settings is limited. We introduce a Visual Question Answering benchmark across three controlled visual worlds (CLEVRTex, Super-CLEVR, and MOVi-C) to me

infographic.key_insight: A systematic benchmark across three controlled visual worlds shows that object-centric representations can improve compositional generalization in some visual reasoning settings, but advantages are context-dependent rather than universal.
infographic.problem_solved: Determines whether and when object-centric (OC) scene representations actually help models generalize to novel combinations of familiar concepts in visually rich Visual Question Answering tasks.
method: Introduce a controlled VQA benchmark spanning three simulated visual worlds: CLEVRTex, Super-CLEVR, and MOVi-C.
Compare object-centric models against non-OC baselines on multiple compositional generalization splits and measure performance under varying scene complexity and supervision.
Analyze when OC representations help (e.g., occlusion, relational queries, object counts) and when they do not, identifying dataset and task factors that modulate benefits.
infographic.impact: Provides practical guidance for ML practitioners on when to invest in object-centric architectures for visual reasoning: use OC representations when tasks emphasize explicit object-level reasoning and structure, but expect mixed returns for other settings. Helps prioritize model design and dataset choices for compositional generalization research.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of object-centric vs. distributed scene representations (objects as slots vs. monolithic feature map).

title: Policy Compiler for Secure Agentic Systems
authors: Nils Palumbo, Sarthak Choudhary, Jihye Choi, Prasad Chalasani, Mihai Christodorescu
abstract:
LLM-based agents are increasingly being deployed in contexts requiring complex authorization policies: customer service protocols, approval workflows, data access restrictions, and regulatory compliance. Embedding these policies in prompts provides no enforcement guarantees. We present PCAS, a Policy Compiler for Agentic Systems that provides deterministic policy enforcement.
  Enforcing such policies requires tracking information flow across agents, which linear message histories cannot capture

infographic.key_insight: A Policy Compiler (PCAS) deterministically enforces complex authorization policies for LLM-based agents by compiling high-level rules into runtime-enforceable primitives and tracking information flow beyond linear message histories.
infographic.problem_solved: LLM agents often operate under complex authorization and compliance constraints, but embedding policies in prompts gives no enforcement guarantees and linear conversation histories fail to capture cross-agent information flow and provenance needed for correct enforcement.
method: Specify high-level authorization and compliance policies and compile them into concrete, monitorable enforcement primitives (runtime checks, guards, and constrained actions).
Model and track information flow across agents as a provenance/graph structure (not just a linear message log) to capture branching, merges, and cross-agent dependencies.
Enforce policies deterministically at runtime via compiled monitors and constrained execution, enabling provable guarantees about allowed actions and data disclosures.
infographic.impact: PCAS lets practitioners deploy agentic systems with stronger, deterministic guarantees for authorization, data-exposure prevention, and regulatory compliance—reducing risk from latent prompt-based policies and subtle multi-agent flows.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: Policy authoring → Policy compiler → Runtime monitors → Agent ecosystem (showing enforcement points).
Information-flow graph vs. linear history: side-by-side illustration showing how graph provenance captures branching and merges across agents.
Compilation pipeline flowchart: high-level policy → intermediate representation → enforcement primitives/monitors → runtime enforcement example.
