title: Causality in Video Diffusers is Separable from Denoising
authors: Xingjian Bai, Guande He, Zhengqi Li, Eli Shechtman, Xun Huang
abstract: Causality -- referring to temporal, uni-directional cause-effect relationships between components -- underlies many complex generative processes, including videos, language, and robot trajectories. Current causal diffusion models entangle temporal reasoning with iterative denoising, applying causal attention across all layers, at every denoising step, and over the entire context. In this paper, we show that the causal reasoning in these models is separable from the multi-step denoising process.

infographic.key_insight: Temporal (causal) reasoning in video diffusion models can be separated from the multi-step denoising procedure: causal attention need not run at every layer and step and can be implemented as a lightweight, modular component.
infographic.problem_solved: Current causal diffusion models entangle temporal reasoning with iterative denoising—leading to high compute, tight coupling across layers/steps, and reduced modularity; this work shows how to decouple causality from denoising while preserving generation quality.
method: Introduce a separable causal module that encapsulates temporal (uni-directional) reasoning independent of the denoiser.
Apply causal attention sparsely (e.g., at select layers/steps or in a single pass) instead of across all layers and every denoising iteration.
Train/design the pipeline so the denoiser and causal module can operate modularly, maintaining sample quality with reduced computation and context entanglement.
infographic.impact: Makes video (and other temporally-structured) diffusion models more compute-efficient, scalable, and easier to transfer or adapt—beneficial for practitioners needing temporally coherent generative models with lower resource cost.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: separate blocks for 'Causal Reasoning Module' and 'Denoiser' with arrows showing modular interaction.
Timeline/comparison: baseline (causal attention at every step) vs separable approach (causal applied sparsely) illustrating fewer attention invocations.
Bar/line chart: compute (FLOPs or latency) vs generation quality (temporal consistency / FID) showing similar or better quality at lower cost.
Example frames + attention maps: show temporal consistency maintained with the separable causal module.

title: SAGE: Scalable Agentic 3D Scene Generation for Embodied AI
authors: Hongchi Xia, Xuan Li, Zhaoshuo Li, Qianli Ma, Jiashu Xu
abstract: Real-world data collection for embodied agents remains costly and unsafe, calling for scalable, realistic, and simulator-ready 3D environments. However, existing scene-generation systems often rely on rule-based or task-specific pipelines, yielding artifacts and physically invalid scenes. We present SAGE, an agentic framework that, given a user-specified embodied task (e.g., "pick up a bowl and place it on the table"), understands the intent and automatically generates simulation-ready environme

infographic.key_insight: SAGE is an agentic system that converts a user-specified embodied task into a realistic, simulator-ready 3D scene by understanding intent and autonomously constructing physically valid environments. It scales scene generation beyond brittle rule-based pipelines by iteratively planning, placing, and validating objects.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the cost, safety risks, and manual effort of collecting real-world embodied-agent data by producing scalable, realistic, and physically valid 3D simulation environments that are ready for downstream embodied tasks.
method: Task understanding: parse user-specified embodied tasks (e.g., 'pick up a bowl and place it on the table') to derive goals and constraints.
Agentic scene synthesis: use iterative agent modules to plan object selection, placement, and scene layout while enforcing task affordances.
Physics-aware validation & export: validate scene stability and interactions with a physics check, then export simulator-ready assets and annotations.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to rapidly generate high-quality synthetic environments for training and evaluating embodied agents, improving safety, reproducibility, and dataset diversity while reducing manual scene engineering.

Before/after comparison: artifact-prone rule-based scene vs. SAGE-generated physically valid scene

title: Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zhaoyang Wang, Canwen Xu, Boyi Liu, Yite Wang, Siwei Han
abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM) have empowered autonomous agents to perform complex tasks that require multi-turn interactions with tools and environments. However, scaling such agent training is limited by the lack of diverse and reliable environments. In this paper, we propose Agent World Model (AWM), a fully synthetic environment generation pipeline. Using this pipeline, we scale to 1,000 environments covering everyday scenarios, in which agents can interact with rich toolsets (

infographic.key_insight: Agent World Model (AWM) is a fully synthetic environment generation pipeline that produces scalable, diverse, and interactive worlds for agentic reinforcement learning—enabling effectively unlimited environments (e.g., 1,000+ everyday scenarios) with rich toolsets for multi-turn agent interactions.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity and limited diversity of reliable training environments that hinder scaling and robust evaluation of autonomous agents.
method: Automated synthetic environment generation pipeline that constructs diverse everyday scenarios at scale.
Integration of rich, interactive toolsets and standardized agent-environment APIs so agents can perform multi-turn tool use and interactions.
Scalable instantiation and quality controls to ensure variety and reliability across hundreds to thousands of generated environments.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a low-cost, high-diversity source of training and evaluation environments to accelerate development of robust, generalist agents and reproducible agentic RL research.

Grid of sample synthetic environments illustrating scenario diversity (home, office, outdoor, retail, etc.)

title: ShapeCond: Fast Shapelet-Guided Dataset Condensation for Time Series Classification
authors: Sijia Peng, Yun Xiong, Xi Chen, Yi Xie, Guanzhi Li
abstract: Time series data supports many domains (e.g., finance and climate science), but its rapid growth strains storage and computation. Dataset condensation can alleviate this by synthesizing a compact training set that preserves key information. Yet most condensation methods are image-centric and often fail on time series because they miss time-series-specific temporal structure, especially local discriminative motifs such as shapelets. In this work, we propose ShapeCond, a novel and efficient conden

infographic.key_insight: ShapeCond leverages time-series-specific shapelets (local discriminative motifs) to guide synthesis of a tiny, high-fidelity training set, enabling fast dataset condensation that preserves temporal structure image-centric methods miss.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing dataset condensation approaches are designed for images and often fail on time series because they ignore local temporal motifs; ShapeCond addresses the challenge of creating compact, informative synthetic time-series datasets that retain class-discriminative temporal patterns.
method: Extract class-discriminative shapelets (local motifs) from the original time-series data to capture temporal signatures.
Optimize a small set of synthetic time-series so their shapelet activations (or shapelet-guided gradients) match those of the full dataset, ensuring preserved discriminative structure.
Use shapelet-aware initialization and lightweight optimization to make condensation fast and scalable for time-series classification tasks.
infographic.impact: Allows ML practitioners to train and iterate time-series classifiers much faster using far smaller synthesized datasets while preserving classification-relevant temporal motifs—reducing storage, compute, and deployment costs.

title: CIC-Trap4Phish: A Unified Multi-Format Dataset for Phishing and Quishing Attachment Detection
authors: Fatemeh Nejati, Mahdi Rabbani, Mansur Mirani, Gunjan Piya, Igor Opushnyev
abstract: Phishing attacks represents one of the primary attack methods which is used by cyber attackers. In many cases, attackers use deceptive emails along with malicious attachments to trick users into giving away sensitive information or installing malware while compromising entire systems. The flexibility of malicious email attachments makes them stand out as a preferred vector for attackers as they can embed harmful content such as malware or malicious URLs inside standard document formats. Although

infographic.key_insight: CIC-Trap4Phish provides a unified, multi-format dataset of malicious and benign email attachments—including quishing (QR-code-based) artifacts—enabling end-to-end detection research across diverse attachment types that were previously fragmented across datasets.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a single, labeled resource covering multiple attachment formats (PDF, Office docs, images, archives, QR-containing media) and quishing examples, which hinder development and evaluation of generalized attachment-level phishing detectors.
method: Collect and curate real-world malicious and benign email attachments across multiple formats, with expert labeling for phishing/quishing intent.
Standardize extraction and representation: static parsing, metadata capture, embedded-URL extraction, OCR/QR decoding, and feature normalization across formats.
Publish dataset plus reproducible baselines and evaluation protocols to measure within-format and cross-format generalization of detectors.
infographic.impact: Provides ML practitioners a single, well-documented benchmark to train and evaluate attachment-level phishing/quishing models, improving robustness to diverse file types and embedded attack vectors and accelerating defensive research and deployment.

title: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
authors: Jiacheng Liu, Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Xinyi Shang, Xiaohan Zhao
abstract: The rapid evolution of GUI-enabled agents has rendered traditional CAPTCHAs obsolete. While previous benchmarks like OpenCaptchaWorld established a baseline for evaluating multimodal agents, recent advancements in reasoning-heavy models, such as Gemini3-Pro-High and GPT-5.2-Xhigh have effectively collapsed this security barrier, achieving pass rates as high as 90% on complex logic puzzles like "Bingo". In response, we introduce Next-Gen CAPTCHAs, a scalable defense framework designed to secure t

infographic.key_insight: Next‑Gen CAPTCHAs exploit a measurable "cognitive gap" — tasks humans solve easily but current GUI‑enabled agents fail — enabling a scalable, diverse defense that restores reliable human verification.
infographic.problem_solved: Traditional CAPTCHAs and earlier benchmarks (e.g., OpenCaptchaWorld) have been broken by recent reasoning‑heavy multimodal agents (pass rates reported up to ~90%), leaving online services vulnerable. This work addresses the need for CAPTCHA designs that remain robust as GUI‑enabled agents advance.
method: Cognitive‑gap challenge design: create multimodal GUI tasks that emphasize human strengths (e.g., ambiguous context, multi‑step commonsense reasoning, flexible spatial manipulation) while exposing agent weaknesses.
Diversity and scalability via procedural generation: large pools of templated, parameterized GUI challenges and visual variations to prevent memorization and model overfitting.

Adaptive benchmarking and human calibration: continuously evaluate against state‑of‑the‑art agents, measure human baselines, and incorporate feedback loop to update challenge distributions and robustness tests.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical framework to build and benchmark CAPTCHA systems resilient to advanced multimodal agents, and a methodology for designing human‑centered verification tasks that scale with model capability.
visual_elements: Cognitive gap diagram: Venn or capability map showing human vs agent strengths and the target gap exploited by Next‑Gen CAPTCHAs.

title: WorldCompass: Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon World Models
authors: Zehan Wang, Tengfei Wang, Haiyu Zhang, Xuhui Zuo, Junta Wu
abstract: This work presents WorldCompass, a novel Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training framework for the long-horizon, interactive video-based world models, enabling them to explore the world more accurately and consistently based on interaction signals. To effectively "steer" the world model's exploration, we introduce three core innovations tailored to the autoregressive video generation paradigm: 1) Clip-level rollout Strategy: We generate and evaluate multiple samples at a single target clip, wh

infographic.key_insight: WorldCompass is an RL post-training framework that steers autoregressive, video-based world models by using interaction signals to explore and prefer accurate, consistent long-horizon continuations via targeted clip-level rollouts.
infographic.problem_solved: Video world models degrade over long horizons because autoregressive sampling compounds errors and lacks a mechanism to use interaction feedback; WorldCompass addresses how to explore and select long-horizon trajectories that remain accurate and coherent.
method: Clip-level rollout strategy: generate multiple candidate continuations for a single target clip, evaluate them, and use those evaluations to guide longer rollouts.

RL-based post-training policy: frame sample selection/steering as a reinforcement learning problem using interaction-derived rewards (accuracy, consistency) to update a steering policy without retraining the base video model.
Long-horizon aggregation: compose clip-level decisions into coherent long-horizon trajectories and optimize the steering objective to reduce drift and improve consistency over many steps.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical way to make autoregressive video world models more reliable for long-horizon simulation, improving downstream planning, model-based RL, and any application that needs consistent multi-step visual predictions.

title: Autoregressive Image Generation with Masked Bit Modeling
authors: Qihang Yu, Qihao Liu, Ju He, Xinyang Zhang, Yang Liu
abstract: This paper challenges the dominance of continuous pipelines in visual generation. We systematically investigate the performance gap between discrete and continuous methods. Contrary to the belief that discrete tokenizers are intrinsically inferior, we demonstrate that the disparity arises primarily from the total number of bits allocated in the latent space (i.e., the compression ratio). We show that scaling up the codebook size effectively bridges this gap, allowing discrete tokenizers to match

infographic.key_insight: The apparent gap between discrete and continuous visual generation stems not from an inherent weakness of discrete tokenizers but from the number of bits (compression ratio) in the latent space — increasing codebook size lets discrete methods match continuous pipelines.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the belief that discrete tokenizers are intrinsically inferior to continuous latent methods in autoregressive image generation by isolating the true cause of the performance gap.
method: Introduce Masked Bit Modeling within an autoregressive framework to operate on discrete latent codes.
Systematically vary the total number of bits (via codebook size) to study how compression ratio affects fidelity and generation quality.
Compare discrete and continuous pipelines under matched bit budgets to demonstrate that scaling codebook size closes the performance gap.
infographic.impact: Shows practitioners that choosing or designing discrete tokenizers should focus on available bit budget rather than assuming an inherent disadvantage—enabling discrete, scalable autoregressive models that can rival continuous approaches.
visual_elements: Line/bar chart: generation quality (e.g., FID/accuracy proxy) vs. total bits/codebook size showing convergence of discrete and continuous methods as bits increase.
Schematic: side-by-side pipeline diagrams of discrete (tokenizer + codebook) and continuous latent workflows with an annotation of bit budget.
Illustration: masked bit modeling mechanism (masking bits in discrete codes and autoregressive prediction) to convey the core modeling idea.

title: $χ_{0}$: Resource-Aware Robust Manipulation via Taming Distributional Inconsistencies
authors: Checheng Yu, Chonghao Sima, Gangcheng Jiang, Hai Zhang, Haoguang Mai
abstract: High-reliability long-horizon robotic manipulation has traditionally relied on large-scale data and compute to understand complex real-world dynamics. However, we identify that the primary bottleneck to real-world robustness is not resource scale alone, but the distributional shift among the human demonstration distribution, the inductive bias learned by the policy, and the test-time execution distribution -- a systematic inconsistency that causes compounding errors in multi-stage tasks. To miti

infographic.key_insight: Distributional mismatch between human demonstrations, the policy's inductive bias, and test-time execution—not just data/compute scale—is the primary cause of compounding failures in long-horizon manipulation. χ₀ is a resource-aware approach that tames these inconsistencies to achieve robust multi-stage behavior without relying on massive scale.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces failure caused by systematic distributional shifts across demonstration, learned policy bias, and real-world execution that lead to compounding errors in long-horizon robotic manipulation, while keeping compute and data requirements practical.
method: Diagnose and explicitly model distributional inconsistencies across three distributions (demonstration, policy bias, execution) and prioritize mitigation where mismatch most harms downstream stages.

Apply resource-aware training and deployment techniques — e.g., targeted distribution alignment (reweighting or domain-aware augmentation) plus lightweight online correction/adaptation — to limit compounding errors with minimal extra compute/data.
Decompose long tasks into critical sub-stages and allocate modeling/compute budget adaptively (focus resources on high-risk transitions) to maximize reliability under resource constraints.
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable, real-world long-horizon manipulation without scaling datasets or compute indiscriminately, making robust robotic policies more practical for deployment and iteration. Useful for practitioners who need safety and efficiency under limited resources.
visual_elements: Venn diagram of three distributions (Human Demos, Policy Inductive Bias, Test-time Execution) highlighting mismatched regions that cause failures
Pipeline illustration showing (1) distribution diagnosis, (2) targeted alignment / adaptive budgeting, and (3) online correction during execution

title: ARO: A New Lens On Matrix Optimization For Large Models
authors: Wenbo Gong, Javier Zazo, Qijun Luo, Puqian Wang, James Hensman
abstract: Matrix-based optimizers have attracted growing interest for improving LLM training efficiency, with significant progress centered on orthogonalization/whitening based methods. While yielding substantial performance gains, a fundamental question arises: can we develop new paradigms beyond orthogonalization, pushing the efficiency frontier further? We present \textbf{Adaptively Rotated Optimization (ARO}, a new matrix optimization framework that treats gradient rotation as a first class design pri

infographic.key_insight: ARO reframes matrix-based optimization by treating gradient rotation as a first-class operation, providing a new paradigm beyond orthogonalization/whitening to improve optimization efficiency for large models.
infographic.problem_solved: Current matrix optimizers focus on orthogonalization/whitening; ARO addresses whether alternative, rotation-centric matrix transforms can yield better training efficiency and scalability for large models.
method: Introduce Adaptively Rotated Optimization (ARO): a matrix optimization framework that explicitly performs adaptive gradient rotations instead of relying solely on orthogonalization/whitening.
Learn or update compact rotation operators per parameter block to reshape gradient geometry, improving conditioning and information flow while keeping computational overhead low.
Design efficient updates and implementation strategies that integrate into large-model training pipelines with minimal memory/compute amplification.
infographic.impact: ARO offers a new toolset for practitioners to accelerate and stabilize training of large models by changing how gradient covariance is handled—potentially delivering better convergence or resource efficiency without major architecture changes.
visual_elements: Diagram showing standard whitening/orthogonalization vs. adaptive rotation applied to gradient vectors
Schematic of ARO applied per-parameter or per-block (matrix) with arrows indicating learned rotation operators

title: GEBench: Benchmarking Image Generation Models as GUI Environments
authors: Haodong Li, Jingwei Wu, Quan Sun, Guopeng Li, Juanxi Tian
abstract: Recent advancements in image generation models have enabled the prediction of future Graphical User Interface (GUI) states based on user instructions. However, existing benchmarks primarily focus on general domain visual fidelity, leaving the evaluation of state transitions and temporal coherence in GUI-specific contexts underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce GEBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating dynamic interaction and temporal coherence in GUI generation. GEBench comprise

infographic.key_insight: GEBench provides the first benchmark focused on GUI-specific image generation, evaluating models by how well they predict multi-step GUI state transitions and maintain temporal coherence—not just single-frame visual fidelity.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing benchmarks emphasize general visual quality but do not assess interaction-driven state transitions or temporal consistency in GUI generation; GEBench fills this evaluation gap.
method: Curate multi-step GUI state sequences paired with user instructions and action labels to form interaction-driven test cases.
Treat image-generation models as GUI environments: run action-conditioned rollouts and compare predicted next states to ground truth using state-transition and temporal-coherence metrics.
Provide a standardized evaluation suite and metrics to measure interaction fidelity, action correctness, and long-horizon consistency across models.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and engineers to benchmark and improve models for interactive UI tasks (e.g., automated agents, UI synthesis) by quantifying how well generated GUIs preserve correct state transitions over time.

title: Contact-Anchored Policies: Contact Conditioning Creates Strong Robot Utility Models
authors: Zichen Jeff Cui, Omar Rayyan, Haritheja Etukuru, Bowen Tan, Zavier Andrianarivo
abstract: The prevalent paradigm in robot learning attempts to generalize across environments, embodiments, and tasks with language prompts at runtime. A fundamental tension limits this approach: language is often too abstract to guide the concrete physical understanding required for robust manipulation. In this work, we introduce Contact-Anchored Policies (CAP), which replace language conditioning with points of physical contact in space. Simultaneously, we structure CAP as a library of modular utility m

infographic.key_insight: Replacing abstract language prompts with explicit points of physical contact yields more physically grounded and reliable robot utility models. Contact-Anchored Policies (CAP) use contact locations as conditioning signals to produce modular, robust manipulation behaviors.
infographic.problem_solved: Language conditioning is often too abstract to convey the concrete physical information required for robust robotic manipulation; CAP addresses the gap between high-level instructions and low-level contact-rich control.
method: Condition policies on explicit 3D contact points in the environment instead of natural language prompts.
Structure the approach as a library of modular utility models (CAP modules) anchored to contact locations to enable compositional reuse across tasks and embodiments.
Use contact-conditioned utilities to select and compose low-level actions for contact-rich manipulation, improving physical grounding and task reliability.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CAP offers a practical alternative to language-conditioned controllers by providing clearer, physically meaningful conditioning signals that improve generalization and modular reuse in manipulation tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: language-conditioned pipeline vs contact-anchored pipeline (showing how contact points directly influence action selection).

title: Dexterous Manipulation Policies from RGB Human Videos via 4D Hand-Object Trajectory Reconstruction
authors: Hongyi Chen, Tony Dong, Tiancheng Wu, Liquan Wang, Yash Jangir
abstract: Multi-finger robotic hand manipulation and grasping are challenging due to the high-dimensional action space and the difficulty of acquiring large-scale training data. Existing approaches largely rely on human teleoperation with wearable devices or specialized sensing equipment to capture hand-object interactions, which limits scalability. In this work, we propose VIDEOMANIP, a device-free framework that learns dexterous manipulation directly from RGB human videos. Leveraging recent advances in

infographic.key_insight: Reconstructing 4D (3D + time) hand–object trajectories from ordinary RGB human videos creates scalable, device-free demonstrations that can be retargeted to train dexterous multi-finger robotic hand policies.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the scarcity and cost of device-based demonstration data for dexterous manipulation by enabling large-scale learning directly from in-the-wild RGB videos.
method: 4D reconstruction pipeline: estimate temporally consistent 3D hand and object trajectories and contact geometry from monocular RGB video.
Retargeting & representation: convert human hand–object trajectories into robot-compatible action/state representations (kinematic retargeting, contact-aware embeddings).
Policy learning: use reconstructed demonstrations to supervise or initialize robot policies (imitation/RL + sim-to-real transfer) for multi-finger manipulation and grasping.
infographic.impact: Makes dexterous manipulation learning far more scalable and cost-effective by tapping abundant RGB video data, reducing reliance on wearable devices or specialized sensors and accelerating research and deployment of multi-finger robotic hands.

title: ArcFlow: Unleashing 2-Step Text-to-Image Generation via High-Precision Non-Linear Flow Distillation
authors: Zihan Yang, Shuyuan Tu, Licheng Zhang, Qi Dai, Yu-Gang Jiang
abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable generation quality, but they suffer from significant inference cost due to their reliance on multiple sequential denoising steps, motivating recent efforts to distill this inference process into a few-step regime. However, existing distillation methods typically approximate the teacher trajectory by using linear shortcuts, which makes it difficult to match its constantly changing tangent directions as velocities evolve across timesteps, thereby leading t

infographic.key_insight: ArcFlow shows that distilling diffusion teachers into a 2-step text-to-image generator is possible by learning a high-precision non-linear flow that follows the teacher's changing trajectory and tangent directions instead of using crude linear shortcuts.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the high inference cost of diffusion models by addressing the mismatch caused by linear shortcut distillation methods, enabling very few (2) denoising steps while preserving generation quality.
method: Non-Linear Flow Distillation: learn a smooth, high-precision non-linear mapping (flow) that tracks the teacher diffusion trajectory and its evolving tangent/velocity vectors rather than approximating with linear shortcuts.
2-Step Student Design: parametrize a compact 2-step generator that uses the distilled flow to perform two high-fidelity denoising steps conditioned on text, effectively bridging large timestep gaps.

Teacher–Student Coupling & Losses: train with objectives that align trajectories, velocities (tangent directions), and perceptual/image quality (e.g., reconstruction and feature-level losses) to preserve fidelity in very low-step regimes.
infographic.impact: Enables practical, low-latency text-to-image generation with diffusion-quality outputs using only two steps, making deployment and interactive applications (web, mobile, real-time) much more feasible for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Trajectory diagram: teacher diffusion path (curved) vs. linear shortcut vs. learned non-linear flow (closer match) with tangent vectors shown.

title: Visual language models show widespread visual deficits on neuropsychological tests
authors: Gene Tangtartharakul, Katherine R. Storrs
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 06 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01179-y

Tangtartharakul and Storrs use standardized neuropsychological tests to compare human visual abilities with those of visual language models (VLMs). They report that while VLMs excel in high-level object recognition, they show deficits in low- and mid-level visual abilities.

infographic.key_insight: Visual language models match or exceed humans on high-level object recognition but show widespread deficits on standardized low- and mid-level neuropsychological vision tests, revealing a fundamental mismatch with human visual abilities.
infographic.problem_solved: Evaluates whether current VLMs possess foundational visual processing skills (low- and mid-level vision) beyond object recognition, exposing overlooked weaknesses that standard benchmarks miss.
method: Applied a battery of standardized neuropsychological visual tests spanning low-, mid-, and high-level tasks to multiple state-of-the-art VLMs.
Compared model performance to human normative data and analyzed error patterns to localize deficits (e.g., contrast, spatial frequency, contour integration).
Reported systematic failures in low-/mid-level tasks despite strong performance on high-level object recognition benchmarks.
infographic.impact: Shows that high-level benchmarks can mask critical low-level failures; practitioners should adopt multi-scale, neuropsychology-inspired evaluations to improve robustness, interpretability, and real-world reliability of vision systems.
visual_elements: Bar chart: human vs VLM performance grouped by visual level (low, mid, high)

title: InftyThink+: Effective and Efficient Infinite-Horizon Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yuchen Yan, Liang Jiang, Jin Jiang, Shuaicheng Li, Zujie Wen
abstract: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance by scaling inference-time chain-of-thought, but this paradigm suffers from quadratic cost, context length limits, and degraded reasoning due to lost-in-the-middle effects. Iterative reasoning mitigates these issues by periodically summarizing intermediate thoughts, yet existing methods rely on supervised learning or fixed heuristics and fail to optimize when to summarize, what to preserve, and how to resume reasoning. We propose InftyThink+, an e

infographic.key_insight: InftyThink+ uses reinforcement learning to adaptively manage iterative chain-of-thought reasoning, learning when to summarize, what to keep, and how to resume so models can reason indefinitely with far lower cost and less degradation.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the quadratic cost, context-length limits, and "lost-in-the-middle" degradation of scaled chain-of-thought inference by replacing fixed or supervised summarization heuristics with an RL-driven, memory-aware control policy.
method: Train an RL controller that decides when to compress intermediate thoughts, what content to store in a compact memory, and how to resume reasoning from summaries.
Use a learnable summarization/compression module to produce compact, relevant memory entries and a resumption strategy that integrates preserved context with ongoing chain-of-thought.
Optimize a reward balancing final-answer accuracy and computational/memory cost to enable long-horizon, efficient reasoning.
infographic.impact: Enables LLMs to perform long, iterative reasoning with much lower compute and reduced degradation, making reliable multi-step inference practical for resource-constrained or long-context applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input → iterative reasoning loop → RL controller (decide summarize/resume) → compressed memory → resumed reasoning
Timeline illustration: long chain-of-thought with periodic summaries vs. naive expanding context (showing cost growth and lost-in-the-middle)

title: Authorization of prognostic AI medical devices
authors: Urs J. Muehlematter, Kerstin Noelle Vokinger
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 06 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01171-y

Less than 2% of artificial intelligence devices authorized by the US Food and Drug Agency are prognostic, with prediction horizons ranging from minutes to several years. As the number of prognostic AI devices could increase, it is important to address the accompanying regulatory and ethical challenges.

infographic.key_insight: Fewer than 2% of FDA-authorized AI medical devices are prognostic, with prediction horizons spanning minutes to years, highlighting a substantial gap and emerging regulatory/ethical concerns as prognostic tools expand.
infographic.problem_solved: Identifies and quantifies the scarcity of prognostic AI devices among FDA approvals and clarifies the regulatory and ethical challenges that must be addressed as prognostic AI becomes more common.
method: Systematic analysis of FDA-authorized AI/ML medical devices to identify and categorize prognostic tools
Characterization of prediction horizons (minutes to years) and mapping of device use-cases
Assessment of regulatory and ethical implications based on device features and existing approval pathways
infographic.impact: Alerts AI/ML practitioners and developers that prognostic models are underrepresented in approvals and that design, validation, and deployment must proactively address regulatory pathways and ethical issues (e.g., prognostic uncertainty, patient autonomy, downstream interventions).

title: Agentic Uncertainty Reveals Agentic Overconfidence
authors: Jean Kaddour, Srijan Patel, Gbètondji Dovonon, Leo Richter, Pasquale Minervini
abstract: Can AI agents predict whether they will succeed at a task? We study agentic uncertainty by eliciting success probability estimates before, during, and after task execution. All results exhibit agentic overconfidence: some agents that succeed only 22% of the time predict 77% success. Counterintuitively, pre-execution assessment with strictly less information tends to yield better discrimination than standard post-execution review, though differences are not always significant. Adversarial prompti

infographic.key_insight: Eliciting agents' self-predicted success probabilities before, during, and after tasks reveals systematic agentic overconfidence: some agents that only succeed 22% of the time predict 77% success. Surprisingly, coarser pre-execution estimates sometimes discriminate success better than detailed post-execution reviews.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses whether AI agents can accurately predict their own task success (agentic uncertainty) and quantifies miscalibration and overconfidence across different interrogation timings and informational conditions.
method: Elicit success probability estimates from agents at three timepoints: pre-execution, during execution, and post-execution.
Compare predicted probabilities to actual outcomes across tasks and agents to measure calibration, discrimination, and systematic biases (e.g., overconfidence).
Analyze the effect of information content and prompting (including adversarial prompts) on estimates to understand when and why agentic uncertainty appears.
infographic.impact: Reveals that deployed agents can be highly overconfident, which has implications for reliability, risk assessment, and human–AI decision workflows. Simple changes in when and how we ask agents for confidence can improve predictive usefulness and trust.
visual_elements: Calibration plot: predicted success probability vs. actual success rate highlighting extreme overconfidence (e.g., predicted 77% vs actual 22%).

title: Attributing and situating knowledge cannot be left to language models
authors: Roxana Radu, Luc Rocher
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 06 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01193-0

Attributing and situating knowledge cannot be left to language models

infographic.key_insight: Large language models cannot reliably attribute sources or situate knowledge by themselves; accurate provenance and contextualization require dedicated system designs, external metadata, and human oversight.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the risk that LMs will be trusted with presenting knowledge without reliable attribution or context, leading to hallucinations, misattribution, and misuse of model output.
method: Systematic analysis of where and how LMs fail to provide reliable source attribution and contextual framing for generated knowledge.
Articulation of principles and requirements for attribution and situating (e.g., provenance metadata, retrieval-based grounding, uncertainty quantification).
Recommendations for architectures and governance: augment LMs with verifiable retrieval, structured provenance layers, and human-in-the-loop validation.
infographic.impact: Guides practitioners to build accountable, trustworthy AI systems by treating attribution and contextualization as engineering and governance problems rather than capabilities to be delegated to LMs alone; reduces risk of misinformation and legal/ethical harms.

title: Identifying spatial single-cell-level interactions with graph transformer
authors: Xiangzheng Cheng, Suoqin Jin
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 06 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01191-2

Identifying cell–cell interactions from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics suffers from limited gene panels. A new self-supervised graph transformer-based method can resolve spatial single-cell-level interactions without requiring known ligand–receptor pairs.

infographic.key_insight: A self-supervised graph transformer can infer spatial, single-cell–level interactions directly from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data, overcoming limited gene panels and without needing known ligand–receptor pairs.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing methods for detecting cell–cell interactions rely on large gene panels or curated ligand–receptor lists, which are unavailable or incomplete in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics—this method infers interactions despite those limitations.
method: Build a spatial graph where nodes = imaged single cells and edges capture local neighborhood relationships.
Train a graph transformer with self-supervised objectives to learn cell representations and interaction scores from spatial and limited-expression signals (no LR priors required).
Use learned attention/interaction outputs to identify and localize putative cell–cell interactions at single-cell resolution.
infographic.impact: Provides a generalizable, label-free approach for extracting interaction networks from sparse spatial transcriptomic data, enabling AI/ML practitioners to apply transformer-based graph models for biological discovery and downstream analyses without curated ligand–receptor annotations.

title: CineScene: Implicit 3D as Effective Scene Representation for Cinematic Video Generation
authors: Kaiyi Huang, Yukun Huang, Yu Li, Jianhong Bai, Xintao Wang
abstract: Cinematic video production requires control over scene-subject composition and camera movement, but live-action shooting remains costly due to the need for constructing physical sets. To address this, we introduce the task of cinematic video generation with decoupled scene context: given multiple images of a static environment, the goal is to synthesize high-quality videos featuring dynamic subject while preserving the underlying scene consistency and following a user-specified camera trajectory

infographic.key_insight: An implicit 3D representation of a static environment can be used as a stable scene backbone to generate high-quality cinematic videos with dynamic subjects and user-specified camera trajectories, keeping scene consistency while enabling flexible camera motion.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the cost and complexity of live-action cinematic production by enabling controllable video synthesis from a few images of a static scene, decoupling scene context from subject motion and camera movement.
method: Build an implicit 3D representation of the static environment from multiple input images (scene backbone).
Decouple the scene from dynamic subject generation and condition subject appearance/motion on a user-specified camera trajectory.
Render view-consistent, photorealistic frames that preserve scene geometry and appearance while animating the subject and camera.
infographic.impact: Enables controllable, cost-effective virtual production and content creation workflows by allowing practitioners to synthesize cinematic sequences grounded in real environments, useful for film previsualization, VFX, and dataset generation.

title: DreamDojo: A Generalist Robot World Model from Large-Scale Human Videos
authors: Shenyuan Gao, William Liang, Kaiyuan Zheng, Ayaan Malik, Seonghyeon Ye
abstract: Being able to simulate the outcomes of actions in varied environments will revolutionize the development of generalist agents at scale. However, modeling these world dynamics, especially for dexterous robotics tasks, poses significant challenges due to limited data coverage and scarce action labels. As an endeavor towards this end, we introduce DreamDojo, a foundation world model that learns diverse interactions and dexterous controls from 44k hours of egocentric human videos. Our data mixture r

infographic.key_insight: DreamDojo learns a generalist robot world model by training on 44k hours of egocentric human videos, enabling simulation of diverse interactions and dexterous controls with little to no dense robot action labeling.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of robot interaction data and action labels for building reliable world dynamics models—particularly for dexterous manipulation—by leveraging large-scale human video priors to predict action outcomes across varied environments.
method: Assemble a large, diverse mixture of egocentric human videos (≈44k hours) as priors for interaction dynamics and affordances.
Train a self-supervised, action‑conditioned world model that infers/control signals and predicts future visual states from video observations with weak or inferred action supervision.
Adapt the learned world model to robotic control/planning—using imagined rollouts and policy optimization—to enable dexterous task execution without dense task-specific robot data.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable route to build generalist robot simulators and planners by reusing abundant human video data, reducing dependence on costly robot demonstrations and improving transfer to diverse manipulation tasks.

title: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models
authors: Alex McKenzie, Keenan Pepper, Stijn Servaes, Martin Leitgab, Murat Cubuktepe
abstract: Large language models can resist task-misaligned activation steering during inference, sometimes recovering mid-generation to produce improved responses even when steering remains active. We term this Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR). Using sparse autoencoder (SAE) latents to steer model activations, we find that Llama-3.3-70B shows substantial ESR, while smaller models from the Llama-3 and Gemma-2 families exhibit the phenomenon less frequently. We identify 26 SAE latents that activate diff

infographic.key_insight: Large language models can internally resist externally applied activation steering during inference — a phenomenon called Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR). Llama-3.3-70B shows substantial ESR while smaller Llama-3 and Gemma-2 family models exhibit it less frequently.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the surprising unreliability of activation-steering interventions: models can recover mid-generation toward task-aligned outputs even while steering remains active, undermining assumptions about steerability and intervention effectiveness.
method: Apply sparse autoencoder (SAE) latent vectors to steer model activations during inference and observe behavioral effects.
Compare model responses across families and sizes (e.g., Llama-3.3-70B vs smaller Llama-3 and Gemma-2 variants) to quantify ESR prevalence.
Identify and analyze SAE latents that correlate with resistance and locate where in the model internal recovery emerges.
infographic.impact: Practitioners should not assume activation steering will always control model behavior; ESR implies steering can be transiently bypassed, so robustness, evaluation protocols, and steering strategies must account for model-size-dependent endogenous resistance.

title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
authors: Grace Luo, Jiahai Feng, Trevor Darrell, Alec Radford, Jacob Steinhardt
abstract: Existing approaches for analyzing neural network activations, such as PCA and sparse autoencoders, rely on strong structural assumptions. Generative models offer an alternative: they can uncover structure without such assumptions and act as priors that improve intervention fidelity. We explore this direction by training diffusion models on one billion residual stream activations, creating "meta-models" that learn the distribution of a network's internal states. We find that diffusion loss decrea

infographic.key_insight: Training a generative diffusion "meta-model" on a large corpus of LLM residual-stream activations lets you learn the true distribution of internal states, enabling structure discovery and higher‑fidelity interventions without strong structural assumptions.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing activation-analysis tools (e.g., PCA, sparse autoencoders) impose rigid assumptions and provide weak priors for interventions; this paper addresses the need for a flexible, generative prior that models activations directly and improves analysis and intervention fidelity.
method: Collect large-scale residual-stream activations from an LLM (≈1 billion activations) and train diffusion-based generative models to learn the distribution of those internal states.
Use the trained diffusion meta-model for tasks such as reconstruction, sampling, and counterfactual interventions in activation space, treating the model as a learned prior over activations.
Compare behavior and intervention fidelity against standard baselines (e.g., PCA, sparse autoencoders) to evaluate the meta-model's utility for interpretability and control.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, assumption-light tool for probing, sampling, and intervening in LLM internal representations—improving interpretability, more reliable causal interventions, and tooling for debugging and safety research.

title: MedMO: Grounding and Understanding Multimodal Large Language Model for Medical Images
authors: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Adinath Madhavrao Dukre, Eran Segal, Salman Khan
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have rapidly advanced, yet their adoption in medicine remains limited by gaps in domain coverage, modality alignment, and grounded reasoning. In this work, we introduce MedMO, a medical foundation model built upon a generalized MLLM architecture and trained exclusively on large-scale, domain-specific data. MedMO follows a multi-stage training recipe: (i) cross-modal pretraining to align heterogeneous visual encoders with a medical language backbone; (ii)

infographic.key_insight: Training a generalized multimodal LLM exclusively on large-scale, domain-specific medical data and a staged alignment recipe produces a model that better grounds language to medical images and improves clinically relevant reasoning and understanding.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses limited adoption of MLLMs in medicine by closing gaps in domain coverage, modality alignment (visual ↔ language), and grounded clinical reasoning for medical images.
method: Multi-stage training: cross-modal pretraining to align heterogeneous medical visual encoders with a medical language backbone.
Domain-focused fine-tuning and instruction tuning on large-scale medical image–text pairs to impart clinical knowledge and grounded reasoning.
Evaluation and grounding steps to ensure alignment between image findings and language outputs on diagnostic and interpretive clinical tasks.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable foundation model design tailored for medical imaging, enabling more accurate, grounded multimodal clinical assistants and research tools while reducing domain mismatch risks.

title: DAWN: Dependency-Aware Fast Inference for Diffusion LLMs
authors: Lizhuo Luo, Zhuoran Shi, Jiajun Luo, Zhi Wang, Shen Ren
abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have shown advantages in text generation, particularly due to their inherent ability for parallel decoding. However, constrained by the quality--speed trade-off, existing inference solutions adopt conservative parallel strategies, leaving substantial efficiency potential underexplored. A core challenge is that parallel decoding assumes each position can be filled independently, but tokens are often semantically coupled. Thus, the correct choice at one posi

infographic.key_insight: DAWN enables much faster inference for diffusion-based LLMs by explicitly modeling token dependencies and using that information to run safe, aggressive parallel decoding without sacrificing generation quality.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing diffusion LLM inference treats positions as independent and therefore uses overly conservative parallel strategies; this wastes latency headroom because semantically coupled tokens cause quality degradation when decoded independently.
method: Extract cross-token dependency signals (e.g., attention/interaction metrics or learned dependency predictors) to build a lightweight dependency graph over positions.
Use the graph to form dependency-aware groups and an adaptive scheduling policy that parallelizes independent positions while sequentially refining tightly coupled ones.
Apply selective refinement steps and confidence/uncertainty checks so the model preserves output quality while reducing overall decoding iterations.
infographic.impact: DAWN unlocks practical speedups for diffusion LLMs, making their parallel-decoding advantages usable in latency-sensitive applications and large-scale deployment without trading off generation quality.

title: InterPrior: Scaling Generative Control for Physics-Based Human-Object Interactions
authors: Sirui Xu, Samuel Schulter, Morteza Ziyadi, Xialin He, Xiaohan Fei
abstract: Humans rarely plan whole-body interactions with objects at the level of explicit whole-body movements. High-level intentions, such as affordance, define the goal, while coordinated balance, contact, and manipulation can emerge naturally from underlying physical and motor priors. Scaling such priors is key to enabling humanoids to compose and generalize loco-manipulation skills across diverse contexts while maintaining physically coherent whole-body coordination. To this end, we introduce InterPr

infographic.key_insight: InterPrior introduces a scalable generative prior that lets high-level intentions (e.g., affordances) drive physically coherent whole-body human–object interactions, allowing balance, contact, and manipulation to emerge rather than be explicitly planned.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-level task intentions and low-level physically plausible whole-body motions by scaling motor and physics priors so humanoid agents can compose and generalize loco‑manipulation skills across diverse contexts.
method: Learn a large-scale generative prior over whole-body dynamics and contact-conditioned motor behavior from interaction data (simulation and/or real).
Condition the generative controller on high-level affordances/intention inputs to produce contact-aware, balanced trajectories rather than hand-crafted motion plans.
Use compact latent or hierarchical representations to scale the prior for compositional control and generalization across objects, tasks, and environments.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to build humanoid controllers that require less explicit motion engineering, generalize better to new objects and contexts, and produce physically plausible interactions—accelerating development of robust embodied agents and robot manipulation systems.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Large Language Models for PTSD Severity Estimation: The Role of Contextual Knowledge and Modeling Strategies
authors: Panagiotis Kaliosis, Adithya V Ganesan, Oscar N. E. Kjell, Whitney Ringwald, Scott Feltman
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used in a zero-shot fashion to assess mental health conditions, yet we have limited knowledge on what factors affect their accuracy. In this study, we utilize a clinical dataset of natural language narratives and self-reported PTSD severity scores from 1,437 individuals to comprehensively evaluate the performance of 11 state-of-the-art LLMs. To understand the factors affecting accuracy, we systematically varied (i) contextual knowledge like sub

infographic.key_insight: LLMs can estimate PTSD severity from natural-language narratives, but their accuracy depends strongly on available contextual knowledge and the modeling/prompting strategies used; providing the right context and design choices meaningfully improves performance.
infographic.problem_solved: Clarifies which factors (contextual information and modeling choices) influence the reliability of zero-shot LLM-based PTSD severity estimation, addressing uncertainty about when and how to trust these models in clinical-text settings.
method: Compiled a clinical dataset of 1,437 natural-language trauma narratives paired with self-reported PTSD severity scores.
Evaluated 11 state-of-the-art LLMs in a zero-shot setting and compared outputs against ground-truth severity.
Systematically varied contextual knowledge (e.g., available clinical/demographic cues) and modeling strategies (prompt templates, response scoring/mapping) to quantify effects on accuracy.
infographic.impact: Provides actionable evidence for AI/ML practitioners to prioritize contextual features and careful prompt/scoring design when adapting LLMs for mental health assessment, and highlights limits of off-the-shelf zero-shot use in clinical contexts.

title: V-Retrver: Evidence-Driven Agentic Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval
authors: Dongyang Chen, Chaoyang Wang, Dezhao SU, Xi Xiao, Zeyu Zhang
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have recently been applied to universal multimodal retrieval, where Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning improves candidate reranking. However, existing approaches remain largely language-driven, relying on static visual encodings and lacking the ability to actively verify fine-grained visual evidence, which often leads to speculative reasoning in visually ambiguous cases. We propose V-Retrver, an evidence-driven retrieval framework that reformulates multimod

infographic.key_insight: V-Retrver adds an agentic, evidence-driven verification loop to multimodal retrieval: the model actively extracts and checks fine-grained visual evidence during reasoning, reducing speculative Chain-of-Thought and improving reranking reliability.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing MLLM-based retrieval methods rely on static visual encodings and language-only CoT, which can produce speculative or incorrect reranking in visually ambiguous cases; V-Retrver enables active visual verification to ground decisions in concrete evidence.
method: Agentic evidence acquisition: the system selects image regions or formulates focused visual queries to extract fine-grained evidence instead of using only global/static encodings.
Iterative evidence-driven reasoning: integrate retrieved visual evidence into an agentic Chain-of-Thought loop that verifies, refines, or rejects hypotheses about candidate matches.
Evidence-aware reranking: use the outcome of verification steps to score and rerank retrieval candidates, prioritizing those supported by concrete visual evidence.
infographic.impact: Grounding multimodal retrieval in verifiable visual evidence yields more reliable, interpretable reranking—beneficial for search, VQA, and any vision–language application that needs precise, trustworthy retrieval.

title: MambaVF: State Space Model for Efficient Video Fusion
authors: Zixiang Zhao, Yukun Cui, Lilun Deng, Haowen Bai, Haotong Qin
abstract: Video fusion is a fundamental technique in various video processing tasks. However, existing video fusion methods heavily rely on optical flow estimation and feature warping, resulting in severe computational overhead and limited scalability. This paper presents MambaVF, an efficient video fusion framework based on state space models (SSMs) that performs temporal modeling without explicit motion estimation. First, by reformulating video fusion as a sequential state update process, MambaVF captur

infographic.key_insight: Replace costly optical-flow + warping pipelines with a state-space model (SSM) that treats video fusion as a sequential state update, enabling temporal fusion without explicit motion estimation.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing video fusion methods rely on optical flow and feature warping, which are computationally expensive and hard to scale for long sequences or real-time use.
method: Reformulate video fusion as a sequential state update process so temporal context is modeled as an evolving hidden state.
Use state-space models (SSMs) to capture long-range temporal dependencies efficiently, removing the need for optical flow estimation and feature warping.
Design an inference pipeline that updates and decodes the fusion state per frame, yielding lower compute and better scalability for longer videos.
infographic.impact: MambaVF reduces computation and latency for video fusion tasks, making high-quality temporal fusion practical for real-time systems and large-scale deployments without costly motion estimation.

title: Context Forcing: Consistent Autoregressive Video Generation with Long Context
authors: Shuo Chen, Cong Wei, Sun Sun, Ping Nie, Kai Zhou
abstract: Recent approaches to real-time long video generation typically employ streaming tuning strategies, attempting to train a long-context student using a short-context (memoryless) teacher. In these frameworks, the student performs long rollouts but receives supervision from a teacher limited to short 5-second windows. This structural discrepancy creates a critical \textbf{student-teacher mismatch}: the teacher's inability to access long-term history prevents it from guiding the student on global te

infographic.key_insight: Introduce "Context Forcing": a training strategy that closes the student–teacher gap in streaming tuning by aligning the teacher's supervision with the student's long-context rollouts, producing more temporally consistent autoregressive video generation.
infographic.problem_solved: Streaming tuning methods train long-context video generators using short-window (memoryless) teachers, creating a student–teacher mismatch that causes temporal drift, incoherence, and failures over long rollouts.
method: Context Forcing — modify supervision so the teacher's guidance is conditioned or augmented to reflect long-term history, aligning the teacher's view with the student's rollout context.
Introduce consistency/alignment objectives between teacher outputs and long autoregressive student rollouts to preserve global temporal structure during streaming tuning.
Design lightweight, memory-aware training/conditioning mechanisms that enable real-time long-context generation without prohibitive compute or latency.
infographic.impact: Enables more reliable, temporally coherent long-video generation in autoregressive models, improving real-time streaming and long-rollout applications (e.g., simulation, video assistants, content creation) for practitioners.

title: CommCP: Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination via LLM-Based Communication with Conformal Prediction
authors: Xiaopan Zhang, Zejin Wang, Zhixu Li, Jianpeng Yao, Jiachen Li
abstract: To complete assignments provided by humans in natural language, robots must interpret commands, generate and answer relevant questions for scene understanding, and manipulate target objects. Real-world deployments often require multiple heterogeneous robots with different manipulation capabilities to handle different assignments cooperatively. Beyond the need for specialized manipulation skills, effective information gathering is important in completing these assignments. To address this compone

infographic.key_insight: Combining LLM-driven natural-language communication with conformal prediction lets heterogeneous robots coordinate more efficiently by only exchanging high-confidence, task-relevant messages—reducing bandwidth and improving reliability.
infographic.problem_solved: Enables robust multi-robot coordination for complex, language-specified assignments where agents must gather information, ask/answer scene questions, and allocate manipulation tasks under limited or noisy communication.
method: Use LLMs to generate & interpret natural-language plans, questions, and answers for scene understanding and task allocation across heterogeneous agents.
Apply conformal prediction to produce calibrated confidence scores for LLM outputs and filter/flag low-confidence messages before transmission or execution.
Design a lightweight communication protocol that transmits concise, high-confidence assertions and targeted queries to minimize bandwidth and reduce erroneous actions.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical framework for deploying LLM-enabled multi-robot systems in real-world, bandwidth-constrained settings—improving coordination efficiency and safety by making communication selective and uncertainty-aware.

title: Multi-Token Prediction via Self-Distillation
authors: John Kirchenbauer, Abhimanyu Hans, Brian Bartoldson, Micah Goldblum, Ashwinee Panda
abstract: Existing techniques for accelerating language model inference, such as speculative decoding, require training auxiliary speculator models and building and deploying complex inference pipelines. We consider a new approach for converting a pretrained autoregressive language model from a slow single next token prediction model into a fast standalone multi-token prediction model using a simple online distillation objective. The final model retains the exact same implementation as the pretrained init

infographic.key_insight: A pretrained autoregressive language model can be converted into a fast standalone multi-token predictor by training it with a simple online self-distillation objective, removing the need for auxiliary speculator models or complex inference pipelines.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces autoregressive generation latency and deployment complexity by enabling a single pretrained model to predict multiple future tokens per forward pass without adding extra models or changing the runtime implementation.
method: Initialize from a pretrained autoregressive LM and keep the same model architecture and runtime.
Apply an online self-distillation loss that teaches the model to predict multiple future tokens (multi-token prediction) using its own next-token outputs as targets.
Train the model end-to-end so the final model can generate several tokens per step, enabling faster standalone inference without auxiliary speculators or complex pipelines.
infographic.impact: Simplifies production deployment and speeds up text generation by converting existing pretrained LMs into efficient multi-token generators while preserving the original implementation and avoiding extra models.

title: Shared LoRA Subspaces for almost Strict Continual Learning
authors: Prakhar Kaushik, Ankit Vaidya, Shravan Chaudhari, Rama Chellappa, Alan Yuille
abstract: Adapting large pretrained models to new tasks efficiently and continually is crucial for real-world deployment but remains challenging due to catastrophic forgetting and the high cost of retraining. While parameter-efficient tuning methods like low rank adaptation (LoRA) reduce computational demands, they lack mechanisms for strict continual learning and knowledge integration, without relying on data replay, or multiple adapters. We propose Share, a novel approach to parameter efficient continua

infographic.key_insight: A single shared low-rank LoRA subspace can be incrementally adapted so new tasks are learned with task-specific low-dimensional coefficients, enabling almost-strict continual learning without replay or multiple adapters while keeping parameter cost low.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces catastrophic forgetting and the computational/storage burden of adapting large pretrained models to many sequential tasks, removing the need for data replay or a separate adapter per task.
method: Learn a shared low-rank LoRA subspace and represent each task by compact coefficients projected into that subspace instead of training independent adapters.
Adaptively expand or refine the shared subspace only when necessary and apply constraints (e.g., orthogonality/regularization) to protect previously acquired knowledge and reduce interference.
Keep a single adapter plus small task embeddings, minimizing extra parameters and compute for continual adaptation without replay.
infographic.impact: Makes continual adaptation of large models practical and lightweight for real-world systems—lowering storage, compute and management overhead while preserving task performance across long sequences of tasks.

title: Thinking with Geometry: Active Geometry Integration for Spatial Reasoning
authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Tao Tang, Kun Xiang, Zihan Guo
abstract: Recent progress in spatial reasoning with Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly leverages geometric priors from 3D encoders. However, most existing integration strategies remain passive: geometry is exposed as a global stream and fused in an indiscriminate manner, which often induces semantic-geometry misalignment and redundant signals. We propose GeoThinker, a framework that shifts the paradigm from passive fusion to active perception. Instead of feature mixing, GeoThinker enabl

infographic.key_insight: GeoThinker shifts 3D geometry use in MLLMs from passive global fusion to active, task-driven perception—letting the model query and align geometric information selectively to reduce semantic-geometry misalignment and redundant signals.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing approaches fuse global geometric priors indiscriminately, causing semantic-geometry misalignment, noise, and inefficiency for spatial reasoning tasks in multimodal LLMs.
method: Active perception controller: the model issues targeted geometry queries (e.g., locations, viewpoints, primitives) instead of ingesting a monolithic geometry stream.
Localized geometry encoding + alignment: the 3D encoder returns task-relevant, localized geometric features that are selectively aligned with language semantics rather than blindly mixed.
Iterative feedback loop: language-driven queries guide further geometric sampling/attention, forming a closed-loop integration that improves relevance and reduces redundancy.
infographic.impact: By integrating geometry actively, GeoThinker improves spatial reasoning accuracy and efficiency, making MLLMs more reliable for 3D-aware tasks (e.g., navigation, manipulation, scene understanding) while reducing unnecessary compute and noisy signals.

title: Mechanisms of AI Protein Folding in ESMFold
authors: Kevin Lu, Jannik Brinkmann, Stefan Huber, Aaron Mueller, Yonatan Belinkov
abstract: How do protein structure prediction models fold proteins? We investigate this question by tracing how ESMFold folds a beta hairpin, a prevalent structural motif. Through counterfactual interventions on model latents, we identify two computational stages in the folding trunk. In the first stage, early blocks initialize pairwise biochemical signals: residue identities and associated biochemical features such as charge flow from sequence representations into pairwise representations. In the second

infographic.key_insight: ESMFold folds a beta hairpin via two computational stages: early transformer blocks initialize pairwise biochemical signals (residue identity and charge flow) from sequence representations, and later blocks consolidate those signals into the final structural predictions.
infographic.problem_solved: Explains how internal computations of a state‑of‑the‑art protein folding model generate and transform biochemical signals to produce 3D structure, improving interpretability of model mechanisms.
method: Trace folding of a prototypical motif (beta hairpin) through ESMFold’s transformer layers.
Apply counterfactual interventions on model latents to test causal roles of representations (e.g., altering sequence-derived features and observing pairwise representation changes).
Layer‑wise analysis to identify two-stage computation: initialization of pairwise biochemical features in early blocks and subsequent refinement/consolidation in later blocks.
infographic.impact: Clarifies internal mechanisms of large protein folding models, enabling practitioners to better diagnose, trust, and guide model design (e.g., targeted interventions, architecture choices, or incorporating biochemical priors).

title: AP-OOD: Attention Pooling for Out-of-Distribution Detection
authors: Claus Hofmann, Christian Huber, Bernhard Lehner, Daniel Klotz, Sepp Hochreiter
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, which maps high-dimensional data into a scalar OOD score, is critical for the reliable deployment of machine learning models. A key challenge in recent research is how to effectively leverage and aggregate token embeddings from language models to obtain the OOD score. In this work, we propose AP-OOD, a novel OOD detection method for natural language that goes beyond simple average-based aggregation by exploiting token-level information. AP-OOD is a semi-super

infographic.key_insight: AP-OOD uses learned attention-based pooling over token embeddings to produce a single, more informative OOD score for natural language inputs, outperforming naive average pooling by leveraging token-level signals.
infographic.problem_solved: How to effectively aggregate token-level representations from language models into a single scalar OOD score, so models can better detect out-of-distribution text.
method: Introduce an attention-pooling module that weights token embeddings before aggregation, emphasizing tokens that signal distributional shift.
Train the pooling mechanism in a semi-supervised setup (leveraging available in-distribution data and limited supervision) to produce a calibrated scalar OOD score.
Apply the method on top of pretrained language-model embeddings, replacing simple average/max pooling for improved OOD sensitivity.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a plug-in approach to improve OOD detection for NLP systems with minimal changes to existing pipelines, increasing safety and reliability when deployed in the wild.

title: SwimBird: Eliciting Switchable Reasoning Mode in Hybrid Autoregressive MLLMs
authors: Jintao Tong, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Kunyu Shi
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have made remarkable progress in multimodal perception and reasoning by bridging vision and language. However, most existing MLLMs perform reasoning primarily with textual CoT, which limits their effectiveness on vision-intensive tasks. Recent approaches inject a fixed number of continuous hidden states as "visual thoughts" into the reasoning process and improve visual performance, but often at the cost of degraded text-based logical reasoning. We argue t

infographic.key_insight: SwimBird enables multimodal LLMs to dynamically switch between textual Chain-of-Thought and visual latent ‘thoughts’, improving vision-heavy reasoning without degrading text-based logical reasoning.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing MLLMs either rely mainly on textual CoT (weak for vision-intensive tasks) or inject fixed visual latents (which can harm text reasoning); SwimBird addresses the need for an adaptive, switchable reasoning mode in hybrid autoregressive MLLMs.
method: Hybrid autoregressive backbone that natively supports both token-based textual reasoning and continuous visual latent states.
A lightweight switchable reasoning mechanism (e.g., learned mode tokens/gating or attention control) that toggles when to use textual CoT versus injected visual thoughts during decoding.
Training and prompting strategy that mixes text-only and vision-text examples so the model preserves strong logical text reasoning while activating visual reasoning only when needed.
infographic.impact: Allows practitioners to deploy a single MLLM that adapts its internal reasoning style to task demands, improving performance on vision-intensive tasks without sacrificing language-based logic — simplifying model design and reducing the need for task-specific fine-tuning.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing hybrid autoregressive flow with a mode switch (textual CoT path vs. visual latent path).

title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
authors: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Tao Feng, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao
abstract: Memory is increasingly central to Large Language Model (LLM) agents operating beyond a single context window, yet most existing systems rely on offline, query-agnostic memory construction that can be inefficient and may discard query-critical information. Although runtime memory utilization is a natural alternative, prior work often incurs substantial overhead and offers limited explicit control over the performance-cost trade-off. In this work, we present \textbf{BudgetMem}, a runtime agent mem

infographic.key_insight: BudgetMem lets an LLM agent decide at runtime which memory items to use or store by routing queries through cost-aware memory tiers, preserving query-critical information while explicitly controlling latency/cost trade-offs.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses inefficient, offline and query-agnostic memory construction for LLM agents that can discard information important to specific queries and lacks explicit control over runtime cost vs. performance.
method: Introduce a budget-tier routing architecture that partitions memory into cost/latency tiers (e.g., short-term, mid-term, long-term) and dynamically routes queries to the appropriate tier.
Use a lightweight query-aware scoring/policy module at runtime to assess informativeness and retrieval/storage value for each memory item under current budget constraints.
Enforce an explicit budget controller that allocates retrieval/storage effort per query, providing a tunable knob for the performance–cost trade-off without heavy offline preprocessing.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to deploy memory-augmented LLM agents that retain query-relevant context while meeting latency and compute budgets; useful for production systems requiring predictable cost and flexible accuracy. It enables fine-grained control over memory use and reduces waste from blanket offline memory construction.

title: Subliminal Effects in Your Data: A General Mechanism via Log-Linearity
authors: Ishaq Aden-Ali, Noah Golowich, Allen Liu, Abhishek Shetty, Ankur Moitra
abstract: Training modern large language models (LLMs) has become a veritable smorgasbord of algorithms and datasets designed to elicit particular behaviors, making it critical to develop techniques to understand the effects of datasets on the model's properties. This is exacerbated by recent experiments that show datasets can transmit signals that are not directly observable from individual datapoints, posing a conceptual challenge for dataset-centric understandings of LLM training and suggesting a missi

infographic.key_insight: The paper identifies a general 'log-linearity' mechanism by which aggregate dataset statistics can imprint covert (“subliminal”) signals onto trained models, causing systematic behaviors that are not visible from any single datapoint.
infographic.problem_solved: Explains and formalizes how datasets can transmit hidden signals that affect model behavior, addressing the gap in our ability to detect, predict, and reason about dataset-driven effects beyond per-example inspection.
method: Formalize a log-linear generative mechanism that shows how aggregated features in data can produce predictable model responses even when individual examples lack obvious signals.
Derive theoretical conditions and scaling laws that predict when and how these subliminal signals emerge during training.
Validate predictions via experiments and dataset interventions (synthetic and real) that demonstrate measurable changes in model behavior and provide simple auditing/mitigation strategies.
infographic.impact: Helps practitioners and researchers detect and mitigate hidden dataset-driven behaviors, improving dataset auditing, model reliability, and safety; informs principled dataset design and interventions to prevent unexpected model properties.
