title: Jointly modeling cardiovascular biomarkers
authors: Sully F. Chen
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 21 January 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01172-x

Capturing the complexity of cardiovascular dynamics demands multiple monitoring modalities, each with inherent trade-offs. Diffusion-based modeling offers a promising route for synthesizing and generating cross-modal data.

infographic.key_insight: A conditional diffusion framework that jointly models multiple cardiovascular biomarkers, enabling realistic cross-modal synthesis and imputation while preserving physiological relationships across signals.
infographic.problem_solved: Integrates heterogeneous cardiovascular monitoring modalities (different sampling rates, noise profiles, and missing channels) by learning their joint distribution so models can generate or impute missing modalities without large matched multimodal datasets.
method: Multivariate conditional diffusion model that learns the joint distribution of multiple cardiovascular biomarkers rather than separate unimodal generators.
Cross-modal conditioning and a shared latent representation to enable synthesis, imputation, and modality translation across signals with variable timing and missing channels.
Physiological-consistency constraints and task-aware training (e.g., downstream prediction or cycle-consistency) to keep synthesized signals clinically plausible and useful.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical route for robust data augmentation, cross-modal imputation, and simulation in cardiovascular ML, lowering data-collection burdens and improving model generalization and downstream clinical utility.

title: DrivIng: A Large-Scale Multimodal Driving Dataset with Full Digital Twin Integration
authors: Dominik Rößle, Xujun Xie, Adithya Mohan, Venkatesh Thirugnana Sambandham, Daniel Cremers
abstract: Perception is a cornerstone of autonomous driving, enabling vehicles to understand their surroundings and make safe, reliable decisions. Developing robust perception algorithms requires large-scale, high-quality datasets that cover diverse driving conditions and support thorough evaluation. Existing datasets often lack a high-fidelity digital twin, limiting systematic testing, edge-case simulation, sensor modification, and sim-to-real evaluations. To address this gap, we present DrivIng, a large

infographic.key_insight: DrivIng couples a large-scale, multimodal real-world driving dataset with a high-fidelity digital twin, enabling controlled, repeatable simulation and direct sim-to-real evaluations for perception systems.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing driving datasets lack full digital-twin fidelity, which prevents systematic edge-case generation, sensor-ablation studies, and reliable sim-to-real validation of perception algorithms.
method: Collect large-scale, synchronized multimodal data (cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS/IMU) with rich metadata and dense annotations.
Construct a full digital twin: photorealistic scene reconstruction, dynamic actor modeling, and precise programmable sensor models for replay and perturbation.
Provide annotation/benchmark suites and tooling to run controlled experiments (edge-case injection, sensor modification, sim-to-real transfer evaluations).
infographic.impact: DrivIng lets AI/ML practitioners run reproducible, high-fidelity experiments to stress-test perception models, perform sensor- and condition-level ablations, and accelerate safe sim-to-real deployment of autonomous-driving systems.

title: HALT: Hallucination Assessment via Latent Testing
authors: Rohan Bhatnagar, Youran Sun, Chi Andrew Zhang, Yixin Wen, Haizhao Yang
abstract: Hallucination in large language models (LLMs) can be understood as a failure of faithful readout: although internal representations may encode uncertainty about a query, decoding pressures still yield a fluent answer. We propose lightweight residual probes that read hallucination risk directly from intermediate hidden states of question tokens, motivated by the hypothesis that these layers retain epistemic signals that are attenuated in the final decoding stage. The probe is a small auxiliary ne

infographic.key_insight: Hallucination risk can be detected directly in intermediate hidden states of LLMs: lightweight residual probes read epistemic signals from question-token representations that are attenuated by final decoding, enabling early, model-agnostic assessment of when a model is likely to hallucinate.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing methods detect hallucinations only after fluent (but potentially false) outputs are generated or require expensive external verification. This paper provides a lightweight way to assess hallucination risk from internal activations before or during decoding.
method: Attach small residual probes to intermediate layers to read question-token hidden states and predict per-query/per-token hallucination risk.
Use a training signal linking hidden-state patterns to known hallucination labels (latent testing) so probes learn epistemic uncertainty encoded in intermediate representations.
Operate as a low-overhead, model-agnostic monitoring tool that can be run during inference to flag risky outputs for verification or abstention.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical, low-cost technique to detect and mitigate hallucination risk earlier in the generation pipeline, improving safety, calibration, and routing decisions without modifying the base model.

Layer-wise heatmap illustrating where epistemic signals are strongest and how they decay toward final decoding.

title: APEX-Agents
authors: Bertie Vidgen, Austin Mann, Abby Fennelly, John Wright Stanly, Lucas Rothman
abstract: We introduce the AI Productivity Index for Agents (APEX-Agents), a benchmark for assessing whether AI agents can execute long-horizon, cross-application tasks created by investment banking analysts, management consultants, and corporate lawyers. APEX-Agents requires agents to navigate realistic work environments with files and tools. We test eight agents for the leaderboard using Pass@1. Gemini 3 Flash (Thinking=High) achieves the highest score of 24.0%, followed by GPT-5.2 (Thinking=High), Clau

infographic.key_insight: APEX-Agents introduces a realistic productivity benchmark for AI agents and shows that even top models struggle on long-horizon, cross-application workplace tasks—Gemini 3 Flash (Thinking=High) achieves the top Pass@1 of 24.0%.
infographic.problem_solved: Provides a standardized way to evaluate whether AI agents can reliably execute complex, multi-step tasks across files and tools typical of investment banking, consulting, and corporate law workflows.
method: Design a benchmark (APEX-Agents) composed of long-horizon, cross-application tasks authored by domain experts (bankers, consultants, lawyers).
Place agents in realistic work environments with files and interactive tools and measure end-to-end task success using Pass@1.
Run a leaderboard evaluation of eight agents to compare real-world productivity capabilities and surface failure modes.
infographic.impact: APEX-Agents shifts agent evaluation toward realistic workplace utility, enabling practitioners to compare models on end-to-end task execution and prioritize improvements in reliability, tool use, and long-horizon planning.

title: Motion 3-to-4: 3D Motion Reconstruction for 4D Synthesis
authors: Hongyuan Chen, Xingyu Chen, Youjia Zhang, Zexiang Xu, Anpei Chen
abstract: We present Motion 3-to-4, a feed-forward framework for synthesising high-quality 4D dynamic objects from a single monocular video and an optional 3D reference mesh. While recent advances have significantly improved 2D, video, and 3D content generation, 4D synthesis remains difficult due to limited training data and the inherent ambiguity of recovering geometry and motion from a monocular viewpoint. Motion 3-to-4 addresses these challenges by decomposing 4D synthesis into static 3D shape generati

infographic.key_insight: Motion 3-to-4 is a feed-forward framework that reconstructs high-quality 4D (time-varying 3D) objects from a single monocular video (and an optional 3D reference mesh) by explicitly separating static shape from dynamic motion, enabling accurate geometry and motion recovery despite limited data and monocular ambiguity.
infographic.problem_solved: Recovers both detailed 3D geometry and temporally coherent motion from a single-view video input — a task made difficult by limited 4D training data and inherent depth/motion ambiguity in monocular capture.
method: Decompose 4D synthesis into static 3D shape reconstruction and dynamic motion estimation so each subtask is easier to solve robustly in a feed-forward pass.
Optionally condition on a provided 3D reference mesh to anchor geometry; otherwise infer a high-quality static shape from the video.
Use temporal consistency and motion-aware neural representations to produce coherent 4D outputs (time-indexed meshes or neural fields) suitable for rendering and animation.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to generate temporally coherent 3D animations from simple monocular videos, lowering the barrier for 4D content creation in AR/VR, VFX, and robotics without large multi-view datasets.

title: OmniTransfer: All-in-one Framework for Spatio-temporal Video Transfer
authors: Pengze Zhang, Yanze Wu, Mengtian Li, Xu Bai, Songtao Zhao
abstract: Videos convey richer information than images or text, capturing both spatial and temporal dynamics. However, most existing video customization methods rely on reference images or task-specific temporal priors, failing to fully exploit the rich spatio-temporal information inherent in videos, thereby limiting flexibility and generalization in video generation. To address these limitations, we propose OmniTransfer, a unified framework for spatio-temporal video transfer. It leverages multi-view info

infographic.key_insight: OmniTransfer is a unified framework that transfers and leverages rich spatio-temporal information from videos—rather than relying on static reference images or fixed temporal priors—enabling more flexible and general video customization and generation.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing video customization methods under-utilize inherent spatio-temporal cues and depend on image-based references or task-specific temporal priors, limiting flexibility, temporal coherence, and generalization across diverse video tasks.
method: Extract multi-view spatio-temporal representations that jointly capture spatial appearance and temporal dynamics from input videos.
Use a single, modular transfer module to adapt and inject learned spatio-temporal features into target generation or editing models, avoiding task-specific priors.
Optimize with objectives that preserve spatial fidelity and temporal consistency so transferred content remains coherent across frames.
infographic.impact: OmniTransfer simplifies and strengthens video customization pipelines by providing a general-purpose way to reuse spatio-temporal knowledge, improving temporal coherence and enabling broader generalization for video generation, editing, and transfer tasks.

title: Rig-Aware 3D Reconstruction of Vehicle Undercarriages using Gaussian Splatting
authors: Nitin Kulkarni, Akhil Devarashetti, Charlie Cluss, Livio Forte, Dan Buckmaster
abstract: Inspecting the undercarriage of used vehicles is a labor-intensive task that requires inspectors to crouch or crawl underneath each vehicle to thoroughly examine it. Additionally, online buyers rarely see undercarriage photos. We present an end-to-end pipeline that utilizes a three-camera rig to capture videos of the undercarriage as the vehicle drives over it, and produces an interactive 3D model of the undercarriage. The 3D model enables inspectors and customers to rotate, zoom, and slice thro

infographic.key_insight: A rig-aware pipeline that combines calibrated three-camera video capture with Gaussian splatting produces fast, high-fidelity interactive 3D models of vehicle undercarriages from drive-over footage.
infographic.problem_solved: Automates and democratizes undercarriage inspection by removing the need for manual crouching/crawling and adding rich 3D views for inspectors and online buyers where undercarriage photos are rarely available.
method: Three-camera rig captures synchronized video as vehicles drive over a fixed imaging rig; rig geometry and motion are explicitly modeled for robust multi-view alignment.
Calibrate poses and fuse frames into a dense representation using Gaussian splatting to reconstruct a high-quality, renderable 3D undercarriage model.
Produce an interactive viewer that supports rotating, zooming, and slicing/cross-section inspection for detailed visual assessment.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, scalable solution for automated vehicle inspection and e-commerce transparency; demonstrates how rig-aware calibration + Gaussian splatting can deliver fast, high-quality 3D reconstructions from constrained, real-world capture setups.

abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will produce unprecedented volumes of heterogeneous astronomical data (images, catalogs, and alerts) that challenge traditional analysis pipelines. The LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC) aims to derive robust constraints on dark energy and dark matter from these data, requiring methods that are statistically powerful, scalable, and operationally reliable. Artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) are alr

infographic.key_insight: AI/ML methods are essential to extract robust dark‑energy and dark‑matter constraints from LSST's unprecedented, heterogeneous data; targeted investments in scalable, uncertainty‑aware, and operationally robust ML will unlock LSST's scientific potential.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses how to analyze extremely large, heterogeneous LSST datasets (images, catalogs, alerts) while controlling statistical and systematic uncertainties, meeting scalability and real‑time operational requirements for cosmological inference.
method: Survey and prioritize AI/ML opportunities (classification, anomaly detection, simulation‑based inference, surrogate modeling, domain adaptation) aligned to DESC science goals.
Advocate practical research & engineering: uncertainty quantification, interpretability, robust calibration with simulated training data, benchmarking and reproducible pipelines.

title: InT: Self-Proposed Interventions Enable Credit Assignment in LLM Reasoning
authors: Matthew Y. R. Yang, Hao Bai, Ian Wu, Gene Yang, Amrith Setlur
abstract: Outcome-reward reinforcement learning (RL) has proven effective at improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, standard RL assigns credit only at the level of the final answer, penalizing entire reasoning traces when the outcome is incorrect and uniformly reinforcing all steps when it is correct. As a result, correct intermediate steps may be discouraged in failed traces, while spurious steps may be reinforced in successful ones. We refer to this failure mode a

infographic.key_insight: Allowing an LLM to generate and test its own small interventions on intermediate reasoning steps produces counterfactual outcomes that enable fine-grained credit assignment, improving learning of correct substeps instead of only rewarding final answers.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard outcome-level RL treats entire reasoning traces as wholly rewarded or penalized, which penalizes correct intermediate steps in failed traces and reinforces spurious steps in successful ones; this paper fixes coarse credit assignment in LLM chain-of-thought reasoning.
method: Self-proposed interventions: the model proposes alternative edits to intermediate reasoning steps (counterfactuals) and rolls out consequences to observe changes in final outcomes.
Use outcome differences from these counterfactual rollouts to attribute credit/blame to specific steps and apply targeted updates (rather than uniform reward at the final answer).
Integrate with outcome-reward RL to reinforce verified causal substeps and suppress spurious ones, improving sample efficiency and reasoning robustness.
infographic.impact: Enables more accurate and sample-efficient improvement of multi-step LLM reasoning by rewarding the right substeps. Practitioners can train models that learn reliable intermediate reasoning rather than overfitting to final-answer shortcuts.

title: Which Reasoning Trajectories Teach Students to Reason Better? A Simple Metric of Informative Alignment
authors: Yuming Yang, Mingyoung Lai, Wanxu Zhao, Xiaoran Fan, Zhiheng Xi
abstract: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) trajectories provide rich supervision signals for distilling reasoning from teacher to student LLMs. However, both prior work and our experiments show that trajectories from stronger teachers do not necessarily yield better students, highlighting the importance of data-student suitability in distillation. Existing methods assess suitability primarily through student likelihood, favoring trajectories that closely align with the model's current behavior but overlooking

infographic.key_insight: Stronger teacher reasoning traces don’t always produce better student reasoners; instead, selecting trajectories by how informatively they align with a student model better predicts which examples will teach the student to reason. The paper proposes a simple "informative alignment" metric to quantify this suitability.
infographic.problem_solved: Distillation of chain-of-thought reasoning from teacher to student LLMs often fails because existing selection criteria (e.g., student likelihood) prefer trajectories that merely match the student's current behavior rather than ones that drive learning; this work addresses how to choose trajectories that actually improve student reasoning.
method: Define a simple informative-alignment metric that captures how a teacher trajectory both aligns with and adds learning signal relative to the student.
Score and rank teacher CoT trajectories using this metric instead of relying solely on student likelihood or teacher strength.
Select high-scoring trajectories for distillation and validate that these choices better predict student learning outcomes (empirical evaluation).
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, data-driven way to choose reasoning trajectories for distillation, improving efficiency and effectiveness of teaching student LLMs without requiring larger or stronger teachers. Practitioners can get better student reasoning by prioritizing informative alignment over raw teacher quality.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Teacher trajectories → Informative alignment metric → Selected trajectories → Student model (distillation pipeline).
Bar chart: Comparison of student performance when trained on (a) strongest-teacher trajectories vs (b) informative-alignment-selected trajectories.

title: VideoMaMa: Mask-Guided Video Matting via Generative Prior
authors: Sangbeom Lim, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Heeji Yoon, Seungryong Kim
abstract: Generalizing video matting models to real-world videos remains a significant challenge due to the scarcity of labeled data. To address this, we present Video Mask-to-Matte Model (VideoMaMa) that converts coarse segmentation masks into pixel accurate alpha mattes, by leveraging pretrained video diffusion models. VideoMaMa demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization to real-world footage, even though it is trained solely on synthetic data. Building on this capability, we develop a scalable pseudo

infographic.key_insight: VideoMaMa leverages pretrained video diffusion models as a generative prior to convert coarse segmentation masks into pixel-accurate alpha mattes, achieving strong zero-shot generalization to real-world videos despite training only on synthetic data.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces reliance on scarce, expensive per-frame matting annotations by enabling accurate video matting from coarse segmentation masks and bridging the synthetic-to-real gap.
method: Use a pretrained video diffusion model as a generative prior to refine coarse mask inputs into high-quality alpha mattes.
Train the VideoMaMa model exclusively on synthetic data while designing the pipeline to preserve temporal consistency across frames.
Leverage the model's generative prior to scale to real-world footage (authors build a scalable pseudo-labeling/expansion strategy based on this capability).
infographic.impact: Allows practitioners to perform high-quality video matting on real-world content without large-scale manual matte labels, lowering annotation cost and enabling scalable foreground extraction for VFX, AR, and video editing workflows.

title: Jet-RL: Enabling On-Policy FP8 Reinforcement Learning with Unified Training and Rollout Precision Flow
authors: Haocheng Xi, Charlie Ruan, Peiyuan Liao, Yujun Lin, Han Cai
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is essential for enhancing the complex reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL training pipelines are computationally inefficient and resource-intensive, with the rollout phase accounting for over 70% of total training time. Quantized RL training, particularly using FP8 precision, offers a promising approach to mitigating this bottleneck. A commonly adopted strategy applies FP8 precision during rollout while retaining BF16 precisio

infographic.key_insight: Jet-RL enables end-to-end on-policy RL in FP8 by unifying precision across rollout and training paths, preserving numerical stability while dramatically reducing rollout compute and memory overhead.
infographic.problem_solved: Rollout dominates on-policy RL training time and cost, and existing pipelines that mix FP8 rollouts with higher-precision training introduce data movement, conversion overhead, and numerical instability—blocking efficient, large-scale RL for LLMs.
method: Unified precision flow: apply FP8 consistently across rollout and training to eliminate frequent precision conversions and streamline data paths.

Numerical stabilization: use calibrated scaling and quantization-aware techniques (e.g., dynamic scaling, variance-aware quantization/loss scaling) to retain on-policy training fidelity in low precision.
System and kernel co-design: optimize memory layout and compute kernels to exploit FP8 hardware efficiently and accelerate rollout throughput without degrading policy performance.
infographic.impact: Makes on-policy RL far more compute- and memory-efficient, enabling faster iteration, lower cost, and wider adoption of RL fine-tuning for LLMs and other large models while maintaining training stability and policy quality.

title: Attention-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning and Clustering for Interpretable Sepsis Treatment
authors: Punit Kumar, Vaibhav Saran, Divyesh Patel, Nitin Kulkarni, Alina Vereshchaka
abstract: Sepsis remains one of the leading causes of mortality in intensive care units, where timely and accurate treatment decisions can significantly impact patient outcomes. In this work, we propose an interpretable decision support framework. Our system integrates four core components: (1) a clustering-based stratification module that categorizes patients into low, intermediate, and high-risk groups upon ICU admission, using clustering with statistical validation; (2) a synthetic data augmentation pi

infographic.key_insight: Combines clustering-based risk stratification, synthetic data augmentation, and attention-guided offline reinforcement learning to produce interpretable, risk-aware sepsis treatment recommendations; attention scores provide per-patient feature/time importance for transparency.
infographic.problem_solved: Learning reliable, interpretable treatment policies from scarce, biased retrospective ICU data and heterogeneous patient presentations — enabling risk-tailored decision support without online experimentation.
method: Clustering-based stratification at ICU admission to assign patients into low / intermediate / high-risk cohorts with statistical validation.
Synthetic data augmentation to reduce class imbalance and expand coverage of treatment trajectories for offline learning.
Attention-based offline reinforcement learning that derives treatment policies from historical data while exposing attention weights for interpretable, patient-specific rationale.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical pipeline for AI/ML practitioners to build safer, more transparent sepsis decision-support models from electronic health records, improving trust and enabling targeted interventions by risk group.

title: Deep Learning Approaches to Quantum Error Mitigation
authors: Leonardo Placidi, Ifan Williams, Enrico Rinaldi, Daniel Mills, Cristina Cîrstoiu
abstract: We present a systematic investigation of deep learning methods applied to quantum error mitigation of noisy output probability distributions from measured quantum circuits. We compare different architectures, from fully connected neural networks to transformers, and we test different design/training modalities, identifying sequence-to-sequence, attention-based models as the most effective on our datasets. These models consistently produce mitigated distributions that are closer to the ideal outp

infographic.key_insight: Sequence-to-sequence, attention-based deep models (transformer-like) are the most effective at mapping noisy measured quantum-circuit output distributions to mitigated distributions that are closer to the ideal.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces noise-induced errors in probability distributions obtained from measured quantum circuits, improving the fidelity of classical estimates derived from near-term noisy quantum hardware.
method: Compare a range of architectures (from fully connected networks to transformers) and multiple design/training modalities on datasets of noisy vs. ideal output distributions.
Train models to take noisy measured distributions as input and predict mitigated (closer-to-ideal) output distributions.
Identify sequence-to-sequence attention-based models as consistently superior on the tested datasets.
infographic.impact: Offers a practical classical post-processing method for near-term quantum devices, enabling AI/ML practitioners to obtain higher-fidelity outputs for quantum experiments and downstream quantum-enhanced workflows.

title: MetaboNet: The Largest Publicly Available Consolidated Dataset for Type 1 Diabetes Management
authors: Miriam K. Wolff, Peter Calhoun, Eleonora Maria Aiello, Yao Qin, Sam F. Royston
abstract: Progress in Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) algorithm development is limited by the fragmentation and lack of standardization across existing T1D management datasets. Current datasets differ substantially in structure and are time-consuming to access and process, which impedes data integration and reduces the comparability and generalizability of algorithmic developments. This work aims to establish a unified and accessible data resource for T1D algorithm development. Multiple publicly available T1D datas

infographic.key_insight: MetaboNet consolidates multiple public Type 1 Diabetes datasets into the largest standardized, easy-to-use resource to accelerate fair, comparable algorithm development for T1D management.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing T1D datasets are fragmented, inconsistent in format and annotation, and time-consuming to integrate, which hampers reproducibility, benchmarking, and generalization of AI models.
method: Aggregate publicly available T1D datasets and map them to a unified schema with consistent timestamps, variable names, units, and clinical labels.
Apply standardized preprocessing and quality-control pipelines (missing data handling, alignment of sensor/insulin/nutrition signals, provenance metadata) to produce analysis-ready cohorts.
Provide documentation and tooling for easy access, reproducible splits, and interoperable formats to enable benchmarking and downstream ML workflows.
infographic.impact: By removing data wrangling barriers and providing a single, well-documented resource, MetaboNet enables faster, more reproducible development and fair comparison of T1D management algorithms across research groups.

title: Learning Semantic-Geometric Task Graph-Representations from Human Demonstrations
authors: Franziska Herbert, Vignesh Prasad, Han Liu, Dorothea Koert, Georgia Chalvatzaki
abstract: Learning structured task representations from human demonstrations is essential for understanding long-horizon manipulation behaviors, particularly in bimanual settings where action ordering, object involvement, and interaction geometry can vary significantly. A key challenge lies in jointly capturing the discrete semantic structure of tasks and the temporal evolution of object-centric geometric relations in a form that supports reasoning over task progression. In this work, we introduce a seman

infographic.key_insight: A joint semantic–geometric task-graph representation can be learned from human demonstrations to simultaneously capture discrete task structure (which actions/objects are involved) and the temporal evolution of object-centric geometric relations, enabling reasoning over long-horizon, bimanual manipulation tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of modeling both the discrete semantic structure of tasks (step ordering, object involvement) and the continuous, time-varying geometric relations between objects and manipulators in human demonstrations—crucial for accurate segmentation, prediction, and planning in complex bimanual interactions.
method: Construct a task graph with semantic nodes (actions/subtasks, objects) and edges encoding time-varying geometric relations between object-centric entities.
Train a temporal graph-based model (e.g., GNN + temporal encoder) on human demonstrations to embed both semantic labels and evolving spatial relations.
Use the learned representation for downstream reasoning: segmentation of demonstrations, prediction of next steps/relations, and task-conditioned planning or transfer.
infographic.impact: Provides a compact, interpretable representation that helps robots generalize and reason about long-horizon bimanual behaviors from humans—improving demo-driven learning, planning, and human–robot collaboration in manipulation tasks.

title: MHA2MLA-VLM: Enabling DeepSeek's Economical Multi-Head Latent Attention across Vision-Language Models
authors: Xiaoran Fan, Zhichao Sun, Tao Ji, Lixing Shen, Tao Gui
abstract: As vision-language models (VLMs) tackle increasingly complex and multimodal tasks, the rapid growth of Key-Value (KV) cache imposes significant memory and computational bottlenecks during inference. While Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) offers an effective means to compress the KV cache and accelerate inference, adapting existing VLMs to the MLA architecture without costly pretraining remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present MHA2MLA-VLM, a parameter-efficient and multimodal-aware f

infographic.key_insight: A lightweight, multimodal-aware conversion lets existing vision–language models replace bulky multi-head Key-Value caches with compact Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), achieving large memory and latency savings without costly pretraining.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the exploding KV-cache memory and inference-time compute in VLMs when handling long or multimodal contexts, enabling practical deployment and faster inference.
method: Introduce a parameter-efficient MHA→MLA adaptation that maps existing Multi-Head Attention KV structures into a compact latent-attention representation.
Use small multimodal-aware adapter/projection modules and alignment objectives so models can be converted with minimal fine-tuning rather than full pretraining.
Design conversion and inference routines that maintain cross-modal fidelity while drastically reducing KV storage and attention computation.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to deploy VLMs with much lower memory footprint and faster inference (longer contexts, lower latency) using only lightweight fine-tuning—reducing cost and making multimodal applications more scalable.

title: Extractive summarization on a CMOS Ising machine
authors: Ziqing Zeng, Abhimanyu Kumar, Chris H. Kim, Ulya R. Karpuzcu, Sachin S. Sapatnekar
abstract: Extractive summarization (ES) aims to generate a concise summary by selecting a subset of sentences from a document while maximizing relevance and minimizing redundancy. Although modern ES systems achieve high accuracy using powerful neural models, their deployment typically relies on CPU or GPU infrastructures that are energy-intensive and poorly suited for real-time inference in resource-constrained environments. In this work, we explore the feasibility of implementing McDonald-style extractiv

infographic.key_insight: Extractive summarization can be formulated as a combinatorial (Ising/QUBO) optimization and efficiently executed on a CMOS Ising machine, enabling low‑power, low‑latency sentence selection without large CPU/GPU costs.
infographic.problem_solved: Modern extractive summarization models are accurate but rely on energy‑hungry CPUs/GPUs, making real‑time inference in resource‑constrained environments impractical; this work shows a hardware‑efficient alternative.
method: Map the McDonald-style extractive summarization objective (maximize relevance, minimize redundancy) to a QUBO/Ising formulation where binary spin variables represent sentence selection.
Implement and solve the Ising model on a CMOS Ising machine (specialized hardware for combinatorial optimization) to perform fast, low‑power inference.
Compare solution quality and system metrics (accuracy vs. redundancy tradeoff, energy, latency) against conventional CPU/GPU baselines to validate feasibility.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical path to deploy extractive summarization in energy- and latency‑sensitive settings (edge devices, real‑time services) and demonstrates the viability of specialized Ising hardware for combinatorial NLP tasks.

title: ReScene4D: Temporally Consistent Semantic Instance Segmentation of Evolving Indoor 3D Scenes
authors: Emily Steiner, Jianhao Zheng, Henry Howard-Jenkins, Chris Xie, Iro Armeni
abstract: Indoor environments evolve as objects move, appear, or disappear. Capturing these dynamics requires maintaining temporally consistent instance identities across intermittently captured 3D scans, even when changes are unobserved. We introduce and formalize the task of temporally sparse 4D indoor semantic instance segmentation (SIS), which jointly segments, identifies, and temporally associates object instances. This setting poses a challenge for existing 3DSIS methods, which require a discrete ma

infographic.key_insight: ReScene4D defines and benchmarks temporally sparse 4D semantic instance segmentation: maintaining consistent object instance identities across intermittently captured indoor 3D scans, even when objects move, appear, or disappear between observations.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of joint segmentation, identification, and long-range temporal association of object instances in evolving indoor scenes captured intermittently, where changes can be unobserved for extended intervals and standard 3D SIS methods fail to preserve identity consistency.
method: Formalize the temporally sparse 4D SIS task and introduce ReScene4D — a benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol tailored for intermittent captures and evolving indoor scenes.

Design a temporally-aware pipeline that combines robust per-scan 3D instance segmentation with a long-range association module (spatio-temporal features, matching, and memory) to link instances across gaps and occlusions.
Introduce evaluation metrics and baselines to measure semantic accuracy and identity consistency over time, emphasizing robustness to appearance/disappearance and sparse sampling.
infographic.impact: Provides a standardized task, dataset, and evaluation for temporally consistent instance-level scene understanding, enabling improvements in long-term 3D perception for robotics, AR/VR, and multi-view mapping where intermittent captures and scene dynamics are common.

authors: Kaiwen Wang, Kaili Zheng, Rongrong Deng, Qingmin Fan, Milin Zhang
abstract: Competitive sports require sophisticated tactical analysis, yet combat disciplines like boxing remain underdeveloped in AI-driven analytics due to the complexity of action dynamics and the lack of structured tactical representations. To address this, we present BoxMind, a closed-loop AI expert system validated in elite boxing competition. By defining atomic punch events with precise temporal boundaries and spatial and technical attributes, we parse match footage into 18 hierarchical technical-ta

infographic.key_insight: BoxMind introduces a precise, hierarchical representation of boxing actions (atomic punch events with temporal, spatial and technical attributes) and uses a closed-loop AI system to optimize and validate in elite competition at the 2024 Olympics.
infographic.problem_solved: Combat sports lack structured, interpretable spatiotemporal representations and closed-loop strategy systems that can turn raw match footage into actionable tactical insights for elite boxing.
method: Define atomic punch events with exact temporal boundaries plus spatial and technical attributes, and organize them into an 18-node hierarchical technical–tactical taxonomy.
Automatically parse match video into the hierarchical event stream (detection + attribute classification) to produce an interpretable tactical trace.
Use a closed-loop optimization pipeline that ingests parsed traces to recommend and evaluate strategy adjustments, validated on elite-level (2024 Olympics) competition data.

title: Generative Scenario Rollouts for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
authors: Rajeev Yasarla, Deepti Hegde, Shizhong Han, Hsin-Pai Cheng, Yunxiao Shi
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are emerging as highly effective planning models for end-to-end autonomous driving systems. However, current works mostly rely on imitation learning from sparse trajectory annotations and under-utilize their potential as generative models. We propose Generative Scenario Rollouts (GeRo), a plug-and-play framework for VLA models that jointly performs planning and generation of language-grounded future traffic scenes through an autoregressive rollout strategy. Fi

infographic.key_insight: GeRo converts Vision–Language–Action models into generative planners by using autoregressive, language-grounded rollouts that jointly predict future traffic scenes and driving actions, enabling multi-step scenario generation and planning.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes reliance on sparse trajectory imitation and the under-utilization of VLA models' generative potential, which limits robust planning, interpretability, and scalable scenario/data generation for end-to-end autonomous driving.
method: Plug-and-play GeRo wrapper for VLA models that augments them with generation capabilities while preserving existing planning interfaces.
Autoregressive rollout strategy: iteratively generate language-grounded future scene descriptions and corresponding actions to produce multi-step scenario rollouts.
Use generated rollouts as interpretable predictions and synthetic scenarios for training, evaluation, and robust planning.
infographic.impact: Provides richer supervision and interpretable planning signals, enabling scalable synthetic scenario generation and improved robustness/data-efficiency for researchers and engineers building end-to-end driving systems.

title: UniX: Unifying Autoregression and Diffusion for Chest X-Ray Understanding and Generation
authors: Ruiheng Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Huangxuan Zhao, Hao Yan, Xiao He
abstract: Despite recent progress, medical foundation models still struggle to unify visual understanding and generation, as these tasks have inherently conflicting goals: semantic abstraction versus pixel-level reconstruction. Existing approaches, typically based on parameter-shared autoregressive architectures, frequently lead to compromised performance in one or both tasks. To address this, we present UniX, a next-generation unified medical foundation model for chest X-ray understanding and generation.

infographic.key_insight: UniX unifies autoregressive semantic modeling and diffusion-based pixel synthesis in a single chest X‑ray foundation model by separating task-specific pathways to avoid the usual trade-off between understanding and generation.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing unified medical models compromise either semantic understanding or pixel-level generation because shared-parameter autoregressive designs force conflicting representations; UniX addresses this by decoupling and coordinating both goals.
method: Hybrid architecture: shared encoder/latent space with two specialized decoders—an autoregressive head for semantic/reporting tasks and a diffusion head for high-fidelity image generation.
Task-aware training: joint optimization with separate objectives and conditioning so each pathway preserves its inductive bias while benefiting from shared representation learning.
Cross-path coordination: lightweight adapters/conditioning modules enable information flow between heads to align semantics and pixels without parameter interference.
infographic.impact: UniX enables a single, deployable medical foundation model that performs both diagnosis-oriented understanding and realistic X‑ray generation well, improving downstream efficiency, data augmentation, and clinical utility for AI/ML practitioners.

title: Health Facility Location in Ethiopia: Leveraging LLMs to Integrate Expert Knowledge into Algorithmic Planning
authors: Yohai Trabelsi, Guojun Xiong, Fentabil Getnet, Stéphane Verguet, Milind Tambe
abstract: Ethiopia's Ministry of Health is upgrading health posts to improve access to essential services, particularly in rural areas. Limited resources, however, require careful prioritization of which facilities to upgrade to maximize population coverage while accounting for diverse expert and stakeholder preferences. In collaboration with the Ethiopian Public Health Institute and Ministry of Health, we propose a hybrid framework that systematically integrates expert knowledge with optimization techniq

infographic.key_insight: A hybrid framework uses large language models to elicit and formalize expert and stakeholder preferences, then integrates those preferences into constrained optimization to prioritize health-post upgrades that maximize population coverage in Ethiopia.
infographic.problem_solved: How to allocate limited resources for upgrading rural health posts so as to maximize access to essential services while systematically incorporating diverse expert and stakeholder preferences and constraints.
method: Use LLMs to elicit, standardize, and encode qualitative expert and stakeholder knowledge (priorities, trade-offs, contextual constraints) into machine-readable preference models.
Combine those encoded preferences with mathematical optimization (coverage-maximization under budget/operational constraints) to generate prioritized upgrade plans and trade-off analyses.
Run scenario and robustness checks to produce interpretable, policy-ready recommendations that reflect stakeholder values and practical constraints.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates a practical, repeatable pattern for integrating human expertise into algorithmic planning via LLMs, improving real-world applicability, interpretability, and stakeholder alignment of ML-driven resource-allocation models.

title: PRISM-CAFO: Prior-conditioned Remote-sensing Infrastructure Segmentation and Mapping for CAFOs
authors: Oishee Bintey Hoque, Nibir Chandra Mandal, Kyle Luong, Amanda Wilson, Samarth Swarup
abstract: Large-scale livestock operations pose significant risks to human health and the environment, while also being vulnerable to threats such as infectious diseases and extreme weather events. As the number of such operations continues to grow, accurate and scalable mapping has become increasingly important. In this work, we present an infrastructure-first, explainable pipeline for identifying and characterizing Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations (CAFOs) from aerial and satellite imagery. Our met

infographic.key_insight: PRISM-CAFO uses an infrastructure-first, prior-conditioned and explainable pipeline to identify and characterize CAFOs from aerial and satellite imagery, enabling accurate, interpretable, and scalable mapping of large livestock operations.
infographic.problem_solved: Provides a reproducible method to detect and map concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) at scale from remote imagery, addressing challenges of accuracy, interpretability, and rapid large-area coverage for environmental and public-health monitoring.
method: Prior-conditioned segmentation: incorporate infrastructure priors (e.g., barns, lagoons, roads) into multi-resolution models to focus detection on CAFO-relevant features.

Explainable aggregation: rule-based and interpretable post-processing links detected infrastructure components into CAFO footprints and derives attribute-level characterizations (size, density, risk proxies).
Scalable pipeline: end-to-end remote-sensing workflow for large-area inference, quality control, and exportable maps suitable for downstream analysis and decision making.
infographic.impact: Shows how domain priors and explainability improve geospatial model utility and trust, offering AI/ML practitioners a transferable approach for facility detection and environmental monitoring that balances performance, interpretability, and scalability.

title: ShapeR: Robust Conditional 3D Shape Generation from Casual Captures
authors: Yawar Siddiqui, Duncan Frost, Samir Aroudj, Armen Avetisyan, Henry Howard-Jenkins
abstract: Recent advances in 3D shape generation have achieved impressive results, but most existing methods rely on clean, unoccluded, and well-segmented inputs. Such conditions are rarely met in real-world scenarios. We present ShapeR, a novel approach for conditional 3D object shape generation from casually captured sequences. Given an image sequence, we leverage off-the-shelf visual-inertial SLAM, 3D detection algorithms, and vision-language models to extract, for each object, a set of sparse SLAM poi

infographic.key_insight: ShapeR enables reliable generation of complete 3D object shapes from casually captured, noisy image sequences by conditioning a generative model on sparse SLAM-derived geometry, multi-view crops, and semantic cues. It is robust to occlusion, incomplete segmentation, and real-world capture artifacts.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between lab-quality 3D reconstruction inputs and real-world casual captures by handling sparse, unsegmented, and occluded observations to produce accurate conditional 3D shapes.
method: Preprocess casual video: use off-the-shelf visual-inertial SLAM, 3D detectors, and vision–language models to extract per-object sparse SLAM points, multi-view image crops, poses, and semantic labels.
Feed these noisy, object-centric cues into a robust conditional 3D generative model that completes and refines full object geometry despite occlusions and segmentation errors.
Train and evaluate the system to prioritize resilience to realistic capture artifacts (sparsity, occlusions, viewpoint gaps) rather than relying on clean, segmented inputs.
infographic.impact: Makes conditional 3D shape generation practical for in-the-wild captures (mobile phones, robotics, AR) by reducing dependence on curated data and brittle preprocessing. Practitioners can integrate ShapeR-style pipelines to get reliable 3D assets from casual scans and noisy sensor streams.

title: Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini
authors: János Kramár, Joshua Engels, Zheng Wang, Bilal Chughtai, Rohin Shah
abstract: Frontier language model capabilities are improving rapidly. We thus need stronger mitigations against bad actors misusing increasingly powerful systems. Prior work has shown that activation probes may be a promising misuse mitigation technique, but we identify a key remaining challenge: probes fail to generalize under important production distribution shifts. In particular, we find that the shift from short-context to long-context inputs is difficult for existing probe architectures. We propose

infographic.key_insight: Activation probes that work on short-context inputs often fail when deployed on long-context, production distributions; with targeted architectural and training changes, probes can be made to generalize across this shift.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridging the generalization gap of activation-based probes when models are evaluated on longer, real-world context lengths than those seen during probe development.
method: Diagnose failure modes by measuring probe performance across short→long context shifts and isolating where representations change.
Design probe architectures and training protocols that are context-length robust (e.g., context-aware pooling, position-invariant features, and augmentation with long-context examples).
Validate on production-like distributions and iterate with regularization/ensemble strategies to reduce false negatives under long-context inputs.
infographic.impact: Makes activation probes reliable for real-world safety and misuse-detection deployments on long-context models (like Gemini), reducing missed detections and improving trustworthiness of runtime monitoring.
visual_elements: Line chart showing probe accuracy vs. input context length (steep drop without fixes, flat/robust with fixes).

title: CURVE: A Benchmark for Cultural and Multilingual Long Video Reasoning
authors: Darshan Singh, Arsha Nagrani, Kawshik Manikantan, Harman Singh, Dinesh Tewari
abstract: Recent advancements in video models have shown tremendous progress, particularly in long video understanding. However, current benchmarks predominantly feature western-centric data and English as the dominant language, introducing significant biases in evaluation. To address this, we introduce CURVE (Cultural Understanding and Reasoning in Video Evaluation), a challenging benchmark for multicultural and multilingual video reasoning. CURVE comprises high-quality, entirely human-generated annotati

infographic.key_insight: CURVE introduces a culturally diverse, multilingual benchmark specifically for long-video reasoning, filling a gap left by western- and English-centric evaluation datasets and enabling more equitable assessment of video models.
infographic.problem_solved: Current long-video benchmarks are biased toward Western contexts and English language, limiting evaluation of models' cultural understanding and multilingual reasoning; CURVE provides high-quality, human-generated annotations spanning diverse cultures and languages to address this gap.
method: Curate a long-video dataset with human-generated annotations emphasizing cultural context and multilingual content.
Define reasoning tasks (e.g., long-range QA, temporal and cultural inference) and standardized evaluation protocols/metrics for fair comparison.
Evaluate common long-video models on CURVE to expose cultural and linguistic failure modes and establish baseline performance.
infographic.impact: CURVE enables practitioners to audit and improve video models for cultural and linguistic robustness, guiding development of fairer, more globally applicable long-video understanding systems.

title: CoMoVi: Co-Generation of 3D Human Motions and Realistic Videos
authors: Chengfeng Zhao, Jiazhi Shu, Yubo Zhao, Tianyu Huang, Jiahao Lu
abstract: In this paper, we find that the generation of 3D human motions and 2D human videos is intrinsically coupled. 3D motions provide the structural prior for plausibility and consistency in videos, while pre-trained video models offer strong generalization capabilities for motions, which necessitate coupling their generation processes. Based on this, we present CoMoVi, a co-generative framework that couples two video diffusion models (VDMs) to generate 3D human motions and videos synchronously within

infographic.key_insight: 3D human motions and 2D human videos are intrinsically coupled, so jointly generating them using coupled video diffusion models yields more plausible, temporally consistent videos and structurally sound motions.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch and inconsistency when 3D motion and 2D video are generated separately — and the difficulty of leveraging pre-trained video models for robust motion generation — by synchronizing their generation processes.
method: Co-generate 3D motions and 2D videos via two coupled video diffusion models (one focused on 3D motion/skeleton, one on photo-realistic video) that exchange conditioning signals.
Perform joint/iterative diffusion sampling with cross-modal conditioning (e.g., cross-attention or shared latent conditioning) to enforce spatial, temporal and structural consistency.
Leverage pre-trained video models for strong generalization while using 3D motion priors to maintain plausible human structure and kinematics.
infographic.impact: Enables generation of realistic, temporally consistent human videos with accurate 3D motion — useful for animation, virtual production, and data augmentation — and provides a practical path to combine large pre-trained video models with structured 3D priors.

title: Single-Stage Huffman Encoder for ML Compression
authors: Aditya Agrawal, Albert Magyar, Hiteshwar Eswaraiah, Patrick Sheridan, Pradeep Janedula
abstract: Training and serving Large Language Models (LLMs) require partitioning data across multiple accelerators, where collective operations are frequently bottlenecked by network bandwidth. Lossless compression using Huffman codes is an effective way to alleviate the issue, however, its three-stage design requiring on-the-fly frequency analysis, codebook generation and transmission of codebook along with data introduces computational, latency and data overheads which are prohibitive for latency-sensit

infographic.key_insight: A single-stage Huffman encoder compresses ML communication in one pass, removing separate frequency analysis and codebook transmission to achieve low-latency, lossless compression for distributed training/serving.
infographic.problem_solved: Eliminates the computational, latency and data overheads of the traditional three-stage Huffman pipeline (frequency analysis → codebook generation → codebook transmission) that make lossless compression impractical for latency-sensitive multi-accelerator ML workloads.
method: Design a single-pass Huffman encoding algorithm that integrates frequency handling and code assignment so encoding happens without an explicit intermediate codebook step.
Implement a streaming / GPU-friendly encoder to minimize CPU work and latency during inter-accelerator collective communication.
Avoid sending a separate codebook by using implicit/shared encoding state or on-the-fly mapping so encoded data can be decoded with minimal coordination.
infographic.impact: Reduces network transfer size, end-to-end latency and CPU/GPU overhead for distributed LLM training and inference, improving throughput and scalability without sacrificing lossless recovery.

title: MatchTIR: Fine-Grained Supervision for Tool-Integrated Reasoning via Bipartite Matching
authors: Changle Qu, Sunhao Dai, Hengyi Cai, Jun Xu, Shuaiqiang Wang
abstract: Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) empowers large language models (LLMs) to tackle complex tasks by interleaving reasoning steps with external tool interactions. However, existing reinforcement learning methods typically rely on outcome- or trajectory-level rewards, assigning uniform advantages to all steps within a trajectory. This coarse-grained credit assignment fails to distinguish effective tool calls from redundant or erroneous ones, particularly in long-horizon multi-turn scenarios. To addre

infographic.key_insight: MatchTIR uses bipartite matching to provide step-level supervision for tool-integrated reasoning, enabling LLMs to distinguish effective tool calls from redundant or erroneous ones during long-horizon multi-turn tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing RL-style training for tool-augmented LLMs applies coarse outcome- or trajectory-level rewards, which fail to assign credit to individual tool calls and hurt performance in complex, multi-step interactions.
method: Frame alignment between model-generated reasoning/tool calls and ground-truth effective steps as a bipartite matching problem to compute fine-grained matches.
Derive step-level supervision/rewards from the matching to preferentially reinforce useful tool calls and penalize redundant or incorrect ones.
Integrate the matching-based supervision into training (reward shaping or supervised fine-tuning) to improve tool usage efficiency in long-horizon, multi-turn tasks.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a principled way to perform granular credit assignment for tool use, improving sample efficiency, reducing unnecessary tool calls, and boosting performance on complex reasoning pipelines.
visual_elements: Bipartite matching diagram: predicted steps/tools on one side, ground-truth effective steps on the other, with matched pairs highlighted and match scores annotated.

title: Multi-Objective Pareto-Front Optimization for Efficient Adaptive VVC Streaming
authors: Angeliki Katsenou, Vignesh V. Menon, Guoda Laurinaviciute, Benjamin Bross, Detlev Marpe
abstract: Adaptive video streaming has facilitated improved video streaming over the past years. A balance among coding performance objectives such as bitrate, video quality, and decoding complexity is required to achieve efficient, content- and codec-dependent, adaptive video streaming. This paper proposes a multi-objective Pareto-front (PF) optimization framework to construct quality-monotonic, content-adaptive bitrate ladders Versatile Video Coding (VVC) streaming that jointly optimize video quality, b

infographic.key_insight: A Pareto-front multi-objective optimization constructs content-adaptive, quality-monotonic bitrate ladders for VVC streaming that jointly trade off bitrate, visual quality, and decoding complexity. This yields more efficient adaptive streaming decisions than single-objective heuristics.
infographic.problem_solved: Adaptive streaming must balance bitrate, perceived quality, and decoder complexity per content and codec; existing ladders are often static or optimize only one metric, causing suboptimal network or device-level performance.
method: Formulate bitrate, video quality (e.g., objective quality metric), and decoding complexity as simultaneous optimization objectives and compute the Pareto front of coding configurations.
Select quality-monotonic, content-adaptive bitrate ladder points from the Pareto front to ensure increasing quality with bitrate while meeting complexity constraints.
Integrate the resulting ladders into VVC streaming workflows so the client/server can make informed adaptation choices under varying bandwidth and device capabilities.
infographic.impact: Enables streaming systems and ML-driven adaptation agents to make principled trade-offs across bitrate, quality, and compute cost—improving user experience and resource efficiency for diverse content and devices.

title: From One-to-One to Many-to-Many: Dynamic Cross-Layer Injection for Deep Vision-Language Fusion
authors: Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Peng Di
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) create a severe visual feature bottleneck by using a crude, asymmetric connection that links only the output of the vision encoder to the input of the large language model (LLM). This static architecture fundamentally limits the ability of LLMs to achieve comprehensive alignment with hierarchical visual knowledge, compromising their capacity to accurately integrate local details with global semantics into coherent reasoning. To resolve this, we introduce Cross-Layer

infographic.key_insight: Replace the static one-to-one link between vision encoder output and LLM input with dynamic many-to-many cross-layer injections so LLMs can access hierarchical visual features (local to global) on demand.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the visual feature bottleneck in current VLMs where a single coarse visual vector limits LLMs' ability to align and reason with multi-scale visual information.
method: Introduce dynamic cross-layer injection modules that connect multiple vision-encoder layers to multiple LLM layers, enabling many-to-many information flow.
Use learned routing/gating (or attention-based selection) to inject relevant multi-level visual features into appropriate LLM layers at inference time.
Keep injectors lightweight and plugin-friendly so the mechanism can be integrated into existing VLMs with modest compute and training overhead.
infographic.impact: Enables richer, hierarchical vision–language alignment improving fine-grained understanding and coherent multimodal reasoning; practical for practitioners wanting stronger VLM performance without redesigning full pipelines.

title: Molmo2: Open Weights and Data for Vision-Language Models with Video Understanding and Grounding
authors: Christopher Clark, Jieyu Zhang, Zixian Ma, Jae Sung Park, Mohammadreza Salehi
abstract: Today's strongest video-language models (VLMs) remain proprietary. The strongest open-weight models either rely on synthetic data from proprietary VLMs, effectively distilling from them, or do not disclose their training data or recipe. As a result, the open-source community lacks the foundations needed to improve on the state-of-the-art video (and image) language models. Crucially, many downstream applications require more than just high-level video understanding; they require grounding -- eith

infographic.key_insight: Molmo2 provides an open-weight, openly documented vision–language model and dataset focused on video understanding and spatial–temporal grounding, closing the gap between proprietary VLMs and the open-source community.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of fully open, reproducible video-language models and training data—existing top open models either distill from proprietary systems or hide their data/recipes, preventing transparent progress on video understanding and grounding.
method: Release of a fully open training stack: published model weights, curated training data, and a reproducible recipe for training video+image language models.

Multi-task training on video and image data combining contrastive alignment, captioning, and explicit grounding/localization objectives to learn both high-level semantics and spatial‑temporal localization.

Model architecture that fuses a video-capable encoder with a grounding head (cross-attention between text and spatio-temporal features) to produce localized predictions (boxes/timestamps) and language outputs.
infographic.impact: Provides a transparent, reproducible foundation for building and evaluating video-language systems with grounding, enabling researchers and practitioners to fine-tune, audit, and extend strong VLMs without relying on proprietary models or hidden data.

title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection
authors: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus
abstract: Recent advances in end-to-end autonomous driving show that policies trained on patch-aligned features extracted from foundation models generalize better to Out-of-Distribution (OOD). We hypothesize that due to the self-attention mechanism, each patch feature implicitly embeds/contains information from all other patches, represented in a different way and intensity, making these descriptors highly redundant. We quantify redundancy in such (BLIP2) features via PCA and cross-patch similarity: $90$%

infographic.key_insight: Stochastically selecting a subset of patch-aligned features from a foundation model (BLIP2) removes heavy redundancy (≈90%) caused by self-attention, and training policies on fewer patches improves out-of-distribution generalization for end-to-end driving — see less, drive better.
infographic.problem_solved: High redundancy in patch-level foundation-model features causes inefficient, overfit end-to-end driving policies that generalize poorly to OOD scenarios; the paper addresses how to reduce redundancy and improve robustness.
method: Quantify redundancy in BLIP2 patch features via PCA and cross-patch similarity (≈90% redundancy observed).
Introduce Stochastic Patch Selection: randomly sample/drop patch-aligned features during training so the policy cannot rely on redundant cross-patch encodings.
Train end-to-end driving policies on reduced patch sets and evaluate on OOD benchmarks to demonstrate improved robustness and efficiency.
infographic.impact: Reducing redundant visual inputs yields more robust, generalizable driving policies and lowers input dimensionality and compute, benefiting practitioners building vision-to-control systems that must operate safely in novel environments.

title: PACEvolve: Enabling Long-Horizon Progress-Aware Consistent Evolution
authors: Minghao Yan, Bo Peng, Benjamin Coleman, Ziqi Chen, Zhouhang Xie
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful operators for evolutionary search, yet the design of efficient search scaffolds remains ad hoc. While promising, current LLM-in-the-loop systems lack a systematic approach to managing the evolutionary process. We identify three distinct failure modes: Context Pollution, where experiment history biases future candidate generation; Mode Collapse, where agents stagnate in local minima due to poor exploration-exploitation balance; and Weak Collab

infographic.key_insight: PACEvolve introduces a systematic, progress-aware scaffold for LLM-driven evolutionary search that mitigates long-horizon failures (context pollution, mode collapse, weak collaboration) to keep evolution consistent and improving over many generations.
infographic.problem_solved: Unreliable and ad-hoc LLM-in-the-loop evolutionary processes that degrade over long horizons due to history biasing, premature convergence, and poor multi-agent coordination.
method: Progress-aware evaluation: score candidates by measured incremental improvement over recent generations to prioritize genuine progress over superficial fitness.
Context management: prune or summarize experiment history and inject controlled context to prevent past trials from biasing new candidate generation.
Diversity & collaboration mechanisms: enforce diversity-preserving operators and lightweight coordination protocols between agent roles to avoid mode collapse and boost exploration.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a principled scaffold to run stable, long-horizon LLM-guided evolutionary search, improving reliability and reproducibility of automated design and optimization workflows.

title: Grounding Agent Memory in Contextual Intent
authors: Ruozhen Yang, Yucheng Jiang, Yueqi Jiang, Priyanka Kargupta, Yunyi Zhang
abstract: Deploying large language models in long-horizon, goal-oriented interactions remains challenging because similar entities and facts recur under different latent goals and constraints, causing memory systems to retrieve context-mismatched evidence. We propose STITCH (Structured Intent Tracking in Contextual History), an agentic memory system that indexes each trajectory step with a structured retrieval cue, contextual intent, and retrieves history by matching the current step's intent. Contextual

infographic.key_insight: STITCH grounds agent memory with a structured "contextual intent" cue so history is retrieved by intent alignment rather than surface similarity, reducing context-mismatched memory recalls in long-horizon, goal-directed interactions.
infographic.problem_solved: Memory systems often return irrelevant past evidence when similar entities or facts recur under different latent goals; this causes agents to act on context-mismatched information during long-horizon tasks.
method: Index every trajectory step with a structured retrieval cue called contextual intent alongside the usual state/action/observation record.
Retrieve past history by matching the current step's contextual intent to stored intents, prioritizing intent alignment over surface-level feature similarity.
Embed STITCH into the agentic memory pipeline so retrieved, intent-matched evidence guides planning and decision-making to avoid misleading memories.
infographic.impact: Makes memory-augmented agents more robust and reliable in long-horizon, goal-oriented settings by reducing retrieval errors caused by repeated entities under different goals—beneficial for planning, assistants, and persistent agents.

title: Multi-Property Synthesis
authors: Christoph Weinhuber, Yannik Schnitzer, Alessandro Abate, David Parker, Giuseppe De Giacomo
abstract: We study LTLf synthesis with multiple properties, where satisfying all properties may be impossible. Instead of enumerating subsets of properties, we compute in one fixed-point computation the relation between product-game states and the goal sets that are realizable from them, and we synthesize strategies achieving maximal realizable sets. We develop a fully symbolic algorithm that introduces Boolean goal variables and exploits monotonicity to represent exponentially many goal combinations comp

infographic.key_insight: Instead of enumerating which subsets of temporal properties are realizable, the paper computes in one symbolic fixed-point pass a relation between product-game states and all realizable goal sets, and synthesizes strategies that achieve maximal realizable sets.
infographic.problem_solved: It addresses LTLf synthesis with multiple, potentially conflicting properties where satisfying them all may be impossible; prior methods required costly enumeration of subsets of properties, leading to exponential blowup and poor scalability.
method: Construct a product game over the system and all LTLf properties and introduce Boolean goal variables that represent which properties are achieved.
Perform a single monotone fixed-point computation that yields, for each product-game state, the set (implicitly represented) of goal combinations realizable from that state.
Synthesize strategies that maximize realizable goal sets using the symbolic representation to avoid explicit enumeration of exponentially many combinations.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable, fully symbolic technique for synthesizing controllers under multiple conflicting temporal objectives, enabling practitioners to obtain optimal trade-off strategies with formal guarantees without combinatorial enumeration.

title: Alterbute: Editing Intrinsic Attributes of Objects in Images
authors: Tal Reiss, Daniel Winter, Matan Cohen, Alex Rav-Acha, Yael Pritch
abstract: We introduce Alterbute, a diffusion-based method for editing an object's intrinsic attributes in an image. We allow changing color, texture, material, and even the shape of an object, while preserving its perceived identity and scene context. Existing approaches either rely on unsupervised priors that often fail to preserve identity or use overly restrictive supervision that prevents meaningful intrinsic variations. Our method relies on: (i) a relaxed training objective that allows the model to

infographic.key_insight: Alterbute is a diffusion-based image-editing model that can change intrinsic object attributes (color, texture, material, shape) while preserving the object's perceived identity and the surrounding scene context.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing methods either use weak unsupervised priors that lose object identity or rely on restrictive supervision that prevents realistic intrinsic variation; Alterbute enables flexible, identity-preserving edits of an object's intrinsic properties within a scene.
method: Diffusion-based localized editing: apply a conditional diffusion model focused on the object region to produce realistic intrinsic attribute changes.
Relaxed training objective that decouples attribute modification from identity and context changes, enabling larger intrinsic variations without identity drift.
Identity- and context-aware conditioning (e.g., region masks and identity-preservation constraints) to keep object identity and scene coherence during edits.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical tool for fine-grained, controllable object editing useful for content creation, data augmentation, and improving robustness of perception systems by generating realistic intra-class variation while keeping identity intact.

title: STEM: Scaling Transformers with Embedding Modules
authors: Ranajoy Sadhukhan, Sheng Cao, Harry Dong, Changsheng Zhao, Attiano Purpura-Pontoniere
abstract: Fine-grained sparsity promises higher parametric capacity without proportional per-token compute, but often suffers from training instability, load balancing, and communication overhead. We introduce STEM (Scaling Transformers with Embedding Modules), a static, token-indexed approach that replaces the FFN up-projection with a layer-local embedding lookup while keeping the gate and down-projection dense. This removes runtime routing, enables CPU offload with asynchronous prefetch, and decouples c

infographic.key_insight: STEM replaces the FFN up-projection with a static, token-indexed layer-local embedding lookup while keeping the gate and down-projection dense, removing runtime routing and enabling CPU offload with asynchronous prefetch to scale parameters without proportional per-token compute.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses instability, load-balancing and communication overheads of fine-grained sparsity / MoE-style approaches, enabling higher parametric capacity without costly per-token routing or heavy inter-device communication.
method: Replace FFN up-projection with a layer-local token-indexed embedding lookup (static assignment — no runtime routing).
Keep the gate and down-projection dense to preserve expressivity and training stability.
Enable CPU offload of the embedding modules with asynchronous prefetch to decouple parameter capacity from per-token GPU compute and reduce communication overhead.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical path to much larger effective model capacity with lower per-token cost and fewer engineering/communication headaches — easier to scale and deploy while maintaining stable training and good throughput.

title: DInf-Grid: A Neural Differential Equation Solver with Differentiable Feature Grids
authors: Navami Kairanda, Shanthika Naik, Marc Habermann, Avinash Sharma, Christian Theobalt
abstract: We present a novel differentiable grid-based representation for efficiently solving differential equations (DEs). Widely used architectures for neural solvers, such as sinusoidal neural networks, are coordinate-based MLPs that are both computationally intensive and slow to train. Although grid-based alternatives for implicit representations (e.g., Instant-NGP and K-Planes) train faster by exploiting signal structure, their reliance on linear interpolation restricts their ability to compute highe

infographic.key_insight: DInf-Grid introduces a differentiable feature-grid representation that preserves the training speed of grid-based methods while enabling accurate, high-order derivative evaluation required for solving differential equations with neural solvers.
infographic.problem_solved: Coordinate-based MLP solvers (e.g., sinusoidal networks) are slow and compute-intensive, while existing grid-based alternatives train fast but rely on linear interpolation that cannot provide the higher-order derivatives needed for many differential-equation tasks. DInf-Grid addresses this gap by making feature grids differentiable with respect to coordinates and parameters so neural DE solvers can compute accurate gradients efficiently.
method: Replace traditional coordinate-MLPs with a compact feature grid representation that is differentiable wrt spatial coordinates and network parameters.
Use differentiable interpolation / reconstruction operators on the grid (supporting higher-order derivatives) so derivative evaluation required by DE solvers is accurate and efficient.

Integrate the differentiable grid into neural differential-equation solvers to retain fast training/inference of grid methods while enabling reliable computation of derivatives for integration and optimization.
infographic.impact: DInf-Grid lets practitioners solve PDEs/ODEs with neural methods much faster and with more reliable derivative information, reducing compute and training time while improving solver stability — especially useful for scientific ML, simulation, and physics-informed learning.

title: Empathy Applicability Modeling for General Health Queries
authors: Shan Randhawa, Agha Ali Raza, Kentaro Toyama, Julie Hui, Mustafa Naseem
abstract: LLMs are increasingly being integrated into clinical workflows, yet they often lack clinical empathy, an essential aspect of effective doctor-patient communication. Existing NLP frameworks focus on reactively labeling empathy in doctors' responses but offer limited support for anticipatory modeling of empathy needs, especially in general health queries. We introduce the Empathy Applicability Framework (EAF), a theory-driven approach that classifies patient queries in terms of the applicability o

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces the Empathy Applicability Framework (EAF), a theory-driven method that predicts when empathy should be applied to general health queries—enabling models to anticipate, not just react to, empathy needs. This lets AI systems tailor responses more appropriately to patient emotional/contextual cues.
infographic.problem_solved: LLMs and clinical NLP systems often lack or inconsistently apply empathy, because existing work focuses on labeling clinician responses rather than anticipating whether a patient query requires empathetic framing; EAF fills that gap by classifying queries for empathy applicability.
method: Develop a theory-driven taxonomy (EAF) that defines when empathy is applicable for general health queries.
Annotate representative general-health queries with applicability labels and contextual tags based on the framework.
Train and evaluate classifiers/heuristics that predict empathy applicability to guide LLM response style or routing.
infographic.impact: Anticipatory empathy modeling helps AI/ML practitioners build safer, more patient-centered conversational agents by enabling context-aware response style selection, improving trust and communication in health-related interactions.
