title: Counterfactual Fairness with Graph Uncertainty
authors: Davi Valério, Chrysoula Zerva, Mariana Pinto, Ricardo Santos, André Carreiro
abstract: Evaluating machine learning (ML) model bias is key to building trustworthy and robust ML systems. Counterfactual Fairness (CF) audits allow the measurement of bias of ML models with a causal framework, yet their conclusions rely on a single causal graph that is rarely known with certainty in real-world scenarios. We propose CF with Graph Uncertainty (CF-GU), a bias evaluation procedure that incorporates the uncertainty of specifying a causal graph into CF. CF-GU (i) bootstraps a Causal Discovery

infographic.key_insight: Counterfactual Fairness conclusions can be brittle when based on a single assumed causal graph; CF-GU quantifies how uncertainty in the causal graph affects fairness assessments by evaluating counterfactuals across a distribution of plausible graphs.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses overconfidence in counterfactual fairness audits that assume a single, certain causal graph — providing a way to incorporate causal-structure uncertainty so fairness claims become probabilistic and robust.
method: Bootstrap a causal discovery procedure to generate an ensemble of plausible causal graphs reflecting graph uncertainty.
For each sampled graph, build corresponding structural causal models and compute counterfactual fairness metrics for the target ML model.
Aggregate results across the graph ensemble to produce distributions, confidence intervals, and robustness indicators for fairness assessments.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to report fairness assessments that reflect epistemic uncertainty about causal structure, reducing false certainty and guiding safer, more informed decisions about model deployment and remediation.

title: Muses: Designing, Composing, Generating Nonexistent Fantasy 3D Creatures without Training
authors: Hexiao Lu, Xiaokun Sun, Zeyu Cai, Hao Guo, Ying Tai
abstract: We present Muses, the first training-free method for fantastic 3D creature generation in a feed-forward paradigm. Previous methods, which rely on part-aware optimization, manual assembly, or 2D image generation, often produce unrealistic or incoherent 3D assets due to the challenges of intricate part-level manipulation and limited out-of-domain generation. In contrast, Muses leverages the 3D skeleton, a fundamental representation of biological forms, to explicitly and rationally compose diverse

infographic.key_insight: Muses is the first training-free, feed-forward system that composes and generates diverse, coherent fantasy 3D creatures by using an explicit 3D skeleton as the primary scaffold for design and synthesis.
infographic.problem_solved: It overcomes unrealistic or incoherent 3D assets produced by part-level optimization, manual assembly, or 2D-to-3D pipelines, enabling plausible out-of-domain creature designs without dataset training or laborious tuning.
method: Use an explicit 3D skeleton as a canonical scaffold to define anatomy, articulation, and part placement for creature designs.
Feed-forward, training-free composition pipeline that assembles and blends parts around the skeleton, then refines geometry and topology for coherence.
Apply skeleton-driven constraints and shape refinement to enforce anatomical plausibility and consistent articulation across generated creatures.
infographic.impact: Muses lowers the barrier to rapid, diverse 3D creature creation without collecting/training on large datasets or manual assembly, accelerating asset generation for research, games, and creative tools.

title: InfiAgent: An Infinite-Horizon Framework for General-Purpose Autonomous Agents
authors: Chenglin Yu, Yuchen Wang, Songmiao Wang, Hongxia Yang, Ming Li
abstract: LLM agents can reason and use tools, but they often break down on long-horizon tasks due to unbounded context growth and accumulated errors. Common remedies such as context compression or retrieval-augmented prompting introduce trade-offs between information fidelity and reasoning stability. We present InfiAgent, a general-purpose framework that keeps the agent's reasoning context strictly bounded regardless of task duration by externalizing persistent state into a file-centric state abstraction

infographic.key_insight: InfiAgent keeps an agent's working context strictly bounded for arbitrarily long tasks by externalizing persistent memory into a file-centric state abstraction, preventing unbounded prompt growth and accumulated reasoning errors.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses failure of LLM agents on long-horizon tasks caused by unbounded context growth, error accumulation, and the fidelity/stability trade-offs introduced by compression or retrieval-based fixes.
method: File-centric persistent state: encode memories, plans, observations and artifacts as external files that the agent can read/write.
Bounded reasoning loop: include only immediate, relevant context in the prompt while relying on the file store for long-term state, keeping prompt size constant regardless of task duration.
Operational primitives: atomic read/write, diff/versioning, and controlled retrieval semantics to maintain information fidelity and reproducibility.
infographic.impact: Makes general-purpose autonomous agents scalable and reliable for infinite-horizon tasks by eliminating prompt bloat and reducing accumulated reasoning errors—improving performance, debuggability, and resource efficiency for practitioners.

title: LTX-2: Efficient Joint Audio-Visual Foundation Model
authors: Yoav HaCohen, Benny Brazowski, Nisan Chiprut, Yaki Bitterman, Andrew Kvochko
abstract: Recent text-to-video diffusion models can generate compelling video sequences, yet they remain silent -- missing the semantic, emotional, and atmospheric cues that audio provides. We introduce LTX-2, an open-source foundational model capable of generating high-quality, temporally synchronized audiovisual content in a unified manner. LTX-2 consists of an asymmetric dual-stream transformer with a 14B-parameter video stream and a 5B-parameter audio stream, coupled through bidirectional audio-video

infographic.key_insight: LTX-2 is an open-source, joint audio–visual foundation model that generates high-quality, temporally synchronized audiovisual content by modeling video and audio with an asymmetric dual-stream transformer.
infographic.problem_solved: Text-to-video generative models produce compelling visuals but lack aligned, semantically rich audio; LTX-2 addresses the missing audio modality and audiovisual synchronization in a unified model.
method: Asymmetric dual-stream transformer architecture: a 14B-parameter video stream paired with a 5B-parameter audio stream.
Bidirectional coupling between streams to enable cross-modal information flow and temporal synchronization of audio and video.
Unified generation pipeline that produces temporally aligned audiovisual outputs from shared/paired conditioning (e.g., text prompts).
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners with an efficient, open foundation for creating synchronized audio–visual content, enabling richer generative media, improved multimodal research, and practical downstream applications (e.g., film VFX, accessibility, multimedia synthesis).

title: The Sonar Moment: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models in Audio Geo-Localization
authors: Ruixing Zhang, Zihan Liu, Leilei Sun, Tongyu Zhu, Weifeng Lv
abstract: Geo-localization aims to infer the geographic origin of a given signal. In computer vision, geo-localization has served as a demanding benchmark for compositional reasoning and is relevant to public safety. In contrast, progress on audio geo-localization has been constrained by the lack of high-quality audio-location pairs. To address this gap, we introduce AGL1K, the first audio geo-localization benchmark for audio language models (ALMs), spanning 72 countries and territories. To extract reliab

infographic.key_insight: The paper introduces AGL1K, the first large-scale audio geo-localization benchmark for audio-language models spanning 72 countries, revealing that current ALMs struggle to infer geographic origin from audio and that high-quality audio–location pairs are essential for progress.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of reliable, diverse audio–location data and a standardized benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on geo-localization tasks.
method: Curate AGL1K: assemble and validate high-quality audio–location pairs covering 72 countries and territories.
Design a benchmark suite and evaluation protocol tailored to audio-language models (ALMs) for geographic inference.
Evaluate representative ALMs on AGL1K to quantify performance gaps and failure modes.
infographic.impact: Provides a standardized dataset and benchmark that enables rigorous development and comparison of ALMs for geo-localization, accelerating research on geo-aware audio understanding and practical applications (e.g., safety, forensics, environmental monitoring).

title: Multi-RADS Synthetic Radiology Report Dataset and Head-to-Head Benchmarking of 41 Open-Weight and Proprietary Language Models
authors: Kartik Bose, Abhinandan Kumar, Raghuraman Soundararajan, Priya Mudgil, Samonee Ralmilay
abstract: Background: Reporting and Data Systems (RADS) standardize radiology risk communication but automated RADS assignment from narrative reports is challenging because of guideline complexity, output-format constraints, and limited benchmarking across RADS frameworks and model sizes. Purpose: To create RXL-RADSet, a radiologist-verified synthetic multi-RADS benchmark, and compare validity and accuracy of open-weight small language models (SLMs) with a proprietary model for RADS assignment. Materials

method: Create RXL-RADSet: a synthetic, radiologist-verified dataset that covers multiple RADS frameworks and encodes realistic report variants and structured RADS labels.
Enforce output-format and guideline constraints in prompts/evaluation to mirror clinical RADS assignment rules.
Conduct head-to-head benchmarking of 41 models (open-weight small language models and at least one proprietary model) measuring label validity and assignment accuracy across RADS frameworks.

title: X-MuTeST: A Multilingual Benchmark for Explainable Hate Speech Detection and A Novel LLM-consulted Explanation Framework
authors: Mohammad Zia Ur Rehman, Sai Kartheek Reddy Kasu, Shashivardhan Reddy Koppula, Sai Rithwik Reddy Chirra, Shwetank Shekhar Singh
abstract: Hate speech detection on social media faces challenges in both accuracy and explainability, especially for underexplored Indic languages. We propose a novel explainability-guided training framework, X-MuTeST (eXplainable Multilingual haTe Speech deTection), for hate speech detection that combines high-level semantic reasoning from large language models (LLMs) with traditional attention-enhancing techniques. We extend this research to Hindi and Telugu alongside English by providing benchmark huma

infographic.key_insight: X-MuTeST integrates LLM-generated high-level semantic rationales with attention-enhancing training to improve both accuracy and explainability of hate speech detection across English, Hindi and Telugu.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses low accuracy and poor interpretability of hate speech classifiers—especially for underexplored Indic languages—by providing a multilingual benchmark and a framework that leverages LLM reasoning to guide model explanations.
method: Build X-MuTeST: a multilingual human-annotated benchmark for hate speech (English, Hindi, Telugu) with explanation annotations.
Use LLMs to generate high-level semantic rationales (LLM-consulted explanations) for examples and incorporate these into supervision.
Combine rationale-guided loss with attention-enhancing techniques (e.g., attention regularization/explanation alignment) to train more interpretable classifiers.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a benchmark and a practical training recipe to produce more accurate, interpretable hate speech models for low-resource languages—improving trust, error analysis, and deployment readiness.

title: Hunting for "Oddballs" with Machine Learning: Detecting Anomalous Exoplanets Using a Deep-Learned Low-Dimensional Representation of Transit Spectra with Autoencoders
authors: Alexander Roman, Emilie Panek, Roy T. Forestano, Eyup B. Unlu, Katia Matcheva
abstract: This study explores the application of autoencoder-based machine learning techniques for anomaly detection to identify exoplanet atmospheres with unconventional chemical signatures using a low-dimensional data representation. We use the Atmospheric Big Challenge (ABC) database, a publicly available dataset with over 100,000 simulated exoplanet spectra, to construct an anomaly detection scenario by defining CO2-rich atmospheres as anomalies and CO2-poor atmospheres as the normal class. We benchma

infographic.key_insight: A deep autoencoder can learn a compact, low-dimensional representation of transit spectra that makes CO2-rich exoplanet atmospheres stand out as anomalies, enabling automated detection of unusual chemical signatures from large simulated catalogs.
infographic.problem_solved: Detecting rare or unconventional exoplanet atmospheres (here: CO2-rich 'oddballs') in very large spectral datasets without relying on labeled anomaly examples; effectively triaging candidates for follow-up.
method: Use the Atmospheric Big Challenge (ABC) dataset (>100k simulated transit spectra) and treat CO2-poor spectra as the normal class and CO2-rich spectra as anomalies.
Train an autoencoder to compress spectra into a low-dimensional latent space that captures typical atmospheric variability.
Score anomalies via reconstruction error and/or latent-space distance to the normal distribution, and evaluate the detector against this constructed anomaly scenario.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable, label-light framework for prioritizing unusual exoplanet atmospheres from massive spectral catalogs; demonstrates how representation learning + anomaly detection can uncover rare physical signatures without explicit anomaly labels.

title: Classifying several dialectal Nawatl varieties
authors: Juan-José Guzmán-Landa, Juan-Manuel Torres-Moreno, Miguel Figueroa-Saavedra, Carlos-Emiliano González-Gallardo, Graham Ranger
abstract: Mexico is a country with a large number of indigenous languages, among which the most widely spoken is Nawatl, with more than two million people currently speaking it (mainly in North and Central America). Despite its rich cultural heritage, which dates back to the 15th century, Nawatl is a language with few computer resources. The problem is compounded when it comes to its dialectal varieties, with approximately 30 varieties recognised, not counting the different spellings in the written forms

infographic.key_insight: The paper demonstrates that several dialectal varieties of Nawatl can be automatically distinguished despite limited digital resources and inconsistent orthography, using a targeted collection and classification approach optimized for low-resource, dialect-rich languages.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses automatic identification and classification of multiple Nawatl dialects when digital corpora are scarce and written forms vary widely across regions and speakers.
method: Assemble and annotate a multi-dialect Nawatl corpus that captures regional varieties and spelling variation.

Train and evaluate supervised classification models (including resource-efficient or transfer-learning strategies) with cross-dialect validation and error analysis to identify confusable pairs.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building dialect-aware NLP tools for low-resource, indigenous languages; enables better documentation, search, and language technologies that respect regional variation.

title: pdfQA: Diverse, Challenging, and Realistic Question Answering over PDFs
authors: Tobias Schimanski, Imene Kolli, Jingwei Ni, Yu Fan, Ario Saeid Vaghefi
abstract: PDFs are the second-most used document type on the internet (after HTML). Yet, existing QA datasets commonly start from text sources or only address specific domains. In this paper, we present pdfQA, a multi-domain 2K human-annotated (real-pdfQA) and 2K synthetic dataset (syn-pdfQA) differentiating QA pairs in ten complexity dimensions (e.g., file type, source modality, source position, answer type). We apply and evaluate quality and difficulty filters on both datasets, obtaining valid and chall

infographic.key_insight: pdfQA delivers a realistic, multi-domain PDF question-answering benchmark (2K human-annotated + 2K synthetic) annotated across ten complexity dimensions, enabling robust evaluation of QA systems on true PDF challenges like layout and modality.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing QA datasets largely start from plain text or narrow domains and do not capture PDF-specific phenomena (e.g., layout, multi-column text, embedded images, varied file types). pdfQA fills this gap by providing diverse, challenging, and realistic PDF QA pairs with explicit complexity labels.
method: Curate multi-domain PDF sources and generate two parallel datasets: real-pdfQA (2K human-annotated QA pairs) and syn-pdfQA (2K synthetic QA pairs).
Annotate each QA pair along ten complexity dimensions (e.g., file type, source modality, source position, answer type) to characterize difficulty and diversity.
Apply quality and difficulty filters to obtain validated, challenging subsets and evaluate system performance across those dimensions.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and engineers to benchmark and improve document understanding models on realistic PDF difficulties (layout, multimodality, retrieval). This drives development of more robust, production-ready PDF QA systems.

title: Heterogeneous Low-Bandwidth Pre-Training of LLMs
authors: Yazan Obeidi, Amir Sarfi, Joel Lidin, Paul Janson, Eugene Belilovsky
abstract: Pre-training large language models (LLMs) increasingly requires distributed compute, yet bandwidth constraints make it difficult to scale beyond well-provisioned datacenters-especially when model parallelism forces frequent, large inter-device communications. We study whether SparseLoCo, a low-communication data parallel method based on infrequent synchronization and sparse pseudo-gradient exchange, can be combined with low-bandwidth pipeline model parallelism via activation and activation-gradi

infographic.key_insight: Combining SparseLoCo (infrequent synchronization + sparse pseudo-gradient exchange) with low-bandwidth pipeline model parallelism using compressed activation and activation‑gradient exchanges dramatically reduces inter-device communication for LLM pre-training while preserving performance.
infographic.problem_solved: How to scale LLM pre-training across heterogeneous, low-bandwidth clusters where model parallelism normally incurs frequent, large inter-device communications that limit scalability outside well-provisioned datacenters.
method: Use SparseLoCo: perform infrequent global synchronization and exchange only sparse pseudo‑gradients to cut communication volume.
Apply low-bandwidth pipeline model parallelism: compress/quantize activations and activation‑gradient transfers and reduce their exchange frequency across pipeline stages.
Integrate both approaches to trade off communication vs. computation adaptively, enabling training on nodes with diverse network capacities.
infographic.impact: Makes large-scale LLM pre-training feasible on heterogeneous, constrained networks (academic clusters, edge or cloud-of-opportunity), reducing bandwidth requirements, cost, and dependency on high‑end datacenter networks while maintaining model convergence.

title: Talk2Move: Reinforcement Learning for Text-Instructed Object-Level Geometric Transformation in Scenes
authors: Jing Tan, Zhaoyang Zhang, Yantao Shen, Jiarui Cai, Shuo Yang
abstract: We introduce Talk2Move, a reinforcement learning (RL) based diffusion framework for text-instructed spatial transformation of objects within scenes. Spatially manipulating objects in a scene through natural language poses a challenge for multimodal generation systems. While existing text-based manipulation methods can adjust appearance or style, they struggle to perform object-level geometric transformations-such as translating, rotating, or resizing objects-due to scarce paired supervision and

infographic.key_insight: Talk2Move frames text-instructed geometric editing as a sequential decision problem and combines reinforcement learning with a diffusion-based transformer to perform object-level translations, rotations, and resizes from natural language — enabling precise spatial edits with limited paired supervision.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing multimodal text-to-image methods can change appearance or style but struggle to perform explicit object-level geometric transformations (translate/rotate/scale) because of scarce paired supervision, ambiguous language grounding, and the need for temporally or spatially coherent actions within scenes.
method: Formulate geometric editing as an RL policy that emits object-centric transformation actions (translate/rotate/scale) conditioned on scene state and a natural-language instruction.

Integrate the learned policy with a diffusion-based transformation/refinement module to produce realistic, spatially coherent edits; training uses sparse rewards (e.g., alignment, IoU, perceptual scores) and self-supervision to reduce reliance on paired data.
Use a scene parser / object grounding module to map language mentions to object slots and constrain the action space, enabling precise per-object manipulation.
infographic.impact: Enables more controllable, interpretable text-driven scene editing for applications like image/video editing, AR/VR content creation, and embodied agents — reducing the need for expensive paired datasets while improving spatial reasoning and object-level control.

title: VAR RL Done Right: Tackling Asynchronous Policy Conflicts in Visual Autoregressive Generation
authors: Shikun Sun, Liao Qu, Huichao Zhang, Yiheng Liu, Yangyang Song
abstract: Visual generation is dominated by three paradigms: AutoRegressive (AR), diffusion, and Visual AutoRegressive (VAR) models. Unlike AR and diffusion, VARs operate on heterogeneous input structures across their generation steps, which creates severe asynchronous policy conflicts. This issue becomes particularly acute in reinforcement learning (RL) scenarios, leading to unstable training and suboptimal alignment. To resolve this, we propose a novel framework to enhance Group Relative Policy Optimiza

infographic.key_insight: Visual autoregressive (VAR) models suffer from asynchronous policy conflicts because each generation step sees heterogeneous inputs; aligning policies across these steps via group-relative updates stabilizes RL training and improves alignment.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses unstable and suboptimal reinforcement learning for Visual Autoregressive generation caused by asynchronous policy conflicts that arise from varying input structures across generation steps.
method: Partition generation steps into consistent 'groups' based on input/conditioning heterogeneity and treat each group as a related sub-policy.

Perform group-relative policy optimization: update policies with constraints/regularizers that enforce consistency across groups (relative updates, KL/consistency penalties) rather than independent asynchronous updates.
Integrate these updates into the RL training loop for VARs to reduce conflicting gradients and stabilize optimization (e.g., prioritized replay or group-aware advantage estimation).
infographic.impact: Provides a practical recipe to stabilize RL for VAR models, enabling more reliable alignment and higher-quality visual generation—useful for practitioners training multimodal/autoregressive generators under RL objectives.

title: DatBench: Discriminative, Faithful, and Efficient VLM Evaluations
authors: Siddharth Joshi, Haoli Yin, Rishabh Adiga, Ricardo Monti, Aldo Carranza
abstract: Empirical evaluation serves as the primary compass guiding research progress in foundation models. Despite a large body of work focused on training frontier vision-language models (VLMs), approaches to their evaluation remain nascent. To guide their maturation, we propose three desiderata that evaluations should satisfy: (1) faithfulness to the modality and application, (2) discriminability between models of varying quality, and (3) efficiency in compute. Through this lens, we identify critical

infographic.key_insight: DatBench defines and operationalizes three core desiderata for vision–language model (VLM) evaluation — faithfulness to modality/application, discriminability between model qualities, and compute efficiency — producing an evaluation suite that more reliably distinguishes real model differences while saving resources.
infographic.problem_solved: Current VLM evaluations are inconsistent: they often fail to reflect real-world multimodal tasks (lack faithfulness), cannot clearly separate stronger from weaker models (low discriminability), and are costly to run (inefficient). DatBench addresses all three simultaneously.
method: Formalize three evaluation desiderata (faithfulness, discriminability, efficiency) and derive measurable criteria for each.
Curate modality-aligned tasks and controlled protocols that emphasize real application behaviors and maximize signal between models (e.g., targeted probes, contrastive task designs).
Optimize the evaluation pipeline for compute (adaptive sampling, lightweight probes, aggregated scoring) to deliver reliable comparisons with lower resource cost.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners and researchers a principled, resource-conscious way to compare VLMs that better reflects real-world performance and uncovers meaningful model differences, accelerating trustworthy selection and iteration.

title: InfiniteVGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer for Endless Streams
authors: Shuai Yuan, Yantai Yang, Xiaotian Yang, Xupeng Zhang, Zhonghao Zhao
abstract: The grand vision of enabling persistent, large-scale 3D visual geometry understanding is shackled by the irreconcilable demands of scalability and long-term stability. While offline models like VGGT achieve inspiring geometry capability, their batch-based nature renders them irrelevant for live systems. Streaming architectures, though the intended solution for live operation, have proven inadequate. Existing methods either fail to support truly infinite-horizon inputs or suffer from catastrophic

infographic.key_insight: InfiniteVGGT enables truly infinite-horizon 3D visual geometry understanding by combining geometry-grounded representations with a streaming transformer that keeps per-step compute and memory bounded while preserving long-term spatial consistency.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-quality batch 3D geometry models and live systems by solving scalability and catastrophic forgetting in continual, real-time visual streams.
method: Geometry-grounded transformer architecture that anchors latent state to 3D cues (pose/depth) for spatially consistent representations.
Fixed-size, compressed geometric memory and online state-update rules (attention with condensation and alignment) to bound compute/memory and avoid forgetting.
Streaming inference loop that incrementally updates geometry and semantics without replay or full-batch reprocessing, ensuring stability over arbitrarily long sequences.
infographic.impact: Makes persistent, large-scale 3D perception practical for live applications (robotics, AR, mapping) by enabling stable, memory-efficient continual geometry estimation and downstream reasoning over endless streams.

title: Falcon-H1R: Pushing the Reasoning Frontiers with a Hybrid Model for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
authors: Falcon LLM Team, Iheb Chaabane, Puneesh Khanna, Suhail Mohmad, Slim Frikha
abstract: This work introduces Falcon-H1R, a 7B-parameter reasoning-optimized model that establishes the feasibility of achieving competitive reasoning performance with small language models (SLMs). Falcon-H1R stands out for its parameter efficiency, consistently matching or outperforming SOTA reasoning models that are $2\times$ to $7\times$ larger across a variety of reasoning-intensive benchmarks. These results underscore the importance of careful data curation and targeted training strategies (via both

infographic.key_insight: Falcon-H1R shows that a carefully designed 7B-parameter hybrid model can match or beat reasoning performance of models 2×–7× larger, proving that small language models can be competitive on reasoning tasks with the right training and test‑time strategies.
infographic.problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving strong reasoning performance without massive model sizes, enabling efficient deployment and test-time scaling while maintaining or improving accuracy on reasoning-intensive benchmarks.

title: VINO: A Unified Visual Generator with Interleaved OmniModal Context
authors: Junyi Chen, Tong He, Zhoujie Fu, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai
abstract: We present VINO, a unified visual generator that performs image and video generation and editing within a single framework. Instead of relying on task-specific models or independent modules for each modality, VINO uses a shared diffusion backbone that conditions on text, images and videos, enabling a broad range of visual creation and editing tasks under one model. Specifically, VINO couples a vision-language model (VLM) with a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT), where multimodal inputs ar

infographic.key_insight: VINO unifies image and video generation/editing in one model by conditioning a single diffusion backbone on interleaved text, image, and video context, enabled by a vision-language model paired with a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT).
infographic.problem_solved: Eliminates the need for separate, modality-specific generators and editing modules by providing a single framework that handles mixed-modal inputs and outputs (text, images, videos) for both creation and editing tasks.
method: A shared diffusion backbone that accepts conditioning from multiple modalities (text, image, video) to produce images or video frames.
Coupling a vision-language model (VLM) with a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT) to encode interleaved omni-modal context and enable cross-modal attention.
Unified training/inference pipeline that supports generation and editing across modalities without separate task-specific modules.
infographic.impact: Simplifies deployment and workflows by providing one model for diverse visual creation/editing tasks, improving consistency across modalities and reducing engineering overhead for multimodal applications.

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Off Ball Defensive Role and Performance Evaluation in Football
authors: Sean Groom, Shuo Wang, Francisco Belo, Axl Rice, Liam Anderson
abstract: Evaluating off-ball defensive performance in football is challenging, as traditional metrics do not capture the nuanced coordinated movements that limit opponent action selection and success probabilities. Although widely used possession value models excel at appraising on-ball actions, their application to defense remains limited. Existing counterfactual methods, such as ghosting models, help extend these analyses but often rely on simulating "average" behavior that lacks tactical context. To a

infographic.key_insight: A role-aware ML framework quantifies the value of off-ball defensive movements by generating context-conditioned counterfactuals and measuring their effect on possession value, revealing coordinated contributions that traditional metrics miss.
infographic.problem_solved: Standard stats and possession-value models focus on on-ball events and average ghosting simulations, failing to capture tactical, coordinated off-ball defense and therefore underestimating individual and role-level defensive impact.
method: Use high-frequency player-tracking data with a possession-value (PV) model to measure attacker threat over time.
Train context-conditioned counterfactual trajectory generators (role-aware ghosting / imitation models) to simulate alternative off-ball behaviors consistent with tactical roles.
Compute marginal defensive value as the PV difference between actual and counterfactual scenarios and aggregate by role to assign credit.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, interpretable way to evaluate and compare off-ball defensive contributions, enabling better feature design, model-based coaching insights, and reward signals for multi-agent learning or scouting workflows.

title: Categorical Reparameterization with Denoising Diffusion models
authors: Samson Gourevitch, Alain Durmus, Eric Moulines, Jimmy Olsson, Yazid Janati
abstract: Gradient-based optimization with categorical variables typically relies on score-function estimators, which are unbiased but noisy, or on continuous relaxations that replace the discrete distribution with a smooth surrogate admitting a pathwise (reparameterized) gradient, at the cost of optimizing a biased, temperature-dependent objective. In this paper, we extend this family of relaxations by introducing a diffusion-based soft reparameterization for categorical distributions. For these distribu

infographic.key_insight: Introduce a diffusion-based soft reparameterization that maps categorical one-hot variables into a continuous diffusion process and uses the learned denoiser to obtain low-variance, pathwise gradients—bridging unbiased score-function estimators and biased continuous relaxations.
infographic.problem_solved: Optimizing objectives with categorical/discrete variables suffers from either high-variance score-function estimators or biased continuous relaxations; this paper provides a new reparameterization that reduces variance while controlling bias.
method: Define a forward diffusion (noising) process that smoothly embeds categorical one-hot vectors into a continuous space (simplex or embedding space) via a noise schedule.
Train/derive a denoising (reverse) model / score estimator that enables sampling and computing pathwise gradients through the continuous diffusion trajectory back to categorical logits.

Construct gradient estimators that use the denoiser/score to produce lower-variance, tunable-bias gradients for learning tasks (e.g., variational inference), trading off noise schedule and estimator bias.
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a practical alternative for training models with categorical latents or discrete choices: lower-variance gradients and a controllable bias/variance trade-off can improve stability and performance in variational inference, discrete optimization, and generative modeling.

title: Exploring the Performance of Large Language Models on Subjective Span Identification Tasks

abstract: Identifying relevant text spans is important for several downstream tasks in NLP, as it contributes to model explainability. While most span identification approaches rely on relatively smaller pre-trained language models like BERT, a few recent approaches have leveraged the latest generation of Large Language Models (LLMs) for the task. infographic.key_insight: Large language models can identify subjective, context-dependent text spans but produce variable outputs; targeted prompting and calibration improve consistency and alignment with human judgments.

method: Benchmark multiple LLMs and smaller pre-trained models on curated subjective-span datasets and tasks.
Compare prompting strategies (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought) and apply post-processing/calibration to stabilize outputs.
Measure model–human agreement, consistency, and document annotation guidelines and evaluation criteria for subjective spans.

Improves annotation and evaluation practices for downstream NLP tasks that rely on interpretability.

title: Bayesian Inverse Games with High-Dimensional Multi-Modal Observations
authors: Yash Jain, Xinjie Liu, Lasse Peters, David Fridovich-Keil, Ufuk Topcu
abstract: Many multi-agent interaction scenarios can be naturally modeled as noncooperative games, where each agent's decisions depend on others' future actions. However, deploying game-theoretic planners for autonomous decision-making requires a specification of all agents' objectives. To circumvent this practical difficulty, recent work develops maximum likelihood techniques for solving inverse games that can identify unknown agent objectives from interaction data. Unfortunately, these methods only infe

infographic.key_insight: A Bayesian inverse-game framework that infers other agents' objectives from high-dimensional, multi‑modal observations and produces calibrated uncertainty over hypotheses, enabling robust reasoning about strategic behavior.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing inverse-game approaches rely on maximum-likelihood estimation and break down with high-dimensional, multi-modal sensor data (images, trajectories, language) and complex strategic coupling; this work provides a scalable, uncertainty-aware solution for recovering objectives from such observations.
method: Formulate inverse games probabilistically: place priors on agent objectives and compute a posterior using a game-theoretic forward model as the likelihood.

Scale inference to high-dimensional, multi‑modal data by combining learned perceptual encoders (e.g., latent representations) with scalable Bayesian inference (amortized/variational inference or MCMC over surrogate differentiable game solvers).
Produce calibrated posterior samples over objectives for downstream planners and evaluate on multi-agent scenarios to demonstrate robustness and uncertainty quantification.
infographic.impact: Practitioners can infer other agents' goals from complex sensor streams while quantifying uncertainty, improving safety and decision-making in multi-agent systems (e.g., autonomous driving, robotics, multi-robot coordination).

title: Pixel-to-4D: Camera-Controlled Image-to-Video Generation with Dynamic 3D Gaussians
authors: Melonie de Almeida, Daniela Ivanova, Tong Shi, John H. Williamson, Paul Henderson
abstract: Humans excel at forecasting the future dynamics of a scene given just a single image. Video generation models that can mimic this ability are an essential component for intelligent systems. Recent approaches have improved temporal coherence and 3D consistency in single-image-conditioned video generation. However, these methods often lack robust user controllability, such as modifying the camera path, limiting their applicability in real-world applications. Most existing camera-controlled image-t

infographic.key_insight: Representing a scene as dynamic 3D Gaussians lets a model convert a single image into camera-controllable video—predicting plausible scene dynamics while rendering novel camera paths with strong 3D and temporal consistency.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the lack of user-controllable camera trajectories and limited 3D consistency in single-image-conditioned video generation.
method: Construct a dynamic 3D Gaussian scene representation (spatially localized Gaussian 'splats') inferred from a single input image.
Learn temporal dynamics on the Gaussian representation so the scene can be forecasted over time and rendered from arbitrary camera trajectories.
Train with photometric and temporal-consistency objectives and render efficiently to produce coherent, camera-controlled video sequences.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to generate realistic, temporally coherent videos from one image with explicit camera control—useful for content creation, AR/VR, and simulation in robotics. It bridges neural rendering and controllable video forecasting for more practical, editable video synthesis.

title: Adapting Natural Language Processing Models Across Jurisdictions: A pilot Study in Canadian Cancer Registries
authors: Jonathan Simkin, Lovedeep Gondara, Zeeshan Rizvi, Gregory Doyle, Jeff Dowden
abstract: Population-based cancer registries depend on pathology reports as their primary diagnostic source, yet manual abstraction is resource-intensive and contributes to delays in cancer data. While transformer-based NLP systems have improved registry workflows, their ability to generalize across jurisdictions with differing reporting conventions remains poorly understood. We present the first cross-provincial evaluation of adapting BCCRTron, a domain-adapted transformer model developed at the British

infographic.key_insight: This pilot study presents the first cross‑provincial evaluation showing that adapting BCCRTron, a domain‑adapted transformer for pathology reports, enables more reliable transfer of cancer‑registry NLP models across Canadian jurisdictions with differing reporting conventions.
infographic.problem_solved: Population‑based cancer registries rely on manual abstraction from pathology reports, which is slow and resource‑intensive. The paper addresses whether transformer‑based registry NLP models can generalize across provinces with heterogeneous reporting styles and how to adapt them to new jurisdictions.
method: Use BCCRTron (a domain‑adapted transformer) as the base model for extracting diagnostic information from pathology reports.
Perform cross‑provincial adaptation and evaluation: transfer the model between registry datasets from different provinces and measure performance changes.
Compare adaptation strategies (e.g., fine‑tuning on target jurisdiction data and targeted domain adaptation) to quantify gains in accuracy and robustness.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates that targeted model adaptation enables practical deployment of registry NLP systems across jurisdictions, reducing manual abstraction burden and highlighting the necessity of cross‑jurisdiction validation for clinical NLP models.

title: Multi-Level Feature Fusion for Continual Learning in Visual Quality Inspection
authors: Johannes C. Bauer, Paul Geng, Stephan Trattnig, Petr Dokládal, Rüdiger Daub
abstract: Deep neural networks show great potential for automating various visual quality inspection tasks in manufacturing. However, their applicability is limited in more volatile scenarios, such as remanufacturing, where the inspected products and defect patterns often change. In such settings, deployed models require frequent adaptation to novel conditions, effectively posing a continual learning problem. To enable quick adaptation, the necessary training processes must be computationally efficient wh

infographic.key_insight: Fusing features from multiple network levels creates representations that are both stable and adaptable, enabling efficient continual learning for changing visual quality inspection tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Enables deployed vision models in volatile manufacturing/remanufacturing settings to adapt quickly to new products and defect patterns without costly full retraining or severe forgetting of prior knowledge.
method: Introduce a multi-level feature fusion module that combines low-, mid- and high-level features to form robust, adaptable representations.
Use the fused representations within a continual learning pipeline to balance plasticity (learning new defects) and stability (retaining prior knowledge).
Optimize for computationally efficient incremental updates so models can be adapted on-device or with limited compute resources.
infographic.impact: Allows AI/ML practitioners in manufacturing to maintain high inspection performance across evolving conditions while keeping adaptation time and compute low — reducing downtime and labeling effort in production settings.

title: IRPO: Scaling the Bradley-Terry Model via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Haonan Song, Qingchen Xie, Huan Zhu, Feng Xiao, Luxi Xing
abstract: Generative Reward Models (GRMs) have attracted considerable research interest in reward modeling due to their interpretability, inference-time scalability, and potential for refinement through reinforcement learning (RL). However, widely used pairwise GRMs create a computational bottleneck when integrated with RL algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). This bottleneck arises from two factors: (i) the O(n^2) time complexity of pairwise comparisons required to obtain relative

infographic.key_insight: IRPO integrates a reinforcement-learning reformulation with the Bradley–Terry generative reward model to remove the costly O(n^2) pairwise-comparison bottleneck, enabling scalable reward estimation for larger candidate sets.
infographic.problem_solved: Pairwise generative reward models (GRMs) used with RL methods like GRPO require O(n^2) comparisons to obtain relative scores, creating a severe computational bottleneck that prevents scaling to many candidates or frequent online updates.
method: Introduce IRPO: an RL-driven reformulation that learns implicit preferences compatible with the Bradley–Terry model without enumerating all pairwise comparisons.
Integrate IRPO into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to estimate relative rewards with far fewer comparisons and enable end-to-end training.
Optimize for training/inference efficiency (reduced compute and memory) while preserving GRM interpretability and refinability via RL.
infographic.impact: IRPO makes generative reward models practical at scale, lowering compute and latency for preference/ranking tasks (e.g., LLM preference learning, response ranking) and enabling faster iteration and deployment of reward-driven systems.

title: An Agentic Framework for Neuro-Symbolic Programming
authors: Aliakbar Nafar, Chetan Chigurupati, Danial Kamali, Hamid Karimian, Parisa Kordjamshidi
abstract: Integrating symbolic constraints into deep learning models could make them more robust, interpretable, and data-efficient. Still, it remains a time-consuming and challenging task. Existing frameworks like DomiKnowS help this integration by providing a high-level declarative programming interface, but they still assume the user is proficient with the library's specific syntax. We propose AgenticDomiKnowS (ADS) to eliminate this dependency. ADS translates free-form task descriptions into a complet

infographic.key_insight: AgenticDomiKnowS (ADS) lets users describe tasks in natural language and automatically generates correct neuro-symbolic DomiKnowS programs, removing the need to learn library-specific syntax while preserving symbolic constraints.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between free-form task descriptions and declarative neuro-symbolic programs by automating translation, synthesis, and verification—reducing the time and expertise required to integrate symbolic constraints into deep learning models.
method: Agentic pipeline that uses large language models to translate free-form task descriptions into candidate DomiKnowS programs.
Symbolic validation and execution step that checks generated programs against constraints and test cases, with automated debugging and iterative refinement.
End-to-end synthesis targeting robustness and correctness while preserving declarative semantics of the underlying DomiKnowS framework.
infographic.impact: Makes neuro-symbolic programming accessible to practitioners who are not experts in a specific DSL, accelerating adoption of constraint-aware models and enabling more interpretable, data-efficient ML solutions.

title: Investigating the Viability of Employing Multi-modal Large Language Models in the Context of Audio Deepfake Detection
authors: Akanksha Chuchra, Shukesh Reddy, Sudeepta Mishra, Abhijit Das, Abhinav Dhall
abstract: While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown strong generalisation in detecting image and video deepfakes, their use for audio deepfake detection remains largely unexplored. In this work, we aim to explore the potential of MLLMs for audio deepfake detection. Combining audio inputs with a range of text prompts as queries to find out the viability of MLLMs to learn robust representations across modalities for audio deepfake detection. Therefore, we at

infographic.key_insight: Multimodal LLMs can be repurposed for audio deepfake detection by combining raw audio (or audio embeddings) with targeted text prompts, yielding promising cross-modal representations while revealing modality-specific adaptation needs.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the unexplored challenge of whether Vision/Multimodal Large Language Models can detect audio deepfakes—reducing reliance on bespoke audio-only detectors and testing if MLLMs generalise to audio-domain manipulation detection.
method: Convert audio to model-compatible inputs (waveform embeddings, spectrograms or pretrained audio embeddings) and feed them into MLLMs alongside designed text prompts.
Use prompt engineering and prompt-as-query strategies to probe MLLMs for deepfake indicators and extract multimodal representations.
Evaluate detection performance across prompt types and baselines (audio-only detectors), analyze failure modes and modality-alignment issues.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates a pathway to unified, multimodal deepfake detectors and highlights practical considerations (prompt design, modality alignment, fine-tuning) for deploying MLLMs in audio security tasks—helpful for practitioners seeking robust, scalable detection systems.

title: Learning intermediate physical states for inverse metasurface design
authors: Chun-Teh Chen
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 31 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01167-8

Deep generative models that learn intermediate surface-current maps, rather than layouts directly, offer a more stable route to inverse design of tunable and stacked metasurfaces.

infographic.key_insight: Training deep generative models to produce intermediate physical states (surface-current maps) instead of layouts directly yields more stable, accurate inverse design for tunable and stacked metasurfaces.
infographic.problem_solved: Directly mapping electromagnetic targets to device layouts is unstable and ill-posed for complex, tunable, or stacked metasurfaces; the paper addresses poor training stability, non-uniqueness, and difficulty incorporating physics and tunability into inverse design.
method: Learn a conditional generative model that predicts intermediate surface-current maps from desired electromagnetic responses and tuning parameters.
Use a physics-aware decoder or deterministic mapping to convert predicted current maps into physical layouts, with simulation/physics losses to enforce accuracy.
Support stacked and tunable metasurfaces by conditioning the model on layer configuration and control variables for robust multi-layer design.
infographic.impact: Provides ML practitioners a compact, physically meaningful latent representation that improves training stability, interpretability, and sample efficiency for inverse design tasks in computational electromagnetics and beyond.

title: From Inpainting to Editing: A Self-Bootstrapping Framework for Context-Rich Visual Dubbing
authors: Xu He, Haoxian Zhang, Hejia Chen, Changyuan Zheng, Liyang Chen
abstract: Audio-driven visual dubbing aims to synchronize a video's lip movements with new speech, but is fundamentally challenged by the lack of ideal training data: paired videos where only a subject's lip movements differ while all other visual conditions are identical. Existing methods circumvent this with a mask-based inpainting paradigm, where an incomplete visual conditioning forces models to simultaneously hallucinate missing content and sync lips, leading to visual artifacts, identity drift, and

infographic.key_insight: Convert noisy inpainting supervision into a clean editing objective via a self-bootstrapping loop: use inpainting outputs to create pseudo paired data, then train an editor that focuses on lip motion while preserving full visual context.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of perfect training pairs for audio-driven visual dubbing, which forces prior methods to hallucinate missing context and causes visual artifacts and identity drift.
method: Stage an initial inpainting-based model to produce pseudo paired examples where only lip motion changes while context is incomplete.
Train a context-aware editing model to modify the lip region conditioned on audio and full-frame context, emphasizing identity and temporal consistency.
Iteratively refine the pseudo-dataset and editor (self-bootstrapping), using the editor's outputs as improved supervision to break the hallucination loop.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical recipe to move from artifact-prone inpainting to robust, identity-preserving lip edits without requiring perfect paired data, making visual dubbing more reliable for research and production.

title: Scaling Open-Ended Reasoning to Predict the Future
authors: Nikhil Chandak, Shashwat Goel, Ameya Prabhu, Moritz Hardt, Jonas Geiping
abstract: High-stakes decision making involves reasoning under uncertainty about the future. In this work, we train language models to make predictions on open-ended forecasting questions. To scale up training data, we synthesize novel forecasting questions from global events reported in daily news, using a fully automated, careful curation recipe. We train the Qwen3 thinking models on our dataset, OpenForesight. To prevent leakage of future information during training and evaluation, we use an offline ne

infographic.key_insight: By automatically synthesizing large-scale open-ended forecasting questions from daily news and training reasoning-capable LMs (Qwen3) on that data (OpenForesight), the paper scales language-model-based prediction of future events while controlling for temporal leakage.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of large, high-quality training/evaluation data for open-ended forecasting and the risk of future-information leakage when training models to reason about future events.
method: Automatically synthesize forecasting questions from global news reports using a careful, fully automated curation pipeline to scale data (OpenForesight).
Train and adapt the Qwen3 ‘thinking’ models on the synthesized dataset to elicit open-ended future predictions.
Prevent leakage of future information via offline dataset snapshots and temporal partitioning / evaluation protocols that respect news timelines.
infographic.impact: Provides a scalable dataset and protocol for training and evaluating models on open-ended forecasting, enabling practitioners to develop and benchmark temporal reasoning and prediction capabilities with better data hygiene.

title: Edit3r: Instant 3D Scene Editing from Sparse Unposed Images
authors: Jiageng Liu, Weijie Lyu, Xueting Li, Yejie Guo, Ming-Hsuan Yang
abstract: We present Edit3r, a feed-forward framework that reconstructs and edits 3D scenes in a single pass from unposed, view-inconsistent, instruction-edited images. Unlike prior methods requiring per-scene optimization, Edit3r directly predicts instruction-aligned 3D edits, enabling fast and photorealistic rendering without optimization or pose estimation. A key challenge in training such a model lies in the absence of multi-view consistent edited images for supervision. We address this with (i) a SAM

infographic.key_insight: Edit3r is a feed‑forward model that reconstructs and applies instruction‑aligned 3D edits from sparse, unposed, view‑inconsistent images in a single pass—removing the need for per‑scene optimization or pose estimation.
infographic.problem_solved: Eliminates slow, per‑scene optimization and the requirement for posed, multi‑view consistent inputs by enabling instant, photorealistic 3D scene edits from sparse, unposed image sets.
method: Feed‑forward 3D reconstruction+editing network that directly predicts instruction‑aligned edits from sparse, unposed, view‑inconsistent images (no pose estimation or per‑scene optimization).

Training strategy that compensates for the lack of multi‑view consistent edited supervision via region extraction (e.g., SAM-based masks), synthetic multi‑view augmentation and consistency-aware supervision to teach the model multi‑view coherence.
Design focused on photorealistic rendering and single‑pass inference to produce multi‑view consistent edited scenes quickly at test time.
infographic.impact: Enables fast, scalable 3D scene editing workflows for content creators and researchers by converting sparse, in-the-wild image edits into coherent 3D results without expensive optimization or pose labeling. This lowers the barrier for AR/VR content creation, rapid prototyping, and interactive editing.

title: GaMO: Geometry-aware Multi-view Diffusion Outpainting for Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction
authors: Yi-Chuan Huang, Hao-Jen Chien, Chin-Yang Lin, Ying-Huan Chen, Yu-Lun Liu
abstract: Recent advances in 3D reconstruction have achieved remarkable progress in high-quality scene capture from dense multi-view imagery, yet struggle when input views are limited. Various approaches, including regularization techniques, semantic priors, and geometric constraints, have been implemented to address this challenge. Latest diffusion-based methods have demonstrated substantial improvements by generating novel views from new camera poses to augment training data, surpassing earlier regulari

infographic.key_insight: GaMO uses geometry-aware multi-view diffusion outpainting to synthesize consistent novel views from sparse inputs, enabling substantially better 3D reconstruction when few camera views are available.
infographic.problem_solved: Improves 3D scene capture quality under sparse-view conditions by generating geometrically consistent additional views to augment reconstruction pipelines.
method: Geometry-aware diffusion outpainting conditioned on sparse input images and camera poses to synthesize large-field novel views beyond observed pixels.
Multi-view consistency enforced via geometric priors (pose/depth/epipolar-aware conditioning) so generated views align with real scene geometry.
Use synthesized views to augment training or inference for downstream 3D reconstruction (e.g., MVS/NeRF), improving completeness and fidelity from few inputs.
infographic.impact: Enables high-quality 3D reconstruction with far fewer captures, lowering acquisition cost and expanding applicability to AR/VR, robotics, and cultural heritage where dense imaging is impractical.

title: Reusability report: Optimizing T count in general quantum circuits with AlphaTensor-Quantum
authors: Remmy Zen, Maximilian Nägele, Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 31 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01166-9

The reusability of AlphaTensor-Quantum is tested and the method is extended to optimize a broad range of quantum circuits without retraining, achieving greater T-count reductions and demonstrating generalizable and efficient quantum circuit optimization.

infographic.key_insight: AlphaTensor-Quantum can be reused without retraining to optimize T-count across a broad range of quantum circuits, achieving larger T-count reductions and demonstrating generalizable, efficient circuit optimization.
infographic.problem_solved: High T-counts in quantum circuits drive up error-correction overhead and resource costs; many ML-based optimizers require retraining for new circuit families. This work removes the need for retraining while delivering substantial T-count savings across diverse circuits.
method: Reuse and extend the pre-trained AlphaTensor-Quantum model as a transfer/zero-shot optimizer to tackle new circuit families without retraining.
Apply model-guided decomposition and rewrite strategies to identify T-gate–efficient circuit transformations and rewrite sequences.
Systematic benchmarking across diverse circuit types to quantify T-count reductions and validate generalizability and efficiency.
infographic.impact: Reducing T-counts without retraining lowers fault-tolerant resource requirements and accelerates deployment of quantum algorithms; practitioners can integrate pre-trained AI models into compilation flows to get immediate gains without costly retraining.

title: Assessing the potential of deep learning for protein–ligand docking
authors: Alex Morehead, Nabin Giri, Jian Liu, Pawan Neupane, Jianlin Cheng
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 31 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01160-1

Morehead et al. introduce the benchmark PoseBench and evaluate the strengths and limitations of current AI-based protein–ligand docking and structure prediction methods.

infographic.key_insight: A standardized benchmark (PoseBench) reveals where current deep-learning protein–ligand docking and structure-prediction methods succeed and systematically where they fail, quantifying strengths in pose recovery but exposing limits in scoring, ligand flexibility handling, and generalization to novel targets.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a comprehensive, standardized benchmark and failure-mode analysis for AI-based protein–ligand docking, enabling fair comparison and revealing practical weaknesses that hinder real-world drug-discovery workflows.
method: Introduce PoseBench: a curated, diverse benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol for protein–ligand docking and structure prediction.
Evaluate multiple state-of-the-art AI-based docking and structure-prediction methods across standardized metrics (pose accuracy, ranking/scoring, robustness to ligand/protein diversity).
Perform systematic failure-mode analysis to identify common error sources (e.g., ligand flexibility, binding-site conformational changes, scoring miscalibration).
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a clear, quantitative roadmap for improving docking models and prioritizing research (better scoring functions, handling of flexibility, domain generalization), accelerating reliable model development for drug discovery.

Attention-like mechanisms produce edge-level influence scores that quantify neighbour impact on a receiver cell’s gene expression.
Lightweight architecture optimized for interpretability and scalability to large spatial transcriptomics datasets.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a practical, interpretable tool to model spatial cell interactions, enabling biologically meaningful downstream analyses (e.g., cell communication, microenvironment effects) while remaining computationally efficient.

title: On the geometry and topology of representations: the manifolds of modular addition
authors: Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja, Gavin McCracken, Harley Wiltzer, Vincent Létourneau, Colin Daniels
abstract: The Clock and Pizza interpretations, associated with architectures differing in either uniform or learnable attention, were introduced to argue that different architectural designs can yield distinct circuits for modular addition. In this work, we show that this is not the case, and that both uniform attention and trainable attention architectures implement the same algorithm via topologically and geometrically equivalent representations. Our methodology goes beyond the interpretation of individ

infographic.key_insight: Architectural differences in attention (uniform vs. trainable) do not produce fundamentally different algorithms for modular addition: both produce topologically and geometrically equivalent representation manifolds, implementing the same underlying computation.
infographic.problem_solved: Resolving a debate from the Clock vs. Pizza interpretations about whether different attention designs necessarily yield distinct circuits and representations for modular addition.
method: Compare the Clock and Pizza interpretation frameworks across architectures with uniform and learnable attention to identify representational correspondences.
Analyze the geometry and topology of learned activation manifolds (e.g., manifold shape, continuity, and mapping) to test equivalence claims.
Use alignment and invariance tests (empirical manifold comparisons and circuit-level mapping) to demonstrate the same algorithmic implementation.
infographic.impact: Shows that interpretability conclusions about algorithmic differences should account for geometric/topological equivalence, simplifying how practitioners reason about architecture choices and transfer of learned circuits across attention variants.

title: SpaceTimePilot: Generative Rendering of Dynamic Scenes Across Space and Time
authors: Zhening Huang, Hyeonho Jeong, Xuelin Chen, Yulia Gryaditskaya, Tuanfeng Y. Wang
abstract: We present SpaceTimePilot, a video diffusion model that disentangles space and time for controllable generative rendering. Given a monocular video, SpaceTimePilot can independently alter the camera viewpoint and the motion sequence within the generative process, re-rendering the scene for continuous and arbitrary exploration across space and time. To achieve this, we introduce an effective animation time-embedding mechanism in the diffusion process, allowing explicit control of the output video'

infographic.key_insight: SpaceTimePilot separates spatial (viewpoint) and temporal (motion) factors inside a video diffusion model, enabling independent, continuous control of camera viewpoint and motion sequence from a single monocular video.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing generative video methods often entangle camera motion and scene dynamics, limiting the ability to re-render a scene under new viewpoints or altered motion trajectories from a single monocular capture.
method: Design a video diffusion model that explicitly disentangles space and time representations so they can be manipulated separately during generation.
Introduce an animation time-embedding mechanism in the diffusion process to provide explicit, continuous control over the output motion sequence.
Condition the model on a monocular input video and a view specification to re-render the scene at arbitrary viewpoints while independently editing temporal dynamics.
infographic.impact: Enables fine-grained, controllable re-rendering and editing of dynamic scenes from simple monocular footage, useful for view synthesis, video editing, AR/VR content creation, and data augmentation for downstream models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input monocular video -> disentanglement module (space vs time) -> diffusion model with time-embedding -> output varying viewpoints and motions.

title: Harnessing the power of single-cell large language models with parameter-efficient fine-tuning using scPEFT
authors: Fei He, Ruixin Fei, Jordan E. Krull, Yang Yu, Xinyu Zhang
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 31 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01170-z

He et al. present a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for single-cell language models that improves performance on unseen diseases, treatments and cell types.

infographic.key_insight: scPEFT introduces a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy that adapts large language models to single-cell transcriptomic data, substantially improving generalization to unseen diseases, treatments, and cell types while only updating a small fraction of model parameters.
infographic.problem_solved: Full fine-tuning of large models for single-cell tasks is compute- and data-intensive and often fails to generalize to novel biological conditions; scPEFT enables effective adaptation with far lower resource cost and better out-of-distribution performance.
method: Introduce scPEFT: a parameter-efficient fine-tuning scheme that modifies a small subset of model parameters (e.g., adapters/low-rank updates) to specialize LLMs for single-cell transcriptomic inputs.
Train on diverse single-cell datasets using biologically framed prompts and objectives, then evaluate transfer to unseen diseases, treatments, and cell types to assess OOD generalization.
Compare scPEFT against full fine-tuning and other PEFT baselines, demonstrating superior generalization and reduced compute/memory requirements.
infographic.impact: scPEFT lets researchers and practitioners adapt large language models to single-cell biology with lower cost and better robustness to novel conditions, accelerating model deployment for discovery and translational applications.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram showing a frozen large language model with small scPEFT modules (adapters/low-rank updates) inserted—highlighting parameter savings.
Bar chart comparing performance on unseen diseases/treatments/cell types: scPEFT vs full fine-tuning vs other PEFT methods.
UMAP/t-SNE of cell embeddings before and after scPEFT showing improved separation and transfer of novel cell states.
Resource-efficiency infographic (memory, GPU hours, % parameters updated) contrasting scPEFT with full fine-tuning.

title: ImmunoStruct enables multimodal deep learning for immunogenicity prediction
authors: Kevin Bijan Givechian, João Felipe Rocha, Chen Liu, Edward Yang, Sidharth Tyagi
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 31 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01163-y

A multimodal deep learning model combines molecular sequence, structure and biochemical properties to predict immunogenicity in an interpretable way, providing a framework for smarter molecular prediction and hypothesis generation.

infographic.key_insight: ImmunoStruct integrates molecular sequence, 3D structure, and biochemical features into a single multimodal deep learning model to predict immunogenicity with interpretable outputs, enabling hypothesis-driven molecular design.
infographic.problem_solved: Predicting immunogenicity is challenging because it depends on complex, interacting sequence, structural, and biochemical signals that single-modality models miss and are often uninterpretable for downstream experimental design.
method: Multimodal architecture that fuses sequence embeddings, 3D structural representations, and computed biochemical descriptors into a joint latent space.
Supervised training on curated experimental immunogenicity datasets with attention/saliency modules to provide per-residue and per-feature interpretability.
Benchmarking against unimodal baselines and providing case studies mapping model attributions onto molecular structures for hypothesis generation.
infographic.impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ImmunoStruct demonstrates how multimodal fusion plus interpretability can improve predictive accuracy and actionable insight for bio-molecular design, accelerating vaccine and therapeutic discovery pipelines.

title: MAMA-Memeia! Multi-Aspect Multi-Agent Collaboration for Depressive Symptoms Identification in Memes
authors: Siddhant Agarwal, Adya Dhuler, Polly Ruhnke, Melvin Speisman, Md Shad Akhtar
abstract: Over the past years, memes have evolved from being exclusively a medium of humorous exchanges to one that allows users to express a range of emotions freely and easily. With the ever-growing utilization of memes in expressing depressive sentiments, we conduct a study on identifying depressive symptoms exhibited by memes shared by users of online social media platforms. We introduce RESTOREx as a vital resource for detecting depressive symptoms in memes on social media through the Large Language

infographic.key_insight: A multi-aspect, multi-agent framework effectively combines specialized reasoning about text, visual cues, and contextual signals to identify depressive symptoms in memes, supported by the new RESTOREx resource for training and evaluation.
infographic.problem_solved: Detecting depressive symptoms conveyed via multimodal memes — which mix images, overlaid text, sarcasm, and cultural context — where single-stream models often miss subtle, multi-aspect signals.
method: Multi-aspect decomposition: break meme interpretation into complementary aspects (e.g., literal text, visual sentiment, humor/sarcasm, contextual cues).
Multi-agent collaboration: deploy specialized agents (or modules) to analyze each aspect and aggregate their judgments via a coordination/ensemble mechanism.
Benchmarking on RESTOREx: curate and use a multimodal dataset/resource for supervised training and evaluation, with large language models or multimodal encoders as reasoners.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical architecture and dataset for more accurate, interpretable multimodal mental-health screening in social media content, enabling AI/ML teams to build safer, more sensitive monitoring tools and to study cross-aspect reasoning in multimodal models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing multiple specialist agents (text, vision, sarcasm/context) feeding into a central aggregator
Annotated meme examples illustrating how each agent labels different aspects (text sentiment, visual cues, implicit depression signals)

title: Vulcan: Instance-Optimal Systems Heuristics Through LLM-Driven Search
authors: Rohit Dwivedula, Divyanshu Saxena, Sujay Yadalam, Daehyeok Kim, Aditya Akella
abstract:
Resource-management tasks in modern operating and distributed systems continue to rely primarily on hand-designed heuristics for tasks such as scheduling, caching, or active queue management. Designing performant heuristics is an expensive, time-consuming process that we are forced to continuously go through due to the constant flux of hardware, workloads and environments.
  We propose a new alternative: synthesizing instance-optimal heuristics -- specialized for the exact workloads and hardware

infographic.key_insight: Large language models can drive a search-and-evaluate loop to synthesize instance-optimal, workload- and hardware-specialized heuristics automatically, replacing brittle hand-designed rules with per-instance high-performance policies.
infographic.problem_solved: Designing and continuously tuning resource-management heuristics (scheduling, caching, AQM, etc.) is costly and brittle as hardware, workloads, and environments change; the paper automates creation of heuristics tailored to each instance.
method: Use an LLM to generate candidate heuristic implementations (pseudo-code or code) conditioned on workload and hardware characteristics.
Evaluate candidates with a performance-guided search loop (simulate or measure on-target), use results to refine prompts / selection, and iterate to converge on instance-optimal heuristics.
Compile/validate the selected heuristic and deploy it to the system, optionally with fallback/safety checks.
infographic.impact: Practitioners get automated, per-instance tuned policies that improve resource utilization and performance while cutting developer effort and time-to-deploy for system-level optimizations.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the LLM-driven loop: workload+hardware → LLM generates heuristics → performance evaluator → feedback → final deployable heuristic
Bar chart comparing performance (latency, throughput, drop rate) of instance-optimal heuristics vs. common hand-designed heuristics across several workloads
Heatmap showing performance gains across combinations of workloads and hardware configurations

title: Current-diffusion model for metasurface structure discoveries with spatial-frequency dynamics
authors: Erji Li, Yusong Wang, Lei Jin, Zheng Zong, Enze Zhu
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 31 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01162-z

Metasurface design driven by AI faces challenges, such as extrapolation to unexplored performance regimes. MetaAI, a physics-aware current-diffusion framework, is introduced to advance metamaterial discovery from interpolation to extrapolation.

infographic.key_insight: MetaAI introduces a physics-aware current-diffusion framework that models spatial–frequency dynamics of electromagnetic currents to discover metasurface structures that generalize beyond the training distribution, enabling reliable extrapolation to new performance regimes.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the limited extrapolation of data-driven metasurface design methods by embedding electromagnetic current dynamics and spatial–frequency priors, so designs remain valid and performant outside previously observed regimes.
method: Physics-aware diffusion operating on current distributions: a generative diffusion process evolves electromagnetic current maps rather than raw geometry, enforcing physically meaningful states.
Spatial–frequency coupling: dynamics link structural geometry and frequency response so the model learns how changes in geometry map to spectral behaviour across frequencies.
Guided generation and selection: the framework produces candidate metasurface patterns and evaluates them with embedded physical constraints to extrapolate to novel target performances.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a pathway to incorporate physical priors into generative models, improving generalization, trustworthiness, and sample efficiency when designing electromagnetic and other physics-governed systems.

Spatial–frequency map visualization showing how a single geometry maps to frequency responses and how the model shifts that mapping for extrapolation

title: Coordinated Humanoid Manipulation with Choice Policies
authors: Haozhi Qi, Yen-Jen Wang, Toru Lin, Brent Yi, Yi Ma
abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise for operating in human-centric environments, yet achieving robust whole-body coordination across the head, hands, and legs remains a major challenge. We present a system that combines a modular teleoperation interface with a scalable learning framework to address this problem. Our teleoperation design decomposes humanoid control into intuitive submodules, which include hand-eye coordination, grasp primitives, arm end-effector tracking, and locomotion. This modu

infographic.key_insight: Decomposing humanoid control into intuitive submodules and training a scalable learning layer of "choice policies" enables robust, coordinated whole-body manipulation across head, hands, and legs with teleoperation-friendly interfaces.
infographic.problem_solved: Enables reliable whole-body coordination for humanoid robots in human-centric environments by addressing the complexity of simultaneously controlling head, arms/hands, and locomotion.
method: Design a modular teleoperation interface that breaks control into submodules: hand–eye coordination, grasp primitives, arm end-effector tracking, and locomotion.
Train a scalable learning framework of choice policies that selects and coordinates submodules to produce smooth, context-aware whole-body actions.
Integrate teleoperation data and policy learning to allow intuitive human control while enabling autonomous switching and refined behaviors.
infographic.impact: Makes whole-body humanoid manipulation more scalable, interpretable, and practical for deployment—reducing operator burden and improving robustness for real-world tasks in robotics and ML research.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: modular teleoperation interface mapped to choice-policy layer and robot actuators (head, arms, legs).
Flowchart: decision-making by choice policies selecting submodules (e.g., grasp vs locomotion) during a manipulation task.

authors: Daniella Bar-Lev, Itai Orr, Omer Sabary, Tuvi Etzion, Eitan Yaakobi

Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 30 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01175-8

Author Correction: Scalable and robust DNA-based storage via coding theory and deep learning
