(Note: this item is an author correction to the original paper; summary reflects the corrected framing of the work.)
infographic.problem_solved: How to make DNA data storage scalable and robust against synthesis, storage and sequencing errors so it can be practical for large-scale archival use.
method: Design of error-resilient encoding schemes from coding theory tailored to DNA constraints (GC content, homopolymers, addressability).
Deep-learning models trained to model channel noise and perform sequence-level error correction / reconstruction from noisy sequencing reads.
An integrated end-to-end pipeline that maps digital data → constrained DNA codewords → physical DNA → sequencing → DL-assisted decoding, validated across scaling scenarios.
infographic.impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a cross-disciplinary blueprint: noisy-channel modeling and learned decoders can materially improve molecular data storage systems, opening opportunities for ML-driven error correction, simulation, and optimization in wet-lab pipelines.

title: OmniAgent: Audio-Guided Active Perception Agent for Omnimodal Audio-Video Understanding
authors: Keda Tao, Wenjie Du, Bohan Yu, Weiqiang Wang, Jian Liu
abstract: Omnimodal large language models have made significant strides in unifying audio and visual modalities; however, they often lack the fine-grained cross-modal understanding and have difficulty with multimodal alignment. To address these limitations, we introduce OmniAgent, a fully audio-guided active perception agent that dynamically orchestrates specialized tools to achieve more fine-grained audio-visual reasoning. Unlike previous works that rely on rigid, static workflows and dense frame-caption

infographic.key_insight: OmniAgent uses audio cues as a driving signal to actively control perception and orchestrate specialized tools, enabling finer-grained audio–visual alignment and reasoning than static omnimodal LLM pipelines.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses poor cross-modal alignment and coarse multimodal reasoning in existing omnimodal models, and the inefficiency and brittleness of rigid, dense frame-captioning workflows.
method: Fully audio-guided active perception: the agent uses sound events to trigger targeted sensing and analysis instead of processing dense video frames.
Dynamic orchestration of specialized tools (e.g., targeted frame sampling, object/scene localizers, temporal reasoners) in a closed feedback loop with the omnimodal model.
Relevance- or uncertainty-driven selection to focus computation on salient audio-correlated visual regions, improving alignment and downstream reasoning.
infographic.impact: Enables more accurate, efficient, and interpretable audio–visual understanding systems by focusing perception where audio indicates importance, benefiting multimodal model deployment and evaluation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: audio input → OmniAgent controller → toolset (frame sampler, detector, temporal reasoner) → fused omnimodal understanding

title: Training AI Co-Scientists Using Rubric Rewards
authors: Shashwat Goel, Rishi Hazra, Dulhan Jayalath, Timon Willi, Parag Jain
abstract: AI co-scientists are emerging as a tool to assist human researchers in achieving their research goals. A crucial feature of these AI co-scientists is the ability to generate a research plan given a set of aims and constraints. The plan may be used by researchers for brainstorming, or may even be implemented after further refinement. However, language models currently struggle to generate research plans that follow all constraints and implicit requirements. In this work, we study how to leverage

infographic.key_insight: Introducing structured 'rubric rewards' to train language models produces research plans that better satisfy explicit constraints and implicit requirements, improving reliability of AI co‑scientists in planning tasks.
infographic.problem_solved: Language models often generate research plans that ignore constraints or miss implicit requirements; this work addresses how to teach models to produce constraint‑compliant, high‑quality plans suitable for researcher use or implementation.
method: Design explicit rubrics that decompose desirable plan qualities (constraint adherence, feasibility, novelty, clarity) into measurable criteria.
Convert rubric scores into reward signals and use reward‑aware training (e.g., reward modeling + policy fine‑tuning / RLHF style updates) to bias the model toward rubric‑aligned outputs.
Evaluate with human raters and automatic metrics on constraint adherence, plan quality, and downstream implementability.
infographic.impact: Rubric rewards make AI co‑scientists more dependable collaborators by aligning plan generation with researcher expectations and constraints, reducing manual post‑editing and improving adoption in research workflows.

title: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
authors: Baixuan Li, Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Kuan Li, Zhongwang Zhang
abstract: Information-seeking (IS) agents have achieved strong performance across a range of wide and deep search tasks, yet their tool use remains largely restricted to API-level snippet retrieval and URL-based page fetching, limiting access to the richer information available through real browsing. While full browser interaction could unlock deeper capabilities, its fine-grained control and verbose page content returns introduce substantial complexity for ReAct-style function-calling agents. To bridge t

infographic.key_insight: Decompose full browser interaction into nested layers of decision-making and observation compression so agents can perform rich, fine‑grained web actions without being overwhelmed by verbose page content.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between lightweight API/URL retrieval and full browser control by addressing the complexity and verbosity that break ReAct-style function-calling agents during deep web information-seeking.
method: Nested/hierarchical agent design: a high-level planner issues goals, mid-level modules choose browsing subgoals, and low-level controllers emit DOM-level actions.
Intermediate compression and abstraction: summarize or extract salient page content into compact observations to reduce bandwidth and decision noise for the policy.

Tool and training wrappers: present browser capabilities as structured, learnable primitives (click, scroll, extract, follow link) and train via imitation/agentic learning to coordinate nested modules.
infographic.impact: Enables agents to leverage the full richness of real browsing for deeper, multi-step information tasks while remaining robust and efficient; practical for building stronger web-capable assistants and search agents.

Flowchart of an information-seeking episode: query → nested decisions → browser actions → compressed observations → updated plan

title: Stream-DiffVSR: Low-Latency Streamable Video Super-Resolution via Auto-Regressive Diffusion
authors: Hau-Shiang Shiu, Chin-Yang Lin, Zhixiang Wang, Chi-Wei Hsiao, Po-Fan Yu
abstract: Diffusion-based video super-resolution (VSR) methods achieve strong perceptual quality but remain impractical for latency-sensitive settings due to reliance on future frames and expensive multi-step denoising. We propose Stream-DiffVSR, a causally conditioned diffusion framework for efficient online VSR. Operating strictly on past frames, it combines a four-step distilled denoiser for fast inference, an Auto-regressive Temporal Guidance (ARTG) module that injects motion-aligned cues during laten

infographic.key_insight: Stream-DiffVSR makes diffusion-based video super-resolution practical for streaming by combining a causally conditioned diffusion model with a four-step distilled denoiser and an Auto-regressive Temporal Guidance module, enabling high-quality SR using only past frames and very few denoising steps.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes the high latency and future-frame dependency of diffusion VSR methods, enabling online/streamable super-resolution suitable for latency-sensitive applications.
method: Causally conditioned diffusion that operates strictly on past frames to enable online/streaming processing.
Four-step distilled denoiser for fast, low-step inference while retaining diffusion-quality perceptual results.
Auto-regressive Temporal Guidance (ARTG) that injects motion-aligned cues from previous frames/outputs to preserve temporal consistency without future-frame access.
infographic.impact: Makes diffusion-quality video super-resolution feasible in real-time and edge scenarios (live streaming, video calls, on-device enhancement) by drastically reducing inference time and removing dependence on future frames, lowering the barrier to practical deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: causal input stream → ARTG module → 4-step distilled denoiser → output, with arrows showing no future-frame access

title: BOAD: Discovering Hierarchical Software Engineering Agents via Bandit Optimization
authors: Iris Xu, Guangtao Zeng, Zexue He, Charles Jin, Aldo Pareja
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong reasoning and coding capabilities, yet they struggle to generalize to real-world software engineering (SWE) problems that are long-horizon and out of distribution. Existing systems often rely on a single agent to handle the entire workflow-interpreting issues, navigating large codebases, and implementing fixes-within one reasoning chain. Such monolithic designs force the model to retain irrelevant context, leading to spurious correlations and poor g

infographic.key_insight: BOAD automatically discovers a hierarchy of specialized software-engineering agents and uses bandit optimization to compose and adapt them, yielding better generalization on long-horizon, out-of-distribution coding tasks than monolithic single-agent chains.
infographic.problem_solved: Monolithic LLM agents struggle with long-horizon, real-world software engineering: they retain irrelevant context, learn spurious correlations, and fail to generalize across large, complex codebases and multi-step workflows.
method: Decompose the SWE workflow into modular roles and instantiate specialist agents for sub-tasks (e.g., issue interpretation, code navigation, patch generation).
Use bandit optimization to discover and adapt hierarchical agent compositions and routing policies that maximize task-level performance.
Evaluate agents through interaction with large codebases and long-horizon benchmarks to select robust, generalizable hierarchies.
infographic.impact: Modular, automatically optimized agent hierarchies reduce brittleness and improve success on complex software tasks, enabling more reliable AI-assisted coding and scalable workflows for ML and engineering teams.
visual_elements: Hierarchy diagram showing top-level controller agent routing to specialized sub-agents (interpret → search → implement → test).
Flowchart of bandit optimization loop: propose agent composition → evaluate on task → update selection policy.

title: Rethinking the Spatio-Temporal Alignment of End-to-End 3D Perception
authors: Xiaoyu Li, Peidong Li, Xian Wu, Long Shi, Dedong Liu
abstract: Spatio-temporal alignment is crucial for temporal modeling of end-to-end (E2E) perception in autonomous driving (AD), providing valuable structural and textural prior information. Existing methods typically rely on the attention mechanism to align objects across frames, simplifying the motion model with a unified explicit physical model (constant velocity, etc.). These approaches prefer semantic features for implicit alignment, challenging the importance of explicit motion modeling in the tradit

infographic.key_insight: Spatio-temporal alignment for end-to-end 3D perception should combine explicit motion priors with attention-based semantic alignment, rather than relying on attention alone or an oversimplified unified physical model.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses unreliable cross-frame alignment in end-to-end 3D perception for autonomous driving, where attention-only approaches and simplistic motion models lose structural and textural priors needed for stable temporal modeling.
method: Diagnose limitations of attention-only alignment and of using a single simplified physical motion model across scenes.
Introduce a hybrid spatio-temporal alignment strategy that fuses explicit motion priors (physical/kinematic cues) with attention-driven semantic feature matching.
Integrate the hybrid alignment into an end-to-end 3D perception pipeline for autonomous driving and evaluate its effect on temporal consistency and object localization across frames.
infographic.impact: Improves temporal robustness and alignment fidelity in E2E 3D perception, helping practitioners build more reliable detection/tracking models for autonomous driving without over-relying on one alignment mechanism.

title: RoboMirror: Understand Before You Imitate for Video to Humanoid Locomotion
authors: Zhe Li, Cheng Chi, Yangyang Wei, Boan Zhu, Tao Huang
abstract: Humans learn locomotion through visual observation, interpreting visual content first before imitating actions. However, state-of-the-art humanoid locomotion systems rely on either curated motion capture trajectories or sparse text commands, leaving a critical gap between visual understanding and control. Text-to-motion methods suffer from semantic sparsity and staged pipeline errors, while video-based approaches only perform mechanical pose mimicry without genuine visual understanding. We propo

infographic.key_insight: RoboMirror introduces an explicit visual-understanding stage before imitation, extracting semantic intent from videos and using those semantics to drive humanoid locomotion—shifting from mechanical pose-mimicry to intent-driven control.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between raw video observations and robust humanoid locomotion by overcoming semantic sparsity and staged-pipeline errors in text-based or pose-only imitation methods, enabling learning from in-the-wild videos rather than curated mocap or sparse text commands.
method: Visual understanding module: parse input video into semantic locomotion intents/affordances (e.g., speed, stepping pattern, obstacles) rather than raw pose sequences.
Intent-conditioned controller: train a humanoid policy that maps semantic representations to dynamically feasible locomotion actions, closing perception-to-control loop.
Joint training/transfer: align visual semantics and control via imitation/reinforcement learning to improve robustness and reduce staging errors from separate pipelines.
infographic.impact: Enables practitioners to train humanoid controllers from unconstrained video data with more natural, adaptable behaviors; reduces dependence on mocap datasets and brittle text prompts, improving real-world applicability of video-to-motion systems.

title: Eliciting Behaviors in Multi-Turn Conversations
authors: Jing Huang, Shujian Zhang, Lun Wang, Andrew Hard, Rajiv Mathews
abstract: Identifying specific and often complex behaviors from large language models (LLMs) in conversational settings is crucial for their evaluation. Recent work proposes novel techniques to find natural language prompts that induce specific behaviors from a target model, yet they are mainly studied in single-turn settings. In this work, we study behavior elicitation in the context of multi-turn conversations. We first offer an analytical framework that categorizes existing methods into three families

infographic.key_insight: The paper extends behavior elicitation from single-turn prompts to multi-turn conversations by introducing an analytical framework that categorizes existing elicitation methods into three families and clarifies how conversational context changes model behaviors.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of reliably inducing and evaluating specific, often complex behaviors from large language models within multi-turn dialogues—where prompt history and turn structure alter elicitation effectiveness and are not captured by single-turn studies.
method: Develop an analytical framework that organizes existing elicitation techniques into three families (taxonomy) to clarify their assumptions and mechanisms.
Systematically analyze how multi-turn context and turn dynamics affect the success of behavior elicitation across models and behaviors.
Use the framework to identify gaps, comparative strengths of methods, and practical diagnostics or guidelines for constructing multi-turn prompts and evaluations.
infographic.impact: Provides researchers and practitioners a principled way to design, compare, and evaluate prompt-based interventions in conversational settings—improving robustness of testing, alignment, and control for deployed dialogue agents.

title: Versatile cardiovascular signal generation with a unified diffusion transformer
authors: Zehua Chen, Yuyang Miao, Liyuan Wang, Luyun Fan, Danilo P. Mandic
abstract:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 29 December 2025; doi:10.1038/s42256-025-01147-y

UniCardio is a unified framework for versatile multimodal cardiovascular signal generation, enabling robust signal restoration and cross-modal translation to detect abnormal conditions and estimate vital signs in real-time health monitoring.

infographic.key_insight: UniCardio is a unified diffusion-transformer framework that generates and translates multimodal cardiovascular signals, enabling robust restoration of corrupted channels and real-time vital-sign estimation from heterogeneous inputs.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a single generative model that can reliably restore, translate between, and synthesize multiple cardiovascular signal modalities (e.g., ECG, PPG, PCG) under noise, missing channels, and real-time constraints.
method: A unified diffusion-based generative model with transformer temporal modeling to capture long-range dependencies across multimodal cardiovascular signals.

Conditional generation and cross-modal translation mechanisms that enable restoration of corrupted/missing channels and conversion between modalities, trained with multi-task losses that preserve clinical signal fidelity.
Optimized inference pipeline for low-latency sampling and incorporation of physiological constraints to support real-time vital-sign estimation and downstream abnormality detection.
infographic.impact: Provides ML practitioners a versatile tool for signal imputation, data augmentation, and cross-modal translation in clinical and wearable monitoring contexts, improving robustness of downstream diagnostics and enabling privacy-preserving synthetic datasets.

title: Web World Models
authors: Jichen Feng, Yifan Zhang, Chenggong Zhang, Yifu Lu, Shilong Liu
abstract: Language agents increasingly require persistent worlds in which they can act, remember, and learn. Existing approaches sit at two extremes: conventional web frameworks provide reliable but fixed contexts backed by databases, while fully generative world models aim for unlimited environments at the expense of controllability and practical engineering. In this work, we introduce the Web World Model (WWM), a middle ground where world state and ``physics'' are implemented in ordinary web code to ens

infographic.key_insight: Web World Model (WWM) encodes persistent world state and physics as ordinary web code, providing a middle ground that is more controllable and engineering-friendly than fully generative worlds while more flexible than fixed database-backed web apps.
infographic.problem_solved: Bridges the gap between rigid, reliable web frameworks and unlimited but hard-to-control generative world models, enabling language agents to act, remember, and learn in persistent, debuggable, and configurable environments.
method: Implement world state and dynamics using standard web technologies (HTML/CSS/JavaScript and backend services) so environments are inspectable and programmable.
Expose interactions through web APIs, DOM events, and conventional web interfaces so language agents can perceive and act using familiar web paradigms.
Combine deterministic engineering primitives (persistence, transactional updates, logging) with configurable generative components to support variability, learning, and reproducible experiments.
infographic.impact: WWM makes it practical to build agent environments that are persistent, observable, and reproducible, reducing engineering friction and improving controllability for research and deployed language-agent systems.

title: Diffusion Knows Transparency: Repurposing Video Diffusion for Transparent Object Depth and Normal Estimation
authors: Shaocong Xu, Songlin Wei, Qizhe Wei, Zheng Geng, Hong Li
abstract: Transparent objects remain notoriously hard for perception systems: refraction, reflection and transmission break the assumptions behind stereo, ToF and purely discriminative monocular depth, causing holes and temporally unstable estimates. Our key observation is that modern video diffusion models already synthesize convincing transparent phenomena, suggesting they have internalized the optical rules. We build TransPhy3D, a synthetic video corpus of transparent/reflective scenes: 11k sequences r

infographic.key_insight: Pretrained video diffusion models have implicitly learned optical rules of transparency (refraction, reflection, transmission); by repurposing these models and training on a synthetic transparent/reflective video corpus, we can recover accurate depth and surface normals for transparent objects.
infographic.problem_solved: Traditional depth sensors and discriminative monocular models fail on transparent and reflective objects—producing holes, wrong values and temporally unstable estimates—this work tackles reliable depth and normal estimation for transparent/reflective scenes.
method: Construct TransPhy3D: a large synthetic video corpus of transparent and reflective scenes (≈11k sequences) to expose models to realistic transparent phenomena.
Repurpose pretrained video diffusion models as geometric priors—extracting or conditioning on internal representations to infer dense depth and surface normals for transparent objects.
Train/finetune a geometry prediction head with temporal consistency constraints so outputs are dense, accurate and temporally stable across video frames.
infographic.impact: Makes robust 3D perception of transparent and reflective objects practical for applications like robotics, AR/VR and 3D reconstruction by filling gaps left by stereo/ToF and standard monocular methods, improving accuracy and temporal stability.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison: input RGB video → baseline depth (holes/artifacts) → TransPhy3D+diffusion depth & normals

title: Memorization in 3D Shape Generation: An Empirical Study
authors: Shu Pu, Boya Zeng, Kaichen Zhou, Mengyu Wang, Zhuang Liu
abstract: Generative models are increasingly used in 3D vision to synthesize novel shapes, yet it remains unclear whether their generation relies on memorizing training shapes. Understanding their memorization could help prevent training data leakage and improve the diversity of generated results. In this paper, we design an evaluation framework to quantify memorization in 3D generative models and study the influence of different data and modeling designs on memorization. We first apply our framework to q

infographic.key_insight: A quantitative evaluation framework reveals that 3D generative models can and do memorize training shapes under many common settings; memorization rises with limited data and high model capacity but is reducible via augmentation and regularization.
infographic.problem_solved: Provides the first systematic, measurable way to detect and quantify memorization in 3D shape generators, addressing risks of training-data leakage and lack of generative diversity.
method: Design a memorization evaluation pipeline using 3D-aware similarity metrics (e.g., Chamfer Distance, EMD, IoU) and nearest-neighbor retrieval plus novelty/coverage statistics.
Perform controlled experiments varying dataset size, model capacity/architecture, and training choices (augmentations, regularizers, objectives) to measure their effect on memorization.
Combine quantitative thresholds with qualitative side-by-side comparisons to identify and categorize memorized vs. truly novel generated shapes.
infographic.impact: Gives practitioners a practical toolkit to detect and mitigate data leakage in 3D generative pipelines and to tune models for better novelty–fidelity trade-offs, improving safety and generative diversity.

title: AI tutoring can safely and effectively support students: An exploratory RCT in UK classrooms
authors: LearnLM Team, Eedi, :, Albert Wang, Aliya Rysbek
abstract: One-to-one tutoring is widely considered the gold standard for personalized education, yet it remains prohibitively expensive to scale. To evaluate whether generative AI might help expand access to this resource, we conducted an exploratory randomized controlled trial (RCT) with $N = 165$ students across five UK secondary schools. We integrated LearnLM -- a generative AI model fine-tuned for pedagogy -- into chat-based tutoring sessions on the Eedi mathematics platform. In the RCT, expert tutors

infographic.key_insight: An exploratory randomized controlled trial (N=165, five UK secondary schools) indicates that LearnLM — a generative model fine-tuned for pedagogy and deployed via chat-based tutoring on the Eedi platform — can support students safely and effectively in classroom math instruction.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the scalability gap of one-to-one personalized tutoring by exploring whether generative AI can provide effective, safe, and classroom-ready tutoring support.
method: Conducted an exploratory RCT with 165 students across five UK secondary schools using integrated chat-based tutoring on the Eedi mathematics platform.
Deployed LearnLM, a generative model fine-tuned for pedagogy, to run tutoring sessions alongside classroom instruction and monitoring.
Evaluated outcomes and safety through classroom deployment and controlled comparison (pre/post and between-group measures) to assess learning impact and potential risks.
infographic.impact: Provides evidence that pedagogy-focused fine-tuning plus careful classroom evaluation can yield practical, safe AI tutoring—encouraging ML practitioners to prioritize domain-specific tuning, rigorous field trials (e.g., RCTs), and safety guardrails when building educational models.

title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
authors: Arnuv Tandon, Karan Dalal, Xinhao Li, Daniel Koceja, Marcel Rød
abstract: We formulate long-context language modeling as a problem in continual learning rather than architecture design. Under this formulation, we only use a standard architecture -- a Transformer with sliding-window attention. However, our model continues learning at test time via next-token prediction on the given context, compressing the context it reads into its weights. In addition, we improve the model's initialization for learning at test time via meta-learning at training time. Overall, our meth

infographic.key_insight: Treat long-context language modeling as a continual learning problem: a standard sliding-window Transformer continues learning at test time via next-token prediction to compress context into its weights, with meta-learning at training time to prepare the model for fast adaptation.
infographic.problem_solved: Enables models to effectively use arbitrarily long context without designing new attention architectures or blowing up memory/compute, by adapting model weights on-the-fly to absorb context information.
method: Base model: standard Transformer with sliding-window attention to keep compute and memory bounded.
Test-time training (TTT): continue training on the provided context via next-token prediction so the model ‘compresses’ context into its parameters.
Meta-learning at training time: optimize initialization so the model can rapidly and stably adapt during TTT at inference.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, architecture-agnostic path to scale context length and improve inference-time adaptation using existing models and modest compute, useful for long-document understanding and dynamic contexts.
visual_elements: Two-panel pipeline diagram: (A) meta-training loop optimizing initialization, (B) test-time training loop compressing incoming context into model weights before final prediction.
Comparison chart: performance vs context length for baseline (no TTT) vs sliding-window + TTT, showing sustained gains at long ranges.

title: Look Closer! An Adversarial Parametric Editing Framework for Hallucination Mitigation in VLMs
authors: Jiayu Hu, Beibei Li, Jiangwei Xia, Yanjun Qin, Bing Ji
abstract: While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have garnered increasing attention in the AI community due to their promising practical applications, they exhibit persistent hallucination issues, generating outputs misaligned with visual inputs. Recent studies attribute these hallucinations to VLMs' over-reliance on linguistic priors and insufficient visual feature integration, proposing heuristic decoding calibration strategies to mitigate them. However, the non-trainable nature of these strategies inheren

infographic.key_insight: Introduce a trainable adversarial parametric editing mechanism that actively adjusts VLM behavior to reduce hallucinations by strengthening visual grounding and weakening misleading linguistic priors.
infographic.problem_solved: VLMs frequently produce hallucinated text that is inconsistent with the input image because they over-rely on language priors and insufficiently integrate visual features; this paper targets systematic mitigation of those hallucinations with a trainable, model-editing approach.
method: Parametric editing module: inject a small, learnable edit into the VLM (weights or adapter-like module) that can be optimized without retraining the whole model.
Adversarial training: generate adversarial queries or perturbations that expose hallucination tendencies and optimize the edit to reduce incorrect, non-visual predictions.
Evaluation & calibration: measure hallucination rates before/after the edit using visual-grounding benchmarks and preserve general language/vision performance while reducing hallucinations.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical, trainable way to reduce visual hallucinations in deployed VLMs, improving reliability and safety for vision-language applications without full model retraining.

title: SketchPlay: Intuitive Creation of Physically Realistic VR Content with Gesture-Driven Sketching
authors: Xiangwen Zhang, Xiaowei Dai, Runnan Chen, Xiaoming Chen, Zeke Zexi Hu
abstract: Creating physically realistic content in VR often requires complex modeling tools or predefined 3D models, textures, and animations, which present significant barriers for non-expert users. In this paper, we propose SketchPlay, a novel VR interaction framework that transforms humans' air-drawn sketches and gestures into dynamic, physically realistic scenes, making content creation intuitive and playful like drawing. Specifically, sketches capture the structure and spatial arrangement of objects

infographic.key_insight: SketchPlay converts freehand air-drawn sketches and gestures into dynamic, physically realistic VR scenes in real time, letting users create playable virtual content as easily as drawing.
infographic.problem_solved: Removes the need for complex 3D modeling tools or prebuilt assets by enabling non-expert users to generate physically plausible VR content through intuitive sketching and gestures.
method: Gesture-driven input pipeline: interpret air-drawn strokes and gesture semantics to capture object structure, spatial arrangement, and intended behaviors.
Procedural geometry + physics instantiation: convert sketches into scene geometry and assign physical properties/constraints for real-time simulation.
Immediate feedback loop: real-time rendering and simulation let users iteratively refine sketches and behaviors through natural gestures.
infographic.impact: Makes VR content creation accessible to non-experts and speeds up rapid prototyping of interactive scenes, with implications for HCI, immersive design, and AI-assisted creative tools.

title: Direction Finding with Sparse Arrays Based on Variable Window Size Spatial Smoothing
authors: Wesley S. Leite, Rodrigo C. de Lamare, Yuriy Zakharov, Wei Liu, Martin Haardt
abstract: In this work, we introduce a variable window size (VWS) spatial smoothing framework that enhances coarray-based direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for sparse linear arrays. By compressing the smoothing aperture, the proposed VWS Coarray MUSIC (VWS-CA-MUSIC) and VWS Coarray root-MUSIC (VWS-CA-rMUSIC) algorithms replace part of the perturbed rank-one outer products in the smoothed coarray data with unperturbed low-rank additional terms, increasing the separation between signal and noise subspac

infographic.key_insight: Introducing a variable window size (VWS) spatial smoothing compresses the coarray smoothing aperture and replaces perturbed rank‑one terms with unperturbed low‑rank contributions, improving signal/noise subspace separation and enabling more accurate DOA estimation from sparse arrays.
infographic.problem_solved: Sparse linear arrays and correlated sources produce rank‑deficient or noisy coarray covariance estimates that limit resolution and robustness of MUSIC/root‑MUSIC; the paper addresses insufficient smoothing aperture and perturbed outer‑product terms that degrade DOA performance.
method: Construct coarray covariance from sparse linear array measurements and apply spatial smoothing with a variable window size to effectively compress the smoothing aperture.
Replace certain perturbed rank‑one outer products in the smoothed coarray data with designed unperturbed low‑rank terms to boost separation between signal and noise subspaces.
Implement VWS-CA-MUSIC and VWS-CA-rMUSIC variants (spectral MUSIC and root‑MUSIC) using the modified smoothed coarray covariance for improved DOA estimation.
infographic.impact: Provides higher-resolution, more robust DOA estimates using fewer physical sensors—beneficial for radar, sonar, wireless sensing, and ML pipelines that rely on accurate direction information for localization, tracking, or sensor fusion.

title: See Less, See Right: Bi-directional Perceptual Shaping For Multimodal Reasoning
authors: Shuoshuo Zhang, Yizhen Zhang, Jingjing Fu, Lei Song, Jiang Bian
abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) often benefit from intermediate visual cues, either injected via external tools or generated as latent visual tokens during reasoning, but these mechanisms still overlook fine-grained visual evidence (e.g., polylines in charts), generalize poorly across domains, and incur high inference-time cost. In this paper, we propose Bi-directional Perceptual Shaping (BiPS), which transforms question-conditioned masked views into bidirectional where-to-look signals that

infographic.key_insight: Bi-directional Perceptual Shaping (BiPS) converts question-conditioned masked image views into bidirectional where-to-look signals that focus reasoning on fine-grained visual evidence (e.g., chart polylines) while reducing unnecessary visual processing.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing VLM reasoning either misses fine-grained visual cues, generalizes poorly across domains, or adds high inference-time cost; BiPS addresses all three by selectively shaping perceptual input to emphasize relevant visual details.
method: Generate question-conditioned masked views of the input image to hide irrelevant regions and emphasize candidate evidence.
Produce bidirectional where-to-look signals (visual guidance in both image→reasoning and reasoning→image directions) to steer token extraction and multimodal reasoning toward fine-grained features.
Integrate the perceptual shaping as a lightweight module or latent-token conditioning step to improve accuracy while keeping inference cost low.
infographic.impact: BiPS enables more accurate, efficient multimodal reasoning by capturing fine-grained visual evidence and improving cross-domain generalization — useful for chart understanding, visual question answering, and other VLM applications where detail matters.

title: ProEdit: Inversion-based Editing From Prompts Done Right
authors: Zhi Ouyang, Dian Zheng, Xiao-Ming Wu, Jian-Jian Jiang, Kun-Yu Lin
abstract: Inversion-based visual editing provides an effective and training-free way to edit an image or a video based on user instructions. Existing methods typically inject source image information during the sampling process to maintain editing consistency. However, this sampling strategy overly relies on source information, which negatively affects the edits in the target image (e.g., failing to change the subject's atributes like pose, number, or color as instructed). In this work, we propose ProEdit

infographic.key_insight: ProEdit identifies that over-reliance on injecting source-image information during inversion-based sampling prevents faithful target edits; by controlling how and when source priors are injected and by modulating attention with prompt guidance, it preserves consistency while enabling stronger, correct edits.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing inversion-based prompt editing methods maintain consistency by heavily reintroducing source information during sampling, which inadvertently blocks intended changes (pose, count, color, etc.) in the edited output. ProEdit solves the trade-off between preserving source identity and allowing prompt-driven edits.
method: Prompt-aligned inversion: compute an inversion that separates editable semantic content from fixed source attributes, enabling prompt-conditioned manipulation without retraining.
Adaptive source-injection schedule: reduce or modulate the amount and timing of source information reintroduced during sampling to avoid overpowering the target edit.

Attention- and guidance-modulation: selectively reweight cross-attention and classifier-free guidance according to prompt signals so edits take effect where intended while preserving unrelated source details.
infographic.impact: ProEdit enables reliable, training-free image/video editing from text prompts that both preserves source fidelity and implements stronger, correct edits—useful for content creators, prompt engineers, and researchers working with diffusion-based editing pipelines.

title: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents
authors: Shukai Liu, Jian Yang, Bo Jiang, Yizhi Li, Jinyang Guo
abstract: Agents based on large language models have recently shown strong potential on real-world software engineering (SWE) tasks that require long-horizon interaction with repository-scale codebases. However, most existing agents rely on append-only context maintenance or passively triggered compression heuristics, which often lead to context explosion, semantic drift, and degraded reasoning in long-running interactions. We propose CAT, a new context management paradigm that elevates context maintenanc

infographic.key_insight: Treating context management as an explicit, callable tool (CAT) for LLM-based software-engineering agents enables proactive, semantic-aware pruning and organization of context, preventing context explosion and preserving reasoning quality over long-horizon interactions.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing SWE agents use append-only context or passive compression heuristics that cause context explosion, semantic drift, and degraded reasoning during long-running interactions with large code repositories.
method: Elevate context maintenance to a first-class tool with explicit operations (ingest, retrieve, summarize/compress, prune, and replace) that the agent can call during reasoning.
Use repository-aware indexing and semantic relevance scoring to prioritize and retain high-value context while applying targeted summarization and provenance-aware compression to older material.
Organize memory hierarchically (short-term working context + long-term archive) and apply policy-driven retention to avoid drift and maintain coherency across extended workflows.
infographic.impact: Makes LLM-driven software agents more scalable and reliable for long-horizon engineering tasks across large codebases, reducing error rates and cognitive overload from oversized contexts while improving end-to-end task performance and latency.

title: Yume-1.5: A Text-Controlled Interactive World Generation Model
authors: Xiaofeng Mao, Zhen Li, Chuanhao Li, Xiaojie Xu, Kaining Ying
abstract: Recent approaches have demonstrated the promise of using diffusion models to generate interactive and explorable worlds. However, most of these methods face critical challenges such as excessively large parameter sizes, reliance on lengthy inference steps, and rapidly growing historical context, which severely limit real-time performance and lack text-controlled generation capabilities. To address these challenges, we propose \method, a novel framework designed to generate realistic, interactive

infographic.key_insight: Yume-1.5 presents a compact, text-conditioned diffusion framework that enables fast, interactive world generation by shrinking parameter footprint, accelerating sampling, and bounding historical context for real-time text control.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses large model sizes, long inference times, and unbounded historical context in diffusion-based interactive world generation while adding robust text-controlled content editing.
method: Parameter-efficient diffusion backbone: modular/compact architecture to reduce model size and memory footprint.
Accelerated sampling & inference: algorithmic improvements that cut required diffusion steps for real-time responsiveness.
Bounded context & text conditioning: history-compression or memory module plus cross-attention text control to keep interaction state compact and controllable by text prompts.
infographic.impact: Makes diffusion-based interactive worlds practical for real-time applications (games, simulation, AR/VR) and lowers compute barriers for practitioners building text-driven, explorable environments.

title: LibContinual: A Comprehensive Library towards Realistic Continual Learning
authors: Wenbin Li, Shangge Liu, Borui Kang, Yiyang Chen, KaXuan Lew
abstract: A fundamental challenge in Continual Learning (CL) is catastrophic forgetting, where adapting to new tasks degrades the performance on previous ones. While the field has evolved with diverse methods, this rapid surge in diverse methodologies has culminated in a fragmented research landscape. The lack of a unified framework, including inconsistent implementations, conflicting dependencies, and varying evaluation protocols, makes fair comparison and reproducible research increasingly difficult. To

infographic.key_insight: LibContinual is a unified, extensible library that consolidates implementations, evaluation protocols, and dependencies for continual learning, enabling fair, reproducible comparison across methods.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the fragmentation in continual learning research caused by inconsistent implementations, conflicting dependencies, and varying evaluation protocols that impede reproducibility and fair benchmarking.
method: Modular APIs and standard interfaces for algorithms, datasets, and metrics to ensure consistent implementations and easy swapping of components.
Curated benchmark suite and standardized evaluation pipelines (task streams, memory/replay settings, and metrics) for fair comparison.
Reproducible tooling and integrations (dependency management, experiment scripts, and plugin system) to simplify adoption and extensibility.
infographic.impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare methods, reproduce results, and accelerate development of continual learning systems by removing engineering friction and standardizing evaluation.

authors: Qi Lai, JunYan Li, Qiang Cai, Lei Wang, Tao Yan
abstract: Real-time instance segmentation for spinal endoscopy is important for identifying and protecting critical anatomy during surgery, but it is difficult because of the narrow field of view, specular highlights, smoke/bleeding, unclear boundaries, and large scale changes. Deployment is also constrained by limited surgical hardware, so the model must balance accuracy and speed and remain stable under small-batch (even batch-1) training. We propose LMSF-A, a lightweight multi-scale attention framework

infographic.key_insight: A lightweight multi-scale attention framework (LMSF-A) enables accurate, real-time instance segmentation in challenging spinal endoscopy scenes while remaining stable under small-batch (even batch-1) training and constrained surgical hardware.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses real-time instance segmentation in spinal endoscopy despite narrow field-of-view, specular highlights, smoke/bleeding, unclear boundaries, large scale variation, and strict compute/memory limits of surgical devices.
method: Design a compact backbone with multi-scale attention modules to capture fine details and large-scale context efficiently.
Fuse scale-aware feature maps and a specialized instance segmentation head optimized for low latency on surgical hardware.
Training and inference strategies (normalization and memory/speed optimizations) to ensure stability and accuracy under small-batch or batch-1 regimes.
infographic.impact: Enables practical deployment of robust, low-latency instance segmentation in operating rooms, guiding safer surgical navigation and informing ML practitioners how to balance accuracy, speed, and stability for resource-constrained medical applications.

title: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
authors: Hanzhang Zhou, Xu Zhang, Panrong Tong, Jianan Zhang, Liangyu Chen
abstract: The development of GUI agents could revolutionize the next generation of human-computer interaction. Motivated by this vision, we present MAI-UI, a family of foundation GUI agents spanning the full spectrum of sizes, including 2B, 8B, 32B, and 235B-A22B variants. We identify four key challenges to realistic deployment: the lack of native agent-user interaction, the limits of UI-only operation, the absence of a practical deployment architecture, and brittleness in dynamic environments. MAI-UI add

infographic.key_insight: MAI-UI introduces a family of foundation GUI agents across model scales (2B → 235B-A22B) and a deployment‑oriented design that closes the gap between research prototypes and real‑world GUI agent usage, prioritizing native user interaction and robustness.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses four practical barriers to realistic GUI agent deployment: lack of native agent–user interaction, the limitations of UI‑only operation, absence of a practical deployment architecture, and brittleness in dynamic real‑world environments.
method: Provide a spectrum of foundation GUI agent sizes (2B, 8B, 32B, 235B‑A22B) to match different compute and capability tradeoffs.
Design for real‑world centricity: enable native agent–user interaction and extend beyond UI‑only control (multi‑modal inputs/outputs and environment awareness).
Propose a practical deployment architecture plus robustness mechanisms (monitoring, adaptation, and environment‑aware strategies) to reduce brittleness in dynamic settings.
infographic.impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to choose appropriately sized GUI agents and deploy them in production with improved interaction fidelity and resilience, accelerating real‑world HCI applications and reducing integration friction.

title: StreamAvatar: Streaming Diffusion Models for Real-Time Interactive Human Avatars
authors: Zhiyao Sun, Ziqiao Peng, Yifeng Ma, Yi Chen, Zhengguang Zhou
abstract: Real-time, streaming interactive avatars represent a critical yet challenging goal in digital human research. Although diffusion-based human avatar generation methods achieve remarkable success, their non-causal architecture and high computational costs make them unsuitable for streaming. Moreover, existing interactive approaches are typically limited to head-and-shoulder region, limiting their ability to produce gestures and body motions. To address these challenges, we propose a two-stage auto

infographic.key_insight: StreamAvatar introduces a causal, two-stage streaming diffusion architecture that enables low-latency, real-time generation of interactive full-body human avatars by decoupling coarse motion prediction from fine appearance synthesis.
infographic.problem_solved: Diffusion-based avatar methods are typically non-causal and computationally heavy, preventing real-time streaming and limiting outputs to head-and-shoulder regions; StreamAvatar addresses low-latency streaming and extends generation to full-body gestures and motions.
method: Two-stage streaming design: a lightweight autoregressive/coarse-stage that predicts temporally consistent motion and a fine-stage that refines appearance details frame-by-frame.
Causal, low-latency diffusion sampling and conditioning (e.g., pose/skeleton + audio/controls) to support interactive inputs and continuous output without future-frame access.
Efficiency optimizations (model modularization, progressive refinement, and sampling reduction) to meet real-time throughput on practical hardware/edge setups.
infographic.impact: Makes high-quality diffusion-based avatars feasible for live interactive applications (telepresence, VR/AR, virtual assistants, gaming), enabling full-body expressive motion with real-time responsiveness for practitioners and product teams.

title: DuaDeep-SeqAffinity: Dual-Stream Deep Learning Framework for Sequence-Only Antigen-Antibody Affinity Prediction
authors: Aicha Boutorh, Soumia Bouyahiaoui, Sara Belhadj, Nour El Yakine Guendouz, Manel Kara Laouar
abstract: Predicting the binding affinity between antigens and antibodies is fundamental to drug discovery and vaccine development. Traditional computational approaches often rely on experimentally determined 3D structures, which are scarce and computationally expensive to obtain. This paper introduces DuaDeep-SeqAffinity, a novel sequence-only deep learning framework that predicts affinity scores solely from their amino acid sequences using a dual-stream hybrid architecture. Our approach leverages pre-tr

infographic.key_insight: DuaDeep-SeqAffinity predicts antigen–antibody binding affinity directly from amino acid sequences using a dual-stream hybrid deep network, eliminating dependence on scarce 3D structural data.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the need for experimentally determined or computationally derived 3D structures for affinity prediction, enabling faster, scalable screening and design from sequence-only inputs.
method: Dual-stream encoding: separate sequence encoders for antigen and antibody that extract complementary sequence-level features.
Cross-stream fusion: a hybrid fusion module (e.g., cross-attention/interaction layers) integrates encoded representations to model pairwise interaction signals.
End-to-end regression: a downstream head maps fused features to a continuous affinity score; training uses affinity-labeled sequence datasets with augmentation and regularization.
infographic.impact: Enables rapid, structure-free affinity estimation useful for high-throughput antibody screening, lead prioritization, and sequence-driven design workflows — lowering experimental cost and accelerating ML-driven discovery.

title: Meta-Learning-Based Handover Management in NextG O-RAN
authors: Michail Kalntis, George Iosifidis, José Suárez-Varela, Andra Lutu, Fernando A. Kuipers
abstract: While traditional handovers (THOs) have served as a backbone for mobile connectivity, they increasingly suffer from failures and delays, especially in dense deployments and high-frequency bands. To address these limitations, 3GPP introduced Conditional Handovers (CHOs) that enable proactive cell reservations and user-driven execution. However, both handover (HO) types present intricate trade-offs in signaling, resource usage, and reliability. This paper presents unique, countrywide mobility mana

infographic.key_insight: A meta-learning framework lets O‑RAN controllers quickly adapt handover policies (choose between Conditional and Traditional HOs and tune parameters) across cells, substantially reducing failures and delay while controlling signaling and resource use.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses high handover failure rates, latency and the signaling/resource trade-offs of Traditional (THO) and Conditional Handovers (CHO) in dense, high‑frequency NextG deployments by enabling fast transfer and per‑cell adaptation of HO decisions.
method: Meta‑learning across cells to learn transferable initial policies/priors that speed up local adaptation to varying mobility and radio conditions.
Online adaptation in the O‑RAN near‑RT RIC: a decision agent selects HO type and parameters, balancing reliability vs signaling/resource costs via a reward function.
Large‑scale evaluation (countrywide mobility traces / realistic O‑RAN testbed simulation) demonstrating robustness and reduced failures/latency while controlling signaling overhead.
infographic.impact: Shows how meta‑learning can solve non‑stationary, distributed control problems in wireless networks and provides a practical blueprint for deploying ML agents in O‑RAN for real‑time radio management.

authors: Wen Jiang, Li Wang, Kangyao Huang, Wei Fan, Jinyuan Liu
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are crucial tools for post-disaster search and rescue, facing challenges such as high information density, rapid changes in viewpoint, and dynamic structures, especially in long-horizon navigation. However, current UAV vision-and-language navigation(VLN) methods struggle to model long-horizon spatiotemporal context in complex environments, resulting in inaccurate semantic alignment and unstable path planning. To this end, we propose LongFly, a spatiotemporal conte

infographic.key_insight: Fusing long-range spatiotemporal context into UAV vision-and-language navigation yields more accurate semantic grounding and stable long-horizon path planning in dynamic, high-density scenes.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of modeling long-horizon spatiotemporal context for UAV VLN in rapidly changing, cluttered environments (e.g., post-disaster), which causes poor semantic alignment and unstable navigation over long missions.
method: Spatiotemporal context encoder that aggregates multi-view observations across time to form a temporally stable scene representation.
Cross-modal alignment module that fuses aggregated visual-temporal features with language instructions for robust goal grounding and semantic understanding.
Memory-augmented / hierarchical planning component that leverages the integrated context to produce stable long-horizon trajectories under viewpoint changes and dynamic structure.

title: Patch-Discontinuity Mining for Generalized Deepfake Detection
authors: Huanhuan Yuan, Yang Ping, Zhengqin Xu, Junyi Cao, Shuai Jia
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic fake facial images, posing serious threats to personal privacy and the integrity of online information. Existing deepfake detection methods often rely on handcrafted forensic cues and complex architectures, achieving strong performance in intra-domain settings but suffering significant degradation when confronted with unseen forgery patterns. In this paper, we propose GenDF, a simple yet effe

infographic.key_insight: Mining local patch-to-patch discontinuities reveals subtle generative artifacts that generalize across unseen deepfake methods, enabling a simple detector (GenDF) to be more robust than complex, cue-specific models.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces severe performance degradation of deepfake detectors when faced with unseen forgery patterns by removing dependence on handcrafted forensic cues and heavy architectures.
method: Patch-discontinuity mining: extract and compare features from neighboring image patches to build discontinuity maps that highlight synthesis boundaries and inconsistencies.
Lightweight detector (GenDF): aggregate patch-level discontinuity signals into a global forgery score using a compact network/pooling strategy, focusing training on domain-agnostic artifacts.

Training objective and augmentation: supervise on image-level labels while encouraging the model to emphasize patch inconsistencies (e.g., contrastive or anomaly-aware losses and diverse augmentations to improve cross-domain generalization).
infographic.impact: Provides practitioners a simple, interpretable approach to build robust deepfake detectors that transfer better to new generative methods, reducing need for continuous re-training on every new forgery type.

title: Backdoor Attacks on Prompt-Driven Video Segmentation Foundation Models
authors: Zongmin Zhang, Zhen Sun, Yifan Liao, Wenhan Dong, Xinlei He
abstract: Prompt-driven Video Segmentation Foundation Models (VSFMs) such as SAM2 are increasingly deployed in applications like autonomous driving and digital pathology, raising concerns about backdoor threats. Surprisingly, we find that directly transferring classic backdoor attacks (e.g., BadNet) to VSFMs is almost ineffective, with ASR below 5\%. To understand this, we study encoder gradients and attention maps and observe that conventional training keeps gradients for clean and triggered samples larg

infographic.key_insight: Classic backdoor attacks (e.g., BadNet) transfer poorly to prompt-driven video segmentation foundation models like SAM2 (attack success rate < 5%), and analysis of encoder gradients and attention maps explains why triggers fail to produce consistent malicious behavior.
infographic.problem_solved: Assesses whether conventional image/video backdoor techniques can compromise prompt-driven video segmentation foundation models and diagnoses why straightforward transfer attacks are ineffective.
method: Empirically apply standard backdoor attacks (BadNet-style) to prompt-driven VSFMs and measure attack success rates (ASR).
Analyze internal signals—encoder gradient norms and attention maps—for clean vs. triggered samples to identify why triggers do not induce target behaviors.
Run controlled diagnostic/ablation experiments to isolate model components and mechanisms that block trigger-conditioned changes.
infographic.impact: Reveals that prompt-driven VSFMs exhibit inherent resistance to naive backdoor transfers, so security evaluations and defenses must be redesigned for prompt-based segmentation systems; attackers and defenders should adopt new threat models and tailored tests.

title: Parallel Token Prediction for Language Models
authors: Felix Draxler, Justus Will, Farrin Marouf Sofian, Theofanis Karaletsos, Sameer Singh
abstract: We propose Parallel Token Prediction (PTP), a universal framework for parallel sequence generation in language models. PTP jointly predicts multiple dependent tokens in a single transformer call by incorporating the sampling procedure into the model. This reduces the latency bottleneck of autoregressive decoding, and avoids the restrictive independence assumptions common in existing multi-token prediction methods. We prove that PTP can represent arbitrary autoregressive sequence distributions. P

infographic.key_insight: Parallel Token Prediction (PTP) lets a transformer predict multiple dependent tokens in one forward pass by embedding the sampling procedure into the model, eliminating the sequential decoding bottleneck while preserving dependency structure. The authors prove PTP can represent any autoregressive sequence distribution.
infographic.problem_solved: Reduces the latency and inefficiency of autoregressive decoding, which requires many sequential transformer calls and often forces independence assumptions in multi-token prediction methods.
method: Integrate the sampling process into the model so it jointly outputs blocks of dependent tokens in a single transformer call.
Design a training/inference scheme that preserves token dependencies (avoids restrictive independence assumptions) while enabling parallel generation.
Provide theoretical proof that the framework can represent arbitrary autoregressive sequence distributions, ensuring expressivity is retained.
infographic.impact: PTP enables much faster sequence generation without sacrificing sample quality or expressivity, making low-latency inference (e.g., real-time applications, edge devices, high-throughput servers) more practical for large language models.

authors: Yue Cao, Yingyao Wang, Pi Bu, Jingxuan Xing, Wei Jiang
abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents can substantially improve productivity by automating frequently executed long-latency tasks on mobile devices. However, existing evaluation benchmarks are still constrained to limited applications, simple tasks, and coarse-grained metrics. infographic.key_insight: AndroidLens provides a challenging, bilingual benchmark of long‑latency Android GUI tasks with nested sub‑targets and fine‑grained step evaluation, revealing capabilities and failure modes that coarse benchmarks miss.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing GUI agent evaluations are limited to few apps, simple tasks, and coarse metrics; AndroidLens fills the gap by offering a diverse, realistic set of long‑latency tasks and more precise evaluation criteria.
method: Curate 571 long‑latency Android tasks (Chinese & English) each requiring on average >26 steps, reflecting real mobile workflows.
Structure tasks with nested sub‑targets to capture multi‑stage objectives and partial progress, enabling step‑level success/failure assessment.
Provide evaluation protocols and metrics that go beyond single end‑state checks to measure intermediate correctness, robustness, and retry behavior.
infographic.impact: AndroidLens enables researchers and practitioners to benchmark mobile GUI agents against realistic, complex workflows and to diagnose fine‑grained weaknesses, accelerating progress on robust, multilingual, long‑latency automation.

title: DreaMontage: Arbitrary Frame-Guided One-Shot Video Generation
authors: Jiawei Liu, Junqiao Li, Jiangfan Deng, Gen Li, Siyu Zhou
abstract: The "one-shot" technique represents a distinct and sophisticated aesthetic in filmmaking. However, its practical realization is often hindered by prohibitive costs and complex real-world constraints. Although emerging video generation models offer a virtual alternative, existing approaches typically rely on naive clip concatenation, which frequently fails to maintain visual smoothness and temporal coherence. In this paper, we introduce DreaMontage, a comprehensive framework designed for arbitrar

infographic.key_insight: DreaMontage produces continuous, one-shot–style videos guided by arbitrary key frames by synthesizing smooth, temporally coherent transitions instead of naive clip concatenation. It unifies frame-guided generation with motion-aware blending to keep visual style and temporal continuity.
infographic.problem_solved: Existing virtual alternatives to one-shot filmmaking rely on simple concatenation of clips, causing style mismatch, flicker, and broken temporal coherence; real-world one-shot production is also costly and constrained. DreaMontage addresses reliable, controllable one-shot video synthesis from arbitrary frame guidance.
method: Frame-guided generation: condition a generative video model on one or more arbitrary reference frames to anchor spatial style and content.
Temporal coherence module: apply motion-aware blending/attention and consistency losses to avoid flicker and ensure smooth transitions between synthesized frames.
Montage-aware assembly: plan and synthesize cut/transition points and perform generative refinement to produce a single continuous one-shot output rather than naïve clip splicing.
infographic.impact: Enables filmmakers and ML practitioners to create controllable one-shot cinematic videos with fewer resources and higher visual continuity; useful for creative production, rapid prototyping, and data augmentation for temporal tasks.

title: GriDiT: Factorized Grid-Based Diffusion for Efficient Long Image Sequence Generation
authors: Snehal Singh Tomar, Alexandros Graikos, Arjun Krishna, Dimitris Samaras, Klaus Mueller
abstract: Modern deep learning methods typically treat image sequences as large tensors of sequentially stacked frames. However, is this straightforward representation ideal given the current state-of-the-art (SoTA)? In this work, we address this question in the context of generative models and aim to devise a more effective way of modeling image sequence data. Observing the inefficiencies and bottlenecks of current SoTA image sequence generation methods, we showcase that rather than working with large te

infographic.key_insight: Represent long image sequences as factorized spatial grids instead of single giant stacked tensors, enabling diffusion models to generate much longer sequences with dramatically lower compute and memory while preserving temporal coherence.
infographic.problem_solved: Current sequence-generation models treat videos/long image streams as huge stacked-frame tensors, causing quadratic memory/compute growth, slow sampling, and poor scalability for long or high-resolution sequences. This work addresses those bottlenecks to make long-sequence generative modeling practical.
method: Factorized grid representation: split frames into a regular spatial grid of patches/cells and model each cell with a diffusion process rather than a single large tensor of stacked frames.

Grid-based diffusion with factorized conditionals: perform denoising locally on grid cells while using lightweight cross-cell communication (hierarchical/global tokens or sparse attention) to maintain spatial and temporal coherence.

Efficient architecture & sampling: design training and inference strategies that exploit parallelism across grid cells and reduce attention/memory complexity, enabling longer sequences with lower latency and resource use.
infographic.impact: Makes high-quality generation of long image sequences (long videos, panoramas over time, multi-view simulations) feasible on practical hardware by cutting compute and memory requirements; enables faster experimentation and deployment of long-form generative systems.

Within this pipeline, surgical scene segmentation plays a central role in accurately perceiving operative events. infographic.key_insight: Combining spiking (event-driven) neural layers with a video transformer backbone yields a segmentation model that maintains high surgical scene accuracy while dramatically lowering compute and energy, enabling near real-time operation on constrained hardware.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the high computational cost and power consumption of state-of-the-art surgical segmentation models, which prevents reliable real-time deployment in resource-constrained operating-room systems and edge devices.
method: Introduce a spike-driven encoder that processes video frames event-style (sparse activations) to reduce redundant computation and power usage.
Integrate the spike encoder with a lightweight video transformer to capture temporal context and long-range dependencies across frames efficiently.
Design for hardware friendliness (sparse attention, low-precision/spike-compatible operations) to enable real-time potential on edge/neuromorphic platforms.
infographic.impact: Enables practical, low-latency surgical scene segmentation for intra-operative assistance and monitoring, making advanced perception models deployable on edge and power-limited systems. Useful blueprint for ML practitioners aiming to trade minimal accuracy loss for large energy and latency savings.

title: Transcriptome-Conditioned Personalized De Novo Drug Generation for AML Using Metaheuristic Assembly and Target-Driven Filtering
authors: Abdullah G. Elafifi, Basma Mamdouh, Mariam Hanafy, Muhammed Alaa Eldin, Yosef Khaled
abstract: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) remains a clinical challenge due to its extreme molecular heterogeneity and high relapse rates. While precision medicine has introduced mutation-specific therapies, many patients still lack effective, personalized options. This paper presents a novel, end-to-end computational framework that bridges the gap between patient-specific transcriptomics and de novo drug discovery. By analyzing bulk RNA sequencing data from the TCGA-LAML cohort, the study utilized Weighted G

infographic.key_insight: A transcriptome-conditioned pipeline converts individual AML patient RNA-seq signatures into personalized de novo small-molecule candidates by combining co-expression-driven target selection with metaheuristic molecular assembly and target-driven filtering. This end-to-end approach links patient biology directly to generative drug design.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses the lack of personalized therapeutic options for molecularly heterogeneous AML patients by automatically translating patient-specific transcriptomic dysregulation into candidate compounds tailored to their disease biology.
method: Extract patient-specific actionable targets from bulk TCGA-LAML RNA-seq via weighted gene co-expression analysis (e.g., WGCNA) and differential expression to prioritize disease modules.
Generate candidate molecules with a metaheuristic assembly engine (optimization-based de novo design guided by transcriptome-derived objectives) to explore chemical space efficiently.
Apply target-driven filtering (in silico affinity prediction / scoring against prioritized targets plus ADMET and drug-likeness filters) to rank personalized leads.
infographic.impact: Demonstrates how integrating omics-driven target selection with optimization-based generative chemistry can produce personalized drug hypotheses — a useful blueprint for ML practitioners building clinically oriented molecule design pipelines and evaluation benchmarks.

title: Autonomous Uncertainty Quantification for Computational Point-of-care Sensors
authors: Artem Goncharov, Rajesh Ghosh, Hyou-Arm Joung, Dino Di Carlo, Aydogan Ozcan
abstract: Computational point-of-care (POC) sensors enable rapid, low-cost, and accessible diagnostics in emergency, remote and resource-limited areas that lack access to centralized medical facilities. These systems can utilize neural network-based algorithms to accurately infer a diagnosis from the signals generated by rapid diagnostic tests or sensors. However, neural network-based diagnostic models are subject to hallucinations and can produce erroneous predictions, posing a risk of misdiagnosis and i

infographic.key_insight: Integrating autonomous uncertainty quantification with neural diagnostic models for point-of-care sensors enables the system to detect and flag low-confidence predictions in real time, reducing the risk of misdiagnosis and inappropriate automated outputs.
infographic.problem_solved: Neural-network-based computational POC sensors can produce hallucinations or erroneous outputs without a reliable measure of confidence, creating safety and trust issues when deployed in emergency, remote, or resource-limited settings.
method: Embed lightweight, on-device uncertainty estimators alongside the diagnostic model to produce per-sample confidence scores (e.g., Bayesian approximations, ensembles, or evidential approaches tailored for edge constraints).
Apply calibration and out-of-distribution detection so predicted probabilities match real-world accuracy and unknown inputs are flagged.
Use autonomous decision logic that triggers abstention, prompts for human review, or routes results for higher-fidelity testing when uncertainty exceeds configured thresholds.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical path for safer, trustworthy POC AI deployments by enabling real-time reliability estimates, improving triage and clinician trust, and supporting regulatory and operational requirements for medical AI at the edge.

title: ReaSeq: Unleashing World Knowledge via Reasoning for Sequential Modeling
authors: Chuan Wang, Gaoming Yang, Han Wu, Jiakai Tang, Jiahao Yu
abstract: Industrial recommender systems face two fundamental limitations under the log-driven paradigm: (1) knowledge poverty in ID-based item representations that causes brittle interest modeling under data sparsity, and (2) systemic blindness to beyond-log user interests that constrains model performance within platform boundaries. These limitations stem from an over-reliance on shallow interaction statistics and close-looped feedback while neglecting the rich world knowledge about product semantics an

infographic.key_insight: Injecting explicit world knowledge and lightweight reasoning into sequential recommender models converts sparse, ID-based item signals into rich semantic representations, enabling the model to capture beyond-log user interests and improve robustness under data sparsity.
infographic.problem_solved: Addresses brittle interest modeling caused by ID-only item representations and the inability of log-driven systems to perceive user preferences outside platform interaction histories.
method: Map ID-based items to semantic world knowledge (e.g., product text, attributes, knowledge graph nodes) to produce content-rich item embeddings.
Apply a reasoning module (retrieval + lightweight inference) to augment user interaction sequences with inferred, beyond-log interests and semantic relations.
Fuse the knowledge-augmented sequence into a sequential modeling backbone (e.g., Transformer/RNN) and train with objectives that encourage generalization and robustness under sparse logs.
infographic.impact: Provides a practical pattern to make recommender systems less brittle and more aware of real-world product semantics and latent user intent, improving cold-start handling and cross-platform generalization for practitioners.

title: HiStream: Efficient High-Resolution Video Generation via Redundancy-Eliminated Streaming
authors: Haonan Qiu, Shikun Liu, Zijian Zhou, Zhaochong An, Weiming Ren
abstract: High-resolution video generation, while crucial for digital media and film, is computationally bottlenecked by the quadratic complexity of diffusion models, making practical inference infeasible. To address this, we introduce HiStream, an efficient autoregressive framework that systematically reduces redundancy across three axes: i) Spatial Compression: denoising at low resolution before refining at high resolution with cached features; ii) Temporal Compression: a chunk-by-chunk strategy with a

infographic.key_insight: HiStream makes high-resolution video generation practical by eliminating redundant computation across space, time, and sampling, using a streaming autoregressive pipeline that denoises cheaply and refines selectively.
infographic.problem_solved: Diffusion-based high-resolution video generation is infeasible in practice due to quadratic compute and memory costs; HiStream addresses this by reducing redundant work so inference becomes efficient and scalable.
method: Spatial compression: perform denoising at lower resolution then refine to high resolution using cached high‑level features to avoid re-computing shared spatial detail.
Temporal compression: generate video in streaming chunks with overlap and temporal feature caching so adjacent frames reuse computation rather than reprocessing entire sequences.
Sampling/computation compression: concentrate expensive high‑res denoising only where needed and reuse denoising trajectories or intermediate features to cut the number of heavy diffusion operations.
infographic.impact: Enables faster, lower‑cost high‑resolution video synthesis on practical hardware and makes large-scale or real‑time applications of diffusion-based video models more attainable for ML practitioners.

title: AnyAD: Unified Any-Modality Anomaly Detection in Incomplete Multi-Sequence MRI
authors: Changwei Wu, Yifei Chen, Yuxin Du, Mingxuan Liu, Jinying Zong
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection in brain MRI remains challenging due to the scarcity of annotated abnormal cases and the frequent absence of key imaging modalities in real clinical workflows. Existing single-class or multi-class anomaly detection (AD) models typically rely on fixed modality configurations, require repetitive training, or fail to generalize to unseen modality combinations, limiting their clinical scalability. In this work, we present a unified Any-Modality AD framework that performs r

infographic.key_insight: AnyAD presents a single unified anomaly-detection model that works with any subset of multi-sequence brain MRI — it handles missing modalities at inference without retraining while maintaining robust anomaly detection.
infographic.problem_solved: Overcomes clinical challenges of scarce annotated abnormalities and frequently absent MRI sequences by avoiding fixed-modality pipelines and eliminating the need to train separate models for every modality combination.
method: Learn modality-agnostic representations and a shared anomaly scoring mechanism so the same model can ingest any available subset of MRI sequences.
Train with simulated missing-modality conditions (e.g., modality dropout / cross-modal consistency) and reconstruction/consistency objectives to enable prediction from incomplete inputs.
Unified inference: compute anomaly scores/maps directly from whatever sequences are present, without modality-specific retraining or ensemble models.
infographic.impact: Makes anomaly detection in multi-sequence MRI practical for real clinical settings with variable imaging protocols, improving deployability and reducing annotation/training burden for AI practitioners working on medical imaging.
